Hellbreakers.name: 地狱破灭 Hellbreakers
Hellbreakers.description:
随着地狱火危机爆发，动乱蔓延至整个阿维斯坦，反抗组织破狱者联盟也在依斯嘉掀起波澜，力图让这个国家摆脱其信奉魔鬼的宗主国切利亚斯的压迫。玩家角色将深入切利亚斯的据点执行大胆的任务，迎战危险的地狱骑士，甚至向地狱本身的势力发起进攻！在此过程中，他们将遭遇新老劲敌，并揭开尘封已久、蕴藏强大力量的古老秘密。玩家角色能否燃起革命之火，挣脱切利亚斯的魔鬼枷锁，还是会被践踏在压迫者的铁靴之下？加入破狱者，为革命尽一份力吧！

《地狱破灭》是一本256页的精装冒险之路，专为四名角色设计。角色将从1级起步，在冒险中不断成长，并在战役激动人心的终章达到10级。本书还收录了介绍依斯嘉风土人情的地志，以及对厄加图娅教派的深入介绍，并提供实用的新物品、精彩的角色选项和众多危险的怪物。

Campaign Summary.name: 战役总结 Campaign Summary
Campaign Summary.text:
战役总结 Campaign Summary

地狱骑士山之战结束后，PC们从布雷克屯前往萨里伽洛，与他们在破狱者联盟中的上级会面。他们执行了数项任务，并得知有一位“地狱骑士”正伺机向联盟复仇。PC们随后被派往乡村，在政府疏于照顾之处援助民众，以赢得他们的支持。旅途中，PC们发现了“地狱骑士”@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole05]针对依斯嘉所策划阴谋的证据——而尖叫森林正是其计划的第一步。得知维罗的计划后，PC们前往尖叫森林，向当地的地精居民求援，请他们协助阻止这名叛离正道的地狱骑士扈从。

当PC们在乡村处理事务时，破狱者联盟的领袖们正在首都谋划对策。身份暴露后，急需有人代替他们出席活动的领袖们召来PC们，让他们以假身份参加海德文六世的魔鬼主题化装晚宴。晚宴上，PC们结识了多位重要人物，其中包括地狱骑士副执棒官@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole01]，他即将领导一支新成立的特别行动队，负责追捕破狱者联盟成员。然而，一群假冒的破狱者突然袭击晚宴，打断了这场盛会。PC们解决了这些冒名顶替者，却很快得知海德文遭人谋杀，而破狱者联盟被指为凶手！随着其他神秘死亡事件接连发生，凯托请求PC们调查此事。真正的凶手是同为宾客的@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole02]。他是一名吸血鬼，也是@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]的追随者；后者图谋将依斯嘉变成一个向@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]纳贡的不死属国。

凯托接管了艾利迪尔，宣布全国戒严，并将海德文之死归咎于破狱者联盟。PC们一边协助壮大当地新成立的破狱者联盟分部，一边筹划逃离城市，但新分部的成员遭到逮捕，令事态急转直下。PC们必须救出新结识的朋友，并大胆逃离艾利迪尔！

PC们返回萨里伽洛后，却得知伊尔凯娜·阿隆诺的不死军队已经开始行动，而凯托拒绝处理这一威胁。眼见无人愿意帮助依斯嘉的民众，PC们再次前往乡村，寻找解决不死生物之患的方法。抵达基拉摩尔后，PC们得知该镇曾遭伊尔凯娜诅咒，任何死在镇界内的人都会复生为受她奴役的不死生物——而她计划通过仪式，将这一诅咒威力强大得多的版本施加于整个国家。PC们必须前往发现者峡谷，彻底击败尸妖之母。

击败伊尔凯娜后，破狱者联盟比以往任何时候都更受民众拥护，但声势日盛也让凯托查明了他们位于萨里伽洛的总部。PC们勉强逃过追捕，必须先夺取臭名昭著的萨里尼庄园作为据点，而后设法解救其他破狱者联盟成员。

与凯托本人正面对决的时刻终于到来。PC们率领集结而来的军队与盟友围攻萨里伽洛，发起反击，解救朋友、夺回家园，并最终赢得自由。

升级轨迹

《地狱破灭》是为四名角色设计的冒险。

1PC们在本冒险开始时为1级。

2PC们在救出洛克拉格并击败切利亚斯忠诚派后，应升至2级。

3PC们在击败金怒魔姐妹后，应升至3级。

4 PC们在阻止维罗·阿哈拉的仪式并拯救依斯嘉后，应升至4级。

5 PC们在潜入海德文的晚宴后，应升至5级。

6 PC们在侦破海德文谋杀案并阻止埃齐奥后，应升至6级。

7 PC们在逃离艾利迪尔后，应升至7级。

8 PC们在击败伊尔凯娜及其不死大军后，应升至8级。

9 PC们在夺回萨里尼庄园后，应升至9级。

PC们应在冒险结束时达到10级。

Timeline.name: 时间线 Timeline
Timeline.text:
时间线 Timeline

以下事件发生在本战役之前，并对其产生了影响。

时间 事件
AR2133 年 塔尔多的第七探索军团击败了当地的依斯嘉人，依斯嘉成为塔尔多的一个行省。
AR4081 年 切利亚斯在双舌征服战中宣布脱离塔尔多独立。依斯嘉在此过程中被吞并，成为切利亚斯的附庸国。
AR4601 年 厄加图娅的年轻女祭司@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]将自己喂给了一群尸妖，随后作为一名@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]之女（daughter of Urgathoa）重生。她屠杀了发现者峡谷的村民，并将他们转化成了她的不死奴仆。
AR4638 年 尖钉骑士团成立，并在依斯嘉的布雷克屯附近建造了阿尔泰林堡。
AR4697-4701 年 来自依斯嘉南部尖叫森林的成百上千的地精类生物在全国范围内发起进攻，开启了地精血战。政府对依斯嘉乡村地区的惨烈冲突反应迟缓，引发了腹地平民的愤恨。最终在切利亚斯地狱骑士、安多安雄鹰骑士以及杜鲁玛佣兵联盟小队的共同努力下，战争得以结束。
AR4701 年 依斯嘉军队在地精血战中蒙受了巨大损失，以至于其统治者海德温六世命令其部队专注于关键贸易路线，任由乡村地区自生自灭。斯戎家族通过@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]教会向战争孤儿提供援助，而伊尔凯娜则利用大量的伤亡转化了更多的不死生物。
AR4702 年 伊尔凯娜·阿洛诺尔诅咒了一名旅行商人，该商人在死后葬于基拉莫尔时在不知情的情况下播下了诅咒。不久，所有村民都相继死去并转化为贪食的不死生物。该地受到诅咒，任何死在那里的人都会变成伊尔凯娜的不死奴仆。
AR4711 年 阿尔泰林堡被彻底废弃。
AR4717 年 吵闹踉跄鬼（Bumblebrasher）部落的地精搬入了阿尔泰林堡。
AR4719 年 英雄们清除了阿尔泰林堡的各种威胁，并将其作为行动基地，致力于阻止一场新的灰烬之年（Age of Ashes）。在成功完成任务后，他们将城堡赠给了布雷克屯的公民。
AR4724 年人文月 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.88vRw2ZVPax4hhga]陨落，神雨在格拉利昂倾泻而下，开启了一场战神碎片军备竞赛。破狱者联盟、伊尔凯娜·阿洛诺尔和卡尔特萨·伊莉斯女士都为了各自的目的收集战神碎片。
AR4724 年魔法月 依斯嘉政府怀疑破狱者联盟将战神碎片藏匿在布雷克屯或附近的阿尔泰林堡内。
AR4725 年财商月 应总督海德温六世的要求，女皇阿波罗盖·斯戎二世派遣了刑架骑士团中忠诚的地狱骑士前往布雷克屯铲除叛国者，并收回他们发现的任何战神碎片。
AR4725 年风海月 刑架骑士团的地狱骑士占领了布雷克屯，软禁了大多数居民。虽然进行了多次公开处决，但在居民中并未发现破狱者联盟的成员。
AR4725 年星梦月 来自切利亚斯的补给使得刑架骑士团的地狱骑士得以在阿尔泰林堡内建立防御工事，并用炼狱结界圣化了建筑，召唤出了一头地狱龙。
AR4725 年阳炎月 由半退休的雷金纳德·科莫斯将军率领的安多安外交团队前往布雷克屯，要求地狱骑士停止压迫该镇民众。地狱骑士勃然大怒，抓捕并公开处决了科莫斯将军；他的随从逃离了该地区。
AR4725 年农狩月 随着科莫斯将军之死在民众中引发了巨大的愤慨，一场紧急人民议会（People’s Council）在阿玛斯（Almas）举行，讨论布雷克屯的事态。经过数日的讨论，雄鹰骑士中的钢隼前往依斯嘉。
AR4725 年人文月 地狱骑士山之战：历经多番艰苦鏖战，雄鹰骑士夺回了布雷克屯和阿尔泰林堡。一些刑架骑士团的地狱骑士被俘，但更多人撤回了切利亚斯。破狱者联盟从附近的山洞中现身，与安多安军队进行交涉。安多安承诺提供援助以换取一枚强大的战神碎片，该碎片随后被送回安多安。
AR4725 年怒灾月 当前的年份和月份。

Relations.name: 关系 Relations
Relations.text:
Relations

Isger is mostly forgotten by Cheliax, mainly retaining any significance due to the river running through it that brings lucrative shipments and trade. Cheliax sent limited aid during the Goblinblood Wars but mostly let the nation fend for itself. Once the wars were over, they sent nuns to perform acts of charity and indoctrinate civilians, for which many citizens are grateful. The opinions on Chelaxian rule are split, with more ire toward the patron nation in the countryside.

Important Locations.name: Important Locations
Important Locations.text:
Important Locations

Chitterwood: A large forest that was mostly burned down during the Goblinblood Wars. It's mostly occupied by goblinoids.

Elidir: The nation's capital, home of the wealthy elites and Cheliax's main supporters.

Finder's Gulch: This town is the headquarters of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} and overrun with undead.

Saringallow: This small city is the base for the Hellbreakers League headquarters.

Names to Know.name: Names to Know
Names to Know.text:
Names to Know

Abrogail Thrune: Abrogail II is the ruler of Cheliax. She doesn't make an appearance in this adventure, but her influence is felt everywhere Cheliax has a hold.

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole04]{Alceo Demetrias}: Cofounder of the Hellbreakers League, Alceo is a cleric of the goddess @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.fTJLgTfEMZreJ19r]{Milani}.

Hedvend VI: Hedvend is the steward of Isger. He's known to consistently prioritize Cheliax's wants over Isger's needs.

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor}: Illcayna is a worshipper of the goddess @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}, and her sole purpose is to turn Isger into a tribute nation to her goddess. She's in possession of a warshard, which she plans to use to achieve her goals.

Kaltessa Iyis: Kaltessa is the mysterious, centuries-old high priestess of the archdevil @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.sNjPI1iaS8Z43YJf]{Mammon}. She only makes a cameo in this adventure, but you might be seeing her again!

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole04]{Phoebe Demetrias}: Cofounder of the Hellbreakers League, Phoebe is an ex-soldier now commander of the rebels.

Terms to Know.name: Terms to Know
Terms to Know.text:
Terms to Know

Cheliax: Cheliax is the patron nation of Isger and worships the archdevil @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}.

The Goblinblood Wars: In this war, hobgoblins from the Chitterwood raised armies of goblins and set about destroying settlements nearby. Isger suffered greatly during this time, and the war's effects still haunt its populace.

Hellbreakers League: A rebel organization dedicated to freeing Isger from Cheliax's oppressive rule.

Hellknight: Hellknights are Chelaxian knights dedicated to law and order above all else. There are several different orders of Hellknights; the most relevant to this adventure is the Order of the Godclaw, which is known to worship @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.JndhOIHnQoMwnsw3]{The Godclaw} pantheon. There are mentions of the Order of the Rack early on.

Warshard: When the god @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.88vRw2ZVPax4hhga]{Gorum} died, several parts of his body and weapons were strewn about the Universe in pieces called warshards. These items hold immense divine power.

Subsystems.name: Subsystems
Subsystems.text:
Subsystems

This campaign makes use of several subsystems. The first is a reputation system that's used throughout the entire campaign. In @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway]{Chapter 6}, several subsystems are used: the Victory Point system, the infiltration system, and the chase subsystem. @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22209thebat]{Chapter 9} uses the research subsystem.

About the PCs.name: About the PCs
About the PCs.text:
About the PCs

The 1st-level PCs are low-ranking members of the Hellbreakers League. People of all types and backgrounds join the Hellbreakers League, including outsiders like an Eagle Knight with a bleeding heart or a Drumish mercenary promised a reward for participation. This Adventure Path caters to a wide range of gameplay styles with social, wilderness, and combat challenges.

Make sure your players read the free Player's Guide to prepare for the adventure and make PCs appropriate for the story. Don't forget that there's a @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16hellbreakera00]{Hellbreaker Archetype} they can take at Level 2, and there's also a @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16newanimalcom00]{New Animal Companion} available.

Campaign Overview.name: Campaign Overview
Campaign Overview.text:
Campaign Overview

Campaign Background

Isger has been neglected by Cheliax and its own government for decades. A group of idealists and former soldiers, sick of the people bearing the brunt of the authorities' poor decisions, founded the Hellbreakers League to gather like-minded rebels in hopes of sparking a revolution. They made little traction until the Godsrain, when they managed to locate and obtain a warshard in the town of Breachill.

However, Isger's steward, Hedvend VI, was alerted to their activity and reported it to Abrogail Thrune. Queen Abrogail II, coveting the warshard and seeking to stamp out rebellion, sent the Order of the Rack to seize Breachill and scour it for her prizes.

The town withered under the subsequent public executions and the Hellknights' harsh rule. Breachill's cries for deliverance made it to the nation of Andoran, who sent a contingent of diplomats, including the retired general Reginald Cormoth, to entreat the Hellknights to stop subjugating Breachill's citizens. The Hellknights responded by executing Reginald.

Outraged by the brutal and unnecessary act of violence, Eagle Knights of the Steel Falcons went to Isger and initiated the Battle of Hellknight Hill, a grueling fight that ended in the Eagle Knights' victory. The Hellbreakers aided the Eagle Knights, and after the battle, they were promised aid from Andoran in exchange for their warshard.

A survivor of the battle, the armiger @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole05]{Viro Ahala}, managed to acquire full Hellknight plate before fleeing the battlefield. He sought aid from the Sisters of the Golden Erinys, who mistook him for a full-fledged Hellknight. Viro used the nuns' resources to learn of a ritual to summon a powerful devil to exact revenge upon the Hellbreakers League.

Meanwhile, in the capital of Elidir, an agent of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} prepares to throw Isger's government into chaos and arrange things so Illcayna can easily take over the nation. @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole02]{Ezio Gaeta} plans to assassinate Hedvend at the steward's own gala, distracting the authorities while Illcayna prepares to enact a powerful ritual to transform all of Isger into her undead thralls.

Ignorant to those who plot against them, the Hellbreakers League is reconvening in Saringallow to take advantage of the momentum from their recent victory.

Content Warning

This adventure contains themes of war, oppression, torture, and political violence. Before you begin, understand that player consent (including that of the Game Master) is vital to a safe and fun play experience for everyone. You should talk with your players before beginning the adventure and modify descriptions of the narrative as appropriate.

A Hellknight's Revenge?.name: A Hellknight's Revenge?
A Hellknight's Revenge?.text:
A Hellknight's Revenge?

As the group draws close to Saringallow, Rhokrag speaks up.

“There's something bigger at play,” Rhokrag says, wincing as he walks. “I overheard the captain telling her crew that ‘Hellknight Ahala' would pay handsomely for information on the League to ‘strike back against the rebels who fomented the violence in Breachill.' If there's a Hellknight out there hunting us down for revenge, we'd best tread carefully until we learn more.”

Reward: For rescuing Rhokrag, award the PCs 80 XP.

Captain's Quarters.name: Captain's Quarters
Captain's Quarters.text:
C6. Captain's QuartersSevere 1

This spacious chamber is lavishly furnished with black and red velvet drapes, overstuffed chairs, a bed, and a mahogany desk. Several trinkets sit on shelves. The grandeur of the decor is marred by fresh bloodstains on the floor. Sitting in the center of the room is Rhokrag, barely conscious and tied to a wooden chair. His face is a map of bruises and cuts. Behind him stands a tall and imposing woman dressed in the uniform of the Chelaxian navy, as well as a grinning devil.

The captain's quarters have been temporarily transformed into an interrogation room, as Captain Bane and her summoned devil accomplice have been questioning Rhokrag here for the past few days. A PC can free Rhokrag with a single Interact action, but his weakened state makes him unable to participate directly in combat.

C6. Captain's QuartersSevere 1

@UUID[Actor.adtxENRwyEjT6CXp]{Zemaniah} @UUID[Actor.6rBzmdt0OsbnNgaD]{Captain Lamperia Bane} @UUID[Actor.iIBwVD8IJiGVrkww]{Rhokrag}

Creatures: Captain Bane is a staunch Thrune supporter and diabolist. Upon capturing Rhokrag, she performed a brief ritual to gain the temporary services of an entrapment devil. Rhokrag has resisted the devil's methods so far, but he grows weaker the longer his torment continues.

Captain Bane is quick to order the devil, Zemaniah, to attack the PCs when they interrupt the interrogation. She isn't afraid to engage in melee and fights to the death to protect her prize (and her ship).

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.73n0nsL61ISaASWv]{Captain's Desk}
The trinkets on the captain's desk are worth 35 gp. A PC who searches the desk also finds a harpy's talon and a pair of simple manacles.

Galley.name: Galley
Galley.text:
C5. Galley

The aft doors lead into the ship's galley, which contains its stores of fresh water and salted meat. Several hammocks hang near the ship's fore, each covered by a thin blanket.

This area serves as the place where the crew eats and sleeps. The Witchfire doesn't have a dedicated ship's cook, so the recruits take turns preparing meager meals.

Hold.name: Hold
Hold.text:
C4b. Hold

The Witchfire's hold is currently empty, save for a human-sized cage that acts as a brig and a single chest at the other end.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.NBPOyEI4HJrh47Sw]{Chest}
Inside the chest is the ship's payroll, consisting of 30 gp. Captain Bane leaves the chest unlocked, as the crew knows better than to try to steal the money. The last swabbie who tried was hanged from the boom.

Witchfire Deck.name: Witchfire Deck
Witchfire Deck.text:
C4a. Witchfire DeckModerate 1

A short gangplank leads up from the riverbank to the deck of this Chelaxian vessel. Most of the planks making up the deck and hull have been painted black, though elaborate wooden scrollwork along the gunwales and across the bow depict curling wicks of flame, the tips of which have been colored a bright green. Other details around the ship have been painted the same color, giving an eerie effect. Doors lead fore and aft, and a ladder leads down into the hold. A Chelaxian flag flies from top the taller of the two masts.

The Witchfire's color scheme is meant to intimidate enemy vessels and help the vessel move stealthily through the night when necessary. It's a well-maintained ship, thanks to Captain Bane's strictness. With such a small crew, she can focus her attention on any one of them at any point to discipline laziness or incompetence.

The rigging here can be climbed with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:10|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] check.

C4a. Witchfire DeckModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.P95K6b2kbfB58nwp]{Chelaxian Marines (2)}

Creatures: Two marines are on board at all times, keeping watch for threats from the river and scrubbing the deck. The marines use their familiarity with the ship to their advantage, climbing up into the rigging and attacking PCs below. Any marines the PCs encounter here have served with Captain Bane for a few years, so they know she expects them to die for her; they fight until brought down to 0 HP.

These marines are a little afraid to leave their posts but are equally worried about allowing intruders to interrupt Captain Bane's interrogations. If they notice a fight at the camp in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01shorecampund00]{C3}, they wait until the third round of combat before rolling initiative and disembarking the ship. When they do so, they begin the fight @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Shore Camp.name: Shore Camp
Shore Camp.text:
C3. Shore CampModerate 1

Three tents have been erected in the narrow stretch between the inn and the river. Pennants with the national symbol of Cheliax fly from each tent, occasionally flapping in a cold breeze coming from off the water. A campfire smolders in the middle of the tents, surrounded by a couple of collapsible cloth camp stools.

Despite having rented out the inn's few rooms, Captain Bane insists that her crew either remain on board the ship or set up camp outside the inn. She doesn't want them “going soft” after sleeping in beds for a few nights. The three tents here are dyed red and black and each hold one sleeper.

C3. Shore CampModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.EI8jeO9iW8n1s0y6]{Chelaxian Loyalist} @UUID[Actor.dZqZzPFjGYz7s7rs]{Chelaxian Recruits (2)}

Creatures: Two recent recruits to the Witchfire's crew have been relegated to camp duty. One of the local loyalists is also here, eager to curry favor with anyone associated with the Chelaxian government. Though the recruits are relaxing, they're still disciplined soldiers. They're wearing their armor and have their weapons within arm's reach as they sit by the campfire.

If they spot the PCs before combat starts, they first attempt to scare off the PCs. When it becomes clear that the PCs aren't civilians, one recruit takes up their guisarme and demands the loyalist backs them up in melee combat, while the other recruit fires arrows at any other ranged combatant or spellcaster. The loyalist tries to flee if either of the recruits are knocked unconscious, but the recruits are steadfastly faithful to Cheliax and Captain Bane and fight until reduced to 0 Hit Points.

By now, the recruits are used to commotions coming from inside the inn as other loyalists drink and get rowdy, so they don't respond to any sounds of combat. However, if the PCs manage to sneak aboard the Witchfire and start a fight, the recruits will take a round to gather their weapons and rush onto the ship; the loyalist doesn't join them.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.Yyv4UES6KyB180Vn]{Tents}
Within the camping crew members' tents are two lesser atrophy bombs and two vials of lesser alchemist's fire.

Waterspout Inn.name: Waterspout Inn
Waterspout Inn.text:
C2. Waterspout InnLow 1

A fire burns in the hearth of this simple tavern to ward off the autumnal chill. A gaudily painted trident hangs above the fireplace. Several tables have been pushed against one wall, their accompanying chairs haphazardly stacked on top. A door leads out to the inn's front yard and a slightly smaller door next to the bar leads out back. A set of stairs leads up to the second floor.

When Captain Bane arrived a few days ago and rented out the whole building, Vinzent, the inn's proprietor, guiltily drank himself into a stupor as he knows the captain is likely to have ill intentions for Isger. He's currently passed out on one of the upstairs room's beds. If the PCs find and wake him, he gives them a warning about Captain Bane: “She consorts with devils, she does!” Otherwise, the rented rooms are empty.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Macro.JzOyolI2GTLbBvkE]{Toggle Inn Ambience}

C2. Waterspout InnLow 1

@UUID[Actor.EI8jeO9iW8n1s0y6]{Chelaxian Loyalists (3)}

Creatures: Three of the loyalists recruited by Captain Bane are on the first floor, occasionally partaking of the inn's alcohol and playing games of darts. They're waiting for the captain to finally break Rhokrag, giving them more targets on which to vent their pro-Cheliax ire. They're cowards at heart, so if one of them is knocked unconscious, the other two try to flee through the most accessible door. This might mean they run out the back, alerting the camp. Otherwise, the recruits are used to hearing the loyalists carousing and don't investigate if they hear noises from the inn.

Innkeeper's Aid: @UUID[Actor.yA1AFtG3MJPIm1nt]{Vinzent's Gift}
To alleviate his guilt in helping Bane, Vinzent offers the PCs a lesser bottled lightning and swift sparrow marvelous miniature that he had in storage.

Inn Yard.name: Inn Yard
Inn Yard.text:
C1. Inn Yard

A small stone fountain, its basin empty except for several fallen leaves, stands just a few yards from the road. The two-story inn beyond it was once painted a bright blue, but the color has faded to gray. A sign above the front door reads “Waterspout Inn” with a crude image of an upward spray of water. A path of churned-up dirt by the fountain leads to an unattached stable.

The inn's fountain has been drained for the autumn and winter seasons. The stable is unoccupied, apart from a few mice nibbling on some old hay.

As they don't know who's inside the inn, the PCs might try to create a diversion to draw out the occupants. To do so, a PC must succeed on a DC 12 skill check, depending on the nature of the ruse; @Check[deception|dc:12] and @Check[performance|dc:12] are likely the most applicable skills. The loyalists inside have grown bored after the brief excitement of capturing Rhokrag, so they're eager to investigate any sounds.

Rhokrag's Rescue.name: Rhokrag's Rescue
Rhokrag's Rescue.text:
Rhokrag's Rescue

Unfortunately, when Rhokrag met his contact at the Waterspout Inn, he was betrayed. With whispers of insurgents and revolutionaries in Isger, the Chelaxian navy sent a patrol ship up the Conerica to make it clear to the citizens who was in charge. This vessel, the Witchfire, is captained by Lamperia Bane (ruthless female human captain 3), a steadfast military woman who signed her soul away to Hell only a few years ago in exchange for a rapid rise up the ranks. Upon arriving in Isger, Captain Bane began announcing that she would double the bounty started by Hedvend for information on dissidents. Most of her informants had little real information with the exception of Rhokrag's contact, who was swayed by greed to help lay a trap for the Hellbreaker at the Waterspout Inn.

Captain Bane drove off the tavern's other customers and recruited local loyalists to help take Rhokrag prisoner when he arrived. She then docked the Witchfire behind the inn and took Rhokrag on board to interrogate him, hoping to learn the activities and locations of his comrades in revolution. He hasn't broken by the time the PCs arrive, but his resolve is beginning to waver, especially since Captain Bane called on the services of Zemaniah (sadistic male interrogator entrapment devil 1). Meanwhile, most of the Witchfire's crew has gone off to harass locals in hopes of weeding out more Hellbreakers. Those who remain have set up camp between the inn and the docks to stand guard.

The PCs arrive shortly before dusk outside the Waterspout Inn approximately 2 days after they leave Saringallow. From the road, they can see a two-masted ship flying the Chelaxian flag docked behind it. In addition, a handful of red-and-black tents have been erected near the riverbank behind the inn. Another Chelaxian banner hangs above them. It's clear that Chelaxian forces have occupied the inn, but what isn't clear is where they might be holding Rhokrag. Luckily, the PCs have the element of surprise at the moment.

If they watch the area from afar for a bit, they notice that no one enters or leaves the inn. A PC who also succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:17] check spots some movement in the windows of the inn's first floor. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[warfare-lore|dc:16] check recognizes that camp is visible from the deck of the ship, and unless they are very stealthy, once they enter the camp, they'll likely be spotted; any fighting within the camp will probably be heard from the ship.

The PCs should decide whether they want to mount their rescue right away or wait a little more than an hour until nightfall. At night, lanterns are lit inside the inn on the first floor, and the Chelaxian soldiers light torches in the camp and lanterns on the Witchfire. These provide light for many ancestries to see at short range, but outside of their radius, the cover of darkness could grant certain characters an edge against the unsuspecting loyalists. Use the Witchfire map for this encounter.

Gone Missing.name: Gone Missing
Gone Missing.text:
Gone Missing

When the PCs get back to the Hellbreakers headquarters, they are debriefed by Maire, who seems a bit distracted. She's pleased with whatever supplies the PCs return with and gives them a brief rundown of the other groups' successes if asked. Afterward, Ethran approaches the PCs to let them know that there are whispers that Rhokrag hasn't yet returned from his own mission. He was scheduled to check in the previous day and is far too disciplined to either miss an appointed time or neglect to send word if he'll be late. If the PCs aren't already concerned, Ethran suggests that they either talk to Maire about the possibility of Rhokrag's capture or death, or track Rhokrag down themselves.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:15|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information learns from the other Hellbreakers (or from Maire if they go right to the source) that Rhokrag had gone off on his own for some reconnaissance on the road to Logas, hoping to get some advance notice if Hellknight forces have regrouped enough to range further into Isger again. Specifically, Rhokrag had a local non-League contact that he was going to meet at the Waterspout Inn, a riverside tavern and lodging house halfway between Logas and Saringallow. If the PCs fail this check, they receive the same information from Ethran, who has since spoken with Maire. Later that same day, if the PCs haven't already volunteered to pursue this lead, Maire asks them to do so.

Returning to Saringallow.name: Returning to Saringallow
Returning to Saringallow.text:
Returning to Saringallow

Even if the PCs didn't stop to rescue any of the Night's Prize crew, some of them made it to shore. They are in no shape to put up a fight and, unless the PCs stop them, they trudge off in the direction of Elidir (or another nearby settlement). If asked or threatened, these individuals promise not to say anything about the PCs to any authorities. In fact, one of them is grateful to the PCs for dealing with Captain Aedin, whom they categorize as a “cruel, unfeeling man.” While some of the crew might be Chelaxian citizens, none of them have strong opinions about the current political situation. If any of the PCs express a sentiment of leaving no witnesses, remind them that they've been asked to kill only in self-defense.

It takes 2 days to return to Saringallow, though it might take longer if the PCs didn't secure a method of transport such as a wagon for the supplies. If the PCs successfully overcame the Aiding the Crew obstacle during the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00]{Sinking Ship!} encounter, those they helped can either aid the PCs in carrying the supplies or procure a cart for them. The journey is uneventful, especially if the characters play the parts of simple traveling citizens.

River Reptiles.name: River Reptiles
River Reptiles.text:
River ReptilesLow 1

The PCs have 10 minutes to catch their breath once everyone is out of the river as the remains of the Night's Prize finishes sinking. Unfortunately, however, the chaos of the moment has garnered the attention of some local fauna. This encounter takes place in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01riverbank00000]{B1}.

River ReptilesLow 1

@UUID[Actor.rl4hQMBHtuZNnv6W]{Gliding River Snakes (2)}

Creatures: A mated pair of gliding river snakes launches out of the water, disturbed from their aquatic nest by bits of debris from the ship. Protective of their territory, they attack anyone on the banks to drive them off.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.cZIPmzlxILoAVmTc]{Night's Prize Remains}
Washed up from the remains of the Night's Prize is a ring of discretion, a greased axle, and a fine compass worth 10 gp.

Sinking Ship!.name: Sinking Ship!
Sinking Ship!.text:
Sinking Ship!Moderate 1

When the animated armor has been reduced to 0 Hit Points, the captain's final failsafe is triggered. Bright red runes flare up on the armor as it collapses, and the PCs hear muffled explosions from below deck. Out of paranoia, when Captain Aedin purchased the animated armor, he magically linked its runes to three containers of alchemist's fire stored within the hull of the ship. He planned to defuse the runes when the Night's Prize reached its destination, but the PCs' attack has justified their installation.

The Night's Prize begins to simultaneously burn and sink. If the PCs want to salvage any supplies before they are destroyed or lost at the bottom of the river, they'll have to act fast. This encounter uses the Victory Point subsystem (Pathfinder GM Core 184) to track how successful the PCs are during this crisis. Each obstacle has a threshold of Victory Points (VP) required to overcome it. Actions are made in phases where each PC can attempt a check to earn Victory Points toward the completion of a chosen obstacle. If the group's VP total for an obstacle equals or exceeds the threshold of that obstacle, they overcome that obstacle. With the exception of the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#swimming-to-safetyobstacle]{Swimming to Safety} obstacle, the PCs can attempt any of the obstacles in any order, and each PC can work toward a different obstacle if they wish. The @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#subduing-the-captainobstacle]{Subduing the Captain} obstacle is available only if Captain Aedin is still alive.

The PCs have six phases before the Night's Prize completely sinks. If the PCs haven't completed the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#swimming-to-safetyobstacle]{Swimming to Safety} obstacle before then, any PC who didn't contribute a VP to that obstacle's completion becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} from their efforts to swim ashore.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.eNNXgP0dNKMAjBMW]{Sink Ship}

You can remove the ship from the scene when it sinks with the above macro, which also removes all fires on the scene.

This scene allows you to spread fire square by square. Enable the Fire Toggle on the Actor Toolbar located in the top left of the screen, and then left click anywhere on the scene!

Aiding the CrewObstacle

Threshold 4; Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:17], @Check[diplomacy|dc:17], or @Check[medicine|dc:17]; @Check[sailing-lore|dc:15]

Some of the Night's Prize crew were injured in the explosions or are panicking fas the ship sinks. The PCs can either tend to their wounds, carry them to safety, or calm them down.

Putting out Fires Obstacle

Threshold 4; Overcome @Check[acrobatics|dc:18] or @Check[survival|dc:18]

A multitude of fires have broken out across the ship. Putting them out will make other tasks easier.

Special A PC who can magically produce water can use the skill associated with the tradition of that magic to overcome this obstacle. If a phase ends and the PCs haven't overcome this obstacle, each PC who hasn't succeeded at a check to overcome the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#swimming-to-safetyobstacle]{Swimming to Safety} obstacle takes @Damage[1d4[fire]] damage.

Securing SuppliesObstacle

Threshold 2; Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:16], @Check[crafting|dc:16], or @Check[thievery|dc:16]; @Check[mercantile-lore|dc:15]; @Check[perception|dc:17]

Several crates of supplies—food, clothing, and alchemical items—are stored in the ship's hold. The PCs must try to secure as much as possible for the Hellbreakers League.

Special The PCs can attempt to overcome this obstacle multiple times. Keep track of how many times the PCs overcome this obstacle for their rewards. If the PCs have yet to overcome the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#subduing-the-captainobstacle]{Subduing the Captain} obstacle (if the captain is still alive), they take a –2 circumstance penalty to checks to overcome this obstacle as the captain tries to stop them from stealing his goods.

Subduing the CaptainObstacle

Threshold 3; Overcome @Check[intimidation|dc:17] or attack roll

If Captain Aedin is still alive, he could prove to be a nuisance to the PCs.

Special A PC who casts spells can expend them to subdue the captain. Attempt a DC 17 spell attack roll or have the captain attempt a saving throw as usual for the spell. A failure on a saving throw grants 1 VP, while a critical failure grants 2. At the GM's discretion, certain spells might completely subdue the captain, immediately overcoming this obstacle.

Swimming to SafetyObstacle

Threshold 4; Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:15], @Check[nature|dc:15], or @Check[survival|dc:15]

Before the Night's Prize completely sinks, the PCs must get off the ship and swim to shore.

Special Once the PCs decide to attempt this obstacle, they can't simultaneously attempt to overcome any other obstacles. Once they overcome this obstacle, the encounter ends.

Reward: @UUID[Actor.PaFEjyB9sjecHoi9]{Sailor's Reward}
If the PCs overcame the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#securing-suppliesobstacle]{Securing Supplies} obstacle at least once in the six phases before the ship sinks, award them 30 XP; if they overcome it three or more times, award them 40 XP. If the PCs overcame the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00#aiding-the-crewobstacle]{Aiding the Crew} obstacle, a grateful sailor gives them a bottle of bortled favorite. In addition, they receive an early Reputation Point (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe]{Chapter 2}) for helping the crew.

Night's Prize.name: Night's Prize
Night's Prize.text:
B2. Night's PrizeLow 1 and Moderate 1

This riverboat is painted mostly red with black accents, mirroring the colors of the Chelaxian flag that flies from its mast. Spiky protrusions line the gunwales. A wide door leads into the ship to the aft, and a hatch leads down into the hull.

The Night's Prize is a fairly typical, if small, vessel. A framed portrait of Abrogail Thrune hangs over the door to the captain's quarters.

B2. Night's PrizeLow 1 and Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.tSkUlDGm057UXQvX]{Night's Prize Swabbies (2)} @UUID[Actor.Qy3RuBzIFY1OTxo3]{Captain Julenus Aiden} @UUID[Actor.45MYOKAqRg4l98iV]{Animated Armor}

Creatures: As the PCs board the Night's Prize, most of the crew throw up their hands and surrender. They aren't paid enough to risk their lives repelling attackers, and a few know about the captain's secret guardian (see The Captain's Armor). However, two younger swabbies are eager to prove themselves to the captain and brandish bottles in response to the PCs' intrusion. Each of them pleads for mercy when reduced to 5 or fewer Hit Points.

The Captain's Armor: Upon hearing the news about the Battle of Hellknight Hill, Captain Aedin spent most of the profits of his previous cargo run on an animated suit of armor in Elidir. This was mainly to protect himself from any anti-Cheliax rebels he believes are roaming the countryside, including fighting off boarders and pirates. At the beginning of the third round of combat with the swabbies or the round after both swabbies have been defeated, Captain Aedin appears in the doorway to his quarters, standing next to an intricate black suit of armor with no one inside. “You have 5 seconds to get off my damned ship,” he says, pointing his dagger at the PCs. No matter what the PCs reply, the two roll initiative.

The animated armor protects the captain at all costs and attempts to always end its turn adjacent to him. Captain Aedin presses his attacks against wounded PCs first. The captain fights to the death, knowing that his animated armor has a final trick up its sleeve (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01sinkingshipu00]{Sinking Ship!}). If the captain is killed before the armor is destroyed, the armor begins acting erratically. It spends 1 action each turn Striding up to 10 feet in a random direction, though it never falls over the edge of the ship.

Riverbank.name: Riverbank
Riverbank.text:
B1. Riverbank

The PCs arrive at the designated spot—an area where the North Conerica River narrows a bit and passes by a rocky outcropping that provides excellent cover against ships approaching from the north—as the sun is setting. Most ships don't travel much at night, so the PCs have time to make camp and prepare the area for an ambush.

Ambushing a ship, even one on a river, isn't like committing highway robbery. There's no easy way to stop the vessel's passage short of completely blocking the river, which is well beyond the PCs' capabilities. However, they should come up with some kind of plan that uses their party's strengths.

Later that day, the PCs spot a potential target in the Night's Prize, a trading vessel flying Chelaxian colors. It's a relatively smaller boat, so it won't have a lot of crew to deal with, and its hull sits low in the water, suggesting it's full of cargo. The Night's Prize is captained by Julenus Aedin (cutthroat male human privateer 1), a successful merchant who has a minor reputation for cruelty. No other boats are in view, so this is a perfect opportunity for the PCs to enact their plan.

Use the following examples as guidelines for how to adjudicate your group's specific plan. Of course, some groups might simply start firing arrows and spells at the crew! Run the first combat from @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01nightsprizea00]{B2} with the PCs on the banks and the swabbies taking cover. Unless they have some way to stop or slow the ship, the PCs have 3 rounds to get aboard before the current takes the ship out of reach. A successful @Check[athletics|dc:12|traits:move,skill,action:swim|name:Swim] check is required to swim in the river.

Faking Distress: Tricky PCs might want to fool an approaching ship into stopping (or slowing down) long enough to be boarded. This requires a convincing reason (such as a false wound); each PC who participates in the ruse must attempt a @Check[deception|dc:18] or @Check[performance|dc:18] check. Less charismatic PCs can hide behind the outcropping by attempting @Check[stealth|dc:16|traits:move,skill,secret,action:sneak|name:Sneak] check. Anyone who fails their check takes a –1 circumstance penalty to their initiative roll. If all the PCs fail their checks, they can still attempt their ambush, but each member of the ship's crew (but not the animated armor) gains a +1 circumstance bonus to the first attack roll they make against a PC.

Show of Force: The threat of violence might be enough to get an approaching ship to allow the PCs to board. Each PC should attempt a @Check[intimidation|dc:20] check; a PC who uses a showy ability or casts a spell that has highly visible effects (like an illusion) receives an outcome one degree of success better. If at least half of the PCs succeed, they quickly get aboard the ship, and if they don't, they have more difficulty once on board; each member of the ship's crew (but not the animated armor) gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative.

Surprise Boarding: A passing boat has to sail close to the outcropping, giving the opportunities for PCs to hide until the right moment and then leap or rappel down into the ship's rigging. As long as they lie low on top of the rock, the group doesn't need to worry about Stealth checks, but each PC must attempt a @Check[acrobatics|dc:18] or @Check[athletics|dc:18] check to get safely from the outcropping to the ship; PCs who can fly or float automatically succeed at this check. On a failure, the PC falls 15 feet to the ship's deck, taking @Damage[7[bludgeoning]|options:fall-damage]{falling damage} and landing prone. On a critical failure, they are also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} for the first encounter in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01nightsprizea00]{B2}. If all PCs succeed, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative for the first encounter.

Riverboat Ambush.name: Riverboat Ambush
Riverboat Ambush.text:
Riverboat Ambush

The journey to the scouted ambush spot takes approximately two days and is relatively uneventful. The PCs continue to spot copies of Hedvend's bounty on so-called traitors nailed up in the villages and farms they pass by, but no one stops them to question their loyalty. If the PCs took precautions to appear like everyday travelers, note that their thinking ahead is the cause of their smooth trip. Use the Riverboat Ambush map to the left for this encounter.

Provisioning the Revolution.name: Provisioning the Revolution
Provisioning the Revolution.text:
Provisioning the Revolution

The next day, Rhokrag and Xerra meet with the agents to discuss the next steps. While they wait for further orders from the Demetriases, Xerra asks that the Hellbreakers here in Saringallow use the time to further provision the organization since their supplies from Logas were compromised. To that end, several groups are heading out of the city to raid some known Cheliax-friendly targets to procure armor, weapons, food, and other necessary materials. In the meantime, Ethran Howell will remain at the headquarters to continue to train a handful of new recruits and wait for any news from the League's leaders.

As he delineates the specifics of each group's mission, Rhokrag gives the following warning.

“I'm not going to lie—what we're about to do will involve some law breaking. But you probably weren't expecting to be upstanding Isgeri citizens when you signed up to be a Hellbreaker. We're only taking what we need for the greater good of the country, and it's not like those we're taking from can't afford to lose something. They'll fight like that isn't true, though, and who wouldn't? You're going to face some danger out there, mostly from hired guards who are just doing their jobs. Which is why, and I can't stress this enough, we must refrain from killing as much as possible.” He briefly looks at each assembled Hellbreaker in turn.

“In the coming weeks and months, we're going to need the people of Isger on our side. They must see us as fighting a good and necessary fight. Some might even join us! But until then, we can't give Cheliax ammunition to paint us as violent marauders just looking to cause trouble. They'll probably try to do that anyway, but let's not leave a trail of bodies in our wake, yeah? Defend yourself if you must, of course, and I'm sure no one will miss a Thrune bootlicker or two, but keep the killing to a minimum.”

The PCs are tasked with some light river piracy. Rhokrag gives them directions to a spot on the North Conerica River that League scouts have determined would be a good place to ambush a passing trade vessel. Ships often move cargo out of Elidir bound for Cheliax. If a PC brings up the fact that Chelaxian ships pass by (and sometimes stop at) Saringallow all the time, Rhokrag responds, “That has a chance of bringing some unwanted scrutiny on the city in which we have our headquarters. Better we operate in places where such attacks could be blamed on bandits. For now.”

Petty Cash: @UUID[Actor.DIPqfkbTp5XdJZFK]{Petty Cash}
Xerra gives the PCs 10 gp to buy anything they think they might need for the mission. “Better come back with more than that in supplies,” the halfling says with a wink.

Main Warehouse.name: Main Warehouse
Main Warehouse.text:
A3. Main WarehouseModerate 1

This is where the Hellbreakers League keeps the majority of their supplies in Saringallow.

Only a few crates occupy this large, open space. The floor is hard-packed dirt with the occasional scattering of straw, and double doors lead south to the road. A woman lies tied up and gagged on top of a single closed crate in the center of the warehouse.

The woman is Gertraud Mildenhall, one of the PCs' fellow League members, who was captured by a group of Chelaxian loyalists earlier in the day. She squirms and yells a muffled warning when she sees the PCs enter. A PC can untie Gertraud or remove her gag each with a single Interact action, though she is effectively a noncombatant in the encounter with the loyalists here.

A3. Main WarehouseModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.jemJpiHGxb7TDhda]{Chelaxian Loyalists (2)} @UUID[Actor.pZIIWk8E3WWdG2tE]{Chelaxian Loyalist Leader}

Creatures: A pair of Chelaxian loyalists, along with their brash leader, lurk in the warehouse to try to capture more dissidents and collect the bounty. While they were confident after capturing Gertraud, they become a bit hesitant when they see the party of PCs. They still attack when at least one PC enters the room, moving out from behind crates and trying to look intimidating. One loyalist uses a crate for cover while firing their crossbow, and the other loyalist and the leader enter in melee. The loyalists want to take the PCs alive for the bounty, so they nonlethally strike at any PC that has already been wounded, taking the –2 circumstance penalty to the attack.

The loyalist leader zealously fights until reduced to 0 HP. The other loyalists try to flee if they're wounded and their leader has been incapacitated, though it's likely the PCs are in the way of the only viable exit. If a fleeing loyalist has no path to freedom, they surrender instead.

Interrogating the Loyalists: If the PCs capture any of the loyalists, they admit they tricked a stevedore into pointing out this warehouse after arriving on a merchant ship from Logas that has since departed for Elidir. A captured loyalist holds no regret for their actions, referring to the PCs and their allies as “scum and vermin.” What the PCs do with any captives is up to them; since the PCs were defending themselves upon being attacked, they can turn any remaining loyalists over to the Saringallow watch—though, as revolutionaries, they might not want to get involved with the authorities. If the PCs give Valerra 5 sp, she'll call the watch for them and keep an eye on any captured and restrained loyalists in the street while the PCs leave the scene.

Supply Inventory: The supposed delivery from Logas seems to have been a mistake or a ruse. Once rescued, Gertraud notes that at least the loyalists didn't damage any of the League's current supplies, which doesn't amount to much. The few crates within the warehouse contain very basic goods: common suits of armor, shields, simple and martial weapons, and some ammunition (arrows and bolts, mainly). Gertraud matter-of-factly adds all weapons confiscated off the loyalists to the crates.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.J7dquSnc7sKgTPk9]{Crated Weapons} @UUID[Actor.R1ojpAfLGTgzk18y]{Gertraud's Gift}
Among the crated weapons is a low-grade silver melee weapon of the same type that one of the PCs uses regularly, and a whispering wire. Gertraud notices the PCs examining that weapon and insists that they take it for rescuing her. In addition, she hands another PC a masquerade scarf that has been passed around several Hellbreakers to aid in keeping a low profile, especially when securing supplies in a less-than-legal fashion.

Warehouse Annex.name: Warehouse Annex
Warehouse Annex.text:
A2. Warehouse AnnexTrivial 1

This attachment to the main warehouse holds some older-looking crates stacked up against the east wall. An open doorway leads onto the warehouse floor to the west.

The Hellbreakers keep old, unused crates here after unpacking their contents in case they're needed to smuggle goods elsewhere. Many of the crates are covered in crumbling forged bills of lading and a layer of dust.

A2. Warehouse AnnexTrivial 1

@UUID[Actor.MrCK7enEm9UaM3JC]{Falling Crates}

Hazard: The first part of the loyalists' plan is to soften up anyone entering the warehouse by collapsing heavy crates onto them. A thin trip wire stretches the width of the annex past a tall stack of crates (indicated by a square on the map); if triggered, it pulls the crates down.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.qDDPY5ExilmuEWVe]{Collapse Crates}

Stealthy Approach: If the PCs trip the trap or otherwise make a loud noise (such as by calling out for Gertraud), the loyalists on the main warehouse floor automatically hear the PCs coming and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls. If more than half of the PCs succeed at @Check[stealth|dc:17|traits:move,skill,secret,action:sneak|name:Sneak] against the Chelaxian loyalist leader's Perception DC of 17 and the trap wasn't triggered, the loyalists are unaware of the PCs' approach and take a –1 circumstance penalty to their initiative rolls. If neither of the above situations occur, the loyalists gain neither a bonus nor a penalty.

Outside Everbloom Imports Warehouse.name: Outside Everbloom Imports Warehouse
Outside Everbloom Imports Warehouse.text:
A1. Outside Everbloom Imports Warehouse

The warehouse is a large, square building with a smaller annex on the eastern side. Double doors the width of a wagon are closed with a heavy chain and sturdy padlock. A regular-sized door leads into the annex.

The annex door is unlocked and slightly ajar. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:17] or @Check[crafting|dc:15] or @Check[carpentry-lore|dc:15] check can see from a faint splintering in the frame that it was forced open. The padlock is an average lock (requiring four successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks to pick), and if the PCs manage to open it and quietly move the chain (@Check[stealth|dc:20|traits:move,skill,secret,action:sneak|name:Sneak]), they can catch the loyalists in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01mainwarehous00]{A3} by surprise.

Dockside Row.name: Dockside Row
Dockside Row.text:
Dockside Row

Saringallow's docks are located on the south side of the city, right on the Conerica River. Warehouses line the street opposite, and throughout the day, a steady stream of stevedores unload cargo from docked ships and into those buildings. Carts arrive periodically to take the goods to their final destinations.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.vAMH66sfOYsU555B]{Docks}

The warehouse for Everbloom Imports is at the eastern end of the street, partially isolated from the other buildings. If the PCs watch it for any period of time, they don't see anyone enter or leave. They might want to ask around the area to see if anyone's noticed anything suspicious. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:16] or a @Check[underworld-lore|dc:14] check spots a dark-haired youth lingering about. This is Valerra Clive (street-smart human female urchin 0), one of Saringallow's less fortunate teens who do odd jobs for anyone who'll pay them. She looks hopeful if the PCs approach her, assuming they need her to run a message or hold onto something not quite legal. When the PCs begin asking her questions about the warehouse, her excitement turns to disappointment, and she clams up. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:18] or @Check[intimidation|dc:18] check convinces her to talk; offering her at least 2 sp achieves the same result.

Once sufficiently persuaded or bribed, Valerra tells the PCs that she saw three shifty-looking people come from the west end of the street and enter the warehouse early this morning after forcing open the side door. Before noon, a woman walked down the northern street and took out a key to open the same door; this woman didn't seem to notice anything unusual. Since then, no one has come out. As a result of collecting this information, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to spot the falling crates trap in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains.JournalEntryPage.01warehouseann00]{A2} and to the hazard's Reflex saving throw.

Reward: If the PCs find out that something is odd about the Red Refuge from Valerra Clive, award them 10 XP.

Warehouse Mystery.name: Warehouse Mystery
Warehouse Mystery.text:
Warehouse Mystery

With their first official mission for the Hellbreakers League complete, the PCs are immediately tasked with another. Rhokrag explains that supplies—armor, weapons, ammunition, rations, and so on—are the fuel that keeps a revolution's fire burning, and the League is in constant need. There isn't enough room within the house HQ to store all such provisions, so the League keeps them in a warehouse at the docks under the name of Everbloom Imports, a fictitious trading company and yet another reference to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.fTJLgTfEMZreJ19r]{Milani}.

Agents posing as merchants arrive in town with (usually stolen) supplies, move them into the warehouse, and then head back out into the country for their next mission. This morning, a League-affiliated vessel arrived at the docks with provisions from Logas. Junior Hellbreaker Gertraud Mildenhall (confident female halfling smuggler –1) was to meet them at the warehouse and inventory the goods, but she hasn't returned to headquarters yet.

Rhokrag is beginning to suspect something untoward might have happened, as Gertraud is known for being quite timely. Saringallow isn't totally free of Chelaxian loyalists who would jump at the chance to collect a generous bounty. To make matters worse, this delivery from Logas was meant to help provision several missions out in the field and the League is running low on weapons and ammunition. The PCs are sent to the warehouse to see if anything happened to Gertraud.

Unfortunately, Rhokrag's suspicions are correct. A handful of Chelaxian loyalists from Logas boarded the ship posing as Hellbreakers and tricked a dockworker into telling them the location of the League's warehouse. They took the ship to the warehouse, grabbed Gertraud when she arrived, and are holding her hostage, intending to capture any additional dissidents who arrive to increase the bounty they'll earn.

Welcome to Hellbreakers Headquarters.name: Welcome to Hellbreakers Headquarters
Welcome to Hellbreakers Headquarters.text:
Welcome to Hellbreakers Headquarters

After crossing the river on the ferry, the PCs can spend the night at the inn and then continue on to Saringallow the next morning. There are no further incidents, and they arrive in the midafternoon at the northeastern gates.

Saringallow is a large walled town on the Conerica River that was founded as Sarini's Hollow by the Chelaxian noble Sarini family a few centuries ago. After a series of mysterious deaths, the townspeople rose up against the Sarinis and publicly hanged them, giving the town its more somber sobriquet. More details about the town's occult history and its current inhabitants can be found on @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22215saring]{Saringallow Gazetteer}.

Despite the town having no love for Chelaxian nobles, the Hellbreakers League must still operate with some modicum of secrecy here. Regardless of whether PCs are from Saringallow or have visited the town before, they know that the League's headquarters is in the basement of an unassuming two-story house on the eastern side of town. Rumors hold that the domicile was once the home of an alchemist who was corrupted by a demonic influence. His family has since moved away from Saringallow, and the founders of the Hellbreakers League purchased the house and constructed a large basement in which to plan their revolution. Agents sometimes stay in the house, but it isn't large enough to lodge the entire League.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.d2fUJQ1dXqZqNV0Q]{Town} @UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.nAQknnhL160D1M0P]{Headquarters}

To gain entrance, the PCs know to knock on the front door and announce that they are “friends of Rose.” This is a reference to the goddess @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.fTJLgTfEMZreJ19r]{Milani}, the patron of those who fight against injustice and tyranny and whose religious symbol is a rose in a pool of blood.

A dark-haired human woman opens the door and says with a smile, “Afternoon! Any friends of Rose can find refuge here.”

This is the proper response to the phrase the PCs gave, a reference to Milani's celestial domain, the Refuge of the Red Rose. The woman answering the door is Maire Phelan (jovial female human storyteller 3), who introduces herself after waving the PCs inside. The house's main room looks like a typical cozy residence, with a hearth on the east wall and a large dining table in the center. After closing the front door, Maire approaches a plain wooden door in the southern wall, which she unlocks with an iron key. This leads to a set of stairs descending into the beating heart of the Hellbreakers League.

A wide basement stretches in front of the bottom of the staircase, crammed with several tables, a handful of chairs, and maps of Isger hung on nearly every wall. The tables are piled with documents, ledgers, and more maps. A tall hobgoblin man sorts through the documents, a stern look on his face. A side room has been cleared of all furniture, and two young soldiers spar within. A second, smaller alcove holds a magically heated iron stove that gives off warmth and light but no smoke. A white-haired halfling stands next to the stove, holding a pan filled with pastries.

The Three Lieutenants

Maire Phelan, Rhokrag, and Xerra Bluebottle are the three highest-ranking members of the Hellbreakers League apart from the founders, Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias. Until @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth]{Chapter 4}, the PCs will be dealing mainly with these three lieutenants. The following descriptions should help you portray these NPCs over the course of the Adventure Path.

Maire Phelan is in charge of recruiting new agents and the League's public relations. She's always pleased to see the PCs and encourages them to describe their heroics in greater, more florid detail, noting that the people of Isger will rally around heroes. Maire is quick to offer a joke or some good-natured ribbing, especially to somber people like Rhokrag.

Rhokrag generally gives the PCs their missions and tends to remain out of the public eye. He recognizes that many are still prejudiced against goblinoids since the Goblinblood Wars, but he believes that getting out from under the thumb of Cheliax will help Isger heal. Rhokrag is quite serious and tends to appreciate PCs who are similarly no-nonsense.

Xerra Bluebottle keeps the League provisioned and armed. They work most days at Gunty's Hearty Breads across town and often bring over the day-old pastries that Gunty Keronna can't sell, warming them on the basement stove. They form an instant rapport with any PC who enjoys cooking or baking.

Maire alerts the assembled group that their newest recruits have arrived (or returned) from Breachill with their Eagle Knight ally. Rhokrag (hardened male hobgoblin warrior 3) is the first to step forward and welcome the PCs; he quickly sizes them up and appears satisfied. He wants to debrief the PCs immediately, but Xerra Bluebottle (kind genderfluid halfling baker 2) gently chides him for being so formal. She offers the PCs the sticky buns she was just toasting on the stove and tells them to grab chairs if they're tired from the journey. Meanwhile, the two recruits, Cole Acton and “Rabbit” Dryden (eager male and female human recruits 1), pause their training to also partake of Xerra's baked goods. The NPCs introduce themselves, and Rhokrag informs the PCs that the Hellbreakers League's founders and leaders, Alceo (wise male aiuvarin cleric 7) and Phoebe Demetrias (righteous female human warrior 7), are currently in Elidir, doing their best to stop Hedvend's bounty on dissidents at the source. While they don't have direct contact with Isger's steward, they're surreptitiously trying to sway other members of the government in the hopes of pressuring Hedvend to rescind the bounty.

Xerra tells the PCs that if they want to rest in the house tonight, they can, though the second-floor accommodations will be a little cramped. Ethran needs to stay here as well until the League can find them a more permanent abode. Most Hellbreakers either have their own residences in Saringallow or stay at an inn in town between missions. Maire tells the PCs they can go the Fiend's Finale, which gives discount rates to League members (5 sp a night for a private room that sleeps two).

But before the PCs can sleep, Rhokrag needs them to do something for the organization first.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.P3l2EKT9GJGvSisV]{Ethran's Reward}
At some point after reaching the Hellbreakers headquarters, Ethran gives the PCs their +1 greatsword for escorting them to Saringallow. Ethran explains that with only one arm, they won't have much use for it. “My job is to teach now, anyway,” they say with a smile.

River Crossing.name: River Crossing
River Crossing.text:
River CrossingSevere 1

A day and a half later, the group arrives at the North Conerica River just before dusk. They only have to cross the river before the home stretch to Saringallow. A regular ferry shuttles travelers back and forth across the wide river. Another large group booked passage several minutes before the PCs, so the party has to wait until the ferry returns for its last trip of the evening. A riverside inn can be seen on the far bank, while the side the PCs are on features only a small shack and dock.

While they wait, the GM should attempt a secret @Check[perception|dc:16|traits:secret] check for each PC. Those who succeed spot a pair of silhouettes against the setting sun that seem to be large flying creatures approaching fast; any successful PCs also receive a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative in the upcoming fight. Use the River Crossing map above for this encounter.

River CrossingSevere 1

@UUID[Actor.4phc6LZwKn14TrMY]{Zombie Giant Bats (2)}

Creatures: @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} (malevolent female daughter of Urgathoa 9) has been operating in Isger for years, and the war has given her the opportunity to escalate her plans to take the nation. As she gathers her power in Finder's Gulch dozens of miles to the west, her necromantic creations sometimes range far from the town. A pair of undead giant bats recently took to the skies in search of victims, turning various animals across the hillside into zombies. While the players are unlikely to learn where these zombie bats came from, their appearance foreshadows the undead troubles that await in later chapters. The zombie bats fight until they are destroyed.

If it looks like the PCs are having trouble during this fight, Ethran can offer them some tactical advice. Each round, they attempt to Aid a struggling PC's next Strike by attempting a Warfare Lore check with a +10 modifier. They otherwise try to stay near the wagon to keep the horse calm, but they do move out of a zombie bat's rotting aura if subjected to it.

The Ferry Arrives: Shortly after the PCs defeat the zombie giant bats, the ferry returns to their side of the river. Utto, the ferry operator, is concerned about the group's safety and quickly ushers them and the wagon onto his ferry. As the vessel makes its way back across, Utto asks the PCs what attacked them and if told, he nods his head knowingly. “My cousin told me that the dead have been mighty restless ever since all that god stuff fell from the sky. She thinks it has something to do with that lich what lives on Lake Encarthan.”

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:18] or @Check[politics-lore|dc:18] check has heard that "that lich" Tar-Baphon has mostly been concentrating his recent efforts on the Gravelands and attempting to subjugate the orcs of Belkzen. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:14] or @Check[zombie-lore|dc:14] check knows that undead attacks can happen for a number of reasons, not all of which are related to a sinister necromancer trying to take over the world.

Draymoor Road.name: Draymoor Road
Draymoor Road.text:
Draymoor RoadModerate 1

Midafternoon on the fourth day of travel out of Breachill, the wagon enters the small farming village of Draymoor.

Only a few squat buildings line the single road, which is muddy from a recent rain. The villagers go about their daily business with only a glance or two at the group. Ethran draws the horse alongside a general store and carefully climbs down to enter. “I'll restock our supplies,” they say. “It should only take a few minutes. Watch the wagon, would you?”

Not long after Ethran heads inside, four angry-looking individuals saunter out of Draymoor's small tavern and begin to approach the wagon. Each of them wears hastily sewn patches depicting the flag of Cheliax and are armed with a light mace and a crossbow, though they haven't drawn them. They accost the PCs with questions about where they're coming from and what their business is in town. Use the Draymoor Road map for this encounter.

Draymoor Road Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.xhmM1hzI3j6UGNlB]{Chelaxian Loyalists (4)}

Creatures: These locals are loyal to Cheliax's rule over Isger and suspicious of all strangers. The PCs can try to get these loyalists to leave them alone by succeeding at two @Check[deception|dc:15], @Check[diplomacy|dc:15], or @Check[intimidation|dc:15] checks; each check can be attempted by a different person and they can use different skills or the same skill twice. If the PCs succeed, the loyalists are either mollified or scared off depending on the group's tactics.

If the PCs fail two of these checks before they succeed, the loyalists get violent. Two of the loyalists fight with their light maces while the other two stand back and fire their crossbows. The loyalists try to remain adjacent to one another as they fight. If the PCs knock out two of the loyalists, the other two flee. The loyalists all flee if each of them is below 5 Hit Points. During an altercation, the other village residents disappear indoors. Draymoor has no local law enforcement and the area's sheriff won't make her rounds here for another four days, so once the loyalists have been driven off or killed, the PCs are in no further danger here.

Reward: @UUID[Actor.WnFKCGHOSfYCkyz2]{Ethran's Gift}
If the PCs defuse the situation without violence, award them XP as if they had defeated the Chelaxian loyalists in combat. When Ethran returns to the wagon, they give the PCs a potency crystal and lesser atrophy bomb they purchased.

Setting out for Saringallow.name: Setting out for Saringallow
Setting out for Saringallow.text:
Setting out for Saringallow

Ethran has purchased a horse and a wagon for the journey. They wish to leave within the hour, giving the PCs an opportunity to purchase any supplies for the trip as they see fit. They'll be on the road for about half a week, but Ethran says that they'll probably have opportunities to buy more rations and other items on the way.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ItTionHYw9zkogLj.PlaylistSound.VcBBe4pwzxLVCtMy]{Wagon Ride} @UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.dIUYMyErQiQrvb69]{Isger Countryside}

The Eagle Knight drives the wagon out of Breachill. The PCs can take seats in the wagon with Ethran's trunk or ride or walk alongside. When the group sets out, the sky is gray and cloudy, presaging some autumnal rains. The road out of town leads west, then eventually turns a bit southwest, passing by farms with empty fields, their harvests already collected. Ethran makes small talk over the rumbling of the cart's wheels, perhaps asking the PCs about any stories they told the night before, inquiring into their veracity or asking for more details. At the end of the first day, the group comes to a roadside inn where the PCs can spot a copy of Hedvend's decree on a signboard outside. The few patrons inside mutter a bit about the country not being safe anymore to anyone who asks, but it isn't clear whether they mean safe from Chelaxian intervention or from rebel activity.

During the next two days of travel, the PCs spot more copies of Hedvend's decree nailed to trees and fence posts along the road. Ethran warns the characters that they should keep a low profile and not tear down these notices.

News from Elidir.name: News from Elidir
News from Elidir.text:
News from Elidir

The next morning, Breachill is abuzz with talk of news out of Elidir that arrived around dawn. Apparently, the Isgeri government placed a sizable bounty on "dissenters and revolutionaries" in a manner that is frustratingly vague. It's obvious to anyone who reads the text of the decree posted outside Breachill's town hall that Steward Hedvend VI (sniveling male human aristocrat 9) is trying to squash any anti-Chelaxian activities by encouraging private citizens to take matters into their own hands. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:16] check or @Check[legal-lore|dc:14] check realizes that people can use this bounty to settle grudges with their neighbors—similar in fashion as to what happens during a witch hunt—while collecting a bit of coin.

As the PCs return to Cayden's Keg to meet Ethran, they can see how this news has cast a pall over the town, somewhat eclipsing the celebratory mood of the previous evening. People in the street mutter to each other about how nearby towns might treat them after the results of the Battle of Hellknight Hill. A small crowd has gathered in Monument Circle near town hall to protest the decree and publicly decrying the idea of Breachill citizens turning on one another. The PCs should feel safe here for now.

Should they express any doubts about their safety, Ethran assures the PCs that no one here is likely to turn them in. They do note that it'll be a different matter outside of Breachill. Their original plan was to travel south to the Conerica River and then west to Saringallow, but now they think it's best to head directly to the Hellbreakers League headquarters, traveling southwest overland. Ethran also suggests they move as incognito as possible; they, for one, intend to hide their Eagle Knight regalia in a trunk. If any PCs sport obvious allegiances to the Hellbreakers League (or other revolutionary groups), Ethran recommends removing those symbols.

Night of Tales.name: Night of Tales
Night of Tales.text:
Night of Tales

The head priestess of Cayden's Keg regularly holds evening storytelling contests to both boost the mood of her customers and as a way to keep the alcohol flowing. After all, everyone loves to hear a good story and people usually stick around to hear a bunch of them told in succession—ordering more drinks in the meantime. Ethran encourages the PCs to participate but doesn't pressure any of the characters, especially if it seems like a character's history might be a sore subject. This is a good way for players to introduce their characters more thoroughly, giving a little backstory (or creating a clever fiction) to bring the group closer together.

As the PCs decide whether they wish to participate, other customers begin to tell their tales. Each one steps to the center of the tavern floor to speak, with all eyes watching and all ears listening. Most relate a brief story about their participation in the Battle of Hellknight Hill, while others spin yarns about a heroic hunt or a personal battle with temptation. A PC can enter the contest by speaking up from the center of the room at any point.

Each character who wants to tell a tale should attempt a DC 15 skill check; @Check[performance|dc:15] is the default skill, but a character could use @Check[deception|dc:15] if they are confabulating or @Check[intimidation|dc:15] if they are trying to scare the audience. If the player wants to tell a story that directly relates to their character's background, they could attempt a check using the Lore skill provided by that background. Other skills are applicable at the GM's discretion.

On a failure, the crowd gives the character some light applause, but it's clear that they're unimpressed. On a success, the tavern gives a livelier response, hooting with delight or even openly weeping if the tale was a sad one. Record the result of each skill check result that meets or exceeds the DC. At the end of the night, Brynne declares the character whose story represents the highest of those results the winner. The assembled drinkers cheer loud enough to nearly bring down the roof as Brynne presents the winner with several mugs of the Keg's finest (and most expensive) ale. Ethran bangs their own mug on the table in appreciation as well.

After another hour of carousing, Ethran declares that they're tired and tells the PCs they'll meet up again in the morning to discuss the details of the journey to Saringallow. Though Cayden's Keg isn't renting out rooms (they're saved for those convalescing), Brynne tells the PCs they can find lodging at the Great Dreamhouse, a temple to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.JgqH3BhuEuA4Zyqs]{Desna}, or Wizard's Grace, a local inn. They can also camp outside, near much of the visiting military.

Reward: If at least one PC succeeds at the storytelling check, award the PCs 30 XP; if more than half the PCs succeed, award them an additional 10 XP. In addition, if more than half the PCs succeed, Brynne thanks them for entertaining the tavern and gives them two minor healing potions before they leave, noting that Cayden told her they might need them "on the road ahead."

Meeting Ethran Howell.name: Meeting Ethran Howell
Meeting Ethran Howell.text:
Meeting Ethran Howell

Several tavern patrons raise their mugs and loudly greet the PCs as they enter Cayden's Keg. The PCs can ask about their contact or cast their eyes across the crowd; either way, they find Ethran Howell (pragmatic nonbinary human soldier 4) at a crowded table. The soldier's left arm was gravely wounded late in the Battle of Hellknight Hell, leaving no choice but for it to be amputated, and they've been recuperating at Cayden's Keg since then. During that time, Ethran decided to focus on the important work of helping to liberate Isger by offering their services as a soldier and tactician to the Hellbreakers League; the Eagle Knights have unofficially approved of Ethran's decision, noting in the records that the veteran is on “semi-permanent convalescence leave.” Read or paraphrase the following when the PCs approach Ethran.

Ethran Howell is difficult to miss in their distinctive blue, black, and golden breastplate decorated with a single golden eagle epaulet. Several townspeople crowd their table thanking them for their service, commiserating about their left arm, and buying them drinks. Ethran looks flattered but slightly embarrassed by the attention as they say to their admirers, “Fellows, I appreciate the chat and the drinks, but I must attend to business.” The small crowd disperses with a final cheer for Ethran, leaving plenty of space at the soldier's table. Ethran smiles, looking a little relieved. “Everyone's in high spirits, as they're right to be. Would you like a drink?”

Ethran is politically aware and can explain any factors leading up to the Battle of Hellknight Hill that the players aren't yet familiar with. If asked, they describe the fight with a pair of Hellknights that left them wounded. If any PCs also participated in the battle, Ethran acknowledges their contribution to the victory with a brief toast. Before the group can begin to discuss the upcoming journey, Brynne rings a bell mounted behind the bar to get the patrons' attention.

The crowd hushes and the fiddler stops mid-tune as the clear tones of the bell ring out. Brynne leans over the bar counter and calls out, “Come now, friends! In the name of all things fun and good as our beloved Cayden Cailean would have it, it's time for tonight's contest!” Cheers erupt as locals excitedly whisper, wondering what the theme of tonight's storytelling will be. Brynne raises a frothy glass. “In honor of those who drove out the scum from our town, the theme of the evening is past battles! Tell us your stories, brave warriors and wily hunters, and let's see who tells them best!”

The Aftermath of Battle.name: The Aftermath of Battle
The Aftermath of Battle.text:
The Aftermath of Battle

The people of Breachill, with the aid of the Eagle Knights and the Hellbreakers League, won a major victory by driving out the occupying Hellknights. After weeks of surviving under the iron fists of their oppressors, most residents are relieved to not have to watch their every move and word. However, as some Hellbreaker rebels are quick to point out: how free could they possibly be when their country is still a vassal state to Cheliax? But that's a problem for another day, as the streets of Breachill fill with celebrants, cheering and singing even as they rebuild ruined homes or honor their fallen neighbors.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.1sG3RasWU2xkMREK]{Caydens Keg} @UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.d2fUJQ1dXqZqNV0Q]{Town}

Nowhere are spirits as high as they are at Cayden's Keg, a tavern and temple to the drunken god @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.v67fHklTZ6LoU54q]{Cayden Cailean}. The primary bartender and priestess Brynne Taithe (jovial female human cleric of Cayden Cailean 5) has offered her healing services for free to many of the wounded, as well as room and board if they require it. Many comrades-in-arms and various local well-wishers congregate alongside the PCs, keeping the ale flowing since the battle's end. The alehouse is packed with people chattering and drinking, while a single musician plays rousing fiddle tunes from one corner. A small fire crackles in the tavern's fireplace, though its heat is hardly necessary to keep out the autumnal weather—the press of bodies does that particular work.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
Getting Started

A Long History

Breachill was the setting of the first few books in the Age of Ashes Adventure Path, and several of the locations and NPCs from that campaign are featured in the beginning of this chapter. To learn more about Breachill and its residents, you can read the “Breachill, Outpost of Secrets” article on page 62 of Pathfinder Adventure Path #145: Hellknight Hill.

The PCs are agents of the Hellbreakers League gathering in Breachill to meet a wounded Eagle Knight who wishes to aid the cause. Each character should have their own reason for joining the League—perhaps they're an Isgeri citizen fed up with Chelaxian rule or maybe they're a mercenary who fought for the League in the Battle of Hellknight Hill. Each player should choose a background from the Hellbreakers Player's Guide that ties their character to the organization. In any case, they have all agreed to aid this Eagle Knight contact, an accomplished soldier named Ethran Howell, in returning to the Hellbreakers headquarters in Saringallow.
