Whether the party has met one another already (and possibly fought together) is up to your group, but they all arrive at Cayden's Keg in Breachill on a crisp fall evening in Lamashan 4726 ar. As they head to this combination temple and alehouse, the overall mood in the town is celebratory.

Against Hell.name: Against Hell
Against Hell.text:
Chapter 1: Against Hell

When Hellknights of the Rack publicly executed retired Andoren general Reginald Cormoth in the town of Breachill for the alleged crime of “providing succor to dissidents against the crown of Cheliax,” they set alight a metaphorical powder keg that exploded into war with the Battle of Hellknight Hill. With the approach of Eagle Knight forces from Andoran into Isger, the Hellknights retreated into a newly fortified Citadel Altaerein. The ensuing siege was joined by rebels of the Hellbreakers League, a group of Isgeri citizens looking to remove the boot of Cheliax from their country's neck.

While most other sieges are long, drawn-out affairs, the fighting at the Battle of Hellknight Hill was short and brutal. Many Hellknights, eager for conflict, ranged out of the citadel and clashed with anti-Cheliax forces in and around Breachill. At one point, the diabolic dragon Kierothax perched atop Citadel Altaerein on behalf of the Hellknights and rained hellfire down upon the gathered armies.

Though both armies experienced heavy casualties, the forces of freedom and liberty eventually triumphed. They slew the dragon and routed the Hellknights, with the surviving Chelaxian forces fleeing southwest back toward Cheliax. The Eagle Knights, Hellbreakers, and their allies were too weary to give chase, and instead began the process of burying the fields of the dead, tending to the living wounded, and repairing damage to Breachill's buildings.

Mission Archive.name: Mission Archive
Mission Archive.text:
F9. Mission ArchiveSevere 2

Bookshelves line the eastern and western walls of this stuffy room filled with books and archived letters. A large, imposing desk made from ebony wood faces the only door.

The sisterhood keeps much of its most valuable information here in the Lucent Mission's archive. The tomes and documents on the shelves are mainly texts on the worship of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}, treatises on the hierarchies of devils in Hell, and illustrated primers on various martial disciplines. Viro Ahala was able to discover a rare ritual here with the sisterhood's help, but took that book with him with Endreah's blessing and permission.

F9. Mission ArchiveSevere 2

@UUID[Actor.ATcnQMlOiObB6Gxi]{Sister Endreah} @UUID[Actor.hQdY01eKZgCkBW96]{Velavi}

Creatures: Sister Endreah has been spending her time in the archive, scouring it for further information that could aid Cheliax in retaining its hold on Isger. She assumes the PCs are affiliated with the country's “less desirable revolutionary element” and immediately opens a book to summon the archivist, a velavi in charge of the monastery's books. During the battle, Sister Endreah lectures the PCs on their lack of discipline but is shaken if the PCs reveal that Viro isn't a real Hellknight, giving the PCs a chance to Demoralize her. If Sister Endreah is reduced to fewer than 6 Hit Points and the velavi has been defeated, she begrudgingly surrenders.

Learning of the Ritual: The PCs should be most interested in the ritual Sister Sylve told them Viro Ahala discovered here. The ritual's purpose is to summon a powerful devil and bind it to one's will, preventing the possibility of getting tricked into a bad deal. If asked, a captured Sister Endreah mockingly tells the PCs they're too late. She doesn't know where exactly in the Chitterwood the ritual will take place, but admits that Viro plans to rid Isger of its “goblin problems” for good, starting in the east. If the PCs killed Sister Endreah, they find a general map of the country with the eastern portion of the Chitterwood circled in red on the desk, giving them the same information.

Surrendered Sisters: If Sister Endreah and any other nuns are alive, they can be taken to Vordia to face justice. While the citizens there have a positive view of the Sisterhood, Sister Sylve's testimony convinces them to take the nuns into custody until the exact nature of their crimes can be determined. The PCs gain 1 RP.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.jlAHDhBI1mR86FvX]{Archive}
Within the Mission Archive is a compendium of scholarly journals on the topic of devils and 60 gp worth of donated trinkets from devotees of Asmodeus.

Training Hall.name: Training Hall
Training Hall.text:
F8. Training HallModerate 2

Two training dummies have been erected near a large straw mat on the floor, and two weapon racks occupy the back of the room. At the southern end of the room is a door.

Much of a sister's time here at the Lucent Mission is spent training in the martial art known as Hell's claw. This involves a lot of sparring practice with other initiates, with bare fists and occasionally asp coils. The sisterhood takes a relaxed attitude toward the deaths of novitiates during this process, so sisters must perfect their combat skills quickly.

F8. Training HallModerate 2

@UUID[Actor.3o4x5DwPn7qG9LBC]{Sisters of the Golden Erinys (2)}

Creatures: Matches between sisters are usually spectated by a more experienced nun to adjudicate the results, so the two sisters here are practicing their skills against the training dummies. One lands a vicious kick to a dummy's head, knocking it clean off, as the PCs enter. The two sisters recognize the PCs as interlopers and attack. If one sister is knocked unconscious, the other retreats to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02missionarchi00]{F9} when reduced to fewer than 6 Hit Points.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.0y3UzgrFJ6YqiN2h]{Weapon Rack}
A +1 whip and a crimson thorn rest in one of the weapon racks. None of the sisters training here has earned the right to wield the iconic weapon of their order.

Scullery.name: Scullery
Scullery.text:
F7. SculleryModerate 2

A steel basin and an iron stove stand against the northern wall. A round table bears the scars and stains of hundreds of meal preparations. Two closed barrels occupy different corners.

This is the mission's simple kitchen, where the sisters prepare meals for anyone staying here. One barrel contains fresh water, while the other contains ground wheat for making bread and gruel.

F7. SculleryModerate 2

@UUID[Actor.Yiigx1brVYvTk8GO]{Orts (2)} @UUID[Actor.3o4x5DwPn7qG9LBC]{Sister of the Golden Erinys}

Creatures: Sometimes, a sister tasked with cleaning up after a meal will “borrow” a tome from the archive to summon low-level devils to perform the drudge work. Currently, two orts stand by the sink, scrubbing plates and pots, while one sister watches over them and keeps them on task. A small pile of broken crockery near the sink is the result of a clumsy ort. The sister orders the orts to kill the intruders, though she isn't above engaging in combat herself.

Dining Room.name: Dining Room
Dining Room.text:
F6. Dining Room

At first glance, this is an unassuming dining room with a large table surrounded by six chairs. However, that notion is dispelled by the intricate scrollwork on the walls near the ceiling depicting hundreds of cavorting devils. There is a door leading further north and another leading east.

When the PCs enter this room, they hear the shattering of crockery and a string of curses in Diabolic coming from behind the northern door. One of the orts there dropped a plate while washing it, rousing the ire of the sister watching over them.

Sisters' Quarters.name: Sisters' Quarters
Sisters' Quarters.text:
F5. Sisters' Quarters

Eight identical rooms line the hall here, each containing a simple cot and a footlocker for the occupant's meager personal belongings. The sisters don't often stay long here, so the rooms contain no personal decorations.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.bRAclsXq5365NxAt]{Footlocker 1} @UUID[Actor.ayLrqK4khCpV163d]{Footlocker 2}
One footlocker contains a +1 bo staff. Another contains 13 gp in a leather pouch.

Temple.name: Temple
Temple.text:
F4. Temple

Three pews occupy the space in front of an impressive pulpit. A massive pentagram has been neatly burned into the wood on the eastern wall. A hallway leads north at the western end of the room, while there is a door a few feet away in the same wall.

The sisters gather here for worship on a nightly basis, murmuring quiet prayers in Asmodeus' name. Occasionally, the highest-ranking sister present will give a sermon at the pulpit, which is decorated in a style similar to most Chelaxian architecture.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.qDoarOIySzx7egZC]{Secret Panel}
Among the unholy scripture found on the pulp, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check finds a secret panel, behind which is an ebony statuette of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} worth 40 gp and +1 handwraps of mighty blows.

Entry.name: Entry
Entry.text:
F3. Entry

This simple entryway is decorated only with a carved wooden plaque above the eastern door that reads “Praise the Bright King of Hell.”

Sisters are expected to genuflect below the plaque before entering the mission proper. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:12] check recognizes the plaque is referring to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}.

Mission Garden.name: Mission Garden
Mission Garden.text:
F2. Mission GardenLow 2

A low stone fence encircles a small garden in front of the wooden building. Two trellises are entwined with grapes and a few bushes bloom with autumn flowers. A pentagram is emblazoned in the wood above the double doors leading inside.

As part of their training, new sisters are tasked with tending this garden. The fruit and flowers here are used in the mission's cooking, usually bland and simple fare. The grapes growing on the vines are small and bitter.

F2. Mission GardenLow 2

@UUID[Actor.hSi9aRbgdhXxU15r]{Novitiates of the Golden Erinys (2)}

Creatures: Regardless of the time of day, two novitiates are here, pruning the bushes or pulling weeds. If the sun has already set, they do so by lantern light. Those not of the sisterhood are usually not allowed at the mission, so the novitiates attack when they see the PCs.

Mountain Trail.name: Mountain Trail
Mountain Trail.text:
F1. Mountain Trail

A rough dirt path winds up through the hills at the outskirts of the Aspodell Mountains. Boulders flank the trail, providing an obstructed view of the building ahead.

If the PCs are quiet, they can set up a small camp here and rest overnight without being spotted by the sisterhood. The sisters have no reason to patrol and do not fear intruders.

Lucent Mission.name: Lucent Mission
Lucent Mission.text:
F. Lucent Mission

The Lucent Mission is a small Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys monastery in the foothills of the northwest Aspodell Mountains. Various orders of the sisterhood use it over the course of the year, training novitiates before sending them to their posts in Isgeri towns. The building also contains an archive of Asmodean texts that the sisterhood has collected over the decades. It's here that Viro Ahala, with the help of Sister Endreah, discovered the ritual he believes will grant him the power needed to enact his revenge.

With directions from Sister Sylve, the PCs are able to find the hidden trail that leads up the hills to the Lucent Mission. The trailhead is about half a day from Vordia, and ascending the path takes a few more hours. If the PCs left Vordia at dawn, it's likely sunset or nighttime if they traveled nonstop through the day. If the PCs took the robes of the Erinys at the orphanage, a PC wearing the robes gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls at the Lucent Mission, as the nuns are thrown off by seeing a stranger in the garb of their sisters.

A Repentant Sister.name: A Repentant Sister
A Repentant Sister.text:
A Repentant Sister

After Vordia's Sisters of the Golden Erinys agreed to help Viro Ahala and took up residence in the Lucent Mission to uncover its secrets, one of them began to have doubts about the supposed Hellknight. Sister Sylve (inquisitive female human novitiate 1) kept a close eye on Viro as he scoured the mission's archives, suspecting that he was an impostor who had not actually gone through the full Hellknight initiation ceremony. A few cleverly worded questions later, her suspicions were confirmed. However, before she could approach her superior, Sister Endreah, with proof, Viro found the ritual he was looking for and set back out into Isger to find the perfect place to enact it. Realizing she couldn't confront him through proper channels, Sylve also slipped out of the mission to follow him, but was unable to pick up his trail. She's been looking for other ways to deal with him since then.

When the PCs reach 10 Reputation Points for the first time, Sister Sylve hears of their activities in the area and seeks them out. She approaches them as they're traveling or as they're recuperating in their latest location for at least a day. Read or paraphrase the following.

A young woman wearing a red habit emblazoned with the symbol of a five-pointed star in golden thread approaches. From her posture, she seems like a tense coil ready to spring, but her face is devoid of any emotion. She holds up a hand in greeting, revealing a missing ring finger.

“Pardon me, I don't wish to alarm,” she says. “My name is Sister Sylve of the Golden Erinys. Perhaps you've heard of our order? I'm aware that you may think of us as the enemy in your campaign to ‘free Isger,' but you must listen to me. There is a dissembler named Viro Ahala falsely calling himself a Hellknight who has deceived my sisters. He took advantage of our resources to find a ritual that will summon a powerful devil to heed his ambitions, and I do not wish to see any more orphans created as the result of this. Unfortunately, I do not know where he intends to perform this ritual. My superior, Sister Endreah, might, but I am afraid she no longer trusts me, as she's wholly placed her faith in this impostor. As much as it pains me to say, I think you can extract that information from her.”

Sister Sylve tells the PCs the location of the Lucent Mission in the Aspodell Mountains and how many of her sisters remain there. She asks them to not kill anyone, but warns them that the sisters will fight back against intruders. If the PCs have exorcised Bright Embers Orphanage, Sister Sylve plans to return there and reopen it.

Sheltered Overhang.name: Sheltered Overhang
Sheltered Overhang.text:
E2. Sheltered OverhangSevere 2

A stone outcropping hangs over the mouth of the ravine, shading it from the sun and making it difficult to spot from the surface. A small pool of brackish rainwater occupies the far end of the ravine, surrounded by a dozen skeletons of rats, rabbits, and other small wildlife.

The walls of the ravine are 20 feet high here, and the area is in dim light, thanks to the shadow cast by the rocky overhang. The pool of water is only a few inches deep and looks stagnant. If anyone dares drink the water, it tastes foul and musty.

E2. Sheltered OverhangSevere 2

@UUID[Actor.l5lcNLr3A4IN5Vjv]{Vipers (2)} @UUID[Actor.9ZWUPSay0SPwJdNe]{Hissbite}

Creatures: When the PCs arrive, Hissbite knows that their plans have been foiled and immediately attacks. Hissbite keeps a pair of venomous vipers as pets, and the loyal snakes defend Hissbite to the death. The gobmob snake fights until reduced to 10 or fewer Hit Points, at which point they surrender. If the PCs allow them to live, Hissbite whines an apology for their actions and promises never to trouble anyone again. If the PCs haven't yet been to Umok, Hissbite warns about some “real bad dogs” in that area.

Development: The PCs likely kill at least one goblin snake or Hissbite. Bringing this corpse back to Fernsby helps the PCs prove that no actual goblins, especially those from Stumpfield, were responsible for the vandalism. Alternatively, the PCs might put Hissbite into custody and bring the creature to Fernsby's officials to face punishment. Either outcome gains the PCs 1 Reputation Point.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.qDnn2U9gjSKVRuzu]{Lair} @UUID[Actor.YgtRfva7MYIYx2pd]{Fernsby Citizens' Reward} @UUID[Actor.Kw9pbWRGUihaEIYy]{Goblins' Reward}
Hissbite's lair holds a pair of lesser soothing tonics stolen from Stumpfield. As thanks for uncovering the truth, the citizens of Fernsby give the PCs a runestone with a +1 weapon potency rune while the grateful goblins of Stumpfield gift the PCs a lesser healing potion.

Mossy Ravine.name: Mossy Ravine
Mossy Ravine.text:
E1. Mossy RavineLow 2

This crack in the earth has been here on the outskirts of the Chitterwood for centuries, likely the result of an ancient quake or constant erosion over the long years. Bright green moss lines the walls of the ravine as it gently descends forty feet into the ground.

The descent isn't steep enough to cause problems, though the PCs dislodge the occasional loose pebble as they traverse the ravine. This ravine is the lair of Hissbite (scheming genderless gobmob snake 4), who has been watching Stumpfield since its founding and grew increasingly jealous and bitter about the relationship Stumpfield goblins have with humans. After months of spying and recruiting a pair of like-minded goblin snakes, Hissbite recently began their plan of poisoning Fernsby against Stumpfield with targeted acts of midnight vandalism. Hissbite told their lackeys to show only their heads, knowing that they could be mistaken for goblins in the dark. Use the Mossy Ravine map for these encounters.

E1. Mossy RavineLow 2

@UUID[Actor.yUM1XyujeyCC5kv6]{Goblin Snakes (2)}

Creatures: A pair of goblin snakes lounge here unless chased by the PCs. They raise their goblin heads and hiss out a warning in Goblin for the PCs to stay out of their territory. They hardly give the PCs time to respond before they attack. Each goblin snake flees if reduced to 5 Hit Points or fewer; they either go to Hissbite's side deeper in the ravine or out into the forest, depending on which direction seems the most favorable for escape.

Fernsby.name: Fernsby
Fernsby.text:
E. Fernsby

Farms and orchards surround this quaint village. Thatched-roof cottages line the streets within the settlement proper, many with porches decorated with pots of flowers. In the center of town, a large oak tree grows in a small village green that has several benches. A few of the flowerbeds and shrubs on the green show recent signs of being unceremoniously dug up and destroyed.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.1axiWXf07jhh8S8U]{Village}

The people of Fernsby are polite but standoffish toward strangers, including the PCs. If the PCs ask around about the recent attacks, they learn that the stories have been blown a little out of proportion. No one has been attacked, but vandals have defaced the village green time and again over the past two weeks. Many residents are fervent about the fact that the space is Fernsby's pride and joy. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:15|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information learns that a few people are convinced they saw goblins on the green the same nights as each incident.

If a PC inspects the latest desecration of the flowers and shrubs and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:17] or @Check[survival|dc:17] check, they don't spot any footprints—goblin or otherwise—in the churned up dirt, only a series of sinuous impressions. On a critical success, they also find a torn leaf with two identical punctures in it, as if from a set of fangs. With this information, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:16] check can deduce that several large snakes recently made their way across the grass. No one in Fernsby has seen these snakes or understands why they would have snakes coming into their town and not attacking any people or animals.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:18] or @Check[society|dc:18] check is approached by a resident named Lilli who tells them that during a recent walk through the woods, she heard a strange hissing coming up from a ravine. Lilli can give the PCs directions to this ravine (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02mossyravine000]{E1}). Alternatively, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[survival|dc:18|traits:concentrate,exploration,move,skill,secret,action:track|name:Track] check to Track can spot enough impressions to follow them to the same ravine. The PCs can also wait until nightfall to see if the snakes return; if they do so, each PC should attempt a @Check[stealth|dc:16|traits:skill,secret,action:hide|name:Hide] check to Hide. If more than half of them succeed, they can catch the goblin snakes from area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02mossyravine000]{E1} unaware in the village green (if a map is needed, one of a field or clearing works well). If half of them fail, the goblin snakes spot them and flee back to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02mossyravine000]{E1}, but the PCs can easily give chase to encounter them in the ravine.

Gaining Reputation Points.name: Gaining Reputation Points
Gaining Reputation Points.text:
Gaining Reputation Points

During this chapter, the PCs gain Reputation Points (RP), which represent the positive opinion and goodwill that the people of Isger have toward the Hellbreakers League and the idea of Isgeri independence. By defeating certain foes and solving problems, the PCs will gain RP automatically, but there will also be opportunities for skill checks to gain additional RP. Keep track of the group's RP total, as they will be important in later chapters, as well as affecting how much the PCs will need to worry about Hedvend's bounty on insurgents as the weeks progress. If the PCs saved the crew of the Night's Prize in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22201agains]{Chapter 1}, they start with 1 RP.

4 or fewer RP: If the PCs mention that they are affiliated with the Hellbreakers League or express open disdain for the Chelaxian government before they gain any RP at a location, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11] check. On a failure, at least a few people in the area still have a positive opinion toward Cheliax and mistrust the PCs' intentions. The PCs take a –2 circumstance penalty to skill checks to gain Reputation Points at this location.

5–8 RP: As above, but the flat check is @Check[flat|dc:5].

9–12 RP: As above, but the flat check is @Check[flat|dc:5] and the PCs only take a –1 circumstance penalty on a failure.

13 or more RP: Most of the people the PCs talk to are receptive to the idea of throwing off the yoke of Chelaxian rule. You don't need to attempt a flat check if the PCs openly mention their affiliation.

Scene Notes Point Tracking

@UUID[Actor.6nKDXyZLn7XLL8bi]{Reputation Points Tracker}

Reward: The first time the PCs have a total of 10 or more RP, award them 10 XP.

Development: When the PCs reach 10 Reputation Points, they're approached by Sister Sylve (See @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02arepentantsi00]{A Repentant Sister}).

Stumpfield.name: Stumpfield
Stumpfield.text:
Stumpfield

Before the Goblinblood Wars, the Chitterwood was several dozen acres larger than it is today. Those missing trees were either cut down or burned by the Isgeri military to deprive the attacking goblins of their homes. The ancient forest is slowly beginning to reclaim this land, but it will be decades or even a century before the new trees mature and it comes close to its previous size.

One section of the northern edge of the forest was cut down to provide lumber to expand the burgeoning town of Fernsby. Recently, the remaining field of stumps has become the home of a collective of artists of both human and goblin ancestries.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.1axiWXf07jhh8S8U]{Village}

This artist's colony was established by Erk Oilfingers (visionary male goblin painter 1) and Jett Saldath (focused nonbinary human sculptor 1) after they met and formed a fast friendship trying to capture the image of the same twisted tree in their respective mediums. By inviting artists of all kinds to live and work in their new town, the two hoped it would foster better relations between their two ancestries. They have yet to change the world, or even the country, but in the 18 months since Stumpfield was founded, it has built a fascinating and supportive community. However, there has been some friction with the neighboring conservative town of Fernsby, which has been inflamed by the actions of the gobmob snake Hissbite and their lackeys (See @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02efernsby000000]{Here}).

When the PCs approach Stumpfield, read or paraphrase the following.

The town ahead is a unique collection of homes built onto the sides of wagons and semi-permanent tents, creating an atmosphere more like a traveling festival than a structured settlement. Several dozen residents—all either goblin or human—are gathered in the center of town around an object made of rope and wicker that resembles a four-legged animal. In turn, each person approaches the sculpture and adds something to it: a lump of clay to form an ear, several splashes of paint along the hide, or a series of colorful scarves wrapped around the neck. After each addition, the others gathered murmur in delight and approval.

The PCs arrive during Stumpfield's monthly practice of “cooperative art,” where the whole town comes together to create something—usually a sculpture or a painting, but other mediums are often involved. A few finished cooperative art pieces can be found throughout the town, and each is similarly chaotic but nonetheless compelling. When the PCs make themselves known, Erk breaks off from the assembled townspeople, introduces himself, and welcomes the PCs to town. He then introduces the party to the other artists and says, “Since we have guests, let's see if they have anything they want to add to this month's collective piece…” The crowd nods in agreement and a few of them even clap in encouragement.

Each of the PCs can add something to the sculpture, whether from their own supplies or from the collections of art supplies strewn about the town center. When they do so, they should attempt a @Check[art-lore|dc:16] or @Check[performance|dc:16] check; you can allow for other skills if the players make good cases for them. On a failure, the Stumpfield artists show only mild appreciation, but on a success, a few of them smile and say something like “Of course, just what it needed!” On a critical success, the townspeople give a hearty cheer. If at least one character succeeds, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to gaining RP in Stumpfield (+2 circumstance bonus if at least one character critically succeeded).

Over the next hour, the town finishes the sculpture and then celebrates into the night. The PCs can meet as many of the artists as they like, including Jett, Stumpfield's other founder. They share a bottle of wine with the PCs, and someone cooks a passable stew in a large cauldron that the whole town partakes of, with a random assortment of ingredients being thrown in. If the PCs discuss recent events in Isger (such as the Battle of Hellknight Hill) with anyone or ask about their opinion of Cheliax, most townspeople aren't overly concerned. A few want to show the PCs their latest piece of art that expresses their views on the subject, but overall the artists don't want to worry about the “outside world.”

However, later in the evening, Erk and Jett pull the PCs aside to explain a small problem the town is having. People are being attacked in the nearby town of Fernsby, and the perpetrators are rumored to be several goblins. Jett nervously explains that the villagers of Fernsby are convinced that Stumpfield is involved in these attacks and are threatening to stop selling them food and other goods. Erk insists that no Stumpfield goblins are as violent as Fernsby claims. The two ask the PCs, as a neutral party, to talk to the people of Fernsby and convince them not to cut off trade with Stumpfield.

Any Stumpfield resident can point the PCs in the direction of Fernsby, which is an uneventful 2-hour walk to the northeast.

Charred Wood.name: Charred Wood
Charred Wood.text:
Charred WoodModerate 2

A PC trained in Nature or Survival can trace the recent fire to its source, an area of the forest that has been almost completely turned to ash. Several days ago, Viro Ahala and some Sisters of the Golden Erinys performed a lesser version of the ritual he is attempting in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils]{Chapter 3}, summoning a pair of hell hounds that has stalked the woods since. Use the Charred Wood map for this encounter.

The trees have been burned down to stumps, and the ground is covered in charred grass in a circular area of the woods about one hundred feet in diameter. The heat has long since dissipated, but the smell of smoke remains.

Charred WoodModerate 2

@UUID[Actor.BQQ0TXGLzNUZGjbm]{Weak Hell Hounds (2)}

Creatures: Two hell hounds, weak from their relatively recent summoning, consider this circle their lair in the mortal Universe and range out from here to start fires in the woods. The fiendish beasts attack the PCs as soon as they enter the area and fight until killed. If Grizzo is with the PCs, she confirms that these are the creatures who attacked her before she hides behind a burned stump.

Presenting Evidence: If the PCs show the bodies of the hell hounds to Ioan Marblemug, he convinces the rest of Umok that the threat has been handled. This exonerates Grizzo, who is grateful to the PCs for their help. The PCs gain 1 Reputation Point. Grizzo is allowed to recuperate in Umok for a few more days before returning to her goblin friends in the Chitterwood. Alternatively, the PCs can bring Grizzo with them to Stumpfield if they haven't yet been to that location.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.ZQFXf1XtsgRsk2xn]{Ioan Marblemug's Reward}
For solving the mystery of the Umok fires, Ioan Marblemug gives the PCs a pair of bracers of missile deflection that has been in his family for generations, as well as 10 gp.

Fire!.name: Fire!
Fire!.text:
Fire!Low 2

As the PCs enter the outskirts of the Chitterwood to investigate the fires, they spot a rising plume of smoke in the distance. Rushing in that direction, they are faced with the beginnings of a brush fire started by the hell hounds that could potentially be quite devastating. They'll need to extinguish the flames before the situation grows out of control. If Grizzo is with the PCs, she cowers in fear of the flames and promptly passes out again.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.4szoYksOu0YbpyMu]{Chitterwood} @UUID[Playlist.ItTionHYw9zkogLj.PlaylistSound.8ufEDjvYhtv7FHLT]{Fire}

Fire!Low 2

This encounter uses a modified version of the Victory Point subsystem (GM Core 184), in which the PCs start with 5 Victory Points and must accumulate 10 total Victory Points. At the end of each phase, after every PC has acted, they automatically lose 1 Victory Point to represent the encroaching fire. If the PCs ever have 0 Victory Points, the fire can't be contained (see failure below).

To put out a portion of the fire, a PC can attempt a @Check[forest-lore|dc:15] or @Check[nature|dc:17] or @Check[survival|dc:17] check, gaining 1 Victory Point on a success (or 2 on a critical success, but losing 1 Victory Point on a critical failure). A spell or ability that creates at least 1 gallon of water automatically grants 1 Victory Point. Other abilities that control fire or starve a fire of oxygen can do the same at your discretion. A PC can also attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:18] check to dig part of a trench to act as a firebreak; successfully doing so doesn't gain a Victory Point but might stop the fire from spreading. At the end of a phase in which a PC successfully does this, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:15]. On a success, the PCs don't lose 1 Victory Point from the fire. If two or more PCs create a firebreak in the same phase, reduce the DC of the flat check to 11.

Success: The PCs put out the fire before it causes too much damage. The gnomes are grateful and the PCs earn 1 Reputation Point.

Failure: The fire rages out of control. Each PC takes @Damage[4d6[fire]] (with a @Check[reflex|dc:16|traits:basic] save) as they flee the scene. Eventually, the citizens of Umok and their animal friends are able to rally to put out the fire before it reaches town. The hell hounds are emboldened by the flames and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02charredwoodu00]{Charred Wood}, and the PCs take a –1 circumstance bonus to skill checks to gain Reputation Points in Umok.

Reward: For putting out the forest fire, award the PCs 60 XP.

A Victim of Happenstance.name: A Victim of Happenstance
A Victim of Happenstance.text:
A Victim of Happenstance

This unfortunate goblin is named Grizzo (hapless female goblin forager 1). She lives within the Chitterwood with her small family who aren't a part of any major goblin settlement. They scrounge for berries and mushrooms and occasionally catch fish. Rarely do they interact with others outside of the forest. Grizzo was unknowingly rooting around the area of the woods near the previous fires and was attacked by the two hell hounds who were the fire's cause (see below). She was burned by their hellfire breath but barely managed to escape, fleeing in the direction of town.

When Grizzo collapses in front of the PCs, she is unconscious with 0 Hit Points. A PC can Treat her Wounds, bandaging the burns and perhaps applying a topical salve, to help her regain consciousness. That PC can also attempt a @Check[medicine|dc:16] check, determining on a success that her burns were caused by a sustained direct blast of fire, perhaps from a magic spell or a creature that can breathe flames, rather than exposure to the flames of something like a forest fire.

Meanwhile, the other PCs see that gnomes are beginning to gather—at a safe distance—curious about Grizzo's presence. Some of the gnomes begin to mutter accusations that she must be responsible for the recent fires. It isn't too long before Ioan Marblemug (steadfast male gnome official 2), the town's captain of the guard and descendant of Umok's historical champion, approaches to assess the situation. He hears what his fellow citizens are saying but waits until it's clear that Grizzo isn't going to die before telling the PCs that “she's got to go.” It's clear that Ioan believes what the other gnomes believe about Grizzo. He explains that the punishment for violating Umok's most important law is banishment.

When Grizzo regains consciousness, she begins blubbering in fear. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:17] check calms her down enough for her to mutter the phrase "fire dog" over and over again. It is unfortunately not enough information for the PCs to be able to Recall Knowledge, but a PC can try to argue that Grizzo's condition and her fear means that she likely didn't set the fires. Getting Ioan to agree requires a @Check[diplomacy|dc:18] or @Check[intimidation|dc:18] check or a @Check[legal-lore|dc:16] check. On a success, Ioan begrudgingly allows Grizzo to remain with the town doctor while the PCs investigate the fires. If a PC critically fails this check, Ioan is adamant that Grizzo be taken out of Umok immediately and firmly suggests that the PCs be the ones to do so.

Umok.name: Umok
Umok.text:
Umok

Umok was founded by gnomes several centuries ago as a peaceful haven for those looking to live in harmony with the nearby Chitterwood. Several times over the years, the gnome residents clashed with nearby goblin camps over local resources, namely game and wood. These conflicts came to an ugly head during the Goblinblood Wars, when hobgoblins tried to burn Umok to the ground. A visiting gnome champion of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.v67fHklTZ6LoU54q]{Cayden Cailean} named Loriwyse Marblemug rallied the town to push back against the hobgoblin raiders, saving everyone. Since then, fire has been outlawed within 500 yards of Umok's perimeter; the punishment is usually banishment, but some past goblin perpetrators have been executed.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.MguIobt9wtyoUc2d]{Umok}

The citizens of Umok use alchemy and magic to heat their food and light their town. They also employ domesticated woodland creatures to act as guards and lookouts in and around the town. If these animals see someone approaching with an open flame, they are trained to return to town to warn the gnomes in charge. Some of the larger creatures, such as wolves, try to scare off any such intruders, to varying degrees of success.

As the PCs approach Umok by road, they spot at about 500 yards from town a sign that reads in Common and Gnomish, “Now Entering the Umok Fire-Free Zone. Please Extinguish All Flames.” A cartoonish illustration of a fire with a big, black X across it has been painted underneath. Many such signs are around Umok, even in the surrounding woods. If the PCs haven't already attempted a skill check to Recall Knowledge about the town, they might want to do so now to learn a little about the history behind this warning.

It is assumed that the PCs comply with the sign, though if they are traveling by day, they have no need of torches to light their way. If they don't comply and approach the town carrying fire, a random PC spots a pair of rabbits bolting in Umok's direction out of the corner of their eye. As a result of the rabbits' warning, the PCs take a –2 circumstance penalty to their skill checks to influence the town's people and gain Reputation Points, regardless of their current RP total.

When the PCs get within sight of the town, read or paraphrase the following.

A quaint town of cottages with peaked roofs and walls covered in ivy becomes visible, nestled between the woods and the hills. Orbs of light, twinkling in every color imaginable, hang in the air above each street corner. Smiling gnomes wave from porches and stoops, their clothing as brightly colored as the lights. Occasionally, a family of deer or a grumpy-looking badger wanders by, though the gnomes don't find this at all unusual. Proud Isgeri boarhounds pant happily as they watch passersby, sometimes rolling onto their backs in hopes of a belly rub.

The town is welcome to outsiders, provided they aren't carrying open flames. If the PCs discretely ask around, they learn that most Umok residents are neutral about Cheliax. The village is far enough away from most of Isger's major sites that they are left to themselves. If they can help it, they'd rather not grab Cheliax's attention with talk of rebellion. Most of the townspeople are more concerned about the rash of small fires that have been breaking out in the woods southwest of town over the past few weeks. Their animal-based early warning system has helped them ensure the fires haven't spread, but they haven't caught the perpetrator. The prevailing opinion around town is that goblins or hobgoblins are to blame. If any PC is of goblin or hobgoblin ancestry, the gnomes of Umok might unfairly treat them with suspicion.

The resident gnomes can point the PCs in the direction of these fires, but before they can leave town, there is a commotion: a badly burned goblin stumbles down the main street and collapses near the PCs.

Nuns' Quarters.name: Nuns' Quarters
Nuns' Quarters.text:
D6. Nuns' Quarters

Until the attic whisperer in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02orphansbedro00]{D5} is defeated, the doors to this portion of the orphanage remain stubbornly closed. Any damage dealt to them is repaired almost instantly, making them impossible to break down. Attempts to use fire or acid to destroy the door result in the PC having it supernaturally bounced back at them, forcing them to attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:18] save and take @Damage[1d4[fire]] or @Damage[1d4[acid]] damage on a failure. Such attempts raise the ire of the attic whisperer in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02orphansbedro00]{D5}, who begins to wail and cry to draw the PCs away from the doors. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:17] or @Check[religion|dc:17] check can sense that a supernatural force (the attic whisperer) is keeping the doors shut.

When the PCs are able to access the area, read or paraphrase the following.

Several sparse rooms line the hallway here, each containing nothing more than a simple wooden cot and a padded beam that is only a few inches off the ground. A red pentagram is painted on each wall above the beam.

These are the personal rooms of the sisters who ran this orphanage, though they show little of any inhabitants' personality. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:13|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] to Recall Knowledge knows the red pentagram is the symbol of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} and that the nuns would use the beam to kneel in supplication for regular prayers to the Lord of Hell.

@UUID[Actor.nb4Qt5V0LrELfgv7]{Under Cot}
A PC who searches these rooms and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:15|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check finds a crumpled piece of parchment under one of the cots. It appears to be a draft of a letter to another sister in an unnamed town, explaining how these sisters are going to a place called the Lucent Mission for an important task that “will bring much glory to Asmodeus.” The final line explains that the recipient is being sent Bright Embers' remaining orphans before ending in a large ink spill. If the PCs show the authorities this evidence, none of them know where the Lucent Mission is, but they thank the PCs for informing them of the true fate of the remaining orphans; the PCs gain 1 Reputation Point.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.fcN1rbm4ebSMWWuh]{Room}
Left behind in one room is an unholy text about the worship of Asmodeus worth 50 gp and a neatly folded robes of the Erinys.

Orphans' Bedroom.name: Orphans' Bedroom
Orphans' Bedroom.text:
D5. Orphans' BedroomSevere 2

Two rows of small, decrepit beds line the walls of this room. Tattered blankets are neatly draped across the beds, and each bed has a small set of drawers next to it, many of which hang open and empty. A canine skull sits on one bed, next to a ratty stuffed bear.

There's room for 12 orphans to sleep communally here. The orphanage hasn't been at full capacity since the first few years after it was built, so often, two or three orphans would have this room to themselves. Thanks to the occult energy engulfing the building, it doesn't look like anyone has slept here for years.

Scene Notes Macros

@UUID[Macro.EqlIoQnpkxwa3a27]{Toggle Haunting} @UUID[Macro.O4MEQtgNnIbgZS1x]{Reveal Attic Whisperer}

D5. Orphans' BedroomSevere 2

@UUID[Actor.4ydWQxo74yE1Tygr]{Lights Out} @UUID[Actor.NayaDGsBiVSOrWQF]{Attic Whisperer}

Hazard: The Sisters made sure that all orphans had the same bedtime, regardless of age. Older children would sometimes lie in their beds in the dark, thinking about new families or soothing the younger orphans to sleep. This unique flavor of quiet despair created this darkness-inducing haunt.

Creatures: The general tenor of the psychic energy in the orphanage has created an undead creature usually associated with forgotten and forlorn children, known as an attic whisperer. When the haunt rolls initiative, the canine skull on one of the beds rises up to attach to the rotting teddy bear. The creature is wrapped in a tattered sheet and begins echoing the cries of many of the orphans who have since grown up. This attic whisperer fights until destroyed.

This Orphanage is Clean: With the defeat of the attic whisperer, the haunts in the orphanage are permanently destroyed, and the doors to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02nunsquarters00]{D6} fly open with a loud bang.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.8zS6T1AakbGgj2xe]{Slam Open Doors}

Play Room.name: Play Room
Play Room.text:
D4. Play RoomLow 2

Faded murals of friendly looking devils are painted across the walls of this playroom, with nuns of Asmodeus holding hands with children as their deity smiles down upon them. Faces that would normally be violent or gruesome in any other scene are depicted as playful and kind. The room is empty save for a dusty toy box in the center.

The Sisters understood that structured play is important to developing minds and allowed the orphans to indulge their childish whims here.

D4. Play RoomLow 2

@UUID[Actor.oNm0gF12cL6Fo4dA]{Play Time}

Hazard: Despite this being a playroom for young children, rambunctiousness was never permitted. A child who pushed another down or pulled their hair was severely reprimanded (out of sight of the other orphans, of course). The wasted potential enjoyment of blocks, dominoes, jacks, and so forth has infused the room's toy box, making it a powder keg of “fun” ready to explode in the PCs' faces when they explore this room.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.P3aVpV46XQXT9AhJ]{Toggle Haunting}

Adds Lighting and Audio to the room.

Dining Hall.name: Dining Hall
Dining Hall.text:
D3. Dining Hall Trivial 2

This room features two table sets, one a bit smaller than the other, with accompanying small chairs to accommodate children. While the larger table has nothing on it, the smaller table is set with four plates but no utensils.

D3. Dining HallTrivial 2

@UUID[Actor.tki1r5Fd8oPYNBoW]{Food Fight}

Hazard: The strict discipline of the sisterhood meant that meals were sedate affairs where no orphan was permitted to act up. This repression steeped into the furniture and is eager to be released now that the nuns have vacated. A spectral food fight breaks out when any creature gets close to the kids' table (as marked on the map).

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.n9L1BsSB2uTEGp9G]{Toggle Haunting}

Adds Lighting and Audio to the room.

Entry Hall.name: Entry Hall
Entry Hall.text:
D2. Entry Hall

A wide hall runs through the building. The floor is scuffed, and all the interior doors hang crookedly from their hinges. A wide staircase leads up to the second floor.

Similar to the deterioration of the front yard, the unkempt state of the building has been hastened by the now-rampant spiritual energy. The PCs hear footsteps all around them as if children were still running around. Through the open doors, the party can see a dining hall and kitchen to the east and a recreation room to the west.

Orphanage Yard.name: Orphanage Yard
Orphanage Yard.text:
D1. Orphanage Yard

Bright Embers is near the eastern outskirts of the town. When the PCs approach the building, read or paraphrase the following.

A walled yard surrounds a rectangular two-story building whose angles seem slightly off, as if the structure were hunched in on itself. Curtains have been drawn in all the windows, but the front door is slightly ajar, occasionally banging against its frame with each stray breeze. A few stunted trees bare of leaves stand watch over patches of dying grass and a lone seesaw whose red paint is chipped and faded. A closed wrought-iron gate at the end of a stone walkway leading to the building features a metal plaque that reads “Bright Embers Orphanage, established 4701 ar.”

Children used to play in this yard, their laughter ringing out to the nearby street, but now it is empty and silent. As the group approaches the front door, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:18] check notices the curtains twitch in one of the upstairs rooms (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02orphansbedro00]{D5}). A PC who examines the yard and succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:16] check can sense that the state of decay the trees, grass, and everything else is in has been supernaturally accelerated.

Bright Embers Orphanage.name: Bright Embers Orphanage
Bright Embers Orphanage.text:
D. Bright Embers Orphanage

The Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys ran the Bright Embers Orphanage for nearly two decades, starting by taking in orphans of the Goblinblood Wars and preparing them to live in a country governed by the rule of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}. This entailed teaching the children pro-Cheliax propaganda and attempting to instill a respect for law and order by emphasizing that the chaos loved by goblinkind got their parents killed, conveniently not mentioning that many of the war's hobgoblin commanders could be as strict as some Hellknight orders.

This constant emotional barrage on the children's minds over the years has left a psychic imprint on the building, causing unusual phenomena to occur within. Former residents have spoken about seeing doors slamming from across the room, hearing agonized cries of terror coming from the walls, feeling like someone unseen is watching, and so on. The Sisters would explain these occurrences as pranks or wild imaginings, and their iron will stopped the orphanage from becoming fully haunted. That ended with the arrival of Viro Ahala.

When Viro convinced Sister Endreah to help him with his plan, her fellow nuns went with her, leaving the orphanage with no staff. With no more nuns in Bright Embers to suppress the building's occult resonance, a handful of unstable spirits have formed from the emotional fallout of the past decades.

As the orphanage is the only lead the PCs have to how the Sisters of the Golden Erinys in Vordia are connected to the mystery Hellknight, they'll need to explore the building to find out more. If the PCs heard the story of the local teens, their curiosity might be piqued. Entering the haunted orphanage isn't necessary to further the League's reputation in Vordia, but they might want to return once they start hearing about how the strange occurrences in other villages might be related to the sisterhood.

Vordia.name: Vordia
Vordia.text:
Vordia

During the Goblinblood Wars, Vordia suffered a fair amount of damage and many of its people were killed. As part of their relief efforts, the Chelaxian government sent a contingent of Sisters of the Golden Erinys to construct an orphanage in the town that would teach the children about the Church of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}. As a result, many of the residents feel a fair amount of goodwill toward Cheliax. When you attempt a flat check if the PCs openly discuss their allegiance to the Hellbreakers League (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02gainingreput00]{Gaining Reputation Points}), roll twice and take the worse result.

A bustling town of several hundred people, Vordia doesn't look much different from any other small settlement in the Isgeri countryside. The one detail that makes it stand out is the dozens of flags bearing either the national symbol of Cheliax or the religious symbol of Asmodeus flying atop nearly every building or from nearly every window. Despite this (or perhaps because of it), the residents look happy as they go about their day.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.1axiWXf07jhh8S8U]{Village}

The town decorations should hint to the players that they need to keep a low profile here. They might not want to stay long, but it's their mission to at least try to quietly sway the populace. It will benefit them to listen and observe to see if the residents have any issues with the Chelaxian government that could be a crack in the pleasantly maintained facade. If they spend time Gathering Information (DC 16), they quickly learn that most townspeople are concerned about the nuns who run the Bright Embers Orphanage. Ever since the town was visited by a strange Hellknight a few weeks ago, the nuns haven't been seen much.

If the PCs want to learn more about this occurrence, one of them must attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:16|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information or a @Check[scribing-lore|dc:14] or @Check[society|dc:14] check to look into the town's public records. On a successful Diplomacy check, the PC learns that two nights ago, a group of local teens dared one another to sneak into the seemingly abandoned orphanage and were frightened off by strange noises coming from the second floor. On a successful Scribing Lore or Society check, the PC finds very recent records of Bright Embers' two current orphan charges both finding families in neighboring towns the day after the Hellknight's visit, but the names of these families are oddly unreadable. By simply asking around, the PCs learn the location of the orphanage and that it is run by the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys, for whom the villagers have nothing but kind words.

Wolfpoint Palisade.name: Wolfpoint Palisade
Wolfpoint Palisade.text:
Wolfpoint PalisadeLow 2 and Moderate 2

When the PCs explore Wolfpoint, they find it devoid of life. It's been abandoned for several weeks at most, but not even mice or stray wolves have attempted to reclaim the buildings. Living creatures just seem to avoid the place. This is the result of the influence of a drude, a shadowy fey creature whose mere presence in the area can invoke terrible nightmares. This particular drude is drawn to areas where calamity has occurred and uses imagery of those events in the dreams they cause. The drude is accompanied by several gremlins who delight in the chaos.

If the PCs set up camp here, their sleep is plagued with nightmares of bloodthirsty goblin hordes attacking their position, stabbing and biting them with sharp dogslicers and even sharper teeth. A PC on watch hears strange noises by the palisade like squawking cries and moans. This encounter takes place in the middle of the night, in darkness. Sleeping PCs likely don't have torches or other light sources lit, so begin this encounter with them extinguished. Use the Wolfpoint Palisades map for this encounter.

Wolfpoint PalisadeLow 2 and Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.jAxkXXB8uxTGL2B4]{Pugwampis (3)} and @UUID[Actor.b3LhVLTnh8wXkZX4]{Mitflits (2)} @UUID[Actor.TdOy9MNs17va4ppA]{Drude}

Creatures: A small pack of pugwampi gremlins have allied with the drude haunting Wolfpoint. They attempt to draw any PCs still awake in the night to the palisade with unusual noises and cries for help, then begin peppering anyone who's drawn close with arrows. Each pugwampi flees when reduced to 3 or fewer Hit Points, knowing that their leader will finish the fight.

Darkness Rising: When the last pugwampi has been slain or driven off, the PCs notice that any shadows they are casting begin to shudder and dance as the drude approaches. They have 1 round to prepare themselves before the drude and their mitflit minions appear and attack. These gremlins have been bullied by the drude into assisting their plan and fight until killed. The drude flees into the darkness if reduced to 5 or fewer Hit Points.

Development: Once the drude has been slain or routed, the nearby shadows return to normal. The PCs can sleep through the rest of the night and report their success to Runa Bloodhammer. The Steel Circle occupies Wolfpoint over the next few days, agreeing to rob only those travelers clearly aligned with Cheliax. The PCs gain 1 Reputation Point.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.qlI0GWXSiHxfguYt]{Crate}
If the PCs take the time to search through the garrison, they discover a crate with a thorn of Milani and a lesser silverscrap bomb left behind by the soldiers.

The Steel Circle.name: The Steel Circle
The Steel Circle.text:
The Steel Circle

The PCs might want to learn a little more about the Steel Circle before heading to Wolfpoint. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:18|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[underworld-lore|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge has heard of the bandit gang. They are a fairly large and organized group of thieves and robbers who operate throughout southern Isger. These bandits rove about the countryside, not staying in a single location long enough for law enforcement to track them down. On a critical success, the PC knows the type of places—hillside caves, hidden crevices, and abandoned farmhouses—the Steel Circle likes to camp in, gaining the result of a successful check to Gather Information noted below.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:18|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information learns that the Steel Circle is currently camped out in an abandoned farm a mile southeast of Wolfpoint. On a critical success, the PC also hears that the bandits tried to set up in Wolfpoint, but something drove them off.

If the PCs approach the farm, they are spotted by well-hidden lookouts, who warn the Steel Circle leaders. Several armed bandits go out to meet the PCs in the middle of the fallow fields. They are led by Runa Bloodhammer (wary female dwarf bandit 4), whose first order of business is to let the PCs know that if they try anything against her or her people, they'll be dead within seconds. The PCs are outnumbered here, sensing a dozen more sets of eyes upon them from the nearby barn and farmhouse.

Runa begins the encounter as unfriendly, though a PC can change her attitude with a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:17|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression] check to Make an Impression. If a PC has a skill feat that allows them to Make an Impression on several people at once (such as Group Impression), they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks to change Runa's attitude. If the PCs have 6 or more Reputation Points, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to skill checks to change Runa's attitude, as the Steel Circle are no friends of Cheliax.

Runa is willing to talk with the PCs long enough for them to attempt three checks to sway her. She asks them their business in the area and tries to gauge their feelings about breaking the law without broaching the subject directly. If the PCs increase Runa's attitude to friendly, she admits that her gang did spend one night camped inside Wolfpoint, but they had terrible nightmares. While the bandits are hardened criminals, they were too frightened to remain in the garrison and set up on this farm. Runa snaps her fingers and proposes that if the PCs investigate Wolfpoint and remove any “curse or creature befouling the place,” she'll have the Steel Circle help the Hellbreakers as best they can. If Runa's attitude is helpful, she'll also agree to donate some supplies to the effort.

If Runa's attitude becomes hostile, she gives a sharp gesture to her fellow bandits and storms off. A volley of arrows rains down on the PCs, dealing @Damage[(2d8+13)[piercing]] damage to each of them with a @Check[reflex|dc:20|traits:basic] save. If Runa's attitude is only indifferent or unfriendly after the PCs attempt three checks, she curtly tells the PCs to go away, warning them to not approach the farm again. If the PCs refuse to leave or later try to return, they suffer the bandits' wrath as if Runa's attitude is hostile.

Reward: For changing Runa's attitude to friendly or helpful, award the PCs 30 XP.

Wolfpoint.name: Wolfpoint
Wolfpoint.text:
Wolfpoint

The Wolfpoint reserve garrison is just south of the Conerica River and was built before the Goblinblood Wars to hold about 300 soldiers and officers, mainly to protect the waterway and nearby roads from bandit activity. The wooden palisade surrounding the many barracks was burned to the ground during the war but has since been repaired. With the tensions and eventual conflict at Breachill, the soldiers that were stationed here were reassigned elsewhere within Isger, leaving the garrison empty for the past several weeks.

As the PCs make their way toward Wolfpoint, they begin to hear rumors of increased bandit activity in the area from other travelers and farmers. They complain that since the soldiers at Wolfpoint have been stationed elsewhere, the local sheriff has been unable to keep a lid on highway crime. Many believe that a group of bandits called the Steel Circle has taken over Wolfpoint, but others insist that something more sinister now occupies the garrison. These people claim to have seen goblins within the palisade walls, lighting fires and preparing for another war. If pressed, they describe small figures with pointy ears that bear only a passing resemblance to goblins. In reality, the Steel Circle did attempt to make Wolfpoint a new semi-permanent base of operations but was scared off by the drude—a malicious nightmare-inducing fey that had already taken up residence there.

Countryside Travel.name: Countryside Travel
Countryside Travel.text:
Countryside Travel

Like in most countries, small roads and paths crisscross the whole of Isger that aren't marked on any map. Most locals know how to get to the three or four places that are most important to them, so these roads lack any consistent signage. However, traveling from one location to another isn't meant to be a challenge for the PCs; a character might even originally be from this area! Most residents are happy enough to point the party in the right direction, especially in some of the larger towns like Vordia. Use the map to chart approximate distances between locations and the party's slowest Speed to determine how many miles they can travel in 1 day.

These journeys should be relatively uneventful, though if you feel the PCs are lacking in XP, a group of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.hellbreakers-bestiary.Actor.SWUOiOIO3w8BOebM]{Chelaxian Loyalists} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.hellbreakers-bestiary.Actor.AcoAyXQwJiEv8Y9g]{Chelaxian Recruits} might attempt to bar their passage on the road. Alternatively, a wild animal or two might be hungry and desperate enough to stalk the PCs as they travel, attacking when they are all alone.

In addition, each day they are on the road, one PC can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:18 check to sway the locals they might interact with on their journey into supporting the Hellbreakers League and Isgeri independence, earning them RP. Diplomacy is the default skill to use for these checks, but a PC might attempt a @Check[deception|dc:18] check to fabricate terrible acts the Chelaxian government is planning, a @Check[performance|dc:18] check to entertain (while hiding anti-Cheliax or pro-Isger sentiment within the performance), or an @Check[isger-lore|dc:18] or @Check[society|dc:18] check to discuss the citizens' everyday problems and how they might be improved with a new government. Players might even propose other skills. At your discretion, the DC might be 1 higher or lower to represent how loyal the locals are to Cheliax.

What Have We Heard?.name: What Have We Heard?
What Have We Heard?.text:
What Have We Heard?

The PCs might want to know about the places they are being sent before they head out of Saringallow. They can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:16|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information or a @Check[isger-lore|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[society|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge about each place, learning the information listed below on a success. Each location also lists an additional skill a PC can use to Recall Knowledge about that location.

Wolfpoint (@Check[warfare-lore|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]): The Wolfpoint reserve garrison was built before the Goblinblood Wars to hold soldiers and officers with the primary purpose of protecting the roads by the Conerica River from bandit activity. The wooden palisade of Wolfpoint isn't impenetrable, though, having burned to the ground during the war. On a critical success, the PC has also heard that the soldiers stationed there have been reassigned to the Andoran border, leaving the garrison unoccupied.

Vordia (@Check[religion|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]): Vordia is a small, traditional Isgeri town northwest of the Aspodell Mountains. During the Goblinblood Wars, it suffered a fair amount of damage and many of its people were killed. The Chelaxian government helped rebuild after the war, creating a fair amount of goodwill with the people that lasts to this day. On a critical success, the PC also knows that the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys has run an orphanage in Vordia since the war.

Umok (@Check[gnome-lore|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]): Umok is a gnome settlement nestled between the Chitterwood and the Aspodell Mountains. The residents have had unfortunate dealings with goblins in the past (not including the Goblinblood Wars) and have outlawed fire within 500 yards of the village. They instead use magic and alchemy for cooking, warmth, and light. On a critical success, the PC has heard that the gnome villagers maintain a network of wild animals to warn them of a dangerous creature's approach. They also know that Umok is known for raising Isgeri boarhounds (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16newanimalcom00]{New Animal Companion}), a breed of dog with a penchant for hunting down extraplanar prey.

Stumpfield (@Check[goblin-lore|dc:16|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge]): Stumpfield is something of an oddity in Isger, as a recently established village of artists of both goblin and human. Located just north of the Chitterwood, the village and its residents are considered “weird but harmless” by most. On a critical success, the PC also knows that there is some tension between Stumpfield and the nearby farming village of Fernsby, which provides a lot of Stumpfield's day-to-day goods.

Building a Political Movement.name: Building a Political Movement
Building a Political Movement.text:
Building a Political Movement

At the end of the week, Rhokrag calls for an organization-wide meeting after receiving a message from the Demetriases.

Hellbreakers fill every corner of the basement headquarters as Rhokrag climbs onto a table and holds up a folded sheet of paper. “We just got word from Alceo and Phoebe, and they are quite pleased with our efforts so far!” A general murmur of satisfaction runs through the assembled. “They especially want to acknowledge the efforts of my rescuers.”

“And to tell you to stay away from boats from now on!” shouts Maire to some scattered laughter.

“We all make mistakes,” coughs Rhokrag. “The Demetriases are reporting that due in large part to our supply raids on various trade vessels, Druma has begun to limit their trade routes on the Conerica. Yes, this will hurt Isger's economy more than Cheliax's, but it's a start. Hedvend is likely going to increase military patrols near the river, maybe even going so far as to ask for soldiers from Thrune.” The crowd boos. “The Demetriases are suggesting that we ease back on the raids for now. We need to show the citizens of Isger that the Hellbreakers League is more than a band of violent insurgents. They need to know that we care about the land and its people. This is OUR land. These are OUR people.” Another cheer rises up, louder than the first.

“Over the next few weeks, you'll be going out among those people to spread the word of why Isgeri independence is so important. Talk to them. Find out what's important to them and convince them it's important to you as well. And if they need help, give it.”

The PCs are assigned an area of Isger south of the Conerica River and north of the Chitterwood that includes villages like Umok, Stumpfield, and Vordia, as well as the garrison at Wolfpoint. The PCs don't need to range as far west as Logas or as far east as Dustpawn as another group has been assigned the southeast portion of Isger east of the Aspodell Mountains. See the map of Isger for these settlements' exact locations; you should also share this map with the players.

The PCs can visit these locations in any order they see fit, though Wolfpoint is the closest to Saringallow. The characters might ask about other villages and farms along their route; such locations are not detailed in this chapter, but you can describe them as being generally peaceful, albeit worried about the brewing hostilities between Andoran and Cheliax. Most Isgeri citizens don't want to be caught in the middle of another bloody war. The PCs can make a single skill check during each day of travel to represent speaking with these townspeople and farmers to gain Reputation Points, as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02countrysidet00]{Countryside Travel}.

There is no time limit for this portion of the adventure, though as the PCs help people and investigate unusual goings-on, they will eventually get a lead on Viro Ahala's plans to get revenge against the Hellbreakers League.

For the Cause.name: For the Cause
For the Cause.text:
Chapter 2: For the Cause

After rescuing Rhokrag from the Witchfire and returning to Saringallow, the PCs have 1 week of downtime for their own personal projects. This is an excellent time for the characters to train and level up, purchase or craft equipment, or rest and recuperate.

Some characters might want to look into the name “Hellknight Ahala,” but there isn't much to find. @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole05]{Viro Ahala} (vengeful male human Hellknight armiger 5) has little to his name, though he aims to fix that. A survivor of the Battle of Hellknight Hill, Viro yearns for vengeance against the Hellbreakers and is plotting their destruction with fiendish obsession.

Having learned about the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys, an Isgeri monastic order fostered by the Church of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}, Viro approached the sisters in the name of the Order of the Rack and was persuasive enough to enlist their aid. Believing him to be a true Hellknight thanks to stolen armor and his confident arrogance, Sister Endreah (steely female human Asmodean nun 4) brought him to a hidden monastery called the Lucent Mission (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02arepentantsi00]{A Repentant Sister}), where he discovered a grand ritual to summon a devil that could give him the power needed to defeat the League. While the PCs are busy recruiting the citizens of Isger, Viro is likewise recruiting several other fleeing Hellknight armigers on his way to a series of caves in the Chitterwood where he can enact his ritual.

A Victorious Return.name: A Victorious Return
A Victorious Return.text:
A Victorious Return

Once Viro Ahala has been defeated and his ritual stopped, the PCs can explore other parts of Stagfall Caves or immediately return to Thorngrip to tell Brakknap the good news. The goblin oracle is already aware of their success from the spirits of his ancestors, and the entire town comes out to meet the PCs as they step through the thorn wall. The PCs are treated as heroes and there's an evening of celebration, especially if they need to rest for a night to tend to their wounds before leaving the Chitterwood. The PCs are especially treated well by the goblin children who have never met non-goblinoids before, as they are curious about the heroes and beg the party for dramatic retellings and reenactments of their defeat of Viro and his fiendish allies. Some children might even dress up as a specific PC. Food and drink is plentiful all throughout the night; the pickle-flavored goblin liquor is especially strong, and a few PCs might wake feeling a little worse than when they went to sleep. Luckily, Mirdona has surefire hangover cure, which also tastes of pickles.

The PCs should then return to Saringallow to debrief with Rhokrag and the other Hellbreakers. They listen with interest as the PCs recount their travels, with Maire taking notes for future stories. Rhokrag is pleased with their success, especially with the friendship the PCs forged with the Thorngrip goblins, and lets them know that the Demetriases want to speak with them directly. At their earliest convenience, the PCs should head north to Elidir, where the Hellbreakers League founders await.

At this point, tally the PCs' current Reputation Point total. They will have the opportunity to gain (or lose) Reputation Points in the coming chapters, but it will be helpful to have a snapshot of the League's reputation in Isger after the PCs' actions; this total is also an extrapolation of how the other teams did in other areas of the country.

  • Fewer than 6 RP The Hellbreakers League is still seen as dangerous troublemakers by most citizens. The PCs have to travel north incognito.
  • 7–9 RP Most people don't believe the League wants to burn down every Isgeri city, but neither do they fully trust its members. The PCs are better not to draw attention to their affiliation for now.
  • 10–12 RP Those who want to throw off the yoke of Chelaxian rule feel more comfortable speaking out, thanks to the efforts of the Hellbreakers League. The PCs won't need to worry about the bounty on their capture, except in areas of deep Chelaxian loyalty.
  • 13+ RP Talk of Isgeri independence is on everyone's lips! The Hellbreakers League are considered the best chance for the future. Some citizens are still loyal to Steward Hedvend and Cheliax, but they might soon be a minority. The PCs are celebrated nearly everywhere they go.

Reward: For defeating Viro Ahala and stopping his ritual, award the PCs 40 XP. If the PCs have a total of at least 15 Reputation Points, award the PCs an additional 40 XP.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.ETw5mojopB8MOYvi]{Awakened Crystal}
Brakknap gifts the crystal pendant to the PCs, which has served its initial purpose and awakens into a pendant of the occult.

Ritual Site.name: Ritual Site
Ritual Site.text:
G11. Ritual SiteSevere 3

Candlelight flickers along the perimeter of this large chamber and the cave is infused with the scent of brimstone. Two men occupy the room, one in the typical accoutrements of a Hellknight armiger and another dressed in the formidable armor of a Hellknight. The false Hellknight stands over an ivory bowl that contains a bright flame in the center of the room, scattered ritual materials piled nearby atop a rough blanket on the stone floor. The air above it wavers with occult energy as he methodically burns a piece of parchment that has been inscribed with blood.

Viro Ahala chose this cave for his ritual site as it courses with magical energy that has gone largely untapped for centuries. The flame in the ivory bowl and the candles together provide bright light for the chamber. A ledge at the back of the chamber requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:14|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] check to Climb, and hidden from view from the ground on this ledge is a tight tunnel that leads south to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03hiddenledge000]{G9}. The top of the ledge is in dim light, so Viro and his companions are unaware of the tunnel.

G11. Ritual SiteSevere 3

@UUID[Actor.VGVm6SUUXLGTSHhO]{Ritual Backlash} @UUID[Actor.ezqASW0IwBFMaj8X]{Novice Hellknight Armiger} @UUID[Actor.9dH742qBDrfMDXB2]{Viro Ahala}

Creatures: If given the opportunity to speak before being attacked, Viro gloats that the PCs are too late to stop his ritual in an attempt to Demoralize the physically most intimidating PC. If the PCs disable the ritual backlash hazard before defeating Viro, he becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. Viro and his fellow armiger won't surrender, fighting to the bitter end.

Hazard: Viro Ahala has been performing a complicated ritual here for several days, one that will grant him only a fraction of the power of Hell, but enough to get his revenge on the Hellbreakers League. He has yet to be successful, but his attempts have caused the magical energy of the cave to become erratic. His attention to the flame within the ivory bowl, the focus of the ritual, has kept the energy in check, but the moment he becomes even momentarily distracted, the backlash manifests. Because Viro has been pouring his mental energy into the ritual all this time, the backlash harms only his enemies. If the ivory bowl is broken, the hazard loses 1 action. If the ivory bowl is destroyed, the hazard loses 2 actions.

Brakknap's Crystal: The crystal Brakknap gave the PCs provides a small amount of protection and the ability to counter some of the ritual's backlash. The PC wearing or holding the crystal, and everyone adjacent to them, gains a +1 status bonus to any Will saving throw against the hazard's Pulse of Fear ability, and resistance 2 to mental damage caused by the ritual's mindburn Strike. They also gain the following reaction.

Rebuke Hellish Healing r (primal) Trigger The ritual backlash hazard uses Vitality of Hell on a target within 10 feet; Effect Attempt @Check[nature|dc:16] or @Check[religion|dc:16] check. On a success, Vitality of Hell is counteracted. On a critical success, the target of Vitality of Hell takes @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.4SGmpdHIjABkKsOo]{Break Ritual Bowl}

Reward: For stopping Viro's ritual, the PCs earn 2 Reputation Points.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.bYAALyWaP7BOYE4H]{Ritual Materials}
The materials Viro was using for his ritual include three rubies that are worth 10 gp each.

Underground Waterfall.name: Underground Waterfall
Underground Waterfall.text:
G10. Underground WaterfallModerate 3

The sound of splashing water fills this cavern due to the 20-foot-tall waterfall coursing down the wall from the ceiling to the northwest. The water collects in a pool, near which a pair of bedrolls have been set up on the ground. Thick logs have been pulled into the cave to form a couple of barricades. Two tunnels exit this chamber to the east.

The small aquifer that runs above the caves comes through the ceiling here to form a gentle waterfall. The water collects in a pond in the northern part of the cave, which slowly drains into the earth. The bottom of the pool is lined with mossy rocks and is home to a tiny number of cave fish that are no more than an inch long.

Viro has commanded his most loyal armiger allies to set up a guard post in this room, thinking it's the only way to get to the cave in which he performs his ritual. Their bedrolls lie near the northern exit, far enough away from the splashing waterfall to stay dry, and a lit hooded lantern near them lights the area with 30 feet of bright light and 30 more feet of dim light. They have also dragged a few thick logs from the forest outside here to create a couple of makeshift but defensible barricades. Crossing through a square with one of these logs is difficult terrain, but a creature can use them to Take Cover. A 5-foot section of log has Hardness 5, 20 Hit Points, and a BT of 10, but they are damp enough not to be set easily alight. A broken section of log is no longer difficult terrain and can't be used to Take Cover.

G10. Underground WaterfallModerate 3
