@UUID[Actor.h8YPfZn2fpbzfKjo]{Insidiator} @UUID[Actor.ezqASW0IwBFMaj8X]{Novice Hellknight Armiger} @UUID[Actor.pbCshaUuQur2gxlu]{Elite Adjutant Hellknight Armiger}

Creatures: Viro left an experienced adjutant Hellknight armiger in charge of the room's defense, along with a novice armiger and a conjured insidiator. The two Hellknights are behind the northern barricades when the PCs enter the room, but the insidiator attempts to hide in the southeast alcove to catch intruders unaware.

The sound of the waterfall is enough to cover most of the sounds of combat from other rooms, but if the armigers do hear something from area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03glowingcolum00]{G8}, they remain here, as part of their orders. However, the adjutant armiger will send the novice armiger to investigate any unusual noises coming from area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03ritualsite0000]{G11} after 1 round, and then follow 2 rounds later if the novice armiger doesn't report back. The insidiator doesn't leave this chamber.

Viro's allies don't begin a fight here until most of the PCs have entered the room. The adjutant armiger remains behind the barricade and fires several bolts before drawing his halberd and entering melee. The novice armiger charges out from behind cover to try to flank with the insidiator, who makes their first attacks from hiding if they're not noticed before that. The insidiator fights until destroyed, and the zealous novice armiger refuses to surrender. The adjutant armiger tries to retreat to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03ritualsite0000]{G11} if reduced to fewer than 6 Hit Points unless he knows that Viro Ahala has already been defeated, in which case he fights to the death.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.pyfidJm6uYMRoVxj]{Bedrolls}
Among the Hellknights' possessions by the bedrolls is a silver chunk and a pouch containing 15 gp.

Hidden Ledge.name: Hidden Ledge
Hidden Ledge.text:
G9. Hidden Ledge

This chamber dead-ends in a pile of fallen rubble where perhaps a tunnel once lead south. A curving passage leads west and large curtains of moss hang down from various spots on the cave ceiling.

The tunnel to the south used to lead to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03rockfallunde00]{G6}, but it collapsed long ago and is now impassable. The rubble has been compacted by decades of the weight of the hillside pressing down on it.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] while Searching the room notices that one of the curtains of moss hanging down from the ceiling conceals a small passageway going north. This hole is about 4 feet high and 5 feet wide and is about 10 feet from the ground. A successful @Check[athletics|dc:14|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] check is required to Climb the wall under it, and the passage is treated as difficult terrain for Medium creatures, while Large creatures will need to Squeeze through. However, this tunnel leads to a ledge in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03ritualsite0000]{G11} that might allow the PCs to get the drop on Viro, provided they don't make too much noise.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.NPYCcW1dGu1FYrmQ]{Remove Moss Curtain}

Glowing Column.name: Glowing Column
Glowing Column.text:
G8. Glowing ColumnLow 3

A slightly glowing stone column connecting floor to ceiling is the only notable feature of this irregular-shaped chamber. The surface of the column is rough and full of millions of small divots, like pumice. Several alcoves in the walls have a similar texture. Tunnels lead west, east, and south.

The column here has absorbed some of the potential magic power from deeper in the cave and so gives off a faint, eerie glow, casting the room into dim light. Every so often, a flicker of this energy moves from one of the indentations in the stone to another, appearing as a translucent, glowing worm. When this occurs, the squares adjacent to the pillar become bright light for 1 round.

G8. Glowing ColumnLow 3

@UUID[Actor.98FbLLgDdUCrE5F9]{Orts (2)} @UUID[Actor.98cjcIgQQdWq3u2L]{Adjutant Hellknight Armiger}

Light of the Glow Worms: In a combat encounter, roll @Check[type:flat|dc:15] at the start of each round. On a success, a glow worm appears and the DC of the next flat check increases by 1. On a failure, reduce the DC of the next flat check by 1. A PC can attempt @Check[arcana|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[nature|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge about the column, learning of this strange property. A PC adjacent to the column can then Interact with it and attempt @Check[arcana|dc:15] or @Check[nature|dc:15], coaxing forth a glowing worm with a success; on a critical success, a glowing worm remains on the surface of the pillar for 1 minute, instead of 1 round.

Creatures: Though the magic of the column is fairly inconsequential, one of Viro's Hellknight armiger allies became convinced that the stone harbors a deeper secret. She has been studying the column for several days, trying to discover more about the stone's magical properties, but has yet to be successful. Recently, she borrowed a conjured pair of orts to test whether their fiendish forms could affect the light in some way. She has been ordering them to interact in all manner of ways with the column, from biting it to standing with a hand on it while she strikes the other side. These experiments have yielded no results, but the Hellknight armiger is determined to uncover the nonexistent truth. This focus means that she doesn't notice the PCs in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03ancientgrave00]{G7}, unless they're fighting the Hellknights from area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03rockfallunde00]{G6} there.

The Hellknight armiger orders the orts to fight until they are destroyed, which they mindlessly do. If she is reduced to 5 or fewer Hit Points, she tries to retreat to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03undergroundw00]{G10l} to get help and will surrender if cornered.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.MYte2cU4NbqTqD48]{Large Sack}
The curious Hellknight armiger collected precious stones and odd natural minerals she found in the cave into a large sack, worth a total of 60 gp.

Ancient Grave.name: Ancient Grave
Ancient Grave.text:
G7. Ancient Grave

Passageways lead southeast, southwest, and north from this bean-shaped cavern. The floor here is mostly smooth stone, with the exception of a patch of uneven ground in which a humanoid skeleton is embedded. One bony arm reaches up toward the ceiling, as if calling for aid.

Centuries ago, when Kellids occupied most of the land that would become Isger, these caves were near a popular hunting ground. One day after a torrential downpour, a Kellid ranger fell through an unexpected sinkhole into this chamber. This Kellid died here, reaching for help that would not come, and their bones were partially preserved by the stone. A PC who spends 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:18] or @Check[archaeology-lore|dc:16] check can determine the skeleton's broken legs are the result of a fall. The sinkhole has since been sealed by time and shifting earth, but a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:22] or @Check[survival|dc:20] check while examining the ceiling can see the barest hint of what was once a hole leading to the surface.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.r4TQIFjK1L8kCqe5]{Skeleton}
A PC who examines the skeleton also finds a quiver that ironically holds two climbing bolts.

Rockfall.name: Rockfall
Rockfall.text:
G6. RockfallModerate 3

A possible tunnel collapse filled the eastern section of this wide cave with tightly packed rubble. A pair of bedrolls have been placed on the ground along the northern wall.

Decades ago, there was a tunnel leading between this cave and area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03hiddenledge000]{G9}, but it collapsed. The rubble has settled in for so long, it would take months of work with heavy picks and shovels to excavate the passage.

The Hellknights here have a hooded lantern lit by the bedrolls. The space within 30 feet of it is in bright light, with dim light for an additional 30 feet.

G6. RockfallModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.ezqASW0IwBFMaj8X]{Novice Hellknight Armiger} @UUID[Actor.98cjcIgQQdWq3u2L]{Adjutant Hellknight Armigers (2)}

Creatures: The bedrolls belong to the Hellknight armigers Viro has stationed here to monitor the basilisk in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03basilisklair00]{G4}. All of them believe Viro is a full Hellknight who bravely vanquished his attackers during the tactical retreat from Breachill. At least two of the armigers are on watch at all times, but when the PCs arrive, they are all awake and in their armor. If the PCs spend 10 minutes examining the skeleton in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03ancientgrave00]{G7}, there's a 50% chance that one of the armigers here spots them and initiates a fight.

The armigers fervently engage in battle, attempting to flank the toughest PC and bring them down before focusing on the others. However, if a different PC is easily hitting one of them, that Hellknight turns their attention to this PC. The adjutant armigers fight to the death, but the novice armiger tries to flee if reduced to 4 or fewer Hit Points. If the only avenue of escape is through area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03basilisklair00]{G4}, the novice surrenders instead.

Natural Steps.name: Natural Steps
Natural Steps.text:
G5. Natural Steps

This tunnel opens up to the west, where a set of natural stone steps have been carved out by millennia of erosion. The occasional drop of water from the ceiling makes these steps slightly damp. A passageway leads north.

Each of the stone steps to the west is about 6 feet tall and, due to their slipperiness, requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:18|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] check to Climb. The tunnel to the north narrows as it enters area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03ancientgrave00]{G7}, but not so much that Medium creatures need to Squeeze through. The water dripping from the ceiling is from a natural aquifer that runs north through the rock to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03undergroundw00]{G10}, creating the waterfall there. In time, the water will erode the stone away enough to turn these steps into a new waterfall.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.cLYC1ouCUI0jG3WM]{Glint}
A small glint from the top of the chamber is noticeable with a successful @Check[perception|dc:18] check. A PC who climbs up to examine it finds a shining symbol.

Basilisk Lair.name: Basilisk Lair
Basilisk Lair.text:
G4. Basilisk LairModerate 3

A pile of nearly equally sized rocks have been piled neatly in the northern end of this cavern. The southern part of this chamber holds a small alcove that is covered with thick moss. The shattered remains of a stone statue of an armored figure lies scattered in the center of the floor.

The body here is one of the Hellknight armigers Viro brought with him, petrified and killed by the basilisk that resides in this cave.

G4. Basilisk LairModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.zmC4L1mkGfyUvBFu]{Basilisk}

Creatures: A singular basilisk feasts on whatever prey has the misfortune to enter this cavern. The ornery creature wants only to be left alone and doesn't follow enemies who leave their lair.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.3lHMo4bP1cAM1dLh]{Lair}
If the PCs defeat the basilisk, they find a crying angel pendant and a bejeweled helmet worth 30 gp.

Intersection.name: Intersection
Intersection.text:
G3. Intersection

Four tunnels lead off in all directions to and from this roughly circular cavern. The northeastern tunnel is a bit wider than the other three.

A PC who inspects the four tunnels and succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:20] or @Check[survival|dc:18] check notices that the southern, western, and northeastern tunnels have seen a lot more foot traffic in the past week. While there is some disturbed dirt and stones in the southeastern tunnel, they indicate that two people entered the tunnel but only one returned. On a critical success, the PC also spots a bit of dried blood smeared on the cave wall near this end of the southeastern tunnel in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03basilisklair00]{G4}; two of Viro's armigers explored that tunnel, which leads to a basilisk's lair. One was killed and the other barely escaped to tell the tale. The basilisk wasn't threatened enough to hunt down its fleeing prey and the armigers avoid that chamber.

Main Cave.name: Main Cave
Main Cave.text:
G2. Main CaveLow 3

Once past the low cave entrance, the chamber opens up, stretching to the north and east, with alcoves in either direction. The rough ceiling is little more than 10 feet high, though it rises up a few more feet at the eastern end of the cave. The old remnants of a makeshift camp can be seen to the east.

When Brakknap's tribe fled from their pursuers, they hid mostly in this part of the caves. The northern alcove contains a ring of stones that surrounded a fire years ago, apparently not having been disturbed in all that time. There are a few pieces of carved wood caked in moss near the fire pit, indistinguishable trinkets left behind by the goblins who sheltered here.

To the east, a pile of rocks blocks an obvious tunnel that leads deeper into the caves. This blockade was placed here by the cave's current residents (see area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03basilisklair00]{G4}), having been ordered to block the way by Viro. The stones aren't packed very tightly, and the PCs can spend 30 minutes clearing away the stones enough to access the tunnel. For each PC who succeeds at @Check[athletics|dc:22] check while doing so, this time is reduced by 5 minutes.

G2. Main CaveLow 3

@UUID[Actor.h8YPfZn2fpbzfKjo]{Insidiators (3)}

Creatures: A trio of conjured insidiators lurks in the room's northern alcove, waiting for any intruders. They have been ordered to attack anyone who enters the cave from outside until told otherwise by Viro. The devils fight until killed but they don't chase fleeing enemies, instead retreating to the eastern alcove where it's difficult to see them from the cave entrance.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.Ik4nqUVcVzTI3Ske]{Remove Rubble}

Cave Entrance.name: Cave Entrance
Cave Entrance.text:
G1. Cave Entrance

A small hill rises here deep within the Chitterwood. At certain angles, the trees atop it look like the antlers of a mighty stag, but the brush at the base of the trees is black and gnarled, as if existing purely out of spite. Slightly hidden behind a tall tree is a small cave leading into the hillside.

The cave entrance is easy to find, especially with Brakknap's directions, but the tree does a good job of hiding it from the view of anyone not paying close attention. The cave entrance is small enough that Medium and larger creatures need to duck their heads to pass through; this counts as difficult terrain during a combat encounter.

Stagfall Caves.name: Stagfall Caves
Stagfall Caves.text:
G. Stagfall Caves

Once Viro Ahala began exploring the Chitterwood to find a place suitable for his ritual, he was slowly drawn to the tunnels the Thorngrip goblins named Stagfall Caves. Deeper in the caves than any goblin had explored is a natural nexus of magical power with the potential to overcharge Viro's ritual and grant him the revenge he's seeking. He, along with a coterie of Hellknight armigers who also fled Breachill and a handful of conjured devils, has explored most of the subterranean tunnels. They established a few defensive areas to protect Viro as he works toward completing the ritual in the caves' rearmost chamber. If the PCs don't find and stop him, he'll succeed in a matter of days (though the exact timing is left vague to let the PCs proceed at their own pace).

The hillside that contains Stagfall Caves is a day's travel through the forest southeast of Thorngrip. The journey is relatively uneventful, but the closer the party gets to the cave entrance, the more they get the sense that something isn't right. There are fewer sightings and sounds of wild animals in the underbrush and the tree branches overhead, as if they're instinctively avoiding the area. A PC who succeeds at @Check[nature|dc:20] or @Check[survival|dc:20] checkspots strange patterns in the bark of trees and clumps of moss close to the caves that resemble screaming, tortured faces; this PC knows that for the trees to have grown that way, it would have taken decades if not centuries, so whatever is happening with Viro's ritual seems to be warping the natural world.

The interior of the cave is in darkness except where noted, and most ceilings are 15 to 20 feet high. The PCs can use any of the caverns they clear out as places to camp if needed, but they can also retreat to outside the cave. The conjured devils are under strict orders to protect the caves, so they don't chase anyone past the cave entrance. The Hellknights, on the other hand, aren't bound by any such verbal loopholes. They will follow any retreating PCs after first tending to their own wounds. If the PCs cause any major ruckus, the Hellknights might even begin searching the caves for the PCs, potentially leaving their posts.

Brakknap's Revelation.name: Brakknap's Revelation
Brakknap's Revelation.text:
Brakknap's Revelation

Once the PCs have investigated the three sites above and dealt with the corrupted magic caused by Viro's ritual, they can return to Brakknap. He seems to know that they've completed their mission and asks to see the crystal he gave them.

Brakknap looks serious as he holds the leather strap and peers at the crystal at the end of it. He stares for a moment and then his eyes go wide. With a mixture of anger and horror he says, “The caves. The hell-human Viro is in the caves.” He realizes that he's speaking vaguely and composes himself. “Before the founding of Thorngrip, my tribe was hunted by humans at the end of the Goblinblood Wars. We hid in a small series of caves near here, but we knew they would not keep us safe forever. My grandmother used the power of the woods to transform into a mighty stag and lead the humans away. She did not survive, but her sacrifice was not in vain. The survivors found this tree and the ancestors helped me raise the wall of thorns around it. We have been safe since then.”

The older goblin takes a deep breath, voice trembling with anger. “We named those caves Stagfall in honor of my grandmother. And now this hell-human Viro is using them for his wicked purposes! This cannot stand!”

With the magic of the eastern Chitterwood returning to normal, the ancestor spirits were able to pinpoint Viro Ahala's location as being within the nearby Stagfall Caves. They tell Brakknap that the Hellknight has discovered tunnels that lead deeper than any goblins have explored and warn that he has many allies. Brakknap passes this information on to the PCs, apologizing that the ancestors can't be more specific. He then hands the crystal pendant back to the PCs, noting that it “still has much power within it.”

Brakknap can give the PCs directions to the caves and even describe the first few chambers (areas @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03caveentrance00]{G1}-@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03intersection00]{G3}), but has no other guidance to give. If the PCs need to rest before leaving Thorngrip again, they can.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.Fp3tHvqvFls5ylA0]{Brakknap's Gift}
In addition to the crystal, Brakknap gifts the PCs a runestone with a +1 striking rune carved into it that is “from the town elders.”

Moss Pond.name: Moss Pond
Moss Pond.text:
Moss PondModerate 3

Moss Pond is less than an hour's walk west of Thorngrip. Use the Moss Pond map for this encounter. When the PCs approach, read or paraphrase the following.

The normal undergrowth of the forest gives way to a large patch of moss a few dozen feet in diameter. The moss appears to be several inches thick on the ground, with patches of various shades of green. The moss undulates slightly as if floating on water, but there is no water to be seen.

Unlike many of the other unusual phenomena in the Chitterwood—which are ancient and timeless in the eyes of the local goblinoids—Moss Pond is a relatively recent addition. With the Plane of Wood's reconnection to the cosmos, this once-normal, albeit large, patch of moss became a faint conduit to that elemental plane. The occasional movement across the surface of the moss experienced by the local goblins was caused by energy from the Plane of Wood seeping through to the mortal Universe; this energy is normally harmless. As Viro Ahala's ritual attempts to draw power from Hell, other planar breaches in the forest are reacting, becoming more unstable by the moment.

Moss PondModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.MwXf1zh7jocD8QvB]{Spore Spears} @UUID[Actor.14e1ZdGQ3qfvsWRV]{Moss Sloths (2)}

Hazard: Unstable planar energy is causing sudden growth and subsequent decay within the moss, creating dangerous “spears” of plant matter. Drawn to other living creatures, these spears of moss strike out at nearly anything that comes near the pond. A creature who takes poison damage from a spore spear Strike has a brief vision of endless burning forests, an overlapping of landscapes from the Plane of Wood and Hell.

Creatures: As the moss pond trap rolls initiative, its connection to the Plane of Wood becomes briefly stable enough to allow creatures to pass through, though the trip is one-way. Two moss sloths, mobile colonies of moss growing on wooden simulacra of sloths, emerge in the center of the moss. Though moss sloths are usually docile, these are confused and disoriented by the planar travel, and they immediately attack the PCs, fighting until destroyed. Once destroyed, they are absorbed into the moss pond.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.nK3xtuq0OnRzaNJn]{Remains}
Strangely, there's a smuggler's padlock left behind in the remains of a moss sloth.

Development: When the spore spears trap has been disabled, the crystal Brakknap gave the PCs changes to a bright green.

Little Tree.name: Little Tree
Little Tree.text:
Little TreeModerate 3

Little Tree is approximately a 30-minute walk southeast of Thorngrip and uses the Little Tree map. When the PCs approach, read or paraphrase the following.

A sapling stands on a little hill, separate from the other trees. Though it's small, the green of its leaves are lush and vibrant even in the autumn weather. An aura of peace and calm radiates from the little tree.

Little Tree is an unusual conduit of primal magic, a rare phenomenon that only appears deep within the oldest forests of Golarion. It represents the eternal youth of spring and while it's a living thing, it never ages, gets sick, nor needs normal photosynthesis. However, when Viro Ahala began his ritual, this primal energy became warped, and all the potential growth Little Tree should have experienced over the decades has been inverted and projected outward.

Little TreeModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.YwrmoQa0itGI3MgO]{Littler Beasts} @UUID[Actor.1HEAvAF52vcFsElV]{Grizzly Bear}

Hazard: The corruption of Viro's ritual has caused Little Tree's energies to shrink nearby creatures instead of rejuvenating itself. A creature shrunken down by this trap also feels resentment and jealousy, a reflection of the emotions burning in Viro's heart.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.s2hSsdGnlrznJgxh]{Toggle Tree Size}

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.Pgp9NujcryQ73Q5m]{Roots}
After disabling the hazard, the roots of Little Tree part to reveal a type I spacious pouch and several rare mushrooms worth a total of 10 gp.

Development: When the trap has been disabled, the crystal Brakknap gave the PCs glows warmly from within.

The Hungry Hole.name: The Hungry Hole
The Hungry Hole.text:
The Hungry Hole Moderate 3

The Hungry Hole is less than an hour's walk south of Thorngrip. When the PCs approach, read or paraphrase the following.

This clearing is devoid of all foliage in an almost perfect circle 40 feet in diameter. Not even the tiniest blade of grass can be spotted in the dirt around a mundane-looking hole in the center of the clearing. The branches of the surrounding trees don't encroach the space, creating a kind of tunnel from the ground to the sky. The edges of the hole shift and undulate like a ravenous mouth, daring anyone to approach.

The Hungry Hole is a kind of bottomless pit created centuries ago when a Chitterwood goblin wizard experimented with the extradimensional magic of a spacious pouch and had a predictable accident. Throughout the years, other goblins have thrown random objects within the pit; these all still exist somewhere within the Hungry Hole, but living things tossed (or that have fallen) into the pit reappeared in this clearing after a few hours… until Viro Ahala began corrupting the Chitterwood with his ritual. Now, the Hungry Hole is quite dangerous.

For this encounter, you can use any Flip-Mat depicting a forest.

The Hungry HoleModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.b6iTiMgLhwkhGzqm]{Ravenous Pit}

Hazard: The twisted energy emanating from Viro's ritual has turned the Hungry Hole into a ravenous pit that tries to swallow the PCs whole if they approach. Any PC swallowed by the pit can faintly hear the laughter of devils and the screams of the damned, as if the extradimensional space within the trap neighbors Hell.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.s948thsJbCPDUGZZ]{Pit}
After the hazard is disabled, the pit spits up a pair of low-grade alloy orbs and 10 gp.

Development: When the ravenous pit trap has been disabled, the inside of the crystal Brakknap gave the PCs becomes slightly less cloudy.

Triangulating the Ritual.name: Triangulating the Ritual
Triangulating the Ritual.text:
Triangulating the Ritual

Brakknap describes the three locations the PCs need to visit and gives clear enough directions that the PCs should be able to find them without issue. The PCs can visit these three locations in any order and can return to Thorngrip at any point they need to rest. They should feel a sense of urgency to find Viro Ahala and stop his ritual but, for the moment, they don't have a hard deadline. If the PCs ask Brakknap for any information about the locations, he will tell them the following.

The Hungry Hole: “No goblin knows who dug the Hungry Hole or even how deep it is, but we do know that it can't be filled, no matter how much we throw into it. I've heard tales of goblins falling into the hole and coming out on the other side of the world. Those are just stories to keep young goblins away. Probably. The ancestors tell me, though, that it's better to stay away from the edge.”

Little Tree: “For as long as I have been alive, Little Tree has been little. It doesn't grow but it hasn't died either. From what we understand about nature, it should be starved for sunlight or water by the other, bigger trees, but it just isn't. The ancestors believe it's fed by magic, and many find Little Tree's presence very soothing.”

Moss Pond: “We call it a pond but it's just a large patch of moss that sometimes ripples like water. You can walk across it if you want, it isn't dangerous. You won't even sink! Sometimes, children will take turns lying on the pond to feel the moss move under them. The ancestors say that it's a connection to the very essence of the Chitterwood, but they can't explain it any more than that.”

The Trust of Goblins.name: The Trust of Goblins
The Trust of Goblins.text:
The Trust of Goblins

Once the PCs have taken care of the Isgeri Slayers, they're met by Brakknap outside of Thorngrip, who ushers them inside. The resident goblins now look at them with admiration and respect as they pass through the streets. Brakknap trusts the PCs enough to reveal some information to them, but if the PCs would like to rest or shop first, he allows them to do so as described in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03downtimeinth00]{Downtime in Thorngrip}.

When the PCs are ready to continue, read or paraphrase the following.

The goblin oracle is waiting at the ancestor shrine and gives a brief smile before getting down to business. “The spirits are pleased that you are here on this day. This Viro Ahala you are searching for is doing something within our wood that has them worried, and we think you can stop it. However, the power he's tapping into has obscured him from our ancestors' sight.” His forehead crinkles a moment in thought. “This veil is not impenetrable. With your help, we can discover where the hell-human is performing his ritual.

“There are three sites of subtle power nearby within the Chitterwood. The ancestors have told me that Viro's ritual has disturbed these places, making them more dangerous to approach than normal. Take this talisman to those sites. It will react to the changes in energy and, after being exposed to all three, it will help me to see Viro's location.” Brakknap holds out a cloudy crystal on a leather cord. “I don't know what you'll find at these sites, but be ready for anything.”

Reward: @UUID[Actor.wiG1HetEkv3u39QC]{Brakknap's Crystal}
For gaining Brakknap's trust, award the PCs 30 XP.

Hunting Party.name: Hunting Party
Hunting Party.text:
Hunting PartyModerate 3

The other two Isgeri Slayers ranged out a few miles west of their camp but were only a little successful, bagging two small rabbits. They return approximately 10 minutes after the PCs deal with the drunken slayers, and aren't expecting to run into trouble. A PC who succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:14] check hears them coming, giving the PCs a few moments to prepare from their arrival if they haven't already. A PC can hide around the camp with a successful @Check[stealth|dc:18|traits:skill,secret,action:hide|name:Hide] check, gaining a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative. Alternatively, a PC can try to impersonate one of the drunken slayers by attempting @Check[deception|dc:18|traits:action:impersonate,concentrate,exploration,manipulate,secret|name:Impersonate] check to catch the returning slayers off-guard.

Hunting PartyModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.493zuqBI7kftOn8M]{Trained Wolf} @UUID[Actor.XonQycAGeNI4pGoZ]{Isgeri Slayers (2)}

Creatures: The two returning Isgeri Slayers have their hunting wolf with them. This trained animal reacts to any violence against the slayers with growls and bites. The wolf fights until killed, but each of the slayers runs away, if possible, when reduced to 4 or fewer Hit Points.

As with the drunken slayers, the PCs don't necessarily need to fight if they don't want to. Intimidating or scaring off these slayers is also an option, though it's more difficult as they aren't inebriated. If the PCs have time to prepare, let them formulate a plan and attempt up to three skill checks using any combination of @Check[deception|dc:20], @Check[intimidation|dc:20], and @Check[performance|dc:20]. If they succeed at two of these skill checks, the remaining slayers and their wolf leave the Chitterwood; a critical success lowers the DC of the next check by 1. If the PCs critically fail a single check or fail two of these checks, the slayers attack without fear. If a PC attempts a Diplomacy check, they take a –1 circumstance penalty as the slayers are not interested in changing their ways.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.xuo9T5fgWiLl7yBq]{Tent}
In one of the tents is a pack with two lesser healing potions and a pouch of stolen trinkets worth 20 gp.

Reward: If the PCs frighten off the Isgeri Slayers and their wolf, award them XP as if they had defeated them in combat.

Development: Any fleeing Isgeri Slayers head northeast out of the Chitterwood. If the PCs capture any slayers alive, Zagnub appears from behind a nearby tree to thank the PCs and relieve them of the burden of having to deal with unconscious humans. They assure the PCs that the slayers won't be harmed and though they're telling the truth, their smile when saying it is slightly predatory. The PCs can haul unconscious slayers out of Thorngrip territory if they wish, though such a task is a bit time-consuming. If the PCs kill any Isgeri Slayers after the fight is over, they lose 1 Reputation Point.

Slayer Camp.name: Slayer Camp
Slayer Camp.text:
Slayer CampLow 3

Five hastily erected tents surround a campfire in this small clearing. A handful of empty whiskey bottles have been pushed bottleneck-first into the dirt near the fire. A couple of logs have been pulled close to the tents to serve as makeshift chairs.

While these Isgeri Slayers have been in the Chitterwood before, they aren't the most competent campers, largely due to their excessive drinking. The tents would likely collapse in a strong wind, but serve their purpose for the Slayers.

Slayer CampLow 3

@UUID[Actor.jpHegZfy6f6GxZtv]{Drunken Isgeri Slayers (3)}

Creatures: Two of the Isgeri Slayers and their trained wolf ranged out into the woods to hunt for food while the remaining three stayed behind and continued to drink. These three are drunk enough that the PCs can easily creep up toward the camp and take them by surprise, giving the PCs a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative. Each of the drunken slayers flees, if possible, when reduced to 6 or fewer Hit Points.

However, the PCs don't have to attack the slayers. The PCs can attempt up to three DC 17 skill checks using any combination of @Check[deception|dc:17], @Check[intimidation|dc:17], and @Check[performance|dc:17] to scare the slayers into leaving. If they succeed at two of these skill checks, they frighten the three drunken slayers off; a critical success lowers the DC of the next check by 1. If the PCs critically fail a single check or fail two of these checks, the drunken slayers grab their weapons and attack. An attempted Diplomacy check automatically fails against the inebriated slayers, who are too out of it to consider listening to reason, and counts against one of the three checks.

Reward: If the PCs frighten off the drunken Isgeri Slayers, award them XP as if they had defeated them in combat.

Development: A PC who takes a few moments to examine the camp notices that two of the tents are devoid of any weapons or armor, meaning their occupants must have taken these items with them. The PCs have only 10 minutes before the hunting party returns. If the PCs have captured a drunken slayer alive and succeed at @Check[diplomacy|dc:15] or @Check[intimidation|dc:15] check, the slayer warns them about the trained wolf.

The Isgeri Slayers.name: The Isgeri Slayers
The Isgeri Slayers.text:
The Isgeri Slayers

The hatred stoked by the Goblinblood Wars two decades ago has not fully dissipated in Isger. Some veterans of that war formed an unsanctioned group of rangers and foresters calling themselves the Isgeri Slayers. The sole purpose of this loose affiliation is to hunt down and kill all goblinoids within the country's borders. The Isgeri Slayers spend days and sometimes weeks within the Chitterwood, hunting down goblins for sport and as an outlet for their rage.

Most goblins manage to escape these bigoted hunters, and more than a few larger tribes have turned the tables on them deep in the woods. Despite a relatively high rate of fatal “accidents” during these hunting trips and the disdain of the general public, the Isgeri Slayers have maintained a somewhat steady membership, and new recruits are usually indoctrinated by older members with propaganda about the vileness and cruelty of goblinkind, continuing the cycle of enmity. A PC who succeeds at @Check[society|dc:16] check is familiar with the Isgeri Slayers and might even have had a run-in with them in the past if they are a goblin or hobgoblin who is from Isger.

A group of Isgeri Slayers spent the past few days in the Chitterwood on one of their “weekend hunts” and got close enough to Thorngrip to concern the residents. Some members of this particular cadre are less dedicated to killing than the others and treat the trip more like a vacation and an excuse to indulge in alcohol. The PCs can attempt @Check[perception|dc:16] or @Check[survival|dc:16] check to locate the slayers; if the PCs fail this check, they don't catch the drunken slayers by surprise and don't receive the bonus to their initiative.

Thorngrip Pariahs.name: Thorngrip Pariahs
Thorngrip Pariahs.text:
Thorngrip Pariahs

On the off chance that the PCs didn't join with the Looksee Party to enter Thorngrip as friends, they have to prove they are worthy of the goblins' help before being allowed inside. If they follow the goblin scouts to the thorn wall, Zagnub yells at them to go away before passing through the thorns. It's unlikely the PCs will be able to find their own way into the town (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03welcometotho00#thorngrip]{Thorngrip} sidebar), and after some time trying, Brakknap appears at the wall to confront the PCs. He tells them bluntly that if they wish to gain the town's trust, they need to deal with the Isgeri Slayers out in the forest. The PCs will get a chance to tell Brakknap their story (and attempt to improve his attitude) once they do so.

Downtime in Thorngrip.name: Downtime in Thorngrip
Downtime in Thorngrip.text:
Downtime in Thorngrip

Though it's a small town, Thorngrip has many of the amenities that one can find in any large city. The goblin residents, however, tend not to use the currency of the land, instead preferring to barter for goods and services. If the PCs want to buy items, they can procure common and magical items up to level 3 and alchemical consumables and talismans up to level 4. A PC receives the standard value for selling an item and can easily trade for an equivalent amount of items. For any difference in value, the goblin merchants don't pay the PCs gold; instead, they give them physical items such as small gems or rare herbs that can later be sold or traded in a larger city for their correct value. If willing, a PC can also take an appropriate amount of food and drink as part of a trade. Instead of receiving currency, a PC who takes some downtime to Earn an Income in Thorngrip is instead paid in goods and services.

The artisans of Thorngrip include Ghugg (gruff male goblin smith 1), who sells weapons and armor with a goblin flair; Mirdona (inquisitive female goblin alchemist 1), who brews alchemical elixirs and the occasional bomb; Ikko (fussy nonbinary goblin magician 1), who fashions talismans from natural materials and carves runes into petrified bark; and Duz (experimental female goblin chef 1), who can pickle just about anything.

Thorngrip has no inns, as they don't expect to have visitors, but there's one house that remains empty for new goblin arrivals to use while they build more permanent abodes. Brakknap allows the PCs to use this house, which is close to the shrine, when they need to rest. If his attitude is helpful, Brakknap will cast a 1st-rank heal on any PCs who are below half their HP before they rest, but he doesn't have any magic to help with curses, diseases, and poisons.

Finally, if the PCs spend downtime to Craft or Retrain, they are allowed to use facilities within Thorngrip to do so at no charge. However, until they help out with the Isgeri Slayers, Brakknap gives them disappointed looks if they dawdle in town for more than a day.

Welcome to Thorngrip.name: Welcome to Thorngrip
Welcome to Thorngrip.text:
Welcome to Thorngrip

Assuming the PCs follow the Looksee Party, they travel through the woods for almost an hour. The goblins seem to be able to easily pick their way through the underbrush, occasionally climbing partially up a tree to swing from one branch to another. If the PCs lag a little behind, Zagnub stops the party and waits for them to catch up, eagerly waving them forward. Each PC can attempt @Check[athletics|dc:17], @Check[nature|dc:17], or @Check[survival|dc:17] check; if at least half of the party succeeds, they keep good time with the Looksee Party and impress Zagnub. They eventually reach an imposing wall of thorns. Read or paraphrase the following.

A massive sequoia rises behind a curving wall of seemingly impenetrable thorns. With practiced confidence, Zagnub walks up to a section of the wall that seems no different from the rest of it, reaches in, and pulls on a branch. The thorns and vines part into a small hole in the wall. The other goblins quickly pile inside, with Zagnub last. The goblin scout gestures to follow with a wide smile that shows every one of their many pointed teeth.

On the other side of the thorn wall is a bustling goblin town centered around the sequoia. Most of the buildings are small, wooden huts with thatched roofs, and a few of them have been built attached to the trunk of the large tree, with ladders and ramps leading up to them. This line of houses reaches no higher than the top of the thorn wall, making them difficult to spot from outside the village.

Several residents greet the returning Looksee Party, and some of the younger goblins stop to stare at the newcomers. Their parents gently guide them away, a few with worried looks on their own faces. “Welcome to Thorngrip,” says Zagnub.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.ZKmG83GSYyN69xVq]{Thorngrip}

Thorngrip

The story of how Brakknap established this town a few decades ago can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole00]{Here}.

ThorngripSettlement 3

  • Town
  • Goblin

Goblin haven nestled within the Chitterwood.

Government council of elders (spirit-chosen leaders)

Population 529 (100% goblins)

Languages Common, Goblin

Religions ancestor worship, goblin animism

Threats Isgeri Slayers, wild creatures of the Chitterwood

Hidden from View Thorngrip is surrounded by a wall of thorns that stands over a dozen feet high. The residents know the secret ways through this wall, but an outsider must succeed at @Check[perception|dc:29] check to find them. Most wildlife tends to ignore the wall.

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole00]{Brakknap} (haunted male goblin oracle 4) Thorngrip's founder and trusted advisor

Neemi (wise female goblin leader 2) Thorngrip's longest-serving council elder

Zagnub (cheerful nonbinary goblin scout 2) Looksee Party leader

Zagnub ushers the PCs through the town toward the base of the sequoia, where a large shrine has been carved into the wood. Many goblin faces have been expertly painted across the shrine with a dark ink or stain. An older goblin kneels at the shrine, offering muttered devotions, though he rises when Zagnub clears their throat. When he turns to face the PCs, they see a flash of blue light in his eyes and, for just a second, the impression that several spectral goblins are standing behind him. The goblin murmurs, “I see Zagnub has made some new longshanks friends. Greetings. I am Brakknap.”

Brakknap (haunted male goblin oracle 4) is Thorngrip's founder and often speaks with the spirits of goblins past to help guide the town. Brakknap has a long and troubled history that can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole00]{Here}, but despite the pain some humans have inflicted on him, he would like to see the two ancestries living in harmony. The goblin ancestor spirits have been perturbed lately by what Viro Ahala has been doing in the Chitterwood, but Brakknap believes that Thorngrip doesn't have the strength to stop him alone, so he's asked Zagnub's Looksee Parties to be watchful for anyone else who might be able to help. However, Brakknap isn't about to trust the PCs without good reason. Luckily for the PCs, tales of some of the work they've been doing around Isger has reached Thorngrip.

Before he gives them any information, Brakknap wants to hear all about the PCs from their mouths; he asks them who they are and their reasons for being in the Chitterwood. If any of the PCs are goblins or hobgoblins, Brakknap asks them about their histories and their opinions about the rest of the party, especially any humans. He is pleased to listen to any accounts of goblins and humans working together toward a common goal. At the end of this conversation, one PC—likely the one who did the most talking—should attempt @Check[diplomacy|dc:18|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression] check to Make an Impression on Brakknap. If the PCs have at least 8 Reputation Points, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this check; if they have at least 12 Reputation Points, this bonus increases to +2. Brakknap's starting attitude is indifferent; if the PCs raise it to friendly or helpful, he allows them to rest or shop in Thorngrip before they head out to perform the task he gives them so they can earn Thorngrip's trust.

Regardless of the result of this check, read or paraphrase the following.

Brakknap appears to be listening to some unheard voices for a moment. He then nods solemnly. “The ancestors can help you find the one you seek, but you must understand that for us goblins of the Chitterwood, trust is not given lightly. Though Zagnub has vouched for you by bringing you here, I would ask you for a favor. Some of our scouts have watched other humans enter our territory whose motives are less worthy than yours. They are part of a group calling themselves the Isgeri Slayers, and they have made it their mission to finish what was started during the Goblinblood Wars.”

Brakknap looks pained, as if remembering something he would rather forget. “I don't care how you do it, but drive them off. The chances they will find Thorngrip are small, but I fear what would happen if they came across any goblins.”

If the PCs agree to help Thorngrip, Brakknap tells them that Zagnub will point them toward where these Isgeri Slayers were last seen. With some remorse, Brakknap also says that the PCs will not be allowed to step inside Thorngrip again until the Isgeri Slayers are gone. Proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03theisgerisla00]{The Isgeri Slayers} if the PCs are eager to get to the action, but if Brakknap is friendly or helpful, they can take some time to look around Thorngrip before they leave.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.bXmZAgKXUoEC7RtC]{Zagnub's Gift}
Zagnub has taken a liking to the PCs and gifts them an oil of potency.

Thorngrip Looksee Party.name: Thorngrip Looksee Party
Thorngrip Looksee Party.text:
Thorngrip Looksee Party

Once a week, the goblins of Thorngrip (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03welcometotho00#thorngrip]{Thorngrip}) put together a Looksee Party to scout around the town for a full day and determine whether there are any threats to their safety. In recent years, each Looksee Party has usually been led by Zagnub (cheerful nonbinary goblin scout 2), a trusted and well-liked member of the community. Zagnub enjoys the responsibility and keeps copious mental notes about what they see, hear, and smell. Recently, one of Zagnub's Looksee Parties spotted Viro and his entourage and reported it back to Thorngrip's ruling council. Since then, the goblins have fielded more Looksee Parties than normal, worried about these intruders. One such party observes the PCs as they make their way through the Chitterwood and waits to see what they do before confronting them.

When the PCs slay the last of the orts at the stump, they slowly begin to feel that they are being watched from the surrounding trees. A PC who succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:21] check notices at least six sets of red eyes peering at them from the tree line to the south. That PC has enough time to warn their allies before a tall goblin steps out from the underbrush, their hands spread wide and away from their weapons.

Though the tall goblin is smiling and deliberately unarmed, their razor-sharp teeth somewhat undercut their message of peace. “Relax, longshanks,” they say in accented Common. “If we wanted to kill you, we would've done so. I be Zagnub of the Thorngrip goblins.” They gesture toward the steaming piles of goo that were once devils. “Devils no friends of yours, yes?”

The PCs immediately get the impression that the answer to this question is the difference between fighting and friendship. This adventure assumes that the PCs answer in the positive and perhaps even tell Zagnub they are looking for more devils and their allies to slay; with a delighted chuckle, Zagnub gestures for the PCs to follow them.

If the PCs lie or attempt to intimidate the goblins, they lose 1 Reputation Point, and the goblins hiding in the trees fire a volley of arrows at them before Zagnub disappears back into the woods. Each PC takes @Damage[(2d6+4)[piercing]] damage (@Check[type:reflex|dc:18|traits:basic] save), and the goblins are unfriendly toward them. That said, the PCs can still Track the Looksee Party to Thorngrip and proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03thorngrippar00]{Thorngrip Pariahs}.

Devils on the Loose.name: Devils on the Loose
Devils on the Loose.text:
Devils on the LooseModerate 3

A petrified stump is the only remnant of what must have once been a towering tree. The brush around it has been cleared away, and several ritualistic candles and shards of crystal have been discarded by a crack in the stump that leads to a small underground hollow.

Approximately a week earlier, Viro Ahala and several other Hellknight armigers who survived the battle at Breachill found this stump and thought it a good place to practice the ritual. A PC who succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:18] or @Check[survival|dc:18] check discovers the presence of several sets of boot prints in the dirt, but they are unfortunately too obscured for the PC to deduce where the group went after moving about this space. If the PCs fear that they've missed their opportunity to thwart Viro, a PC who succeeds at @Check[arcana|dc:16], @Check[occultism|dc:16], or @Check[religion|dc:16] check discerns that the magical energy lingering near this stump is the result of a much smaller ritual.

The PCs enter this area from the northwest. Because of the tree cover, this area is cast in dim light during the day. Use the Ritual Stump map for this encounter.

Devils on the LooseModerate 3

@UUID[Actor.mLzZQTcloPNmEfr3]{Orts (3)} @UUID[Actor.kVtgAdZKNBC96s0W]{Elite Ort}

Creatures: Viro's practice ritual was successful and summoned a small group of drudge devils that Viro bound to this stump. He hopes that any havoc they cause will be enough of a distraction to keep anyone hunting him (including the Hellbreakers League) busy. One of the four orts was empowered by the ritual to be a little stronger than the others, and its enhanced presence bolsters the group. The orts emerge from the hollow under the stump when the PCs approach and fight until destroyed, as stipulated by Viro's orders.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.tYvvOore7OXKZAaj]{Hollow}
A PC who succeeds at @Check[perception|dc:16] check when examining the hollow under the stump finds an imposing shield that was left behind by one of Viro's followers as well as 30 gp worth of unused ritual supplies that were discarded when Viro obtained better quality materials.

Into the Chitterwood.name: Into the Chitterwood
Into the Chitterwood.text:
Into the Chitterwood

Despite many of the trees being cut or burned down along the outskirts in the aftermath of the Goblinblood Wars, the Chitterwood is still an imposing old-growth forest. Any signs of the central Isgeri farmlands are swallowed by the surrounding trees within only a few minutes after entering. The forest canopy overhead blocks much of the day's light. The sounds of wildlife can be heard all around: chirping birds, rustling underbrush, and snapping twigs as animals pass by.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.4szoYksOu0YbpyMu]{Chitterwood}

There are no roads into the Chitterwood, only a few sparse game trails widened by hunters and foresters that penetrate only a mile into the forest. The native goblin populations tend to keep to themselves, ranging only short distances from their caves and small villages to forage, which has very little impact on the surrounding terrain. As the PCs begin exploring the Chitterwood, either trying to find the spots where people mentioned seeing a figure in armor or searching for other signs of Viro, one of them should attempt @Check[survival|dc:20|traits:secret,concentrate,exploration,move,skill,action:track|name:Track] check to Track. On a success, after about an hour, that PC spots what could be heavy boot prints in the dirt; on a critical success, they can tell the tracks are about a week old. Following the prints leads them to a large stump that appears to have a few extinguished candle stubs near it. On a failure, the PCs stumble around the woods for a few hours and accidentally come across this same scene, but the devils by the stump gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative checks.

Devils of Chitterwood.name: Devils of Chitterwood
Devils of Chitterwood.text:
Chapter 3: Devils of Chitterwood

After investigating the Lucent Mission of the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys, the PCs have learned that the false Hellknight Viro Ahala is planning to conduct a ritual somewhere in the eastern Chitterwood that could spell big trouble for Isger. Unfortunately, they don't know his exact location, and time could be running short!

If the PCs haven't visited the four locations in central Isger that they've been asked to help out and still need more XP to reach level 3, they can aid those places now. There is no ticking clock for Viro's ritual, and gaining more Reputation Points could help the PCs leverage these new connections for more information. They can also return to Saringallow to rest, resupply, and ask for advice. If they do so, Rhokrag suggests they revisit areas near the Chitterwood (Stumpfield or Umok, for instance) to ask around if anyone has seen anything suspicious in the woods. This could be a chance for the PCs to gain Reputation Points in those towns if they haven't already (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02gainingreput03]{Here} and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02gainingreput02]{Here}).

To Gather Information about Viro's plot in Stumpfield or Umok, the PCs must succeed at @Check[diplomacy|dc:20] check. If they have at least 8 Reputation Points, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this check; if they have at least 12 Reputation Points, this bonus increases to +2. On a success, they pick up on rumors spread by local farmers and foresters of recently seeing “a figure clad in black armor” stalking through the woods. If a PC presses an eyewitness, they learn more details that confirm that the armor this figure wore is similar to the iconic Hellknight full plate. By following up on this lead, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Survival check to navigate the Chitterwood; if their Diplomacy check was a critical success, this bonus increases to +2.

Alternatively, the PCs can head directly to the Chitterwood after leaving the Lucent Mission to begin looking for signs of Viro. In such a case, proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03intothechitt00]{Into the Chitterwood}. If they haven't returned to Saringallow, the PCs will have a chance to buy or craft new items in Thorngrip.

Event: False Flag.name: Event: False Flag
Event: False Flag.text:
Event: False FlagModerate 4

The gala was supposed to conclude with Hedvend VI's announcement, but Ezio has a surprise planned—an attack by guards posing as Hellbreakers League revolutionaries! The attack is not only intended to cause chaos by killing important Elidirans and whipping up fury against the Hellbreakers, it's a distraction from Ezio's simultaneous murder of Hedvend himself.

Shortly before the attacks, Ezio's accomplice, Lefranek Meyal (zealous female human agent of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} 4), lures three guards to his side to be dominated and to recover the false Hellbreakers League flag she's prepared for the charade. Make a secret @Check[perception|dc:21|traits:secret,skill] check for each PC—on a success, the PC notices the guards left their posts, presumably to escort Hedvend to the party at last, giving them a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative roll when combat begins. On a critical success, the PC also notices the guards return without the steward; due to the suspicious behavior, the PC is quickened on the first round of combat, and can use the extra action to Interact to draw a weapon or other item.

Read or paraphrase the following.

The music comes to a sudden stop as a woman's harsh yell silences the party. “Enough! For too long have you and Hedvend been Cheliax's lapdog and neglected our beautiful Isger! We shall remove your devilish taint from our country! It's time for everyone here to die, in the name of the Hellbreakers League!” She waves an unfamiliar flag depicting a flaming sword piercing Asmodeus's red pentagram as her masked compatriots attack.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.8H2T2BAup3vuECUb]{Panicking Gala Crowd}

The stunning announcement ends the gala's festivities and concludes the chapter, continuing in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma]{Chapter 5}.

Event: No Thank You Bite.name: Event: No Thank You Bite
Event: No Thank You Bite.text:
Event: No Thank You Bite

One or more PCs notice a disgusted-looking servant, Otton Nettlebrush (disgruntled male halfling servant 0) in an imp costume furiously scrubbing a wall stained with debris from some food, the remains of which sit in a pile on the ground. If a PC asks, the servant tries to deflect their attention. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:17] or @Check[intimidation|dc:17] check to get more information from Otton learns that it was a caramelized garlic tart that Ezio threw against the wall in disgust after a single bite. If a PC asks Ezio, he sheepishly admits it and apologizes for the bad behavior. He says the cheese had clearly gone rancid but the truth is he reacted to the garlic in the dish, a clue to his true nature. Ezio then takes the opportunity to hobnob, granting the PCs he speaks with an additional social round with an NPC of their choice.

Event: Social “Foe” Pas.name: Event: Social “Foe” Pas
Event: Social “Foe” Pas.text:
Event: Social “Foe” PasLow 4

A cry cuts off in a gurgle as a velstrac lifts a human servant in an ort costume into the air by his throat. Spilled wine drips off an imperial-looking woman with an enraged expression. “I wore this dress to Aroden's wake!” she snarls. “It's worth more than your life, you miserable little worm!”

The hapless servant had the misfortune of spilling wine on Lady Kaltessa Iyis (mysterious female human priestess of Mammon 20), who has stopped at the party on her way to Cheliax. The PCs can attempt a @Check[society|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge to recognize her as a seemingly immortal noblewoman also known as the Widow Queen who resides in the Iron Rose manor among the Menador Mountains. A successful @Check[religion|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge reveals that she is a high priestess of the archdevil @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.sNjPI1iaS8Z43YJf]{Mammon}; on a critical success, they've heard rumors she's centuries old thanks to an infernal pact.

The PCs can attempt to save the servant's life by appealing to Kaltessa for mercy with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:21] or @Check[religion|dc:21] check or a @Check[intimidation|dc:23] check; on a success, Kaltessa decides the servant is not worth the trouble. If no PC succeeds, she's offended by the intrusion and has three imp attendants teach the meddling PCs a lesson.

Event: Social “Foe” PasLow 4

@UUID[Actor.hHHorEXtvDVxYTfd]{Iron Rose Imps (3)}

Creatures: Lady Kaltessa Iyis is a challenge beyond the PCs' means at this point, but fortunately doesn't wish to dirty her own hands with their blood. She instead has three fiendish attendants attack while she and the velstrac observe.

Reward: If the PCs talk Lady Iyis into allowing the servant to live, award them XP as if they'd defeated the imps in combat.

Development: If the PCs talk Kaltessa into sparing the servant, defeat the imps, or a PC is reduced to 0 Hit Points, Lady Iyis decided she's had enough and stalks out without a word. The confrontation becomes the talk of the party for a time, interrupting the normal flow of conversation; no social rounds pass during any time the PCs need to spend Treating Wounds.

Event: A Game of Manticore.name: Event: A Game of Manticore
Event: A Game of Manticore.text:
Event: A Game of Manticore

A small group of partygoers enjoys a game of manticore, which involves throwing darts at targets set up in a playing field, and the associated gambling on the manor grounds.

Snow has been cleared from a strip of the lawn on the manor grounds. Three painted straw targets are arranged on the field: a halfling twenty feet away, a goblin forty feet away, and a human peasant sixty feet away.

Any PCs are welcome to join in the game or place wagers. Each PC can wager up to 20 gp on someone to win the match or before an individual throw—up to 1 gp that someone will hit the halfling, 3 gp that someone will hit the goblin, and 5 gp that someone will hit the human target.

Running Manticore: Each participant gets six darts, which they throw at targets until each has used all their darts. Each target is AC 18, though throwers take penalties due to range for farther targets (–2 and –4, respectively). They get 1 point for hitting the closest target, 2 for the next target, or 3 for the farthest; on a critical hit, they hit the target's head, and get double points. A player can also throw two darts at the same target at the same time. In this case, both Strikes take the multiple attack penalty. Each hit from a double-throw earns double points: 2, 4, or 6 for a hit, or 4, 8, or 12 for a critical hit. Using magic is technically not allowed, but most spectators find it amusing that someone would resort to such tactics for a game and will let subtle uses slide.

The contestants: Three other partygoers participate in the game. You can roll for each of their turns with the listed attack modifier, or simply use their usual score if you wish to speed the event along.

  • Ambassador Vrig (attack modifier [[/r 1d20+8]]{+8}; usual score 8) is a talented warrior, but cautious. He uses his own darts, which he throws one at a time at the nearest target.
  • Colonel Rithert (attack modifier [[/r 1d20+6]]{+6}; usual score 6) chafes at xir lack of combat opportunities, and takes the opportunity to show xir skill. Xe throws twice at the goblin target before double-throwing twice at the same target.
  • Rencelos Azri (attack modifier [[/r 1d20+15]]{+15}, usual score 12) is a skilled combatant, but cares little about winning. He throws all his darts two at a time at the farthest target. He laughs uproariously at every hit (his or other players') and makes up stories about the target deserving it.

Social Round: A PC who participates in the game gains an additional social round they can use to Influence Colonel Rithert.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.YjWAv9crs4OIcGez]{Ambassador Vrig's Reward}
If a PC outscores Ambassador Vrig, he congratulates them and offers one of his personal low-grade silver darts as a prize. If multiple PCs outscore him, he offers it to the highest scorer.

Gala Events.name: Gala Events
Gala Events.text:
Gala Events

A number of events take place during the gala between social rounds. They occur in the following order, culminating in the False Flag event, which follows the final social round.

Minor Attendees.name: Minor Attendees
Minor Attendees.text:
Minor Attendees

In addition to the NPCs who the PCs can Influence to befriend, there are several other NPCs they can interact with who play some role in later events at the gala or in its aftermath.

Ambassador Vrig (cautious male hobgoblin diplomat 4), a former officer in the Ironfang Legion, was sent to Isger to find allies for Oprak. He has largely given up that hope for lost, realizing that Hedvend has little ability to make any alliances without permission from Cheliax. He wears an Ironfang Legion uniform and is a dour presence that sees the party as a necessary part of his job, not an enjoyable one.

Fesimwyth “Fessy” Finwinkle (anxious female gnome cleric of Abadar 3) found her faith following the Goblinblood Wars as she tried to help rebuild her native town of Umok. She came to Elidir seeking help, only to become frustrated by the elite's lack of concern about the areas outside the Conerica Straits. Despite this, she fears the Hellbreakers League's disruptions will only make matters worse. Fessy was sent to the gala as a representative of her temple, since the local archbanker had no interest in attending. She's wearing her usual religious garb of white and gold rather than a costume. She isn't comfortable at the party and stands off by herself, but is happy for anyone to approach her. She's eager to talk, and latches on to anyone who is kind to her.

Lezinia (status-seeking female human wannabe diva 1)—one name only, and often said as though followed by an exclamation point—is dressed as finely as anyone at the party, in an outfit that likely cost enough to pay for a small family's food and housing for a month. Her dress clearly evokes a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.s492qJ4psEb4FXuy]{Gylou}, with the ribbon tentacles that make up her skirt showing off her legs to good effect. Lezinia came to Isger at Hedvend's invitation after catching his eye on one of his trips to Cheliax. It was an opportunity she couldn't turn down—she's not talented enough to gain the same level of opportunity in Cheliax, but in a backwater like Isger? She's a big fish in a little pond. In conversation, Lezinia typically steers discussion to herself, her talents, and her stardom. Despite her very clear self-interest, she's not inherently cruel or callous like many of the Isgeri elite.

Merpelia Carafo (inconsiderate female human noble 1) is a typical Elidiran elite, content with the way life is in Isger, and incapable of understanding why anyone would rebel. Prattling on about whatever catches her attention, she just can't understand why so many Isgeri are upset about their conditions. Surely if it were as bad as they claim, they would move to Elidir or somewhere else. If they can't be bothered, then they're either too lazy, or just exaggerating for attention. Merpelia wears a fine golden fur made from a rare cat found in the Menador Mountains over her blue silk sari imported from Vudra, and jewelry made of gold, duskwood, and rare gemstones. Her outfit is not on theme.

Rencelos Azri (greedy male human war profiteer 6) is one of the richest men in Elidir, thanks to being one of the Isgeri army's primary suppliers of arms following his service in the Goblinblood Wars. He's thrilled by the unrest since it means more demand for his services. Rencelos is dressed like a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.BlTEvlCUKPOfBYMR]{Nessari}, complete with spiked armor, wings taken from a drake he hunted for the occasion, and a bare chest that shows off his aging, but still firm, physique. His conversations mostly consist of laughing at those who are poorer than him and lamenting that his son was nearly killed a few days ago by some fool who let loose a giant boar.

Dramatis Personae.name: Dramatis Personae
Dramatis Personae.text:
Dramatis Personae

Some of the gala's guests play a larger role in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma]{Chapter 5} and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway]{Chapter 6}. Below are the most prominent, of whom Quoster, Caeto, and Ezio are the most important to the adventure; feel free to add other guests as needed.

Scene Notes Point Tracking Effect

@UUID[Item.6Wm5w0LXHEHPldtg]{Influence Points}

You can drag this effect onto the NPC's tokens to track individual influence points.

Quoster ThistlewaitCreature 4

  • Unique
  • Small
  • Halfling
  • Humanoid

Male halfling Druman trader

Perception +8

Will +10

Discovery @Check[mercantile-lore|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[perception|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover] or @Check[performance|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[society|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover]

Influence Skills @Check[mercantile-lore|dc:19|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence], @Check[diplomacy|dc:21|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] and @Check[society|dc:21|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence], @Check[crafting|dc:24|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence]

Influence 0 Quoster is undeterred from his demands for a lucrative trade deal. He agrees to help the Hellbreakers League, but the concessions prove onerous and—if the PCs win freedom for Isger—unpopular. Reduce the Hellbreakers League's Reputation Points by 2.

Influence 2 The PCs persuade Quoster to accept reasonable terms beneficial to both sides. The Hellbreakers League gains 1 Reputation Point.

Influence 4 Quoster agrees to a deal that lets him profit in return for commensurate aid to the rebels. The Hellbreakers League gains 2 Reputation Points and Quoster promises a devilwing badge to the PCs after the gala.

Influence 6 @UUID[Actor.IMqed3vyTvOF8yYI]{Quoster's Gift}
Quoster's bargain benefits him alongside Isger—the better the country does, the more Quoster profits. The Hellbreakers League gains 3 Reputation Points and Quoster immediately gives the PCs the devilwing badge.

Resistances Quoster plays the fool to get ahead, but disdains those who don't see the truth. PCs who treat him as a fool or act foolish themselves take a –2 circumstance penalty on checks to Influence him.

Weaknesses Quoster has a strong distaste for Cheliax due to its history of slavery and iron grip on the Conerica River trade routes. PCs who frame negotiations in terms of how it would hurt Cheliax gain a +2 circumstance bonus on Influence checks.

Background Growing up in Druma, Quoster realized how much better his life was than most halflings. While he sees his wealth as his birthright, he also knows it protects him. He's devoted resources to helping causes he deems worthy, such as the Bellflower Network, but prioritizes those that benefit him personally.

Appearance Quoster is dressed in over-the-top finery, wearing a ruffled black blouse under a red velvet coat with long tails and golden fastenings. His fine leather boots curl up at the toes. He carries a silver cane with a large ruby.

Personality Quoster is a shrewd merchant, which he hides behind a carefully cultivated image as a fop. He is remorseless in business, seeking to gain every advantage, and justifies his cutthroat attitude by using his resources to help those less fortunate.

Caeto VulaunexCreature 11

  • Unique
  • Medium
  • Human
  • Humanoid

Self-righteous male human Hellknight

Perception +18

Will +20 (+22 against mental)

Discovery @Check[intimidation|dc:24|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[perception|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[religion|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[society|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover]

Influence Skills @Check[intimidation|dc:19|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to show a steely will), @Check[religion|dc:21|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to discuss how @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.d56paSkcwvll2OhR]{Abadar} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} both teach about the importance of law and order), or @Check[deception|dc:24|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:24|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to talk about Isger)

Influence 2 @UUID[Actor.uTNKk55Dpqw38ifT]{Caeto's Gift}
Caeto senses a common interest in Isger's welfare and disdain for Hedvend VI's stewardship. He offers the PCs a diplomat's badge and urges them to use their voices to improve conditions in the country.

Resistances Caeto can't stand lies. A PC who fails a Deception check to Influence him cannot attempt to Influence him again (though the PC can still attempt to Discover information about him).

Weaknesses Caeto grew up near Saringallow, a childhood he remembers fondly. A PC who mentions the village gains a +2 circumstance bonus on checks to Influence him as long as they don't mention Hellbreaker activity in the area.

Background Caeto rose through the ranks while fighting in the Goblinblood Wars before leaving Isger with the Hellknights. He recently returned, and Hedvend invited him to Elidir to head a special task force to hunt down Hellbreakers. See @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole01]{Caeto Valaunex} for more on Caeto.

Appearance Caeto wears the full symbols of his status as a Hellknight, including armor and weapons.

Personality Caeto can be charming and affable, if a little condescending. His long absence from Isger makes him slightly awkward due to his lack of in-depth familiarity with current events.

Special Caeto plays a larger role in future chapters. He should appear friendly and even open-minded to set up his allyship and ultimate betrayal of the PCs in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma]{Chapter 5}.

Ezio GaetaCreature 7

  • Unique
  • Medium
  • Undead
  • Unholy
  • Vampire

Male vampire agent of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}

Perception +16

Will +18

Discovery @Check[deception|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[perception|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[society|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover]

Influence Skills @Check[diplomacy|dc:19|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] or @Check[society|dc:19|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to discuss current events), @Check[arcana|dc:22|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence], @Check[nature|dc:22|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence], @Check[occultism|dc:22|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence], or @Check[religion|dc:22|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to reveal a magical trick), @Check[thievery|dc:24|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to perform some sleight of hand)

Influence 2 Ezio happily shares gossip about other guests. All PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Discovery checks for the rest of the gala.

Influence 4 Ezio deftly smooths over misunderstandings for the PCs to show the value of his friendship. Once during the gala, if a PC critically fails an Influence check, they get a failure instead.

Influence 6 Ezio offers to help make connections. Once during the gala, a PC can roll twice on an Influence check and take the better result.

Resistances Ezio dislikes bores; a PC who critically fails a check to Influence him takes a –2 penalty on all future checks made to Influence him.

Weaknesses Ezio enjoys gossip. A PC who discusses someone else at the gala gains a +2 circumstance bonus on checks made to Influence him.

Background Ezio is an agent of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} playing a public role as a loyal, trusted advisor and fixer for the city's elite, including Hedvend VI, who gets things done for his friends. See @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole02]{Ezio Gaeta} for more on Ezio.

Appearance Ezio is a large man with ruddy skin. He's dressed as an ayngavhaul, a heresy devil, with a cape that forms the illusion of an iron throne whenever he sits. (If a PC recognizes it and asks about the odd choice, he jokes that it's a reference to critics of his advice.)

Personality Ezio is eccentric, just a little too off-putting and ingratiating for people to really like him, but he's useful enough that they overlook those traits. He's always open for new opportunities and sees potential in the PCs if they approach him.

Special Ezio plays a much larger role in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma]{Chapter 5}. He should appear as someone the PCs can make use of here, before his true allegiances and actions are revealed.

Colonel RithertCreature 3

  • Unique
  • Medium
  • Human
  • Humanoid

Sycophantic agender human officer

Perception +9

Will +9

Discovery @Check[diplomacy|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[performance|dc:24|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[society|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover]

Influence Skills @Check[deception|dc:17|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to shamelessly flatter Rithert), @Check[athletics|dc:19|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] or @Check[survival|dc:21|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to show personal prowess)

Influence 2 Influencing Colonel Rithert reveals xir eagerness to get ahead would make xim an easy target for future Hellbreaker activities. If xe survives the gala, the PCs can use this information later.

Resistances Rithert is jealous of those who have seen combat. Any PC who discusses a battle they have been in takes a –2 penalty on checks made to Influence xim.

Weaknesses Rithert easily succumbs to flattery. PCs who discuss how xe clearly should be serving in the field gain a +2 circumstance bonus on checks to Influence xim.

Background Too young to have fought in the Goblinblood Wars, xe ended up in a logistics role in the army, much to xir frustration. Xe desperately wants a war xe can prove xemself in.

Appearance Rithert wears xir military uniform, with a headdress that resembles a vordine devil's horns.

Personality Xe believes xe needs to work through Cheliax to advance xir career, and plays the role of devil's advocate to get ahead.

Sastoli BruncCreature 3

  • Unique
  • Medium
  • Human
  • Humanoid

Blunt genderfluid human dockmaster

Perception +9

Will +11

Discovery @Check[labor-lore|dc:15|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover], @Check[perception|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,action:discover|name:Discover]

Influence Skills @Check[intimidation|dc:20|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to appeal to his tough nature), @Check[athletics|dc:22|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to show physical prowess), @Check[crafting|dc:24|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] or @Check[medicine|dc:24|traits:concentrate,linguistic,action:influence|name:Influence] (to show knowledge of skills Sastoli considers actually useful)

Influence 2 Sastoli becomes friendly toward the PCs (which benefits them in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway]{Chapter 6}).
