Resistances Sastoli disdains empty talk. A PC who fails a check to Influence them takes a –2 penalty to Influence them for the remainder of the gala.

Weaknesses Sastoli appreciates those who do physical work. A PC whose highest attribute is Strength gains a +1 to any checks to Influence Sastoli.

Background Sastoli came up through the ranks on the docks, becoming one of the dockmasters who oversees the workers that make the city's trade economy function. Their competence secures their position, and earns them invitations to galas like this one.

Appearance Sastoli stands out among the finely dressed elites in the worst way possible—they're wearing plain dockworker's clothes, except for a plush sarglagon draped around their shoulders as a conceit to the theme.

Personality Sastoli is blunt and out of their element, breaking all manner of etiquette such as grabbing fistfuls of appetizers from servants, and delights in the quiet outrage of the elites who can't kick them out.

Reward: For each influence threshold the PCs meet, award them 40 XP.

Reevesrest Manor.name: Reevesrest Manor
Reevesrest Manor.text:
I. Reevesrest Manor

Reevesrest is fully described in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05ireevesrest000]{Chapter 5}, when the PCs have free rein to explore. For now, the party is largely confined to the great room (area I2) and grounds outside. PCs who wish to explore can enter areas including the library, dining room, gallery, and garden, but are restricted from other areas by guards and servants, who steer them back to the public rooms. The upstairs is fully off limits, and two guards stand at the bottom of the stairs in the great room, preventing access.

The Gala.name: The Gala
The Gala.text:
The Gala

The gala is scheduled to take place one week after the PCs arrive in the city. Once they arrive at Reevesrest, read or paraphrase the following.

Floating balls of red and white light illuminate the great room of the mansion. Music performed by a string quartet on a stage in the western wing of the room fills the air over the sound of conversation. Many of the assembled guests wear costumes to evoke Hell—elaborate pieces with horns and other devilish features embellish fine silk and velvet dresses and suits—or armored Hellknights.

A curved grand staircase with painted balusters leads up to a landing and a walkway that stretches across the room. A few figures look down from above, but a pair of armed guards, dressed as devils complete with a false tail attached to their armor, stand guard at the foot of the stairs, preventing most people from ascending.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.WtESyy9BSUW0INxj]{Gala}

Larger Parties

You might want to reduce the number of social rounds for groups with more than four PCs, who will find it much easier to accomplish their goals. For groups of five PCs, you may want to have five influence rounds, or just four for groups of six PCs. Events can be spread out over the evening, with one or two per influence round.

The gala, filled with the elite of Elidir as well as the guards and servants who care for them, takes place over six social rounds, each taking about an hour. During this time, the PCs should reach a deal with Quoster Thistlewait using the influence subsystem (GM Core 187). They can also meet other important people in attendance. Because the PCs must maintain their disguises, they can't influence the NPCs to help the Hellbreakers League, but can win personal favor.

Influence Rounds: Let the PCs know they have at least six social rounds, as the party will likely last into the small hours of the night, leading up to the actual anniversary of the Hellknights' march. In addition, a number of events, starting @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04galaevents0000]{Here}, occur during the course of the evening, some of which give the PCs additional social rounds.

Event: Injustice is Served.name: Event: Injustice is Served
Event: Injustice is Served.text:
Event: Injustice is ServedLow 4

A sudden harsh shout—“You there! Stop! It's the Gyve for you!”—booms over the noise of the streets of Elidir as a guard patrol moves with practiced skill through the parting crowds.

Justice has little place in Elidir, where the rich get away with all manner of behavior, and the poor face harsh repercussions for crimes they commit to survive. When a starving goblin urchin tries to steal from the PCs, they get the chance to experience this state of matters firsthand as a guard spots her and promises harsh consequences in the city's notorious prison.

Ozney Cacklemouth (desperate young female goblin urchin –1) attempts to steal coins from a random PC. She attempts a single Thievery check with a +7 modifier against all the PCs' Perception DCs. In the unlikely event she succeeds, the PCs might think the guards are coming for them, but it's quickly clear that the guards have spotted Ozney and plan to drag her away to the Gyve. If the PCs didn't learn about the Gyve earlier, they can attempt a @Check[elidir-lore|dc:17|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[society-lore|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge to know it's the city's main prison, where suspects are tortured to get confessions and even minor crimes can result in forced labor (they can also ask the guards, who inform them it's the city's prison).

Ozney begs for forgiveness, saying she simply wanted a few coins to buy food, but the guards are unmoved. The PCs can attempt to talk the guards into releasing Ozney, though they're hesitant about "letting a criminal go free." Convincing them requires succeeding at a @Check[legal-lore|dc:17] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:19|traits:action:request,auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental|name:Request] check to Request that the guards let her go, or @Check[intimidation|dc:19|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental,skill,action:coerce|name:Coerce] check to Coerce them into doing so. If the PCs fail (or don't intervene), the guards begin dragging the sobbing goblin away. The PCs can fight the guards to stop them, but warn them that doing so will gain them Suppression Points.

Event: Injustice is ServedLow 4

@UUID[Actor.U3Gz8HOONrLhTqnF]{Watch Officer} @UUID[Actor.mquLLZyEPeaQekH3]{Guards (2)}

Creatures: The three guards fight back if the PCs initiate combat. Ozney hides nearby if combat breaks out, but if you need statistics for her, you can use the urchin (NPC Core 40).

Reward: If the PCs talk the guards into releasing Ozney, award them XP as if they'd defeated the guards in combat.

Development: If the PCs fight the guards, they gain 1 Suppression Point, or 2 if they kill any guards. If they prevent Ozney's arrest, she thanks them while clutching her stomach in hunger—she's sincerely grateful for being saved, but also tries to milk the situation to get food or money. She also offers to help if they need anything; award the PCs 1 Uprising Point.

Event: Who's Laughing Now?.name: Event: Who's Laughing Now?
Event: Who's Laughing Now?.text:
Event: Who's Laughing Now?Low 4

A small pack of young men points and laughs as a laborer struggles to get an enormous daeodon to move through the crowded streets. As the creature stops to relieve itself, the group's apparent leader stoops down and picks up a rock, throwing it at the beast. “Look, two piles of dung in the street!” he yells, as his friends laugh raucously.

The pack of awful teenagers is led by Moccoviz Azri (spoiled male human brat 4), the son of a rich merchant the PCs meet at the gala. Spotting the laborer's struggles with a daeodon he's transporting through the city, Moccoviz exploits the situation for his own amusement. Unfortunately for him, the stone hits the beast, who reacts immediately, pulling its lead free and charging the teens. Let the PCs attempt a @Check[perception|dc:19] check; on a success, the PC realizes the handler intentionally dropped the lead and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative.

Event: Who's Laughing Now?Low 4

@UUID[Actor.2K4bOvVvUG6ninH9]{Elite Daeodon}

Creatures: The daeodon charges the teens, leaving them scattered and bruised, before turning its attention to the PCs, who are in the wrong place at the wrong time. The handler laughs as the daeodon charges the teens, but cries out in alarm as it attacks the PCs, calling for them to not kill it. A PC who saw the handler release the beast can spend a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to make a @Check[intimidation|dc:21|traits:concentrate,skill] check to tell him to control it. On a success, he does so at the end of the round, or at the end of the PC's turn on a critical success, ending the combat.

Development: If the PCs get the handler to control the daeodon, he mutters an apology and departs with the creature before Moccoviz can take out his anger on him. If they kill the beast, the handler looks distraught, blaming them for the punishment he'll face. Dirty from his fall in the street, Moccoviz says it's no less than the man deserves. The humiliated teen grudgingly thanks the PCs and tosses [[/r 1d6]] sp on the ground for them as he departs.

Event: A Poor Death.name: Event: A Poor Death
Event: A Poor Death.text:
Event: A Poor Death

Life in Isger is difficult for those without money, and that's no less true in Elidir despite the riches that pass through the capital. Among those down on their luck is Padisco (stubborn male human war veteran 3), an old soldier whose legs were badly injured in the Goblinblood War and currently survives by begging for coins. He's crossing the street in front of the PCs when his crutches slide on a patch of ice under the snow, leaving him sprawled on the ground just as a speeding carriage approaches. If the PCs want to save him, they have only moments to react.

Allow PCs to determine what approach to take for a rescue, such as pulling Padisco to safety in the nick of time with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:19] check, redirecting the carriage with a @Check[driving-lore|dc:17] check, or a @Check[intimidation|dc:19] check or @Check[nature|dc:19|traits:auditory,concentrate,action:command-an-animal|name:Command an Animal] check to Command an Animal. A PC could also try to stop the carriage with a @Check[crafting|dc:19] or @Check[thievery|dc:19] check to jam something into the spokes of the wheel.

If no PC succeeds, the carriage tramples poor Padisco, leaving him at dying 2 but giving the PCs opportunities to save him by using Battle Medicine, alchemy, or magic. If any PC critically fails in their attempt, they are also trampled by the carriage and take @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:19|traits:basic] save).

Reward: If the PCs save Padisco's life, award them 30 XP and 1 Uprising Point. Padisco promises to help them any way he can.

Elidir Events.name: Elidir Events
Elidir Events.text:
Elidir Events

While the PCs plot rebellion, they face a deeply divided city inhabited by wealthy, self-interested elites who wield power under Cheliax's yoke, and the downtrodden masses that make up the bulk of the population. The following events occur in no particular order during this part of the adventure. Use them to emphasize the inequity of the current regime and power structure in Elidir.

Father Kindness's Bedroom.name: Father Kindness's Bedroom
Father Kindness's Bedroom.text:
H8. Father Kindness's BedroomModerate 4

Children's drawings hang on the rough wooden walls in this room, contrasting with several marble busts and golden statuettes on the bureau. A lush bearskin rug covers the floor in front of a large canopy bed.

Father Kindness's private quarters are furnished with stolen items from his guild's activities and mementos from the orphans' childhood. The door to this room remains locked at all times, and the guild members all know better than to attempt to enter without permission.

H8. Father Kindness's BedroomModerate 4

@UUID[Actor.sNpAQ5pKquOBq4YS]{Father Kindness} @UUID[Actor.fsNUzqf2sQQvBKpz]{Blinding Spray}

Creatures: Father Kindness is alone in this room unless the guild is on high alert, in which case he can be found outside the orphans' dormitory. If he hears combat from the dormitory, he activates the trap on his door (if it wasn't already activated), draws his weapon, and moves to the door to limit his opponents to fighting him one-on-one. If reduced to 25% of his Hit Points, he attempts to flee, but if unable, he throws down his weapon and cries for mercy.

Hazard: If the thieves are wary, Father Kindness activates the trap on the main door to blind any intruders.

Treasure: Father Kindness was intrigued by the lazybones pendant, which he's been examining in his room. In addition, the stolen artwork can be sold for 60 gp.

Development: @UUID[Actor.4hqfIV70tH0nTnqV]{Bedroom}
If any of the thieves survive, the PCs can try to recruit them for the Hellbreakers League. Doing so requires a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:17] check; increase the DC by 1 for each thief the PCs killed. They earn 2 Uprising Points if successful—double on a critical success, as the Children's Charity members help recruit other disaffected members of the lower classes.

Bathroom.name: Bathroom
Bathroom.text:
H7. Bathroom

The shared bathroom has two tubs fed with rainwater from spigots in the wall. A shelf on the back wall holds soap and several bottles of perfumed oils.

Hidden in the base of the tubs are several secret compartments, where the guild keeps its stolen money. A PC who Searches the room can discover it with a successful @Check[perception|dc:19|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.Ccaoe4FacMt3RJVt]{Secret Compartment}
The hidden chambers contain stolen noble crests worth 30 gp.

Storeroom.name: Storeroom
Storeroom.text:
H6. Storeroom

The shelves of this room contain bedding, cleaning supplies, and other such sundries. Hidden under the obvious items is guild equipment, which can be found with a successful @Check[perception|dc:19|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check to Search.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.N1bEjU1KiWNwrI0s]{Storeroom}
The items here include an elite disguise kit, 2 lesser elixirs of life, a shacklebreaker, and an infiltrator thieves' toolkit.

Orphans' Dormitory.name: Orphans' Dormitory
Orphans' Dormitory.text:
H5. Orphans' DormitoryLow 4

Faded paintings on the walls of this room depict a mountain scene, a dark forest, a city, and a verdant field. Several neatly made bunk beds occupy the center of the chamber and fine rugs cover the floor between them. Two small chests sit at the head and foot of each bed.

The thieves have used this dorm since childhood. The rooms are otherwise largely bare of adornment other than the bunk beds, stolen rugs and murals depicting scenery around Isger. A secret door, which can be discovered with a successful @Check[perception|dc:19] check, opens to the outside where the thieves can Climb down the side of the building if they need to escape.

H5. Orphans' DormitoryLow 4

@UUID[Actor.AgNXbcwMS0ORdiTz]{Children's Charity Housebreaker} @UUID[Actor.Iv364B0HgflxNYjE]{Children's Charity Hustler}

Creatures: Two thieves are in this room. If they are unaware of the PCs, they're awake but relaxing in bed. If the guild is on high alert, they wait to ambush anyone who comes up the stairs. One hides in the northeastern corner of the room, while the other hides between the western bunk beds. In addition, Father Kindness waits just outside his room (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04fatherkindne00]{H8}); his presence makes this a severe encounter. After using ranged weapons from hiding, the thieves attempt to flank enemies to use their sneak attack.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.JcgHY3iLg4bowMe9]{Small Chests}
Small chests at the foot of the beds contain the thieves' clothing and other personal items, including stashes of stolen jewelry from the last two decades, which can be sold for 20 gp.

Rec Room.name: Rec Room
Rec Room.text:
H4. Rec RoomTrivial 4

Several training dummies with painted faces resembling goblins and Isgeri army soldiers stand in this large room, holding wooden swords and shields. Faded paintings on the wall show children battling giant spiders and river bandits.

Father Kindness first entertained and then later trained his charges in this area.

H4. Rec RoomTrivial 4

@UUID[Actor.Ya5KBcz9ebe74O8v]{Practice Guard's Grasp} @UUID[Actor.xTUZbVwXc7cgXCjv]{Disarming Dummy}

Creatures: This room is empty if the guild is not wary or on high alert; otherwise the Children's Charity pilferers in the dining room (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04diningroomun00]{H2}) wait here. One lurks at the foot of the stairs, just out of sight, waiting for anyone to enter. The other waits in the southeast corner, hoping to lure an intruder into the hazards. Their presence makes this a moderate encounter.

Hazards: The training dummies work as traps for the unwary. The Practice Guard's Grasp is in the area marked T1 and the Disarming Dummy is in the area marked T2. The Children's Charity members are familiar with the traps and don't trigger them even when adjacent.

Reward: Disabling the dummies earns the PCs 60 XP.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
H3. Kitchen

The smell of a meat stew fills this room, coming from a large pot hung over a fireplace in the far corner. A small butcher's block table fills the center of the kitchen, and pots, pans, knives, and other cooking implements hang from the walls.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.inciVyy0F4NJFgn1]{Kitchen}
A large amount of stolen silverware worth 40 gp can be found here, along with a low-grade silver filcher's fork.

Dining Room.name: Dining Room
Dining Room.text:
H2. Dining RoomModerate 4

A wooden table runs the length of this room, its surface scratched and marred. Mismatched chairs line the table.

H2. Dining RoomModerate 4

@UUID[Actor.OGEA9Jmn3rdx1GO1]{Children's Charity Pilferers (2)}

Creatures: Unless the guild is wary or on high alert, two members can be found here helping themselves to a snack. If the PCs catch them unawares, they shout in alarm (putting the guild on high alert), draw their weapons, and attack. If they can, they flee into the rec room (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04recroomundef00]{H4}), where they attempt to use the hazards to their advantage. If the guild is already wary or on high alert, these thieves are instead in the rec room.

Front Entrance.name: Front Entrance
Front Entrance.text:
H1. Front EntranceTrivial 4

Stairs lead to a landing in front of a weathered door with a broken brass knocker hanging from a single nail. The plate is a cherub's face, though it's badly dented where the clapper hits its smile.

The exterior door is locked at all times.

H1. Front EntranceTrivial 4

@UUID[Actor.OsjWkH2G5h64xcuG]{Stair Spikes}

Hazard: Father Kindness installed a trap here when the orphanage became a thieves' guild headquarters. The thieves avoid it by only entering one at a time.

Reward: If the PCs bypass the trap without setting it off, award them 40 XP.

House of Found Family.name: House of Found Family
House of Found Family.text:
H. House of Found Family

The PCs can easily find the old House of Found Family orphanage in a rundown area of the city. Its ceilings are 10 feet high and the walls are wooden slats with doors of reinforced wood. The exterior door is locked, but can be opened with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks to Pick the Lock. The interior doors are typically unlocked unless otherwise noted; if they're locked, they can also be opened with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks. Only Father Kindness has a key—he expects his charges to be able to let themselves in and out without one. The windows are all lined with iron bars close enough together to keep out anything Small or larger. Wooden slat shutters are usually opened during the day to let in light, but closed at night for warmth and security. An everlight crystal hangs in a hooded lantern in each room, providing all the rooms bright illumination at night or when the shutters are closed, unless someone closes the lantern.

The PCs can spend a day staking out the orphanage to get a better sense of comings and goings. With a successful @Check[perception|dc:19] check, their observations reveal that there are typically four thieves in the building at all times (plus Father Kindness, but they don't have a chance to observe him); on a critical success, they also realize that when multiple thieves come or go from the front door, they do so one at a time, with each fully descending or ascending the stairs before the next follows (this is to avoid the trap in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04frontentranc00]{H1}). The PC must also attempt a @Check[stealth|dc:19|traits:move,skill,secret,exploration,action:avoid-notice|name:Avoid Notice] check to Avoid Notice to avoid raising suspicions among the thieves' guild. On a failure, the thieves become wary; on a critical failure, or if the thieves are already wary, they instead are on high alert.

Wariness: If the thieves are wary, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all initiative rolls and the PCs take a –1 penalty to their Perception and Stealth checks if they try to stake out the orphanage. If the thieves are on high alert, in addition to the effects of being wary, they close the wooden shutters on the windows, and use Stealth for their initiatives. If the thieves become aware of the PCs' presence in the orphanage through combat or an alarm, they go on high alert, which they also do if the PCs leave the area to recover. Once they go on high alert, they remain in that status throughout this adventure.

While the Children's Charity members want to defend their home, they place a higher priority on their lives. When they're reduced to 25% of their Hit Points they try to escape, either out the front entrance or the secret door on the second floor.

Children's Charity.name: Children's Charity
Children's Charity.text:
Children's Charity

The blue ribbon was a brainchild of Tobmer Qinro, a petty thief who rehabilitated himself after a revelation that caring for Isger's orphans was his higher purpose. He hoped the ribbon would become a status symbol and raise gold to build orphanages across the country, but it largely failed. Tobmer made just enough to buy a small building, where he raised a handful of children on his own. Angry about Elidir's stinginess, Tobmer took on the moniker Father Kindness (disillusioned male aiuvarin thief 5) and trained his charges to be con artists and thieves. He dubbed his nascent thieves' guild the Children's Charity and three decades later, his now-grown charges leave blue ribbons at the scenes of their crime as a (largely overlooked) message that their stolen prizes are what Elidir's less fortunate are due.

After learning about the blue ribbon, a PC can attempt a @Check[elidir-lore|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[underworld-lore|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check or a @Check[society|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge to know the ribbon's history and the former orphanage's location. If that fails, they can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:19|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information, with the following results.

Success The PC learns the origins of the blue ribbon and the location of the former orphanage.

Failure As success, but the PC's inquiries make their way to the Children's Charity. The thieves become wary (see Wariness, below).

Critical Failure As failure, but the thieves are already on high alert when the PCs arrive.

Love Sting Printing House.name: Love Sting Printing House
Love Sting Printing House.text:
Love Sting Printing House Moderate 4

Read or paraphrase the following as the PCs approach Love Sting Printing House.

A high-pitched voice pleads, “Please, you don't have to do this! They're just harmless entertainment!” A bruised elf lies crumpled in the snow in front of a shop. A trail of smoke wafts out the shop's door.

Love Sting Printing HouseModerate 4

@UUID[Actor.u0o2f128WZlZFFvJ]{Odvolos} @UUID[Actor.UUqBdrTPVuHXTc6e]{Goblin Pyro} @UUID[Actor.Q3vs3kPPRPanTN5g]{Spreading Fire}

Creatures: The elven man is a Calistrian devotee named Ievis (romantic male elf author 1), the writer, artist, and publisher of the copper dalliances. If the PCs attempt to enter the building or help him, a goblin calls out to the odvolos, who is torching unsold pamphlets inside, and attacks. The odvolos emerges and joins the battle, trying to prevent PCs from entering the building.

Hazard: The fire is spreading inside, threatening to destroy the entire building, including the safe house on the second floor. Though it's inside, it's included as part of this encounter due to the PCs' need to stop it from spreading. Eliminating the hazard requires dousing the flames. Water clears a 5-foot square if the amount is small (such as that from create water or hydraulic push). Larger amounts of water, such as a full bucket, douse a 10-foot-by-10-foot area. Throwing a bucket of water on flames requires an Interact action. A waterskin doesn't contain enough water to put out even 1 square of fire. Cold can also put out fire, but only if the cold can affect an area; cold is usually less effective than water, so a frost vial typically puts out 1 square of fire, and frostbite is ineffective.

Four large barrels of oak gall ink near the entrance offer gallons of nonflammable liquid PCs can use to fight the fire. A bucket hangs on the wall near each barrel, which the PCs can fill with ink with an Interact action. Each barrel contains enough ink to fill 20 buckets.

Other methods might also help control the fire, as you determine. For example, the PCs might be able to find something to barricade the fire with to control its path, or use a cloak to beat out some of the fire.

Instead of fighting the fire, PCs might try to dash upstairs to grab the lazybones pendant. If they do, they find the single, large storeroom empty and clearly looted. The only thing in the room is a blue ribbon pinned to the wall. If the PCs don't make it upstairs, Ievis discovers the blue ribbon afterward and informs them that the necklace is gone.

Scene Notes Fire

@UUID[Macro.uwnPYC7QdFlooJKc]{Remove All Fires}

This scene allows you to spread fire square by square. Enable the Fire Toggle on the Actor Toolbar located in the top left of the screen, and then left click anywhere on the scene!

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.OtUK90lJ4YxseAhG]{Levis' Reward}
Ievis offers the PCs two unassuming face paints as thanks. If the PCs saved the shop, he also gifts them a rare manuscript of the banned play Abrogail I, which is worth 300 gp.

Development: The PCs can now recruit Ievis to write copper dalliances with anti-Cheliax content to rally readers against the government, earning them 2 Uprising Points. The first is called Breaking Hell for Her.

Operation: Proper Identification.name: Operation: Proper Identification
Operation: Proper Identification.text:
Operation: Proper Identification

Before Alceo and Phoebe were identified by the authorities, Quoster sent them a lazybones pendant for them to wear as a sign of what he could provide, and a way of recognizing them when they finally met. The PCs need to collect it from where it's being stored in a room above Love Sting Printing House, a one-elf publisher of “copper dalliances,” incredibly popular smutty serials with titles like The Archer All Aquiver, His Longsword of Love, and The Allure of Secret Sects, which sell for a copper apiece.

Unfortunately for the PCs, the room was looted by a thieves' guild known as the Children's Charity. Worse, the PCs arrive at the site just after an odvolos has decided that copper dalliances are a bad influence on the people of Elidir. Use the Love Sting Printing House map for this encounter.

Operation: Dress to Impress.name: Operation: Dress to Impress
Operation: Dress to Impress.text:
Operation: Dress to ImpressLow 4

Proper attire lets the PCs fit in at the gala—and even bring in weapons and armor if it fits their costume. Alceo and Phoebe direct the PCs to Reirsumli Brightgate (meek male dwarf tailor 1) at his shop, the Silver Ribbon. Phoebe saved Reirsumli's life during the Goblinblood Wars, and he owes her greatly. The PCs can tell him that the costumes are for Phoebe and he'll happily make them for free.

The PCs must describe what they want their outfits to look like; give each PC a chance to describe their devilish garb and attempt a relevant DC 19 check to fully explain their vision. The PCs will also need costumes for any animal companions, familiars, or other creatures in their party as well.

Appropriate checks for costume design are @Check[religion|dc:19] to describe a devil costume, @Check[society|dc:19] to describe a Hellknight or other proper Chelaxian figure, or @Check[crafting|dc:19] or @Check[performance|dc:19] for a general sense of what they're trying to achieve. The party needs to make a number of checks equal to the number of PCs, but the checks can be made by a single PC and the PCs can attempt to Aid each other. If anyone expresses concern about bringing larger weapons or armor into the gala, Reirsumli suggests dressing as a Hellknight or vordine. He tells the PCs to return just before the gala and he'll have the costumes ready.

Whenever the PCs return, they find a well-dressed man with two hulking bodyguards in the shop confronting Reirsumli. He spotted the PCs' outfits set out to be handed over and demanded them for himself!

To retrieve their costumes, the PCs must dissuade the noble by flattery, fear, or force. Each PC can attempt a @Check[deception|dc:21] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:21] check to persuade the noble with kindness, or a @Check[athletics|dc:21] or @Check[intimidation|dc:21] check to make them rethink their acquisitiveness. If the PCs get a number of successes equal to half the number of PCs, the noble backs off. If not, he decides to teach the PCs a lesson and attacks!

Operation: Dress to ImpressLow 4

@UUID[Actor.vomc90aVM40cNzHo]{Noble} @UUID[Actor.joyTSlYACQNNJmdY]{Bodyguards (2)}

Creatures: The noble and his guards aren't looking to kill the PCs, just teach them their place. They use their attacks with the nonlethal trait as long as the PCs do. If the noble is knocked unconscious, his two bodyguards retreat with him. If he's killed, the PCs' Suppression Points increase by 1.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.s0Ryb9pma5PLCb7h]{Reirsumli's Reward}
If the PCs successfully dissuade or defeat the noble, Reirsumli gives them a +1 armor potency rune and raiment rune as thanks. If the PCs are defeated, Reirsumli instead provides secondhand costumes he has available. The poor display means the PCs take a –1 item penalty to skill checks to influence or learn about NPCs during the gala.

Reward: If the PCs dissuade the noble from taking the costumes, award them XP as if they'd defeated him and his guards in combat.

Operation: The Invitation of the Season.name: Operation: The Invitation of the Season
Operation: The Invitation of the Season.text:
Operation: The Invitation of the Season

The PCs need invitations to the gala! Fortunately for them, Alceo and Phoebe already did most of the legwork and know that a clerk at the city tax office, Orimos (petty nonbinary hellspawn nephilim human tax clerk 0), is responsible for the invites. They suggest the PCs approach Orimos with the truth, but warn that the clerk is wary of upsetting the authorities, so the PCs need to be subtle.

During the day, the PCs can find Orimos laboring in the Trade House, a bustling hive of bureaucracy filled with government officials, merchants, guards, and others coming and going with arms full of paperwork. The clerk is publicly officious and uninterested in discussing whatever trivial matter the PCs are bothering them with.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.h65rC0mOCb73F92G]{Establishment}

The easiest way to get them into somewhere private is to present them with a seemingly legitimate bit of paperwork, a tax problem, or other such minor governmental issue that they would normally discuss in a private office, which a PC can do with a successful @Check[accounting-lore|dc:17] or @Check[legal-lore|dc:17] check or @Check[society|dc:19] check. Alternatively, they can persuade Orimos to take them somewhere else with a successful @Check[deception|dc:21|traits:action:impersonate,concentrate,exploration,manipulate,secret|name:Impersonate] check to Impersonate an official on a legitimate task or to @Check[deception|dc:21|traits:action:lie,auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret|name:Lie] about their reasons for needing to speak with Orimos, @Check[diplomacy|dc:21|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression] check to Make an Impression to make them friendly, or a @Check[intimidation|dc:21|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental,skill,action:coerce|name:Coerce] check to Coerce them into a private conversation. On a critical failure, the PC takes a –1 circumstance penalty to any future checks they make with Orimos. If at any point the PCs bring up Alceo, Phoebe, or the Hellbreakers League, they frighten the clerk and the DC of all checks to get them somewhere private increases by 1.

Alternatively, the PCs might stake out the office and follow Orimos to somewhere they can talk in private, such as Orimos's home. If the PCs get Orimos to somewhere private and earn their trust, the PCs can reveal their true needs. At that point, Orimos drops their facade and reveals themself to be petty and eager to harm the elites of Cheliax and Isger, whom they hate for making their life difficult. They easily provide invitations to the PCs.

If the PCs fail to persuade Orimos to talk privately, the clerk sighs deeply before giving them one more chance. They urge whichever PC came closest to succeeding at their check to lean in, and then whispers that if the PCs' concerns are urgent enough, they should put their money where their mouth is. With an appropriate bribe—3 gp per PC—Orimos provides the invitations.

Reward: If the PCs acquire the invitations without needing to resort to a bribe, award them 40 XP.

Party Preparations.name: Party Preparations
Party Preparations.text:
Party Preparations

Once they've defeated the guard patrol, Sarevial rushes the PCs to Alceo and Phoebe's safe house. Alceo offers to tend to any wounds (via magic or Medicine) the PCs might have from the encounter. When everyone's healed up, he gets straight to business.

Alceo takes a deep breath in his seat, Phoebe standing protectively behind him. “We've spent the past month stirring up discontent against Cheliax's puppet elites and the city authorities. There's been some success, but Hedvend's cracked down on protests and used his own army's violence against the people to frame us as rioters.”

“In some ways that's helped us,” Phoebe interjects. “We've been hesitant to officially start a League chapter here, but the people are all but demanding one. They need someone to organize them and focus their anger, or there will be real riots. Unfortunately, Hedvend managed to identify us and spread our image around, so we're handing off our operations to you.”

Alceo nods. “The immediate problem is that we were on the verge of arranging a deal with a Druman merchant, Quoster, to supply the League in return for certain trade rights once we've liberated Isger. Unfortunately, Hedvend outing us has spooked him. He wants proof of our abilities, and is demanding we show them by meeting him at Hedvend's upcoming gala. You'll have to make that meeting in our place and negotiate a deal that benefits both sides.”

Operating out of the safe house, the PCs must acquire three things before the gala at Steward Hedvend VI's manor home, Reevesrest: forged invitations, appropriate costumes, and the lazybones pendant (See @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04hhouseoffoun00]{Here}) that Quoster supplied for Alceo and Phoebe to identify themselves. These can be done in any order, and Alceo and Phoebe try to answer any questions the PCs have. Likely questions and their responses are as follows.

How were you identified? “We're not sure,” Phoebe says. “Our best guess is someone we were working with was caught and broke in the Gyve.”

The Gyve? “It's the prison.” Alceo's face twists with disgust. “An awful place known for torturing those who end up there until the wardens hear what they want to hear.”

What can you tell us about Quoster? “He's a halfling and motivated more by self-interest than concern for Isger. But he's willing to help, and everything we've been able to learn about him makes us think we can trust him.”

Where's the necklace? “Safely tucked away above a print shop called Love Sting. They make some saucy novels.” Phoebe grins and Alceo's ears go pink.

What should we do about starting a League chapter? “The more immediate concern is Quoster and the gala. After that, look for recruits and sign up as many as you safely can. We trust you can handle it.”

After answering questions (or if asked what they'll be doing), Alceo and Phoebe inform the PCs they plan to leave Elidir the morning of the gala, making a show of it to draw attention away from the Hellbreakers League's continuing activities in the city. In the meantime, they'll remain in the safe house and transition operations to the PCs.

Isgeri Circle.name: Isgeri Circle
Isgeri Circle.text:
Isgeri CircleModerate 4

While the Taldans “pacified” the Isgeri in 2133, outbreaks of violence continued for some time. To ease tensions, the first Taldan governor of Isger allowed the Isgeri tribes to create this monument devoted to @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} in her guise as a goddess of bounty. Attempts to remove it over the ensuing centuries all failed, as workers mysteriously grew ill when they approached. Most residents of the city now give it a wide berth.

Badly worn carvings of produce such as grapes, apples, nuts, and squashes top the ancient standing stones that surround a simple stone altar in this clearing.

Unable to safely venture out themselves, Alceo and Phoebe enlisted Sarevial (loyal male elf baker's apprentice –1) to check several times each day to see if the PCs have arrived. Unfortunately, a guard patrol has grown suspicious and closes in when Sarevial approaches the PCs.

Isgeri CircleModerate 4

@UUID[Actor.YaCyUc8wwL1vC3rn]{Adiutor} @UUID[Actor.fLsLiPKHZwyWVQ7L]{Toadies (2)}

Creatures: In response to the protests against Cheliax, loyalists formed patrols to maintain security. Led by adiutors—mortals invested with infernal power also known as auxiliary devils—these patrols investigate any hints of subversion. They attempt to arrest Sarevial and the PCs for questioning. If the adiutor is slain or knocked unconscious, his toadies flee. Sarevial doesn't participate in this combat; if you need his stats, use those of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-npc-core.Actor.APn9B54hhRtr0oCQ]{Commoner}.

Entering the City.name: Entering the City
Entering the City.text:
Entering the City

As the PCs approach the capital, read or paraphrase the following.

The Conerica River runs through the capital, bisecting the walled city. Ships laden with goods anchor outside huge river gates, waiting to enter as small sentry boats row back and forth delivering inspectors. Along the roads to Elidir, walled caravanserai teem with people, horses, wagons, and beasts of burden making use of the inns, stables, and trade facilities that facilitate the city's lifeblood.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.oXfScI7GXUmtJgnL]{Caravanserai} @UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.XmZulqLJLcLEc72S]{Elidir}

City Maps

Elidir is a large city, and it's possible the PCs get into fights in areas that aren't mapped (especially if you add some random encounters with guards). GMs who prefer premade maps can use flip-mats and flip-tiles to create suitable maps in moments. Some particularly useful maps are noted below.

  • GameMastery Flip-Mat: City Square
  • Pathfinder Flip-Mat Classics: City Streets
  • Pathfinder Flip-Tiles: Urban Slums Expansion
  • Pathfinder Flip-Tiles: Urban Starter Set
  • Pathfinder Flip-Mat: City Districts Multi-Pack

The PCs don't draw any attention in the caravanserai outside the city walls as traders come and go constantly, with many travelers stopping in hopes of joining a caravan. Movement in and out of Elidir is tightly restricted, and the PCs must find a way past the guards without raising suspicions. The easiest way to do so is to join a group entering the city and pass through the gates right under the guards' noses. Fortunately for the PCs, several people and groups are also looking to enter Elidir, and each has a secret that makes them amenable to welcoming a stranger.

Introduce the following groups, then allow each PC to attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:19|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information or @Check[perception|dc:19] check to learn more about one group of their choice. On a success, they learn the best skill to pose as part of the group. If a PC sneaks in with that group, they can use that skill instead of Deception or Performance to fool the guards. On a critical success, the PCs also learn the group's secret. Doing so incentivizes the group to help any PCs that enter with them, giving each PC a +1 circumstance bonus on the subsequent check to make it past the guards. Reward the clever use of resources such as magical items, feats, and spells with bonuses or even an automatic success.

Eineel Havenmark

Description Eineel is a mild-mannered human farmer who routinely brings in produce to sell at the market.

Secret Eineel is a smuggler, taking less for her services than official fees.

Skill @Check[nature|dc:19|traits:auditory,concentrate,action:command-an-animal|name:Command an Animal] to Command the animals pulling her carts.

Joward Yatly

Description Joward is a nervous dwarven trader from Absalom with a shipment of wooden clockworks he's been hired to deliver.

Secret Joward is actually Andoren, but fears he'll be turned away due to the conflict between the countries.

Skill @Check[crafting|dc:19] to demonstrate knowledge of the devices.

Northern Warriors

Description A half-dozen partisans, led by Maurisno Rabesi (eager male human warrior 0), have come from northwest Isger to join the army to defend the nation from rebels and rabblerousers.

Secret The young hopeful soldiers have almost no actual experience with their weapons and are as likely to stab themselves as anyone else.

Skill @Check[athletics|dc:19] to show off martial prowess.

The Menagerie of Fey Fantastico

Description The Menagerie is a traveling circus that has received permission to enter the city to put on a week's worth of shows.

Secret Several of the troupe are thieves, who use the traveling show as cover for their activities.

Skill @Check[acrobatics|dc:19] to pose as a tumbling troupe member.

Once the PCs each join a group, each PC must make it past the guards without raising suspicions. They can attempt to do so with a DC 17 check with the associated skill, or a @Check[deception|dc:19] or @Check[performance|dc:19] check, with the following results.

Success The PC enters Elidir without raising any suspicions.

Failure The guards' suspicions are raised. The PCs gain 1 Suppression Point.

Critical Failure As failure, but the PCs gain 2 Suppression Points.

Sneaking In: The PCs can also attempt to enter the city by directly sneaking in, but the guards are on high alert and this may be more troublesome than blending in with other groups. A PC must succeed at two checks to enter unnoticed: a @Check[stealth|dc:19|traits:move,skill,secret,action:sneak|name:Sneak] check to approach unseen, and then a @Check[acrobatics|dc:21] or @Check[athletics|dc:21|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] check to either scale the walls or swim through the river. They gain 1 Suppression Point for each failure (2 on a critical failure).

Papers, Please.name: Papers, Please
Papers, Please.text:
Papers, PleaseModerate 4

Harassment by Cheliax loyalists is the status quo as the authorities try to quash dissent in the city. The PCs are approached by such loyalists looking to impress their superiors.

Papers, PleaseModerate 4

@UUID[Actor.DEBpqpV7VebC5K6b]{Adiutor} @UUID[Actor.f82EeyDM6IxHAKVN]{Infantry Soldier}

Creatures: PCs face an adiutor and infantry soldier, who try to arrest the PCs for "suspicious activities." The PCs can successfully explain their presence on the street with a successful @Check[deception|dc:19] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:19] check, or @Check[intimidation|dc:21] check; each DC is increased by 3 in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway]{Chapter 6}. On a failure, the patrol attacks.

Suppression Points.name: Suppression Points
Suppression Points.text:
Suppression Points

When the PCs' Suppression Points reach each threshold, the effects of the government's opposition make their work more difficult. The effects of each threshold are cumulative, but end if the PC's Suppression Points total goes down, reducing the threshold. If a PC kills someone, they must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:10]; on a failure, they gain a Suppression Point.

1. Repression (1–3 SP): Outside of combat, the DC of any skill or Perception checks involving another humanoid are increased by 1.

2. Paranoia (4–6 SP): During the gala, the number of Influence Points to reach each threshold increases by 1.

3. Crackdown (7–9 SP): Each time the PCs go in the city streets, the GM rolls a @Check[flat|dc:5]; on a failure the PCs face the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04papersplease00]{Papers, Please} encounter below.

4. Martial Law (10–12 SP): Outside of combat, the DC of any skill or Perception checks involving another humanoid are increased by 1 (for a total of 2).

Uprising Points.name: Uprising Points
Uprising Points.text:
Uprising Points

When the PCs' Uprising Points reach each threshold for the first time, they gain the listed benefit. Each benefit can be used once by each PC and the PC must be in an area where popular support could affect the situation. This criteria is determined at the GM's discretion; for example, it might be allowed while on Elidir's streets or in the Gyve prison, but not in the steward's manor.

1. Sedition (1–3 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can add +1 to a skill check or Perception check after they have rolled.

2. Subversion (4–6 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can add +1 to an attack roll or saving throw after they have rolled.

3. Insurrection (7–9 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can reroll a check after they have rolled. They must use the second result, even if it's worse. This has the fortune trait.

4. Revolution (10–12 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can roll a check twice and take the better result. This has the fortune trait.

Elidir's Status.name: Elidir's Status
Elidir's Status.text:
Elidir's Status

An open rebellion is closer than ever in Isger's capital, but the army is working hard to maintain order. It's not full-out martial law in the city as Hedvend tries to maintain some semblance of normalcy, but tensions are high. To reflect these competing pressures while in Elidir, the PCs accumulate both Uprising Points, which measure how successful they are in hampering Hedvend's activities and recruiting Hellbreakers, and Suppression Points, which measure the army's awareness of them and ability to quash dissent (refer to Victory Points in GM Core 184–185).

As the PCs reach certain thresholds, they discover opportunities or face additional complications. The points and thresholds accumulate concurrently.

Scene Notes Point Tracking

@UUID[Actor.GpuBXWL10pA0XnNz]{Uprising & Suppression Tracker}

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
Getting Started

Chapter 4 begins when the PCs are summoned by Rhokrag to the Hellbreakers League headquarters.

“I have something new for you all. While we've been working here, Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias have been trying to stir up the capital. But they've run into trouble—the authorities figured out who they are, and they can't work freely anymore.

“They asked me to send a few Hellbreakers I trust to get things done. You've shown your skill and smarts the last few months; we need you in Elidir now. Phoebe says the army is on high alert, and while they mostly ignore us out here in the hinterlands, they keep a tight grip on the capital and the rest of the Conerica Straits. Whatever you do, keep a low profile and do not get identified as League members. Once you get into Elidir, go to the Isgeri Circle and wait. Alceo and Phoebe will have someone checking for you who can bring you to their safe house.”

He shakes his head. “Get going. Hedvend's throwing a gala in about ten days and he doesn't know it, but you're on the guest list.”

@UUID[Actor.f9x0nNSPID5Wdnxv]{Rhokrag's Gift}
Rhokrag can't answer many questions as the message purposely didn't have much detail. He urges the PCs to leave immediately, as it's a three-day journey to Elidir, and gives them a lifting belt for the mission. The trip to the capital passes uneventfully, though if your PCs need more Experience Points to reach 4th level, you can have them encounter bandits, wild animals, roving undead, or some other such encounter on the way.

Into the Jaws.name: Into the Jaws
Into the Jaws.text:
Chapter 4: Into the Jaws

While the PCs were busy in the south of Isger, events were also unfolding in the capital, Elidir. Alceo Demetrias (wise male aiuvarin cleric of Milani 7) and Phoebe Demetrias (righteous female human warrior 7), the leaders of the Hellbreakers League, have been organizing resistance at the heart of the country's critical trade route. The husband and wife have led numerous protests over the hardships faced by those outside the Conerica Straits and the Isgeri government's Cheliax-centric policies. They seek to sow dissent against the country's self-interested elites while generating support and finding recruits for the Hellbreakers League.

As part of their efforts, they have made tentative contact with a Druman trader named Quoster Thistlewait (opportunistic male halfling merchant 4), who has a strong distaste for Cheliax due to its history of slavery and iron grip on the Conerica River trade routes. He is willing to provide supplies in return for a lucrative trade deal when Isger is free of Cheliax.

The protests and disruptions caused by the PCs to the south have alarmed Hedvend VI. He's used the army to crack down on gatherings, and then used the resulting clashes and bloodshed caused by his own forces to characterize the League as violent revolutionaries. Painting largely peaceful protests as vicious riots, he dubbed Alceo and Phoebe the Riotmongers, and placed a bounty on their heads. Unable to act freely, Alceo and Phoebe call for the PCs to come to Elidir.

Though Hedvend has the city on high alert, he is simultaneously trying to convince its citizens—and Caeto Vulaunex (self-righteous male human Hellknight 11), who has newly returned to the country from Cheliax—that the city and country remain firmly under his control. As part of his front, he announced plans for a gala in his manor to mark the 25th anniversary of the Hellknights agreeing to march to Isger's rescue during the Goblinblood Wars.

Unbeknownst to Hedvend and his political opponents, @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} (malevolent female daughter of Urgathoa 9) has determined the time is right to claim the country in the name of Urgathoa. Her follower Ezio Gaeta (crafty male vampire spy 7) plans to lay waste to guests at Hedvend's gala, destabilizing the country for his master's plans.

Epilogue.name: Epilogue
Epilogue.text:
Epilogue

@UUID[Actor.JyWBN2WhJaqPZa9f]{Ezio}
Following their victory, the PCs discover a skeletal encryption ring Ezio used to send coded messages to his agents hidden as part of his costume. The discovery allows them to decrypt the wheel cipher they found among Lefranek's items (if they haven't already), revealing for certain that an Urgathoan faction has gotten involved in the battle for Isger, though there's no information about where they're based or what their next plan is.

Caeto thanks the PCs for solving Hedvend's murder and uncovering Ezio's perfidy. He promises he will do everything he can in his power to build a better country that works for all its citizens. The PCs can tell he is sincere about this. He tells them he hopes they'll be part of his efforts and allows everyone to depart for home.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.XRmncFkiqoBZyGXv]{Caeto's Reward}
Caeto gives the PCs an imposing shield and dreamcrusher as a reward for their work.

Inquiry: Hunting for Hedvend VI.name: Inquiry: Hunting for Hedvend VI
Inquiry: Hunting for Hedvend VI.text:
Inquiry: Hunting for Hedvend VISevere 5

Once the PCs realize a vampiric Hedvend is stalking the mansion, their first inclination might be to try to find him, either by setting up a trap for him or hunting him down. Caeto gives them free rein to do either, though declines to participate. He expresses confidence in the PCs' abilities while at the same time remaining busy making sure the attack in the manor isn't a prelude to a full-scale surprise Hellbreaker attack on Elidir.

Setting a Trap: Following the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventmurders00]{Murders in the Night} event, if the PCs learn that Hedvend is killing people important to the Isgeri government and that his killings all occur in rooms with access to the outdoors, they have all the information they need to set a trap; all they require is bait. They can determine who would make sense to use as a stalking horse with a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check or @Check[society|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check—a success reveals that any of the still-living named victims from the Murders in the Night event would serve well in that role, as would Rencelos Azri. A critical success reveals that Fessy would also be an option.

The next challenge is persuading the bait to play the role. A PC can do so with a successful @Check[deception|dc:20] check to try to trick them into going alone into the PC's ambush site, a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22] check to try to persuade them, or a @Check[intimidation|dc:24] check to try to make them. If the PCs attempt to get Fessy to be the bait, she automatically agrees to help.

Once they have a potential victim, the PCs can choose any Reevesrest location they want for the ambush other than the great room, which remains crowded. Allow them to make any preparations they want. Once they're ready, they can attempt a @Check[flat|dc:6] check every 15 minutes; on a success, Hedvend enters the room and attacks.

Pursuing the Killer: The PCs might want to look for Hedvend's tracks once they realize he's likely hiding outside between murders in the manor but the snowstorm outside makes this difficult. If they persevere, the PCs can track him to the roof of the mausoleum with a successful @Check[survival|dc:25|traits:secret,concentrate,exploration,move,skill,action:track|name:Track] check to Track. If they're successful, the conditions are likely to make this a more difficult fight. Although it's likely still nighttime, the area in a 60-foot radius around the mausoleum is in bright light (and then dim light for another 60 feet) due to the everlight crystals' light reflecting on falling snow. The winter storm imposes a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks and physical ranged attacks, snuffs handheld flames (such as from a torch or candle), and makes creatures concealed if they're more than 30 feet away. The snow cover makes the entire area difficult terrain.

Ezio's Involvement: By the time the PCs face Hedvend, Ezio is fully aware of the threat they pose to him and, more importantly, Illcayna's plans. Considering the secluded nature of this encounter, he sees it as an opportunity to eliminate the PCs and blame it on Hedvend. If you feel that Ezio wouldn't have reason to think the PCs are suspicious of him by the time they face Hedvend, he'll instead face them one-on-one later in the evening.

The PCs might be more concerned with Ezio than Hedvend once they realize that he's the original killer and manipulating events around he gala. They can choose where and how to stage any confrontation, making any necessary preparations. If the PCs confront him, Ezio initially denies any responsibility but finally acknowledges he's lost once the PCs lay out all their evidence.

If the PCs confront Ezio before hunting down Hedvend, Ezio smiles and compliments the PCs on their investigative work, acknowledging that he would likely have gotten away with it if it weren't for them. “Let the devil worshippers and the rebels fight,” he says. “In the end when they fall, our undead army will grow fat with their blood and bodies, and we will reclaim this land for the Pallid Princess! No more will our resources go to feed others. Isger will be for Isger and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}!”

Inquiry: Hunting for Hedvend VISevere 5

@UUID[Actor.xD8oAws7UjuLHpmA]{Hedvend VI} @UUID[Actor.huNrwPlZACOWYpy2]{Ezio Gaeta}

Creatures: Hedvend VI, consumed with hunger, fights until destroyed. If the PCs used an NPC as bait to set a trap, that character flees at the start of the first round of combat. Ezio rolls initiative at the start of the second round of combat and joins the fight at his initiative spot in that round. He enters through a door from the manor interior, using his Change Shape ability if necessary. Fully cognizant that he will be exposed if he doesn't kill all the PCs and expecting that his Cloud of Plague ability will preserve his unlife, Ezio fights until reduced to 0 HP. If Ezio isn't involved in this fight, it becomes a trivial encounter.

Ezio fights until reduced to 0 HP, and fully expects to be able to revive with Cloud of Plague. If Hedvend VI hasn't been destroyed, Ezio summons the vampire steward to aid him. Roll initiative for Hedvend VI, who arrives in [[/r 1d3]] rounds; if the battle takes place in a room with access to the outdoors, he instead arrives in [[/r 1d2]] rounds. If Hedvend isn't involved in this fight, it becomes a moderate encounter.

Event: Lezinia Has Left the Building.name: Event: Lezinia Has Left the Building
Event: Lezinia Has Left the Building.text:
Event: Lezinia Has Left the BuildingModerate 5

This event occurs signals the start of the end game. If the PCs confront Ezio and his Alibi Attack fails to divert attention from him, he triggers it. Otherwise, it should happen after the PCs have completed all available inquiries or after Colonel Rithert has been killed by Hedvend. With telepathic prompting from Ezio, Lezinia loudly decides she does not need to stick around for this investigation, and how dare anyone try to make her! She storms out the front door only to run into the aurocan patrolling the manor walls. The terror is enough to break briefly break Ezio's hold on her, and she flees back into the manor with the guards in hot pursuit.

Event: Lezinia Has Left the BuildingModerate 5

@UUID[Actor.VKIR5MXwtaPyy6uO]{Weak Aurocan}

Creatures: Lezinia races to hide behind the PCs as the aurocan attacks. It fights until either it's destroyed or the PCs convince it they're not trying to escape.

Clear-minded Diva

@UUID[Actor.c9lNFHrdZkLezAp3]{Lezinia's Googles}
There is a small chance that Lezinia will no longer be dominated by Ezio if the PCs discerned that she was under some control and successfully dispelled the magic. In that case, she doesn't confess but gives the PCs the obsidian goggles as a reward for saving her life, automatically letting them see the red cloak in the closet (which they might also find if they search the room).

Suspicious Diva: Following the fight, Caeto orders the terrified singer back to the boudoir and declares that no one may enter or leave that room without his express permission. A concerned-looking Ezio approaches the PC, with whom he says he has the best relationship, and voices his suspicions of Lezinia.

If Ezio is aware the PCs learned about the red cloak he wore earlier in the evening (which he hid in Lezinia's closet), he suggests they search her room If the PCs follow his advice, a guard insists they can't enter without Caeto accompanying him. Caeto joins them at their request.

This scene concludes with Lezinia—under Ezio's control—ultimately confessing to killing Hedvend, but how exactly that plays out depends on the PCs' actions. If they come in and accuse her, she confesses immediately. If they instead want to search the room, she petulantly allows it. A @Check[perception|dc:10|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check to search the room reveals a red cloak balled up around several magical items in the back of Lezinia's closet; on a critical success, the PC realizes there were a number of places it could have been hidden that would have made it far more difficult to find.

Once the PCs accuse her—or if they go to leave without doing so—Lezinia confesses in dramatic fashion. Read or paraphrase the following:

“Fine,” Lezinia suddenly declares. “You caught me! I did it! I killed that miserable old man! He promised me he would marry me and make me queen of Isger. That's what tonight was supposed to be about, our engagement! But then he said he wasn't going to do it; when he still wouldn't agree to marry me, I killed him! I don't know what happened afterward!” She breaks down in sobs.

Because the confession is pure fantasy, Lezinia has few other details she's able to give the PCs and can't say how she supposedly killed Hedvend. She claims she took the items because he owed them to her and wrapped it in the first cloak she found.

If a PC is suspicious, they can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,action:sense-motive|name:Sense Motive] check to Sense Motive. On a success, they know Lezinia isn't acting normally, while a critical success reveals she's certainly being magically controlled.

Regardless of the PCs' reactions, Caeto is suspicious of the unexpected confession and Lezinia's ability to pull off such a calculated murder. He insists the PCs find some way to test if she is a vampire, but if they don't have any other options, he says they should go get a leftover caramelized garlic tart from the kitchen and test her with that. The reference to garlic calls back to the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04eventnothank00]{No Thank You Bite} event in Chapter 4, pointing to Ezio's true status as a vampire; GMs might want to remind players of that moment if they've forgotten, but give them a chance to make the connection themselves first. Alternatively, Caeto could question why they suspected Lezinia, also directing them back toward Ezio.

Lezinia fails whatever test the PCs attempt to determine whether she's a vampire, but she continues to proclaim her guilt. A PC can convince her that she's not a vampire or a murderer with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20] or @Check[intimidation|dc:20] check. If they are successful, Lezinia is confused about why she confessed. She admits that nothing she said is true; she and Hedvend were in a relationship but he hadn't promised her anything, but can't explain anything else.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.Ik7kTJQc2APO5r3C]{Lezinia's Reward}
If the PCs persuade Lezinia that she was not the killer, she rewards them with 200 gp in jewelry gifted to her by Hedvend and the greater whispering wire and oil of revelation that were wrapped with the cloak.

Reward: Award the PCs 30 XP if they persuade Lezinia that she is not a murderer. Award an additional 80 XP if they put the pieces together and realize Ezio's guilt after this inquiry.

The Jig Is Up.name: The Jig Is Up
The Jig Is Up.text:
The Jig Is Up

By the time they have completed all the inquiries, the PCs should have a strong suspicion of vampiric activity. They likely know that Hedvend was killed by a vampire, turned into one himself, and killed a number of people in the last few hours. Some PCs might prioritize finding Hedvend, but Ezio tries to turn their attention to Lezinia.

Event: Fessy's Fear.name: Event: Fessy's Fear
Event: Fessy's Fear.text:
Event: Fessy's Fear Low 5

Ezio's contingency plan involves implicating Lezinia, but he's cunning enough to also try to remove a potential threat to himself and source of support for the PCs: Fessy. He sends the dominated Chelaxian diva to suggest that Fessy find somewhere safe to rest and refresh. Lezinia also provides her with a scroll to summon a celestial that she claims she acquired in Cheliax in case of devil attack. In truth the scroll is from Ezio, and it's tainted by Illcayna's warshard. The scared gnome cleric hides in the private dining room, where she locks the door and falls into an exhausted sleep.

This event ideally occurs if the PCs look for Fessy to help heal them following a battle. A servant informs them that she went to the private dining room on the second floor (area I20) a short while ago. If the PCs don't need Fessy's help, this event occurs after @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventextermi00]{Exterminate the Pests} but before Colonel Rithert's murder by Hedvend. A servant timidly approaches the PCs to express concern about Fessy after seeing her go into the private dining room and never emerge.

The door is locked, but a PC can open it with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks or Force it Open with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|traits:attack,skill,action:force-open|name:Force it Open] check. In either case, the noise startles Fessy awake and she quickly casts from the scroll, summoning a gnokesh just as the PCs open the door.

Event: Fessy's FearLow 5

@UUID[Actor.4YSVjBAc3K9hwsgj]{Elite Gnokesh}

Creatures: Filled with battle lust by the warshard-tainted scroll, the gnokesh takes the PCs for threats and attacks, castigating them as devil worshippers. It continues fighting until slain, despite not being sustained, and ignores any attempts to appeal to its true nature or attempts to stop or Dismiss it.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.3WhbhD8lAocdNxRp]{Fessy's Reward}
As an apology for setting the gnokesh on them, Fessy insists the PCs take her lesser elixir of life and marvelous miniature (horse) to make up for it.

Development: Following the fight, Fessy tearfully apologizes. If she has any heal spells remaining in her divine font, she insists on using them to heal any injured PCs. She informs them that Lezinia suggested she find a safe spot to rest and gave her the scroll to protect herself. A PC can also attempt a @Check[religion|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic] check to Identify Magic. On a success, they recognize that the scroll appears to have been tainted somehow so that the celestial it summoned was enraged.

If the PCs question Lezinia, she remembers getting the scroll in Cheliax, but doesn't recall details. A @Check[perception|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,action:sense-motive|name:Sense Motive] check to Sense Motive reveals her lack of memory seems unusual; she's not so successful that getting such a scroll would be a small matter. On a critical success, a PC realizes her memory has been magically tampered with (though not that she's still currently dominated).

Event: Exterminate the Pests.name: Event: Exterminate the Pests
Event: Exterminate the Pests.text:
Event: Exterminate the Pests Low 5

As the PCs' investigation progresses, they increasingly threaten Ezio's plan and he decides to eliminate them. This event should occur sometime after he approaches the PCs for the first time, likely after they have completed one or two more inquiries and might have discovered signs that point to a vampire in Reevesrest but not yet be certain of its presence. It can take place anywhere in the manor, but you might want to choose an area where the PCs haven't spent much time (and haven't had a fight before), such as the conservatory, downstairs dining room, gallery, or library.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ItTionHYw9zkogLj.PlaylistSound.muw9fVI61dNnDZa7]{Creatures of the Night}

Event: Exterminate the PestsLow 5

@UUID[Actor.7gqakL2Zwo7qTidx]{Creatures of the Night}

Hazard: Ezio summons creatures of the night from the city environs, directing them to kill the PCs. The creatures, which are represented as a hazard, enter the building through the foundations and chimneys and make their way to the PCs. The hazard occupies the entire room where this encounter occurs.

Development: After the PCs defeat the swarms, they can attempt a @Check[religion|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge. On a success, they know that some vampires can summon such creatures and communicate with them telepathically if they're within 100 feet, which means almost certainly somewhere in the manor. On a critical success, they also know only more powerful vampires have such abilities, and such creatures can also likely turn into mist and dominate lesser-minded creatures.

Event: The Alibi Attack.name: Event: The Alibi Attack
Event: The Alibi Attack.text:
Event: The Alibi Attack

It's possible the PCs become suspicious of Ezio early in this chapter, likely if they discover he was seen talking with a named victim of Hedvend in a @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventmurders00]{Event: Murders in the Night} event. If they attempt to question or confront him, he triggers this event. Allow the PCs to have a brief interaction with Ezio, who rejects any allegations of culpability in the night's events. Even as he talks to the PCs, he telepathically commands Hedvend to go to the servants' parlor (area I11) and kill the first creature he sees there (if the PCs happen to be in the servants' parlor, the killing takes place outside the upstairs storeroom). The PCs' questioning is then interrupted either by a scream if they're near the murder scene or the panicked arrival of a servant.

Unlike most of the murders Ezio orchestrates, the hurried nature of this one leaves a witness: the unfortunate Otton Nettlebrush. He babbles that something was trying to eat the human woman who now lies dead and bleeding on the floor. A PC can attempt to calm him down with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20] or @Check[medicine|dc:20] or a @Check[intimidation|dc:22] check. If they succeed, Otton tearfully admits it looked like Hedvend before it scrambled outside when he screamed (either through the door or, if the attack occurred upstairs, through the window).

Development: If the PCs return to the conversation with Ezio, he attempts to lead them to the conclusion that he can't be responsible since there was another killing while he was in their presence without outright saying so. If the PCs press the issue, he triggers @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventlezinia00]{Event: Lezinia Has Left the Building}, and the mystery moves into its end game.

Event: Murders in the Night.name: Event: Murders in the Night
Event: Murders in the Night.text:
Event: Murders in the Night

Hedvend strikes again, killing another person in the mansion. This event occurs multiple times over the course of the night, repeating every hour or so until the PCs discover the murderer(s), adding urgency to the PCs' investigation and possibly narrowing their pool of suspects. In terms of gameplay, the event likely follows every 1–2 completed inquiries. While several of the targets are selected to weaken Isger, others are random victims of Hedvend's hunger. Ezio's targets are killed in the following order, interspersed with unfortunate guards and servants. The location and circumstances of the deaths are included below, while the guards and servants can be found in any room with access to outside.

  • Merpelia Carafo, whom Ezio targets to end her support of Isger's army, is murdered in the gallery.
  • Ambassador Vrig, targeted to prevent any chance of an alliance with Oprak, is killed in the library.
  • Sastoli Brunc, whose command of the docks facilitates Isger's trade, is killed in the kitchen (Hedvend climbs down through the chimney).
  • Colonel Rithert, an important logistics officer in the Army, in the conservatory.

With a successful @Check[perception|dc:20] check to examine a body, a PC reveals a pair of fang marks on the victim's neck. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:20] check to examine the body reveals the same, and that the likely cause of death appears to be exsanguination.

The first time a named target is killed, the PCs can attempt a @Check[isger-lore|dc:21|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check or @Check[society|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge to realize the death would be an additional blow to Isger's government. For each subsequent named target, reduce the DC by 1. They can attempt the same check, at the current DC, after each guard or servant's death to realize that they don't seem to fit the pattern, and could have simply been in the wrong place at the wrong time.

A PC who wants to learn more about a victim's actions or behavior in their final moments can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information. The DC for an unnamed servant or guard is 20, with a success revealing they were acting normally and doing their job. The DC for a named victim begins at @Check[diplomacy|dc:25|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information], and goes down by 1 for each subsequent victim. On a success, PCs can learn that the victim was last seen speaking with Ezio. On a critical success, PCs learn that they seemed to be having an intense conversation with a lot of direct eye contact, before the victim seemed to just turn and wander away. See @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventthealib00]{Event: The Alibi Attack} (below) and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05thejigisup0000]{The Jig Is Up} for Ezio's reactions if they confront him.

After Ambassador Vrig's death, and each subsequent death, a PC can attempt a @Check[architecture-lore|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[crafting|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge to realize the each death is occurring in a room with a window to the outside, or in a room that has a chimney.

Development: If the PCs realize all the deaths are in rooms with access to outside, they can warn guests to avoid them. This prevents any further reoccurrences of this event.

Reward: If the PCs learn any of the deaths are intended to harm the Isgeri government, award them 30 XP. If they learn of Ezio's conversations with any of the victims, award them an additional 30 XP. If the PCs warn gala guests to stay out of rooms with access to the outdoors, award them 80 XP.

Event: Ezio Gets Involved.name: Event: Ezio Gets Involved
Event: Ezio Gets Involved.text:
Event: Ezio Gets Involved

Ezio becomes concerned when he sees Caeto summon the PCs at the start of the chapter, and decides he needs to involve himself with this unexpected complication to his plans. He approaches them the first time they descend from the second floor after their meeting with Caeto, likely during the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05inquiryfalse00]{False Hellbreakers} or Get the Dirt inquiry. He plays the role of concerned guest, asking PCs for information about what's happening. If the PCs successfully influenced him at all during the previous chapter, he offers to help them again, suggesting he could facilitate any discussions with other guests thanks to his connections or anything else the PCs need. He attempts to keep tabs on the PCs throughout the course of this chapter, steering them in directions he wants while disrupting their investigation as much as possible. He doesn't take the risk of attempting to Dominate them, however.

The Plot Thickens.name: The Plot Thickens
The Plot Thickens.text:
The Plot Thickens

Events don't remain static in the mansion as the PCs investigate. While most of the NPCs wait anxiously, some wander around the mansion, falling prey to Hedvend—either to sate his hunger or at Ezio's instructions. Ezio, meanwhile, works to obfuscate his role and create confusion. The events likely occur in generally the following order, though some might need to happen sooner or later depending on what the PCs do and your needs to keep the story engaging for players.

Inquiry: The Red Cloak.name: Inquiry: The Red Cloak
Inquiry: The Red Cloak.text:
Inquiry: The Red Cloak

The PCs might want to find the red cloak that Ezio wore while dominating a number of people in the gala. Unfortunately, he hid it in Lezinia's closet in the boudoir. Unless they begin a room-by-room search, this is a dead end, leading to more @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventmurders00]{Murders in the Night} events and making Ezio aware the PCs know about the cloak and are searching for it. Should the PCs somehow find it ahead of Ezio's schedule, he brings it up later in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05eventlezinia00]{Lezinia Has Left the Building}.

Inquiry: Soiled Sheets.name: Inquiry: Soiled Sheets
Inquiry: Soiled Sheets.text:
Inquiry: Soiled SheetsModerate 5

PCs who become aware of the dirty tracks in Hedvend's bedroom or the boudoir might want to follow them, which they can attempt to do with a @Check[survival|dc:20|traits:secret,concentrate,exploration,move,skill,action:track|name:Track] check to Track (on a critical success, they make out enough details to determine the dirt comes from a Small creature wearing shoes and with a tail that dragged through the soil). The tracks lead from Hedvend's bedroom, through the secret door into the boudoir, and then through the halls to the servant stairway in the western part of the manor, before ultimately leading outside through the servant's entrance to the family mausoleum.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.9heJxTjbFklr8au8]{Toggle Path}

Shows the path of the footprints on both Manor Floors as a red line leading south.

A large stone mausoleum is lit by softly glowing everlight crystals, which almost seem to sparkle in the falling snow. Trimmed hedges, small trees, and a few topiaries surround the historic resting place of stewards, creating a sense of serenity, even amid the storm.
