Use the Mausoleum map. The winter storm imposes a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks and physical ranged attacks, snuffs out handheld flames, and makes creatures concealed if they're more than 30 feet away. The snow cover makes the entire area difficult terrain. Although it's likely nighttime when the PCs investigate, the area in a 60-foot radius around the mausoleum is in bright light (and then dim light for another 60 feet) due to the crystals' light reflecting on falling snow.

Inquiry: Soiled SheetsModerate 5

@UUID[Actor.lQOR92VHNA0IwFmf]{Hound Topiaries (2)} @UUID[Actor.D5PSX1wUjlao8R29]{Tiger Topiary}

Creatures: Unfortunately for the PCs, Ezio's attack on Hedvend activated some of the manor's magical defenses. They don't respond to manor servants but the PCs don't have that protection, and three topiaries leave their perches and attack. They fight until destroyed.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.izPbOXJC8sHRDu4f]{Animate Topiaries}

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.9284ep46pd6le3SM]{Living Topiary Remains}
The PCs discover a primeval mistletoe among the remains of the living topiaries.

Reward: Award the PCs 30 XP if they successfully track the soil to the servant.

Development: After the fight, PCs can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:18|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check to search around the mausoleum. On a success, they find a small recently dug hole in the soil, and an imp tail torn off one of the costumes being worn by the manor servants. PCs who investigate the mausoleum discover that it's locked, with no evidence that it's been opened anytime recently.

PCs can attempt to find the servant with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information, @Check[perception|dc:20] check to spot them, or a @Check[survival|dc:20|traits:secret,concentrate,exploration,move,skill,action:track|name:Track] check to Track. If they succeed, the scared servant confesses that a person in a red cloak with burning eyes told them to go dig up the dirt from outside the mausoleum and put it on Hedvend's body, which was in the bedroom at the time. The servant doesn't remember any other details about the person in the cloak.

Inquiry: Private Dining Room.name: Inquiry: Private Dining Room
Inquiry: Private Dining Room.text:
Inquiry: Private Dining Room

Fortunately for the PCs, while Ezio is a canny conspirator, Lefranek was far less capable. As she prepared for the false Hellbreaker attack in the private dining room, Lefranek left her devil costume and other incriminating items here. PCs can discover these items if they search this room, which is where Lefranek brought the guards to be dominated.

In addition to Lefranek's discarded devil costume, the PCs find 12 vertebrae fused into a column. Each vertebrae spins independently and is inscribed with several letters in Necril. The device is a magical wheel cipher, used by agents of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} to send coded messages. The most recent message was: “Bring the guards to a servant cloaked in our most sacred color. Illcayna will reward you when Isger is hers.”

  • A PC who succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:15] check recognizes the vertebrae as part of a human spine.
  • A PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[society|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge recognizes the contraption is a wheel cipher used to encode and decode messages.
  • A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge recognizes the wheel cipher as a tool used by agents of Urgathoa.
  • A PC can attempt a @Check[arcana|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic], @Check[nature|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic], @Check[religion|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic], or @Check[occultism|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic] check to Identify Magic. Doing so gives them a +2 circumstance bonus on a Society check to Decipher Writing, or +4 on a critical success.

Finally, a PC can attempt a @Check[society|dc:25|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:decipher-writing|name:Decipher Writing] check to Decipher Writing; on a success they decipher enough of the message to understand it included instructions from an Urgathoan, telling the recipient to bring their fellow guards to a red-cloaked man in the dining room, and that the plot was masterminded by someone named Illcayna, who seeks control of the country.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.8JnE86NiFCK47GLb]{Table}
Left on the table by Lefranek is a platter of putrid dreams and a skeleton key.

Reward: Award the PCs 30 XP if they succeed on at least one check to learn about the Urgathoan wheel cipher. If they Decipher the Writing and learn the message, award them an additional 80 XP.

Inquiry: Second Victim.name: Inquiry: Second Victim
Inquiry: Second Victim.text:
Inquiry: Second Victim

One of the manor guards was searching for clues to Hedvend's murder in the guest room when the vampire steward slipped in from outside and ripped out his throat before drinking as much of the guard's blood as he could. When the PCs enter the room, read or paraphrase the following:

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.eBX8nN1bRnBdX6el]{Toggle Body}

Toggles the body tile in I17

A small spray of blood covers the floor around a corpse in chain mail and the uniform of the manor guard. A frozen expression of shock remains on the man's face above where his throat was brutally torn out.

A PC can attempt a @Check[medicine|dc:18] check to examine the body. If their check exceeds the DC listed below, they learn the following:

  • DC 18: It appears the guard's throat was torn out by claws.
  • DC 20: Based on the lack of any defensive wounds, the guard likely was taken by surprise.
  • DC 22: There's less blood than there should be based on the guard's size. The spray looks like it came from the killing blow, but there's a conspicuous lack of a pool of blood afterward.
  • DC 25: The guard has fang marks on his neck, which likely were made moments after he was killed.

A PC can also attempt a @Check[perception|dc:20] check to examine the room. On a success, they discover the floor is slightly damp around the window A @Check[nature|dc:20] or @Check[survival|dc:20] check indicates the dampness is because the window was opened briefly, allowing in snow that then melted; Hedvend moved in and out of the room by opening the window with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.pwzdSlJgYqN7bs2w]{Telekinetic Hand}.

Reward: Award the PCs 30 XP for each discovery they make here, up to 150 XP if they learn everything about the body and the open window.

Inquiry: Hedvend's Body.name: Inquiry: Hedvend's Body
Inquiry: Hedvend's Body.text:
Inquiry: Hedvend's Body

Hedvend's body was taken to his private quarters, where it was laid on his bed. A single Hellknight stands guard at the ornate double doors that lead into the room, but she allows the PCs to enter freely. Unfortunately, the PCs' efforts to examine the body are doomed to failure: Hedvend's body is missing!

Thick velvet maroon curtains cover the walls and a bearskin rug covers the floor of this luxurious grand bedroom. A glaive seemingly made of folded silver hangs as a trophy above the fireplace, where flames dance in a cold breeze. A drift of snow and a melting puddle both grow beneath an open window. Against the southern wall, a neatly made canopy bed shows no sign of an occupant except for a slight indent in the heavy quilt.

A closer examination of the scene reveals what appears to be a few handfuls of dirt scattered across the bed. PCs who investigate the dirt can attempt a @Check[nature|dc:20] check. On a success, they recognize it as freshly dug soil, likely from the manor grounds; a requirement for the steward's vampiric awakening. Upon awakening as undead, Hedvend VI escaped out the window, which he left open. (A PC can attempt a @Check[nature|dc:20] or @Check[survival|dc:20] check to realize the snow and puddle indicate the window was opened only recently).

In addition to the clues above that PCs can see with no real difficulty, they can Search the room. If their check exceeds the DC listed below, they discover additional clues:

  • DC 20: The rug also has dirt on it, as if it were tracked into the room at some point. (If they choose to investigate it, see the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05inquirysoile00]{Soiled Sheets Inquiry}.)
  • DC 22: Small scratches on the floor against the western wall indicate a secret door leading into the suite's boudoir (installed decades ago to allow discrete assignations).
  • DC 30: The tracks on the rug clearly were made by a Small creature wearing shoes. It appears whoever made them came in from the secret door in the west, moved to the bed, then turned around and retraced their steps.

Scene Notes Macros

@UUID[Macro.UJH0M5ZaUTlhx6eO]{Toggle Puddle} @UUID[Macro.rjENZRZJkeJSrSbi]{Toggle Rug Footprints}

The Hellknight guard is shocked if the PCs inform her that Hedvend's body is missing and rushes in to verify the claim. Other than the PCs, she hasn't seen anyone enter or exit since she was placed here to guard the body. She was unaware of the secret door and had no reason to think anyone could enter or exit Hedvend's bedroom without her knowledge.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.DG5jtaLYcQW35Zpg]{Hidden Compartment}
A PC who Searched the room (@Check[perception|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search]) discovers a hidden compartment with ledgers tracking bribes and corruption in and outside of the city. This ledger is worth 400 gp to the right people, though it might be worth even more to others. An astute PC also notices the glaive is a magical item, but the PCs won't have the opportunity to claim it for themselves until @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway]{Chapter 6}.

Reward: If the PCs discover the tracks in Hedvend's room, award them 30 XP.

Inquiry: Scene of the Crime.name: Inquiry: Scene of the Crime
Inquiry: Scene of the Crime.text:
Inquiry: Scene of the Crime

A solid wooden door hangs off its hinges, revealing a stately game room. The taxidermied heads of several monsters look down from the walls while the smoldering remains of a fire burn in the ornate fireplace.

An ivory and mahogany game table fills much of the space, with a half dozen well-cushioned chairs arranged around it. One chair at the head of the table is overturned and speckled with blood. In front of the overturned chair, a hand of cards is laid out face up on the table and a single key sits nearby. A second hand of cards rests face down in front of an adjacent seat.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.DtxLjSp0guKb9Gfz]{Toggle Crime Scene}

Hedvend VI was in his game room passing the time before his grand entrance to the gala when he met with Ezio and his demise. After killing the steward, Ezio locked the door and slipped out using Mist Form. He returned to the party downstairs, where he waited for the inevitable discovery. A short time later, Caeto searched for the steward after the false Hellbreaker attacks and broke the door down, discovering Hedvend's body.

The room offers a number of clues for observant PCs. Some players might notice these or ask specifically about these topics but if not, point out the clues to PCs who succeed at a listed skill check.

  • @Check[games-lore|dc:18], @Check[society|dc:20]: Two sets of cards at the table suggest Hedvend knew his killer and was not surprised at their presence.
  • @Check[athletics|dc:20] or @Check[perception|dc:20]: There are no signs of a struggle in the room, indicating that Hedvend was somehow subdued or that he had no chance to react to the attack (Ezio dominated Hedvend).
  • @Check[medicine|dc:20] or @Check[perception|dc:20]: There are a few drops of blood in one of the chairs, but not enough to indicate a major wound (Ezio drank most of the blood).
  • @Check[crafting|dc:20] or @Check[thievery|dc:20]: The key is on the table next to where Hedvend was sitting, indicating that the room was locked from the inside and the killer was then able to leave the locked room.

@UUID[Actor.Q6UPUaPpUWFsst2z]{Crime Scene}
In addition to the clues above that PCs can see with no real difficulty, they can Search the room. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:18|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check notices a small brass hourglass talisman filled with a black sand under the table. This was a grave time talisman that Illcayna created with her warshard to expedite the process of transforming Hedvend into Ezio's vampire servitor. Ezio affixed the talisman to Hedvend's body but it was inadvertently knocked off by Caeto's men when they moved the steward, leaving the talisman still intact and Hedvend in a state of near-feral perpetual hunger.

A PC who closely examines the hourglass can attempt a @Check[nature|dc:20] check; on a success they realize the sand is actually onyx. With a successful @Check[religion|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge, a PC is aware that onyx is used in rituals to create undead. A PC can also attempt to Identify Magic on the talisman with a @Check[religion|dc:22|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic] check; on a success, the PC understands the item would affect the flow of time on a body, likely to preserve it or accelerate its decomposition. Note any critical success on this check—when the PCs start realizing a vampire is involved in the murders, the PC realizes the talisman could also make it as if three nights had passed in an instant, the time typically required for a creature to be buried in the earth before turning into a vampire servitor.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.WJvBE0F3K0ZEhOnI]{Under Table}
Underneath a table is an onyx idol of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} worth 10 gp.

Reward: If the PCs discover the grave time talisman, award them 30 XP. Award them an additional 30 XP if they discover either the presence of onyx or identify the talisman's purpose.

Inquiry: False Hellbreakers.name: Inquiry: False Hellbreakers
Inquiry: False Hellbreakers.text:
Inquiry: False Hellbreakers

Caeto had the false Hellbreakers taken to the guard post (area I13). Survivors are bound hand and foot with good-quality manacles. Caeto gives PCs free rein in their investigation except that the guards can't be freed. Caeto has a single scroll of talking corpse available (@UUID[Actor.YXMu6EcOZtuKaED5]{Caeto's Scroll}), which he allows the PCs to use if all of the guards are dead (Fessy can cast the spell if no PC is able to).

The lower-level fakes, including those that attacked the Hellknights, were guards that Ezio magically dominated. A PC can Coerce them into answering questions with an @Check[intimidation|dc:15|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental,skill,action:coerce|name:Coerce] check against their DC 15 Will save. If the PCs attempt to use talking corpse on any deceased guards, they answer willingly and truthfully. Each tells the same tale: Lefranek brought them to the private dining room, supposedly to meet with Hedvend on a minor matter. Instead, they found a red-cloaked individual there. The last thing each remembers was looking into the figure's eyes and feeling that they needed to obey their commands.

The leader of the false Hellbreaker attack, Lefranek Meyal, is an Urgathoan cultist who infiltrated Hedvend's guards at Illcayna's instructions. She has more knowledge of the plot, though she's unaware of Ezio's identity and his role in events. Before the gala, she received a coded message that instructed her to bring her fellow guards to Hedvend's private dining room. There, Ezio cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate} on them and sent them to kill as many guests at the gala as they could with Lefranek as their willing leader.

If alive, Lefranek is largely uncooperative during any attempts to get information, though the PCs can try several different methods. PCs can attempt to Coerce her with a @Check[intimidation|dc:19|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental,skill,action:coerce|name:Coerce] check, but they take a –2 circumstance penalty, as Lefranek isn't afraid of dying. With a successful @Check[perception|dc:19|traits:concentrate,secret,action:sense-motive|name:Sense Motive] check to Sense Motive, a PC discerns this information; on a critical success, a PC realizes she's afraid of dying without the chance to be turned into an undead, which they can use to negate the penalty. PCs could also try to trick her up in conversation with a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:21] check or a @Check[deception|dc:23|traits:action:impersonate,concentrate,exploration,manipulate,secret|name:Impersonate] to impersonate another false Hellbreaker.

If Lefranek is dead, the PCs can attempt to use the scroll of talking corpse on her. If they successfully get her to talk, Lefranek brags about her role in the plot, calling it the first step in freeing Isger from the tyranny of Cheliax and delivering it for "the Bountiful Lady of Harvests." A successful @Check[religion|dc:20] check reveals this is a title for @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} based off an ancient Isgeri conception of her as a harvest goddess. Lefranek admits she delivered the other guards to a person in a red cloak, but truthfully says she doesn't know who it was.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.WwH4zSijH7jaOQie]{Supply Closet}
Otton Nettlebrush approaches the PCs, finding them less intimidating than the Hellknights, and nervously informs them that he saw Lefranek leave a supply closet during the gala. Following his tip, the PCs uncover a staff of the dead and an intricately carved onyx skull for ritual practices worth 200 gp.

Reward: If the PCs get any information from any of the false Hellbreakers, award them 30 XP. Award them an additional 30 XP if they learn of Lefranek's allegiance to Urgathoa.

The Game's Afoot.name: The Game's Afoot
The Game's Afoot.text:
The Game's Afoot

After about an hour, a nervous-looking servant approaches the PCs, informing them that Caeto Vulaunex wishes to speak with them. If they agree, she escorts them upstairs to the study (area I21), which Caeto has appropriated for his own uses as it gives him privacy, but also lets him easily step out to look down on what's happening in the great room. If the PCs refuse to accompany her, Caeto comes down to ask them to meet with him. If they still refuse, he promises the PCs that no harm will come to them and they are not in trouble. Read or paraphrase the following:

“I'm told you were responsible for stopping those Hellbreakers from killing everyone at the gala. That, along with a new development, has convinced me you were not involved with this slaying. Given that, and your obvious skill, I would like to ask you to investigate what is happening here. I thought there was likely one or two more conspirators among the partygoers who I would uncover, but this new development…”

His expression darkens. “Someone, or something, killed one of my guards. I'm convinced there's more going on here. However, following Hedvend's death, I need to make sure the city and country are secure. My guards are talented, but they are not investigators. It would appear you are my best option. If you agree, you will be allowed free movement to investigate, though you will still not be allowed to leave the manor grounds until these murders are solved and the captor killed or in custody.”

The A-ha Moment!

One of the most iconic moments in a good murder mystery is when the intrepid detective puts together all the assorted clues—the seemingly obvious facts and innocuous observations—to suddenly realize who the culprit is (the investigator class plays heavily on this very idea). While a novel author has free rein to create that moment, it might not be as obvious for players in a tabletop roleplaying game. Some players who are attuned to such stories might pick up on some of the clues in the ensuing pages and piece them together. But for those who aren't, you can offer skill checks to help the PCs make those connections—suggested skills and DCs are listed with many clues. (If the PCs are having fun with the mystery, you could even make the checks secretly, noting any success, and doling out realizations to the players later if they get stuck, or at dramatic moments.)

Another option is to have Caeto stop in to check up on the PCs and point out something they might be missing, though take care not to let him steal the spotlight as he's busy preparing to declare martial law over Isger.

This is an opportunity for the PCs to get themselves out of this situation and uncover the mystery of the false Hellbreakers. They could even earn favor with the apparent new leader of Isger, which would be a major opportunity for the League. Once the PCs agree, they have four likely initial approaches to begin solving the mystery: the false Hellbreakers, the murder scene, Hedvend's corpse, and the slain guard. Give players the opportunity to decide what to do first, but Caeto can suggest any or all of those if they need help getting started. He tells the PCs to keep him informed of any developments, and that he will try to provide anything they need to help them solve the crimes. The inquiries below detail avenues of investigation the PCs might undertake, including ones that develop after the four initial approaches.

Reevesrest.name: Reevesrest
Reevesrest.text:
I. Reevesrest

The steward's home is made of fine wood, with reinforced doors, which are unlocked during the gala. The first floor is 15 feet high (except for parts of the great room that are open to the building's roof, 25 feet up), and the second floor is 10 feet high. Most rooms have one or more fireplaces or braziers going to keep them warm against the cold Abadius weather. The windows are closed with wooden shutters, which are locked with a simple bar from the inside; from outside, the DC to Force them Open is 22. Magical lights provide bright light in the entire household. Below are basic descriptions of the areas; note that several of them have more specific details related to the mystery of Hedvend VI's murder and the false Hellbreakers described later in the chapter.

I1: Vestibule: The dark wood of the formal entrance is engraved with numerous nearly invisible runes, which trigger magical traps. They are all deactivated during the gala.

I2. Great room: The stewards of Isger built the great room to impress visitors. The opulent chamber features high ceilings across much of the eastern portion of the room. A stage offers a place for musicians and other entertainers to perform. A grand staircase with painted balustrades leads to the second floor. The walls are painted with murals supposedly depicting Isger's greatness.

I3. Library: The library, like the great room, is designed to impress visitors. Four of its walls are lined with shelves reaching to the ceiling, each filled with books. Ladders on rollers make it easy to reach the books on the upper shelves. The books are carefully curated to be acceptable to Chelaxian tastes.

I4. Privy: Reevesrest contains several privies. The upstairs privies also contain bathtubs.

I5. Statue hall: This room has a statue of a stern-looking woman wearing the amulet denoting Isger's stewards. A plaque identifies her as Adraldine I, the first steward of Isger.

I6. Art gallery: The art gallery features valuable art and artifacts collected by stewards over the centuries. Large paintings hang on the wall showing scenes supposedly from Isger's history, though designed to convey modern messages: the original Isgeri tribe surrendering to Taldor's army, and later Cheliax coming to Isger's rescue during the Even-Tongued Conquest.

I7. Conservatory: Plants, many of them edible, grow in barrels in this greenhouse, which remains warm and moist thanks to druidic magic arranged by an early steward. Wide windows let in the light during the day.

I8. Kitchen: The well-stocked, well-equipped kitchen is designed to provide almost anything the steward or their guests could want at any time of day or night. A fire always burns here, and usually two or three chefs and bakers are cooking or ready to cook. That number increases to a half dozen during events like the gala.

I9. Storeroom: Reevesrest contains several well-organized store rooms. On the first floor, the one attached to the conservatory contains gardening supplies, and one attached to the kitchen contains cooking staples (though most goods are brought in fresh daily). Upstairs, a larger storeroom contains linens.

I10. Dining room: A silver chandelier drips with crystals. The massive table is an incredible slab of black marble resting on an elaborate duskwood stand with feet carved to resemble a dragon's. Duskwood chairs evoke Isger's role in the Inner Sea, with a trading ship carved into the headrest and the armrests evoking the waves of the Conerica River.

I11. Servants' parlor: This room serves as an entrance and gathering place for the manor's servants. Shelves along the walls contain fine dishes, silverware and other such serving items.

I12. Servant's quarters: Several servants—the majordomo, head chef, and chamberlain—live full-time in the manor, staying in these small rooms. Each contains a bed, dresser and other personal effects.

I13. Guard post: This is the headquarters for the steward's personal guard, who also take care of Reevesrest's security. A table and several chairs let guards relax when they are not on duty but still required to stay available in case of emergency.

I14. Guard quarters: The heads of the steward's guard live on the premises, in these rooms. Each contains a bed, as well as a chest containing their personal items.

I15: Armory: The armory contains a number of weapons of all types for the guards' use.

I16. Upstairs landing: The grand staircase in the great room leads to the upper landing, which runs almost the entire length of the manor. The eastern portion is open so the steward and his closest guests can participate and be seen during events without having to mingle with those of lesser importance. Painted balustrades at about waist height for a human provide some minimal protection from a fall.

I17. Guest room: This impressive, opulent bedroom serves personal guests of the steward. It contains a large canopied bed and numerous dressers. Padded benches line the northern seating area, where guests can take in a view of the entire city through the floor-to-ceiling windows. An attached room (I17a) contains beds for a pair of servants or guards permitted to guests.

I18. Game room: This room offers a private, less formal area for the steward to relax with guests. It contains a game table with built-in drawer. A mounted cabinet on the wall contains pipes, tobacco, bottles of liquor, and crystal goblets.

I19. Hedvend's bedroom: Hedvend's bedroom is his primary living space. It includes a large, comfortable bed, dressers and chests for his clothing, and other personal items. Personal trophies, gifts, and other items celebrating him and his governorship of Isger hang on the walls.

I20. Private dining room: The upstairs dining room offers a smaller area where the steward can eat. Padded chairs surround a duskwood table, formal enough to not offend any guests here, but also more comfortable for a steward and their family to dine together.

I21. Private study: The private study contains Hedvend VI's personal papers, including correspondence with other rulers and various other matters of state.

I22. Solarium: This octagonal room is designed for stewards to relax. It contains several comfortable padded chairs and benches, as well as book cases filled with novels and other relaxing reads. Windows offer an expansive view of the city.

I23. Boudoir: This private bedroom in the steward's apartments was designed for their family, offering separate quarters should they be needed. In the case of single stewards, like Hedvend VI, it officially serves as another guest quarters, though the secret door connecting it to the steward's bed chamber gives easy access to occupants for romantic assignations. Lezinia and Hedvend have taken advantage of this private passage since she settled in the chamber following her arrival in Elidir several months ago.

Dramatis Personae.name: Dramatis Personae
Dramatis Personae.text:
Dramatis Personae

The cast of this chapter is largely the same as in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth]{Chapter 4}, though several of the NPCs introduced there play different roles here:

Steward Hedvend VI is dead, long unlive Steward Hedvend VI. In the immediate aftermath of Hedvend's death, Caeto had his body moved to his bedroom and left to lie there in a respectful manner until his murder is solved and he can be properly buried. Unknown to Caeto, Ezio Gaeta transformed Hedvend into a vampire by using a unique talisman Illcayna created with her warshard to expedite the usual three-day transformation process. Hedvend is partially under Ezio's control and being used as a weapon to take out more of Elidir's elite. However, the rapid transformation process has left him ravenously hungry and he is also feeding on random innocents in the mansion. When he's not actively hunting, Hedvend climbs out of the manor and hides at Ezio's command.

Where's Quoster?

While Quoster is an important part of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth]{Chapter 4} and plays a role again in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway]{Chapter 6}, he has little to do in this chapter and is not a target of Ezio or Hedvend. He tries to keep his distance from the PCs so as not to tip off anyone to his deal with the Hellbreakers League and urges them to do the same if they approach him.

Caeto Vulaunex enlists the PCs' help once a second body is discovered in the manor. Already impressed by the PCs for their fight in the great room, he knows they aren't responsible for the second death because they are under guard at the time and concludes they are likely not responsible for Hedvend's either. Caeto serves as an ally at this point, and PCs should be allowed to believe that he could, in the right circumstances, end up as a long-term friend in their struggle for Isger. While he is already privately planning how he will fill the vacuum left by Hedvend's death, he remains interested in the investigation in the manor and checks in with the PCs on their progress. He can also be used to help push the investigation forward if needed, giving you a chance to lead players to hints if they appear stuck or frustrated.

Ezio Gaeta fully expected the mansion to be locked down after Hedvend's murder, which he saw as a perfect opportunity to cause more death. He assumes the Hellbreakers League will take the blame for the night's events, leaving him free to continue as Urgathoa's agent among Isger's new leadership. Ezio has multiple contingency plans ready including pinning the blame for the murder on Lezinia, whom he Dominated early in the evening. When the PCs get involved, he tries to befriend them so he can stay fully informed of their investigation and manipulate them as needed. He doesn't reveal his true self until he is absolutely forced to.

Death Notice.name: Death Notice
Death Notice.text:
Death Notice

Once everyone is in a stable condition, read or paraphrase the following.

The tromp of heavy boots cuts short the continuing sound of screams and crying, silencing everything but the moans of the wounded. As armor-clad guards take up positions at all of the exits to the room, a Hellknight in full plate mail—Paralictor Caeto Vulaunex—moves to the top of the stairs. The knights look slightly battered, as if they've just had their own battle.

Caeto looks down and calls out: “Ladies and gentlemen, I regret to inform you that Hedvend VI, steward of all Isger, has been murdered!” Gasps fill the room. “You are all under arrest until we get to the bottom of this. Remain in this room for your own safety. Certain magical defenses have activated with the attack, so leaving the manor could be dangerous. In addition, the guards outside will assume anyone who tries to leave is complicit in this heinous crime, and they will be dealt with accordingly.”

It should be clear to the PCs that trying to fight their way out past Caeto's forces would almost certainly be a fatal mistake. The PCs have about an hour to recover before events conspire to force them to take action. Fessy approaches and offers to heal them if needed (she has four 2nd-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal} spells in her divine font and offers to cast them as the PCs need, either now or later during this chapter). PCs also gain access to any benefits they receive from becoming level 5, such as an alchemist's field discovery, additional spell slots, etc.

The other guests are in shock at the events of the last hour. They largely huddle in small groups, whispering about the events and what they might mean for Isger. Who will rule Isger going forward is a big topic among the more politically inclined as Hedvend VI had no clear successor.

Into the Fray!.name: Into the Fray!
Into the Fray!.text:
Into the Fray!

False HellbreakersModerate 5

This combat takes place in the manor's great room (area I2) and the eastern part of the upstairs landing (area I16) that overlooks the floor. The ceiling of the western part of the great room and below the landing is 15 feet high; it's 25 feet high in the eastern portion of the room where it reaches to the top of the manor. The upstairs landing has small railings that provide some measure of safety, but otherwise is open below, making it a perfect vantage for archers. Banners on the wall help anyone trying to Climb; @Check[athletics|dc:20|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb].

False HellbreakersModerate 5

@UUID[Actor.38afCYk9Mog2oXup]{Lefranek Meyal} @UUID[Actor.zNPHuRYPp2mQpnSF]{False Hellbreakers (2)} @UUID[Actor.iEq4ocsfXPYYl6Dr]{Gala Crowd}

Creatures: Lefranek descends the stairs to prevent anyone from coming up. She Denounces at least once every round, trying to ratchet up anger against the Hellbreakers League. She arranges the guards to be at each end of the landing. They target the gala crowd (see hazard, below) until the PCs act, then typically use their first 2 actions to target them, and their third action to target the crowd until they run out of arrows or a PC approaches, at which point they switch to their trident and whip. The third false Hellbreaker stays at the foot of the stairs, trying to prevent anyone from reaching the archers.

Hazard: The floor of the great room teems with guests (excluding Ezio, who is killing Hedvend in the game room). Unlike most hazards, this one doesn't intentionally take actions to hurt the PCs, but does get in the way. The crowd is so packed guests can't easily escape, and the floor is considered difficult terrain—but also provides lesser cover to the PCs. If the PCs Disable the hazard, they clear the floor. However, damage done by the false Hellbreakers on the hazard represents people they've killed, and for every 10 damage, the Hellbreakers League loses 1 Reputation Point (up to 6 Reputation Points), representing the reaction to the carnage that's blamed on the rebellion.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.rs89hip0G4FJeVTD]{Toggle Gala Crowd}

Toggles Difficult Terrain and panicking crowd ambience.

Development: If any PCs are dying following the battle with the false Hellbreakers, immediately resolve recovery checks or actions to save them, though they won't have time immediately to Treat Wounds or use other exploration activities.

Dead Man's Party.name: Dead Man's Party
Dead Man's Party.text:
Chapter 5: Dead Man's Party

Chapter 5 begins immediately after the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth]{Chapter 4}, beginning combat against the false Hellbreakers. You can remind the PCs that they know they were the only Hellbreakers at the gala. The Hellknights at the gala are missing from this encounter, as dominated guards lured them away and attacked them in a separate area of the mansion.

Chapter Organization

This chapter follows the PCs as they investigate Hedvend's murder and has two different types of encounters, inquiries (starting in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05thegamesafoo00]{The Game's Afoot}) and plot events (starting in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22205deadma.JournalEntryPage.05theplotthick00]{The Plot Thickens}). Inquiries are encounters where the PCs investigate and learn information about the murder while plot events show what else is happening in the manor during the investigation.

Once combat ends, the Hellknights discover that Hedvend has been murdered. Everyone in the gala is a suspect, though Caeto eventually enlists the PCs to help solve the mystery. The PCs also face another mystery that only they are aware of—who were the false Hellbreakers and why did they attack now? They soon face yet another conundrum, as deaths continue to pile up, with victims among both Elidir's elite and the servants and guards in Reevesrest. This chapter is a closed-box murder mystery, and much of it will be free-flowing, with PCs able to pursue various leads to solve the mysteries they face. During this process, various events break up the story, moving events forward, though they're not specifically timed. This investigation probably happens overnight—with bodies continuing to drop, there isn't really time to take a period of rest—but there isn't actually a specific time limit. Caeto keeps the manor locked down for as long as it takes to solve Hedvend's murder.

Mission: The Druma Road Gate.name: Mission: The Druma Road Gate
Mission: The Druma Road Gate.text:
Mission: The Druma Road GateSevere 6

The massive wooden doors that form the Druma Road Gate rise above the city walls, a point of defensive construction meant to keep the city safe from any external threat.

Unfortunately for the PCs, one more obstacle stands between them and freedom: Caeto and most of the army are busy dealing with the chaos caused by the PCs' actions (and perhaps literally putting out fires), but the Hellknights also responded to word of the prison break by sending units to secure the exits from the city. Use the Druma Road Gate map for this encounter. The PCs notice the enemy as they approach the gate, and can begin this encounter mounted or on foot.

Mission: The Druma Road GateSevere 6

@UUID[Actor.B2CnznD4IZobDXWl]{Weak Hellknight Cavalry Brigade} @UUID[Actor.8dzcW7KgoOng553t]{Line Infantry} @UUID[Actor.7jG0GMDG6mD829mZ]{Standard Bearer}

Creatures: Caeto sent a brigade of his Hellknights to assist the guards already at the gate. They consider the Hellbreakers traitors and murderers, and fight until slain or knocked unconscious to prevent their escape. While the PCs must deal with the primary threat here, you can describe smaller battles between other guards and the escaping Hellbreakers.

Development: Once the PCs successfully defeat the gate guards, they can escape into the storm and leave Elidir behind. They return to Saringallow where Alceo and Phoebe are waiting to greet them along with the new Hellbreakers they've brought along.

The new Hellbreakers are welcomed to Saringallow and soon given dominion over Highfort, an abandoned hobgoblin fortress close to the city. The PCs have plenty of time to rest and catch up with their peers, who are delighted to see them back. Rhokrag, Maeve, and Xerra are particularly happy to see the PCs and welcome them with great enthusiasm.

However, not all is well. Caeto still maintains an iron grip on Elidir, and therefore the powers that be in Isger, and a new threat grows in the West that Caeto is all too happy to ignore. Ezio Gaeta may have been defeated, but his master's plans are still in motion, and soon to come to fruition.

Mission: Ride or Die.name: Mission: Ride or Die
Mission: Ride or Die.text:
Mission: Ride or Die

Once the PCs have rescued all of their fellow Hellbreakers from the Gyve, they must make their way out of the chaotic prison, avoiding guards and prisoners to reach the army stables through a winter storm that has gathered over the city. Once they make it to the stables, they can steal mounts both to speed their passage out of the city and prevent pursuit.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.5dnar8XOFHf4iZyO]{Ride or Die}

Chase: This encounter uses the chase subsystem (GM Core 192) as the PCs try to avoid falling into Caeto’s clutches in their rush toward freedom. Each round of this chase takes 15 minutes. Because the PCs are fleeing and trying to avoid pursuit, they act first. On their turn, the pursuers gain [[/r 1d4]] Chase Points. In addition, the pursuers get a bonus to the roll equal to the PCs’ Suppression Point threshold (up to 4) and a penalty equal to the PCs’ Uprising Point threshold (up to 4), though these might cancel each other out. If the PCs were successful Placing Bombs earlier, remind them they can use those to help during their escape.

If the pursuers catch the PCs, a patrol cuts off their path and they must fight their way past it before they can resume their pursuit. When this happens, the PCs are presumed to be mounted unless they indicate otherwise (likely because they have a Speed greater than 30, or they’re too large to ride a horse). If they dismount, assume some of the other Hellbreakers catch their horses and they can remount freely after the fight.

Mission: Ride or Die

@UUID[Actor.G80bkBfYEx8f54hE]{Adiutor} @UUID[Actor.4mYoMvxcn7u7wWJH]{Unsanctioned Sheriff} @UUID[Actor.SceBgvuW3W3Y5lrN]{Equestrian Constable} @UUID[Actor.oOwVKAkBJ73R2Utv]{Elite Infantry Soldier} @UUID[Actor.buxbI0ylfAT1biAt]{Conscript Squad} @UUID[Actor.OR8JoQDjAhxw4fc4]{Watch Officer}

Creatures: A number of army units rush to stop the PCs’ escape. Because they are not well organized, these are low-threat encounters. Because they can happen multiple times, you can mix and match who catches the escapees, drawing from the creatures below so the encounters feel different each time. You can build an encounter using the XP budget (GM Core 75) or use one of the following combinations: One adiutor and two elite infantry soldiers, one unsanctioned sheriff and two elite infantry soldiers, two equestrian constables and a conscript squad, two elite infantry soldiers and two watch officers.

If a PC wants to spend their round Treating Wounds, Refocusing or another such activity, they can do so instead of making a check to overcome an obstacle. Even though such activities usually only take 10 minutes, because the PCs are on the move even as they work, it takes a full 15-minute round. Allow PCs to Refocus even if they normally would need to be still or undertake some other specific action as part of the activity.

Chase Obstacles: The characters must overcome these six obstacles in the following order to successfully finish the chase.

Prison RiotObstacle 6

Chase Points 4; Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:27] to muscle your way through, @Check[intimidation|dc:24] to persuade a group of guards or prisoners to look for an easier target, or @Check[stealth|dc:22] to avoid being spotted

Bloody, violent clashes break out throughout the Gyve as prisoners try to escape and guards try to stop them.

Weather the StormObstacle 6

Chase Points 2; Overcome @Check[diplomacy|dc:27] to persuade someone to give you directions, @Check[perception|dc:27] to notice significant landmarks, @Check[society|dc:24] to remember the city layout, or @Check[survival|dc:22|traits:secret,exploration,skill,action:sense-direction|name:Sense Direction] to find your way

The intensity of the winter storm picks up, and the blast of driving snow makes it hard to tell left from right.

Call the CavalryObstacle 6

Chase Points 4; Overcome @Check[crafting|dc:27] to tack up the horses, @Check[nature|dc:22|traits:auditory,concentrate,action:command-an-animal|name:Command an Animal] to handle the animals, or @Check[thievery|dc:24] to unlock the stables and supplies

At the army stables, horses need to be saddled and prepared for the elements.

Fire and IceObstacle 6

Chase Points 4; Overcome @Check[acrobatics|dc:24] to maintain your balance, @Check[intimidation|dc:27] to startle people into getting out of the way, or @Check[nature|dc:22] to Ride

The chaos in the city spooks the horses and fills the streets with shocked residents gawking at the goings-on.

Spies in the SkiesObstacle 6

Chase Points 3; Overcome @Check[religion|dc:22] to ward off the fiends, @Check[stealth|dc:27] to stay out of sight, or @Check[survival|dc:24] to mask your passage

Imps search for the Hellbreakers from above.

Roads to PerditionObstacle 7

Chase Points 4; Overcome @Check[arcana|dc:23], @Check[occultism|dc:23], or @Check[religion|dc:23] to counter the magic; @Check[survival|dc:25] to find a new path

The remaining watchmages unleash a powerful magic to twist the roads beneath the Hellbreakers, leading them back toward the prison, and capture.

Oubliette.name: Oubliette
Oubliette.text:
K13. OublietteLow 6

A damp chill pervades this round, subterranean chamber. Water drips from the black stone, a constant trickle that seems somehow amplified into strange echoes, and almost instantly begins to feel monotonous. Rusty shackles hang from the ceiling and walls. In the main chamber, an iron smell of blood underlies the grave-like scent of the earth. A torture rack stands in the center of the room beneath a pulley system hanging from the ceiling, clearly visible in the light from flaming braziers. Cruel pokers, blades, and other implements of torture hang on the back wall.

Who's there?

The two Hellbreakers being held in area K13 aren't named. If the PCs have formed a connection with any of the recruits, they might work well here, but be careful to consider whether that might be too upsetting.

Gyve jailers extract confessions, true or not, from prisoners in this torture chamber that was designed to prey on all the senses of its victims. Victims hang from manacles in the antechamber (K13a), where they're forced to listen to others' screams, while others wait in the main area (K13) and are forced to see what awaits them. Two Hellbreaker captives are here, both hanging from chains in the main chamber while their torturer prepares for another interrogation session.

The area is kept well-lit both so prisoners can see what awaits them and also as a contrast to the darkened cells above. The strange echoing properties enhance noises here—any effect that does sonic damage does an additional 1 point of sonic splash.

K13. OublietteLow 6

@UUID[Actor.516RGBm2lUsjV4bS]{Rovimi Scaphe} @UUID[Actor.ZMoA7gsjiYfLJAx8]{Torturer}

Creatures: In addition to the shackled Hellbreakers, the prison's head interrogator is here with an assistant, planning for another session with her victims. If she hears PCs approaching in the antechamber, she moves to the northwest side, forcing them to enter the main chamber, where she enters melee. She fights to the death, though her assistant is willing to surrender once reduced to 10 Hit Points.

Development: Rovimi Scaphe has keys, which the PCs can use to unlock the shackles in this area as well as any doors in the cell block. The freed Hellbreakers can tell the PCs that they were held in the cell block before being brought to the oubliette, but don't know if all the other captives are there.

Warden’s Tower.name: Warden’s Tower
Warden’s Tower.text:
K12. Warden's TowerModerate 6

This hexagonal chamber is finely appointed, with a rug covering the dark stone floor and simple ink drawings hanging on the wall between the barred windows. A large wooden desk stands in the middle of the room, covered in papers. One large, throne-like chair stands behind the desk and three smaller ones in front of it, two of them with leather straps on the arms and legs.

The warden rules the prison as a personal kingdom from this office. The smaller chairs are for her subordinates or, occasionally, prisoners who are restrained and brought here for interviews. The area is lit with everlight crystals, so it's always bright light here.

K12. Warden's TowerModerate 6

@UUID[Actor.bgMOZgYkpnZRoik9]{Warden Irkazer}

Creatures: Warden Irkazer (relentless female human warden 8) runs the prison from this tower. She works day and night and can be found here at any time. She attacks any PCs who enter, fighting to the death.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.xJsYNLwvW0ll6o0D]{Chest}
The warden's room holds a chest containing five silver ingots.

Development: If PCs search the room after defeating the warden, they can find records on her desk about the Hellbreakers' imprisonment. Among the contents are notes that indicate the authorities learned about the Hellbreakers hideout after they captured Otton and tortured him over several days. They also learn that almost all of the Hellbreakers are imprisoned in the cell block, except for two who remain in the basement, where the prison torturer Rovimi Scaphe (sadistic female human torturer 6) continues to try and extract information from them about the PCs' potential whereabouts. The warden has keys to all areas in the prison, and a paper on her desk includes the daily pass phrase.

Cell Block.name: Cell Block
Cell Block.text:
K11. Cell BlockLow 6

A small wooden panel at head height sits in each of the solid wooden doors that line this hallway of dark stone. Occasional moans, sobs and other noises—even unhinged laughter—drift out from inside the cells. The stench of misery fills this area along with the miasma of unwashed bodies and excreta.

This outer hallway of the cell block is unlit and in darkness. A few candles burn low in the inner “courtyard,” leaving that area in dim light, a very small privilege for the better-behaved inmates that are kept in those cells. Two slightly larger cells in the western wall have one small window each—they're typically given to prisoners who inform on their fellow inmates to the guards. The panel in each cell door can be opened to allow guards (or PCs) to look in.

K11. Cell BlockLow 6

@UUID[Actor.XTylCP0qAZWMYRzW]{Rencelos Azri} @UUID[Actor.fcA0pTUoUALFITxN]{Moccoviz Azri}

Creatures: If the PCs successfully completed the Talisman Job, the Azris have been imprisoned here. As they've mostly been arrest for the optics, their cell doors are kept unlocked and they're free to roam the floor as a special privilege. When the PCs enter, the Azris recognize them from previous encounters and attack in a rage! The pair focus on a single target at a time and protect each other's backs. If the Azris weren't arrested, the PCs can free their companions without issue.

Development: Almost all of the captured Hellbreakers—other than two who are being interrogated in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06oubliette00000]{K13}—are in the small, unlit cells in this area. They know the missing Hellbreakers were brought into the prison, but don't know what happened to them since then. Among the prisoners here is Otton, who is in awful shape after being tortured for information before being dumped back here. He tearfully apologizes and explains that he was captured and tried to stay quiet, but eventually told his torturer where the Hellbreakers were meeting. If the PCs show kindness toward Otton, the Hellbreakers League's Reputation Points increase by 1.

Tool Bin.name: Tool Bin
Tool Bin.text:
K10. Tool Bin

A slightly indented path from constant travel stretches between the north and south doors of this room. Tools hang from hooks on the walls.

Tools for working in the Moil are kept here, collected under guard each morning and returned each night.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.IMlcq7xoynWG9We0]{Tool Bin}
In addition to almost any type of long or short tool here, PCs can find a levered crowbar and enough equipment to Craft two lesser silverscrap bombs.

Holding Cell B.name: Holding Cell B
Holding Cell B.text:
K9. Holding Cell BLow 6

The odor of stale sweat permeates the mass cell, a foul funk that only compounds the misery of being locked away here. The few mounds of straw and linens that make up beds only seem to emphasize how awful this place is.

Prisoners who break rules or get on a guard’s bad side are moved into holding cell B. It has the same light conditions as the other cell.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ItTionHYw9zkogLj.PlaylistSound.A1csk6nMbhBhvsy3]{Prison Break}

K9. Holding Cell BLow 6

@UUID[Actor.YhqByz5H0xIF62Uy]{Prison Break}

Hazard: The captives in this cell take the opportunity to try to escape when the PCs open the door, crushing anyone in their path.

Development: If the PCs Disable the hazard without reducing it to 0 HP before it automatically ends, they can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22] check to get the remaining prisoners to join them. On a success, the PCs gain 1 Uprising Point, or 2 points on a critical success.

Holding Cell A.name: Holding Cell A
Holding Cell A.text:
K8. Holding Cell A

Dirty straw covers the floor of this room, piled in places into crude sleeping pallets with stained, unpleasant linens as the only blankets.

Prisoners sentenced to labor in the Moil sleep in this shared cell when they aren’t working. This room has no torches; if the PCs arrive during the day, the light coming in through the barred windows leaves the entire area in dim light, otherwise it’s dark.

A dozen people of various ages and ancestries are incarcerated here at the time of the PCs’ arrest. If the PCs free them, decrease their number of Suppression Points by 1 as army resources are diverted to recapturing them. The PCs can also attempt to recruit them with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22] check. On a success, many of the prisoners agree to join, and the PCs gain 1 Uprising Point; on a critical success, they all join enthusiastically, and the PCs gain 2 Uprising Points. If the PCs allowed Ozney to be arrested in Chapter 4 (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04eventinjusti00]{Event: Injustice is Served}), they can find her here. However, she recognizes the PCs and loudly proclaims they let her be thrown into the Gyve without any remorse, giving the PCs a –1 circumstance penalty to any Diplomacy checks here.

Storeroom.name: Storeroom
Storeroom.text:
K7. Storeroom

Closed chests line the walls of this room beneath shelves laden with neatly labeled bottles.

This room is used to temporarily store goods created in the Moil that are too valuable to leave in the work areas. Only the warden has the keys to this room, and she doesn't unlock it except when someone is bringing in items. The room has an average lock, requiring four successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks. The torches in this room are only lit when it's in use; it's in darkness except for any light provided by the PCs.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.NqCwm57i48VgpFBh]{Storeroom}
PCs can find a number of valuable supplies here, crafted in the Moil but not yet delivered to the army. The bottles hold 3 lesser elixirs of life, 3 lesser bottled catharsis, and 2 surging serums. In the chests are clawed bracers and a runestone with a ready rune.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
K6. Kitchen

A heavy iron cauldron sits in the large fireplace of this kitchen, filling the room with a rich, savory scent. A wooden table with a heavily scarred work surface fills much of the room, and various cooking implements hang on the wall.

No one is working in the kitchen at the time of the PCs' attack, giving them an opportunity to rest here briefly to Treat Wounds or Refocus.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.jK1zVw1BnSM18OX0]{Cauldron} @UUID[Actor.u9BwLU07Cg2hWQB6]{Table}
The cauldron contains four doses of mender's soup being prepared for inmates scheduled to work on the most dangerous tasks the next day. The PCs can eat it immediately, or if they have containers, take it with them. There is also a greater ration tonic on the table.

Guardhouse.name: Guardhouse
Guardhouse.text:
K5. GuardhouseLow 6

This well-lit room holds a small table and chairs, offering relief from the cold, stark prison environment. Arrow slits on the walls allow easy view of the winding corridor outside.

The guards relax here and watch for anyone in the Descent when they're not patrolling. The door to the room is hidden as an added precaution against prisoners, though being opened multiple times a day has made its location more obvious; it can be found with a successful @Check[perception|dc:22] check.

K5. GuardhouseLow 6

@UUID[Actor.XTCqpv889mSdEc3A]{Elite Archer Sentries (3)} @UUID[Actor.wWplNuy8ZKU9BTDh]{Mage for Hire}

Creatures: Four guards are stationed in this room at all times. If they are on alert, they open fire through the arrow slits in this room at anyone in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06descent0000000]{K4}. They don’t open the secret door unless someone gives the correct code phrase. If they hear anyone try to open the secret door without permission, they move to the far side of the room so they can fire arrows at anyone who enters until they enter melee. Once a guard is reduced to 10 Hit Points, they surrender; if three guards are killed or surrender, the fourth surrenders when they’re reduced to 20 Hit Points as long as the PCs haven’t attacked another guard who attempted to surrender.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.KDCMfXpeXC9eGLbu]{Guardhouse}
This room contains weapons for the guards to use while on duty—PCs can find any common weapon they desire. The PCs can also find a number of contraband and confiscated goods worth a total of 50 gp. The guards here have keys that can open any door in the prison.

Descent.name: Descent
Descent.text:
K4. Descent

Manacles hang from rusty chains attached to the dark stone walls of this winding corridor. Arrow slits line all of the inner wall.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Macro.92HT1u2DzJQ2cTuj]{Toggle Interior Ambience}

Named because it's the path into the hell that is the Gyve, this winding passage leads around the guardhouse, giving jailers multiple opportunities to fire arrows at anyone trying to escape through the main entrance (or enter without permission, though the idea someone would attempt that would baffle almost everyone in the Gyve). Prisoners are forced to change into prison robes made of a thin, scratchy burlap, which hang from hooks to the west of the main entrance. Any possessions taken from arriving prisoners are claimed by the guards or destroyed.

Guard Tower.name: Guard Tower
Guard Tower.text:
K3. Guard TowerLow 6

This stone tower rises 10 feet above the prison walls. Two bull's-eye lanterns are mounted on the walls, and a ballista points in toward the prison grounds.

Twin towers to the east and west of the Moil house guards who watch for escapees. A ladder on the first floor (K3a) goes up to a trapdoor. If the guards see someone enter the first floor of the tower, they lock the trapdoor. The range of fire from the top of the tower (K3b) effectively includes the tower's entire half of the court yard, but prevents the guards from targeting enemies on the far side of the prison grounds.

K3. Guard TowerLow 6

@UUID[Actor.CbksTScmvvrEfXU3]{Artillerists (2)} @UUID[Actor.In6nGL09V86qAVJf]{Weak Sniper}

Creatures: Three guards are stationed in this area, day or night, and don't leave the tower under any circumstances. If they see PCs in the Moil, they shoot at them from this location, with the artillerists using their actions to operate the ballista (Guns & Gears 74) and the sniper using his own weapons. If it's night, the sniper turns the lanterns to keep the PCs in light. If the PCs enter the tower, the guards switch to melee combat. They fight until reduced to 10 HP, at which point they attempt to surrender or flee.

Scene Notes Macros

@UUID[Macro.KvEZUjKluom9bM8S]{Toggle West Upper Floor} @UUID[Macro.2wJ2BWKpWpMJr28g]{East}

Removes the wall restrictions, so that tokens on the upper floor can view the yard, and vice versa.

Moil.name: Moil
Moil.text:
K2. Moil

Makeshift buildings and canvas canopies lean against the walls of this courtyard. Large piles of wood and other raw materials sit next to them, scattered about the yard for use by the prisoners of the Gyve. Old, rusted manacles lie broken on the ground, remnants of the courtyard's past.

The former slave auction attached to the prison was transformed into a labor camp after the Emancipation Edict in 4722 ar. Debtors and minor criminals are sentenced to work here, earning coppers to pay off their obligations by crafting supplies used by the army. This area is open to the sky and might have lighting based on the time of day the PCs attack. The prisoners are locked inside, so the area is empty (either because it's night or because of Caeto's lockdown orders) with nothing of note or value.

Purgatory.name: Purgatory
Purgatory.text:
K1. PurgatoryTrivial 6

The grim gates of the prison await those doomed.

The entranceway to the prison grounds acts as an airlock—the interior and exterior gates are never opened at the same time. By Caeto's orders, the prison is under lockdown until the Hellbreakers have been executed. Three guards are stationed here, with keys for both gates, but they'll only open them for guards with the pass phrase. The gates to the north and south of this area are iron, with Hardness 18, and 72 HP (Broken Threshold 36), and the DC to Force them Open is 27.

K1. PurgatoryTrivial 6

@UUID[Actor.eOLWp9PcrGQ2E5n8]{Jailers (2)} @UUID[Actor.OR8JoQDjAhxw4fc4]{Watch Officer}

Creatures: The guards only open the gates if they hear the proper pass phrase. Otherwise, if the PCs enter this area, they attack. They fight until reduced to 10 HP, at which point they attempt to surrender or flee. If the guards hear a disturbance in the Moil (such as an explosive entrance by the PCs), they rush to investigate, likely encountering the PCs in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06moil0000000000]{K2}.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.MOwdPNb4uaaMtJVM]{Gate Guard}
In addition to their listed gear, the gate guards carry keys to the Purgatory gates and the exterior doors of the prison.

Mission: Break the Fetters.name: Mission: Break the Fetters
Mission: Break the Fetters.text:
K. Mission: Break the Fetters

Content Warning

The Gyve is intentionally a horrible place, a prison designed to cause suffering and includes mention of torture. Before you begin, understand that player consent (including that of the Game Master) is vital to a safe and fun play experience for everyone. You should talk with your players before beginning the adventure and modify descriptions of the narrative as appropriate.

Once the PCs finish their preparations, they can begin their assault on the Gyve at any time. The prison is made of well-maintained masonry (Hardness 14, HP 56 [BT 28], @Check[athletics|dc:22|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb]), with 10-foot-high ceilings. Its doors and portcullises are wood (Hardness 10, HP 40 [BT 20]) and are locked unless otherwise noted. They require two successes on a @Check[thievery|dc:22|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick the Lock] check to Pick the Lock or can be Forced Open with a @Check[athletics|dc:27|traits:attack,skill,action:force-open|name:Force Open] check. The windows are barred with iron, but have been poorly maintained while the government has used its limited resources on other priorities—they have Hardness 10, HP 40 (BT 20), and can be Forced Open with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:24|traits:attack,skill,action:force-open|name:Force Open] check. Torches on the first floor provide bright light throughout the area. The rest of the prison is in darkness unless indicated otherwise.

If the PCs wish to know more about the prison, they can attempt a @Check[society|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge or a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] check to Gather Information. On a success, they learn that prisoners are kept on the upper floors, while a torture chamber is in the basement. On a critical success, they learn specifics about the prison: Give them a map of the first, second, and third floor, though don't let them know where the secret entrance to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06guardhouseun00]{K5} is.

Jenvirick strongly recommends the PCs blow a hole in the surrounding walls of the prison to enter, which they can do with supplies they’ve acquired from Soldier’s Aegis. Allow them to pick a spot on the outer walls where they want to set a bomb. When it explodes, it blows a 5-foot-wide gap the PCs can use to enter directly into the Moil (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06moil0000000000]{K2}), and from there the Gyve. If they have Volcanic Diversion Points, they can spend 1 to create an additional 5-foot hole in the Gyve’s outer wall, or in the prison itself.

Scene Notes Macros

@UUID[Macro.D35zVuCS7Utnvp1g]{Breach Wall 1} @UUID[Macro.tTuxUQTWSdAV3JtP]{2} @UUID[Macro.NRjOJXfL9jCLAB3y]{3} @UUID[Macro.oISCo4p11fXRzZDB]{4} @UUID[Macro.QXM69pqz2jVDC5aD]{5} @UUID[Macro.RvtF3P8vRRn4MCsU]{6} @UUID[Macro.TQ2P2FZW2g14jPl3]{7}

Some PCs might want to try a stealthier approach. One option—which Jenvirick strongly recommends against—is to get themselves arrested. They can do this very easily via street patrol (use the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04papersplease00]{Papers, Please} encounter). This would bring them into the prison via Purgatory and then the main entrance to the Descent, but the guards would take any armor, weapons, and magic items unless they were successfully concealed with Stealth or magic. They could also attempt to get a man on the inside through a hefty bribe of 300+ gp or an extremely difficult @Check[diplomacy|dc:30] check, but this might take time they can't afford.

If a PC wants to impersonate a guard, warn them through a NPC that the guards have a daily code phrase that they use to identify themselves. The phrase on the day the PCs break in is "It's colder than a rime dragon's breath," and the PCs must find a guard and get the code out of them with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:27] check or a @Check[intimidation|dc:29] check.

Mission: Prepare the Path.name: Mission: Prepare the Path
Mission: Prepare the Path.text:
Mission: Prepare the Path

Having successfully obtained supplies from the veteran’s home, the PCs now must place the frozen lava in the most optimal locations to cause mass chaos during their final escape from the city. Doing so uses the following special activity. A PC can attempt the activity up to three times, but they gain 2 Suppression Points the second time they try and 3 Suppression Points the third time as their activities attract attention.

Place Bomb

  • concentrate
  • Exploration
  • Secret

You spend an hour finding the best location to place an explosive to provide the optimum benefit during the escape from the Gyve. Attempt a DC 20 check with an appropriate Lore (such as @Check[elidir-lore|dc:20], @Check[engineering-lore|dc:20], or @Check[warfare-lore|dc:20] Lore) or a @Check[crafting|dc:22], @Check[society|dc:22], or @Check[stealth|dc:22] check.

Critical Success You gain 2 Volcanic Diversion Points, as described in Success.

Success You gain 1 Volcanic Diversion Point. Before any check during the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionrideo00]{Ride or Die} uprising, you can spend a Volcanic Diversion Point to describe how the frozen lava helps, either by clearing the way or distracting or damaging pursuers. Doing so improves the degree of success by 1 step.

Failure You fail to properly set the frozen lava.

Critical Failure As failure and you gain a Disaster Point that decreases the degree of success of your check by 1. You must use your Disaster Point on a check during Ride or Die or take @Damage[5d6] damage from the frozen lava exploding on you.

Forge.name: Forge
Forge.text:
J6. Forge

A fire in the forge against the southern wall fills this room with heat. Crafter's tools fill much of the area, including an anvil, hammer, and tongs for working with metals, as well as chisels and planes for shaping wood. A shelf built on the wall near the door holds several labeled potion bottles.

The skirmancers craft the physical implements they use in this kitchen-turned-smithy.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.pzPl8lSH0o60ZNqE]{Shelf}
The shelf holds two moderate healing potions intended to help anyone injured during the crafting process or during tests in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06guardhouseun00]{K5}.

Proving Ground.name: Proving Ground
Proving Ground.text:
J5. Proving Ground Low 6

Tears and slashes in the hay padding which covers the walls of this room reveal metal reinforcements, though even those bear nicks and dents that indicate they take a large amount of abuse. A pit yawns open in the northeast corner of the room, the stone rim chipped and blackened.

This is where the skirmancers test their munitions. The pit is 15 feet deep and the DC for Athletics checks to Climb out of it is @Check[athletics|dc:15|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb].

J5. Proving GroundLow 6

@UUID[Actor.WemAOg509o5LZxo1]{Skirmancer Engineer} @UUID[Actor.y7VmiIwJhYOoV68F]{Clockwork Soldier}

Creatures: A skirmancer is working here, along with a construct used to test magical armaments. The skirmancer is absorbed in her work and doesn't notice any sounds of combat from outside, but attacks if the PCs enter the room. She surrenders if reduced to 10 Hit Points or fewer. The clockwork soldier attacks any PCs that enter the room, but doesn't leave the room, fighting until destroyed.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.1PlDVN5SDshVwmsQ]{Pit}
The PCs can find a large amount of unexploded frozen lava in the pit. The exact amount isn't specified because the PCs are expected to use most of it in the rest of this chapter to blow their way into the prison and then out of Elidir. They can keep 2 frozen lavas and an eternal eruption for their personal use.

Vault.name: Vault
Vault.text:
J4. Vault

The skirmancers keep items that haven't been sold yet in this hidden vault.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.z3M7NzqrGrHfpoRk]{Vault}
The vault currently holds a martyr's shield, a runestone with a wounding rune, and a greater smoke ball.

Arcane Smithy.name: Arcane Smithy
Arcane Smithy.text:
J3. Arcane Smithy Trivial 6

The acrid smell of magic and alchemy permeates the air. A spellbook floats in a silver ritual circle with arcane runes of power set in the floor of this wooden room. Shelves hold various magical loci and other crafting elements, all carefully stored and labeled.

The skirmancers use this room, with its protective warding circle, for their magical crafting. While activated, the circle prevents anything from crossing. Creatures in the circle gain a +2 status bonus to AC against any attacks made from outside the area. In addition, a creature that attempts to enter the circle must make a @Check[will|dc:22] save. On a failure, the circle stops their movement (though they can still attempt any other actions that were part of an activity as long as they meet the requirements, such as a Strike that is part of a Sudden Charge). On a critical failure, the entire activity ends and the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}. A creature cannot be summoned inside the circle, and a creature with the magical or summoned trait that tries to enter the circle treats the results of its save as one degree worse.

J3. Arcane SmithyTrivial 6

@UUID[Actor.a5IXLyMoIihp2H1b]{Skirmancer Mage}

Creatures: A skirmancer is working here in the warding circle. They remain in the circle, hoping its magic will protect them, and they respond to any intruders with deadly intent. If the Azris are in the lounge, the skirmancer rushes in to help them if they hear combat. The skirmancer surrenders if reduced to 10 Hit Points or fewer.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.C6PLnuUNUQ1RtDgO]{Skirmancer}
The skirmancer’s spellbook, worth 128 gp, includes the spells the skirmancer knows: fireball, gravity well, dispelling globe, and two additional arcane spells of the GM’s choice.

Lounge.name: Lounge
Lounge.text:
J2. Lounge

Several thickly padded chairs and side tables are scattered around this comfortable room. Magical light illuminates the corners where bookcases along the walls hold a number of titles. A dozen bottles of wine fill a rack, which also holds crystal goblets.

The Azris take care of the skirmancers whose creations make them so much money, and have maintained this lounge for them to relax when they're not working. A small bathroom connects to the lounge through a door to the west. It includes a secret door to the vault, which can be discovered with a successful @Check[perception|dc:22|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:search|name:Search] check.

J2. Lounge

@UUID[Actor.XTylCP0qAZWMYRzW]{Rencelos Azri} @UUID[Actor.fcA0pTUoUALFITxN]{Moccoviz Azri}

Creatures: If the Azris weren’t taken to the Gyve at the end of the Talisman Job, they retreated here. They respond to intruders with lethal intent even if they recognize the PCs.

Vestibule.name: Vestibule
Vestibule.text:
J1. VestibuleTrivial 6

A painting of Rencelos Azri in military attire hangs on the wall opposite the door in this finely paneled wooden foyer. By the door, a coat rack holds several warm jackets, and a small bucket holds water and a rag to wipe dirt off muddy boots.

The door from the outer courtyard to the vestibule is locked. A PC can Pick the Lock with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:22|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks.

J1. VestibuleTrivial 6

@UUID[Actor.K0gziy9KprWeM8bn]{Slashing Rune}

Hazard: The door to the courtyard is warded with a magical trap.

Reward: The PCs earn 40 XP for disabling the trap.

Mission: Up in Arms.name: Mission: Up in Arms
Mission: Up in Arms.text:
J. Mission: Up in Arms

After the Goblinblood Wars, Rencelos Azri opened a veteran’s home called Soldier’s Aegis for members of his company. In the beginning, this was a genuine act of charity for those who’d aided him throughout the war. In time, however, he began having them craft magical munitions for him to sell to the highest bidder. Soldier’s Aegis slowly transformed from respite home to a magical arms workshop staffed by veterans known as skirmancers.

Soldier's Aegis's walls are wooden slats, and the doors are wood. It has magical lights in each room that provide dim light unless one of the skirmancers is in the room, in which case it provides bright light. The windows are closed with wooden shutters, but can be Forced Open with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:22|traits:attack,skill,action:force-open|name:Force Open] check. The windows are big enough for a Small creature to enter, but Medium or larger creatures need to Squeeze through. Use the map above for the following encounters.

Part 3: The Great Escape.name: Part 3: The Great Escape
Part 3: The Great Escape.text:
Part 3: The Great Escape

After the PCs have attempted all of Jenvirick's missions, they move on to Part 3 of this chapter. About three weeks after the gala, as Abadius draws to a close, the PCs receive word that Quoster is finally being allowed to leave and they should meet him at the docks along with everything they wish to take with them out of the city.

The timing is serendipitous, as the PCs' departure comes minutes before the headquarters is raided by the Isgeri army. Unrealized by anyone, Otton Nettlebrush was captured some time ago. He finally broke under torture at the Gyve and revealed the Hellbreakers' location. Jenvirick is barely able to escape, and rushes to bring word to the PCs.

Quoster urges his men to quickly finish the preparations, carefully having them arrange crates on the ship to create a hiding place where they can smuggle multiple people out of Elidir. Their work is interrupted as a guard calls out, “Boss, there's someone coming!”

As everyone tenses, a solitary figure limps into the warehouse. It's Jenvirick, but she's clearly been in a fight. She holds one arm carefully against her chest with the other, cradling it to prevent the injured limb from being jarred. Her hair is matted with blood, and one eye is swollen closed. “It's the army, they found us! They attacked us moments after you left,” she says, clearly in pain. “I barely escaped. Everyone else has been captured—they've all been taken to the Gyve!” Her voice cracks with a sob as the final word escapes her lips.

The PCs likely have questions for her, which Jenvirick struggles to answer as best she can. She doesn't know how the authorities found their headquarters, but they came in force and addressed them as Hellbreakers, so they clearly knew what they were walking into. She tells the PCs that the other revolutionaries are almost certainly in the prison by now—she didn't know what else to do, so she hid until she knew it was safe to come find the PCs. She urges the PCs to break them out of prison; otherwise, they'll likely be publicly executed, which would all but end any hope of rebellion in the capital. If the PCs agree, read or paraphrase the following.

“I don't think you can just assault the Gyve—that would be suicide. Even if you got in, you'd never get out again. But I have an idea! One of my parents' friends fought in the Wars, and he was always talking about the chaos that all the goblins' bombs caused. If we had some explosives, that could give you an easy way in and out of the prison! And maybe we set up some around the city, cause chaos—away from people, of course. Then the army has to deal with that and can't come after you.”

Jenvirick's heard rumors that a veterans home run by Rencelos Azri doubles as a secret workshop where he has munitions made to sell to the army. If there's anywhere that might have enough explosives to make her plan work that's without drawing the army's immediate ire, that would be it. Once the PCs get the supplies, they can set them up in the city to create distractions at the proper time. Then, after they get in and out of the prison, they'll need to steal the army's mounts—that will both let them escape quickly and prevent the army from following. The PCs might have a chance to rest after @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionprepa00]{Prepare the Path}, but warn them that once they enter the prison, they likely won't get to rest until they escape the city.

Refusal: If the PCs refuse to help, Quoster frowns but agrees that he'll still help them leave the city. However, that attempt is foiled when they arrive at the gates and find that they've been closed—Caeto isn't allowing anyone to leave the city until he's executed the captured Hellbreakers.

Mission: Propaganda.name: Mission: Propaganda
Mission: Propaganda.text:
Mission: Propaganda

This uprising is an optional event for if the PCs are lacking Uprising Points.
