The city is being beaten down by Caeto's brutal crackdown on rebellious elements, but the Hellbreakers can turn public sentiment further against him through this uprising. First, the PCs must attempt to create anti-Cheliax propaganda with a @Check[crafting|dc:22] or appropriate Lore check. If the PCs received the Abrogail I script from Ievis (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04lovestingpri00]{Love Sting Printing House}), they automatically succeed.

Next, the PCs must bring their propaganda to the public. They can do this quietly or loudly, each with their own risks and benefits. If the PCs choose to take the quiet approach, they can wait until night and sneakily distribute their materials with a @Check[stealth|dc:24] or @Check[thievery|dc:24] check. If they choose the loud approach, they stage a public forum protesting Caeto's rule and rousing a mob with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:24], @Check[intimidation|dc:24], or @Check[performance|dc:24] check.

On a success, the PCs gain 1 Uprising Point (2 if they went loud). On a failure, they gain no Uprising Points. On a critical failure, they draw attention from guards and are confronted (2 guards for quiet, 4 for loud).

Mission: Propaganda

@UUID[Actor.DPE5ZMJdOXOh6X2s]{Guards (2-4)}

Mission: The Dock Job.name: Mission: The Dock Job
Mission: The Dock Job.text:
Mission: The Dock JobLow or Moderate 6

This uprising occurs after the PCs complete two of the previous uprisings. Quoster approaches the PCs and says he’s having trouble persuading the authorities to let him leave the city. Fortunately, Jenvirick has an idea: she suggests the PCs to stage a robbery to pile on pressure.

Quoster runs his hands through his hair, looking haggard. “I still think I can get you out with my goods, but the authorities are being stubborn devils. They’re refusing to let me leave, and I need some leverage.”

Jenvirick lets out a squeak: “Oh, I have an idea! What if you stage a robbery down at the docks and intentionally get spotted so there’s no chance it’s overlooked? Then Quoster can use that to emphasize that his goods aren’t safe here!”

It’s not important that the PCs actually steal anything, but Quoster needs them to be spotted so he can point to the threat of thieves as a reason he should be allowed to move his goods out of Elidir lest Caeto risk him kicking up enough of a fuss to cause an international squabble. Quoster suggests going at night when the docks are largely empty other than security patrols, which typically consist of a few guards. He urges the PCs to avoid killing anyone, since that could backfire and make Caeto tighten his grip.

If the PCs successfully influenced Sastoli Brunc in Chapter 4 (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04dramatispers00]{Dramatis Personae}) and he survived the gala, Quoster suggests they try to enlist his aid. A PC who goes to the docks to talk to him can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20|traits:action:request,auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental|name:Request] check to Request his help. On a success, he informs the PCs about what a typical guard patrol consists of, including the spells the watchmage has prepared and the presence of the hell hound. On a critical success, Sastoli agrees to divert some resources away from where the PCs plan to stage the robbery; remove one dock guard from the encounter, reducing it from moderate to low.

This encounter uses the Docks map. If the PCs want to scope out the scene ahead of time, they can do so easily. Once they're ready to proceed, allow them to set up where they would like. At least one PC needs to visibly play the thief role for the guards to spot. Have any PCs who wish to be caught robbing the docks attempt a @Check[performance|dc:22] check or a @Check[acrobatics|dc:24], @Check[deception|dc:24], @Check[thievery|dc:24], or @Check[stealth|dc:24] check to make a show of breaking in while intentionally failing to do so, or a @Check[athletics|dc:27] check to knock over items and create a racket. A PC who succeeds gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative roll when the guards confront them; on a critical success, they are quickened on the first round of combat and can use the extra action to Step, Stride, Strike, or Take Cover.

Mission: The Dock JobLow or Moderate 6

@UUID[Actor.P5YeqclKS9xb0DEu]{Watchmage} @UUID[Actor.593XkDKvCaU7lOmT]{Dock Guards (2)} @UUID[Actor.CzJ4UNM5q4lbUVh6]{Hell Hound}

Creatures: The typical guard patrol along the docks consists of a watchmage and two guards. Amid the crackdown in the city, Caeto has supplemented their forces with a hell hound. The guards prioritize capturing the PCs over killing them if possible, but the hell hound has no such concerns.

Development: The PCs’ fight with the guards is noisy enough to draw more guards. The PCs can hear people approaching, but easily have time to escape unseen, though not to complete a robbery. While the PCs ultimately won’t have the chance to sneak out of the city with Quoster (see @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06part3thegrea00]{Part 3: The Great Escape}), the merchant’s efforts to apply pressure still benefit them as the authorities divert forces to the docks to stop “a rash of brazen thefts.” Reduce the PCs’ Suppression Points by 2. If the PCs kill any human guards, the paralictor uses it to justify further crackdowns and the PCs gain 1 Suppression Point for each guard killed (Caeto doesn’t care what happens to the hell hound).

Reward: If the PCs persuade Sastoli to reduce the guard patrol, award them 20 XP.

Mission: The Talisman Job.name: Mission: The Talisman Job
Mission: The Talisman Job.text:
Mission: The Talisman Job

“They’re accusing us of killing Hedvend even though we didn’t, right?” Jenvirick asks in a voice that indicates she knows the answer already. “It’s all a frame job to come after us. But I think I have my best idea yet! What if we did the same thing to them?”

The PCs have had a couple of interactions with the Azri family, who represent the very worst Isger has to offer: unparalleled wealth, less concern for the common person than the dirt on their exquisite custom shoes, and fewer scruples than a devil from the Hells. Unfortunately, their status and connections as one of the primary providers of weapons and supplies to the Isgeri army have largely made them untouchable as does their immense amount of private security. Framing the Azris as Hellbreakers would force Caeto to arrest them, even if only to acquit them. While they might be able to buy their freedom, the charges would be serious enough that they would be imprisoned, which would in turn interfere with the army’s weapon supply.

Jenvirick lays out an elaborate heist for the PCs, which involves spreading rumors about a shipment of talismans from Druma intended for Elidir’s army that have disappeared. Next, the PCs must find a way to connect the talismans to the Azris by posing as thieves who offer to sell them to the corrupt nobles. The PCs can then slip word to the army, claiming the Azris were the ones who stole the supposed shipment in the first place with plans to sell them to the Hellbreakers League. Once all those hooks are baited, it’s simply a matter of luring both sides to the same location and getting away unseen and untouched. This uprising uses the Infiltration system from GM Core 196.

Scene Notes Point Tracking

@UUID[Actor.lszOsNQtPGGo7xUp]{Infiltration Points Tracker}

Create a PrizeObstacle 6

Infiltration Points 2 (group); Overcome @Check[deception|dc:24] to spread word of the missing items, @Check[performance|dc:27] to act as merchants who have had their goods stolen, or @Check[warfare-lore|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[underworld-lore|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] to Recall Knowledge about army supplies and local thieves' guilds

The PCs need to “create” a missing shipment of talismans to intrigue the Azris and anger army officers by spreading rumors.

Bait the HookObstacle 6

Infiltration Points 2 (group); Overcome @Check[arcana|dc:22], @Check[crafting|dc:22], @Check[nature|dc:22], @Check[occultism|dc:22], or @Check[religion|dc:22] to create a fake sample talisman, @Check[deception|dc:24], @Check[diplomacy|dc:24] or @Check[mercantile-lore|dc:24] to negotiate terms, or @Check[society|dc:27] to arrange a deal

The PCs must meet with the Azris and arrange for them to buy the supposedly stolen shipment.

Start the HuntObstacle 6

Infiltration Points 2 (group); Overcome @Check[deception|dc:24], @Check[diplomacy|dc:24], or @Check[performance|dc:24] to get a message to the proper authorities, @Check[legal-lore|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[warfare-lore|dc:22|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] to Recall Knowledge about army procedures, or @Check[society|dc:27] to create clues for army investigators to find

Once the PCs rope the Azris into the scheme, they need to alert the army to the supposed corruption.

Special If the PCs successfully Influenced Colonel Rithert during Chapter 4 and xe survived the gala, reduce the DCs for this obstacle by 2; if Colonel Rithert didn’t survive the gala, increase all DCs by 1 as xir replacement is still learning the job and is slow to respond to the PCs’ prompts.

Gather the MarksObstacle 6

Infiltration Points 2 (group); Overcome @Check[deception|dc:27] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:27] to bring everyone together, @Check[survival|dc:24] to lay false tracks for army investigators, or @Check[thievery|dc:22] to plant a fake talisman

The PCs must arrange for army investigators to catch the Azris red-handed with the supposedly stolen talismans.

Leave Them Holding the BagObstacle 6

Infiltration Points 2 (group); Overcome @Check[acrobatics|dc:24] or @Check[athletics|dc:24] to get over walls, @Check[elidir-lore|dc:25] or @Check[society|dc:27] to find the best escape routes in the city, or @Check[stealth|dc:22|traits:move,skill,secret,action:sneak|name:Sneak] to Sneak away

The last thing for the PCs to do is slip away, as if they never existed at all, leaving the Azris with supposedly stolen goods and a nonsense explanation about the alleged deal.

The PCs’ Awareness Points total has the following effects (in addition to any effects from Uprising Points or Suppression Points).

  • 5 Awareness Points: The Azris grow wary. Increase the DCs for obstacles in this uprising by 1.
  • 10 Awareness Points: The Army blames the Hellbreakers for the supposed theft of the talismans. Add 1 to the PCs’ Suppression Points.
  • 15 Awareness Points: The hunt for the missing talismans intensifies. Increase the PCs’ Suppression Points by a total of 2.
  • 20 Awareness Points: The Azris become suspicious and abandon the plan. The Talisman Job fails.

Development: If the PCs successfully complete the Talisman Job, the Azris are arrested and sent to the Gyve (where the PCs encounter them later). The disruption to the army’s activities reduces the number of Suppression Points by 2.

Reward: If the PCs successfully complete the Talisman Job, award them 10 XP.

Mission: The Army Job.name: Mission: The Army Job
Mission: The Army Job.text:
Mission: The Army Job

An evil grin crosses Jenvirick’s face. “I have an idea!” she says excitedly. “I was looking for something to eat earlier and I accidentally snapped at Sarevial because I wanted some bread. People get cranky when they’re hungry, and they don’t always make the best choices. What if we did that to the army? Who knows if Vulaunex has fully wrapped his greedy fists around the army’s hilt, but I bet we can make things uncomfortable there!”

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.xFxoBJfTP2d2zmNB.PlaylistSound.XA3gyEXpL89W9Hza]{Isger's Fist}

Jenvirick suggests the PCs take advantage of the confusion around Caeto’s takeover to disrupt the Isgeri army’s operations. If they impersonate Chelaxian couriers, they could send supplies or even forces to the wrong places, creating shortages and opportunities for other activities. Doing so requires the PCs to create false orders and infiltrate Isger’s Fist, the army headquarters, which takes an entire day.

The PCs must first falsify documents, which they can attempt to do with a @Check[society|dc:22] check to Create a Forgery or a @Check[crafting|dc:22|traits:downtime,skill,secret,action:create-forgery|name: Create a Forgery] check to create the paper, inks, and seals associated with the army's written orders. This check should be made secretly. The PCs then must deliver the orders, which requires a @Check[deception|dc:22] or @Check[performance|dc:22] check. If the PCs successfully influenced Colonel Rithert in Chapter 4 (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04dramatispers00]{Dramatis Personae}) and xe survived the gala, reduce each DC by 1.

If the PCs succeed at both checks, they disrupt the army’s supply lines, reducing their number of Suppression Points by 2; if they critically succeeded at one of the checks, they instead reduce the number by 3, or by 4 if they critically succeed at both checks.

If they fail at either check, they aren’t able to deliver the false orders, but can attempt to do so again. If they critically fail at one of the checks, they raise suspicions and gain 1 Suppression Point. If they critically fail at both checks, they gain 2 Suppression Points and can’t attempt this uprising again.

Reward: If the PCs successfully complete the Army Job, award them 10 XP.

Mission: The Manor Job.name: Mission: The Manor Job
Mission: The Manor Job.text:
Mission: The Manor Job

Jenvirick approaches with a familiar halfling. “This is Otton Nettlebrush. I heard him talking with another League member and, well, you should hear what he has to say!”

Otton mumbles to himself nervously and shifts his feet for a moment before he begins. “Right... Jenvirick says I should tell you that I served in Reevesrest until Hedvend got exactly what he deserved. After that, Vulaunex sacked most of the staff, just left a few guards and servants. But here’s the thing: that manor has a lot of valuables in it. Coins, of course, but also artwork, rare books, even that glaive that hangs in the steward’s room—the older servants used to say it was some sort of ancient magical weapon that stewards have kept since they defeated the original Isgeri.”

Vibrating with excitement, Jenvirick interrupts. “So that gave me an idea! We could go loot it. Then we use the money to help the city’s needy, which should bring them to our side!”

Caeto remains ensconced in the Chelaxian Quarter, also known as the Devil’s Acre—the walled area of the city that houses the Chelaxian elite—leaving Reevesrest largely empty other than a few guards and servants to maintain it. The PCs, who already know the manor’s layout, have a golden opportunity to sneak back in and loot the place. Jenvirick suggests some of the treasure could help fund the nascent chapter of the Hellbreakers League, but the rest could be distributed to the needy to earn favor for the rebellion.

To succeed at this mission, the PCs need to sneak past the guards and quietly enter the home. This uprising is a skill challenge using the Victory Points mechanic (GM Core 184). This is a two-step challenge over about 8 hours that can be done day or night. Each PC can attempt one check per step and a PC who uses an appropriate non-cantrip spell can earn an automatic success, or a critical success if it’s the highest rank spell they can cast.

In the first part of the challenge, the PCs must avoid both human and animal guards. They can attempt to do so with a @Check[acrobatics|dc:22] check using Acrobatics to go over and around gates and guards, @Check[deception|dc:22|traits:action:impersonate,concentrate,exploration,manipulate,secret|name:Impersonate] to Impersonate a new servant or guard, @Check[nature|dc:22|traits:auditory,concentrate,action:command-an-animal|name:Command an Animal] to Command an Animal, @Check[stealth|dc:22] to avoid being seen, or @Check[perception|dc:22] to Spot approaching patrols.

  • 0–1 Victory Points: The PCs are spotted, and fail to get past the guards.
  • 2–3 Victory Points: The PCs make it past the guards, but raise suspicions. They suffer a –1 circumstance penalty to any skill checks in the second part of this challenge.
  • 4 Victory Points: The PCs slip into the manor grounds completely undetected.

If the PCs have enough VP to proceed to the second part of the challenge, they must break into the manor and bypass locks and magical traps set to secure the location. They can do so with a DC 22 check using @Check[athletics|dc:22|traits:attack,skill,action:force-open|name:Force Open] to Force Open a door or window, or a @Check[arcana|dc:22], @Check[crafting|dc:22], @Check[occultism|dc:22], @Check[religion|dc:22], or @Check[thievery|dc:22] check to bypass the magical security.

  • 0–1 Victory Points: The PCs fail to get into the manor and need to retreat.
  • 2–3 Victory Points: The PCs get into the manor, but can’t access all of its valuables.
  • 4 Victory Points: The PCs strip the manor of everything that’s not nailed down.

If the PCs fail at either challenge, they escape unscathed and can try again on another day. Each failed attempt gains the PCs 1 Suppression Point, but also reduces the DCs in both parts of the challenge by 1 as they gain familiarity with the security (this reduction is cumulative if the PCs make multiple attempts).

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.Gmug37OVwh5Q4rtG]{Manor}
If the PCs strip the manor of all its valuables, they claim a token of salt and earth as well as the glaive in Hedvend’s room, an ancient Isgeri weapon called Lifebloom. In addition, they earn 2 Uprising Points as the Hellbreakers distribute Hedvend’s wealth to those who need it. If they couldn’t access all of the valuables, they get the two treasures and only gain 1 Uprising Point.

Reward: If the PCs successfully get into the manor and get any valuables, award them 10 XP.

Part 2: Raising Hell.name: Part 2: Raising Hell
Part 2: Raising Hell.text:
Part 2: Raising Hell

Once the PCs return to the safe house, Quoster is elated that they saved Siadrius.

“I can't think you all enough, I... Siadrius means more to me than you'll ever know. If what you did at the gala wasn't enough, this only proves I'm making the right choice by supporting the Hellbreakers League. Stay here, rest and recover, and I'll get us all out of Elidir as quickly as possible.”

Siadrius, as a way of thanks, says even with his current legal troubles, he has enough friends in the city that he can buy (or sell) anything the PCs might need, letting them shop safely during this part of the adventure. He says he'll contact a friend, Jenvirick (excitable female nephilim halfling antiques collector 3), whom he trusts to serve as an intermediary, and will send her to the PCs' safe house.

Jenvirick arrives shortly after the PCs have had a chance to rest and recover from the fight at the Moil. The daughter of Goblinblood War veterans, she's tired of watching her parents and her country be taken advantage of. While she's always been excitable (as well as a bit of a conspiracy theorist), Siadrius's request to work with the Hellbreakers has ignited her into a full-blown radical. She soon approaches the PCs about starting a local chapter of the Hellbreakers League. The exact timing for this request is up to you—it might work well immediately after she returns from a first shopping expedition for the PCs, but could be sooner if they don't immediately have any goods they want to buy or sell.

Jenvirick serves as an important NPC in this section. She pushes the PCs to start a chapter of the Hellbreakers League in the city and offers them missions to advance their cause.

Jenvirick nearly thrums with excitement, shifting her weight from foot to foot as if she's only barely holding herself back from rushing into action. “I can do more than just shop. I joined the protests before Hedvend—” She stops to spit on the ground as she mentions the now-dead steward. “—cracked down on the Riotmongers. I've heard about what the Hellbreakers League is doing in the south, and Siadrius told me how you rescued him. The time is now! Elidir is ready for its own chapter. That protest at the Moil proves it. We just need leaders! And you showed you can lead! Let me join, let me help! I have so many ideas!”

If the PCs agree, Jenvirick claps her hands. When they're ready, she spills out ideas for missions the PCs can undertake. Her ideas make up the following encounters: @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionthema00]{The Manor Job}, @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionthear00]{The Army Job}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missiontheta00]{The Talisman Job}, which the PCs can do in whatever order they chose. After they complete the second of Jenvirick's missions, Quoster approaches them about @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionthedo00]{ The Dock Job} uprising. If the PCs feel they're low on Uprising Points, they can also attempt the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionpropa00]{Propaganda} mission. This section of the adventure lasts about 2–3 weeks, giving PCs time to rest, craft, or shop between missions. You could even have missions overlap to convey a sense of time passing—especially with perhaps one or two obstacles from the Talisman Job happening around other uprisings, though you should make sure doing it this way won't confuse your players.

If the PCs rebuff her, Jenvirick is disappointed, but continues to press them over the following days, arguing that the League has been a positive force for other areas of Isger and that Elidir deserves the same. If they still refuse, she decides to take matters into her own hands, slowly bringing more and more revolutionaries into the safe house and holding meetings right under the PCs' noses—such meetings lead to wilder and wilder ideas that the PCs should be able to immediately tell would result in mass casualties. If the PCs don't quickly take a leadership role, they become aware that the unauthorized Hellbreakers League is trying to incite misbehavior and provoking Caeto to increase his efforts against them. From here, the PCs' Suppression Points increase by 1 per day. After three days, Quoster approaches the PCs to share his concerns about the high-profile actions being attributed to the League and their repercussions, and urges the PCs to take leadership of the group.

Riot at the Prison Gates.name: Riot at the Prison Gates
Riot at the Prison Gates.text:
Riot at the Prison GatesSevere 6

This encounter takes place in Purgatory (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06purgatoryund00]{K1}). Because of the mob, the entire area is difficult terrain and a creature can Hide or Sneak in the chaos. A PC or guard can attempt to control the crowd with the following special action:

Control the Crowd 1

  • Auditory
  • Concentrate

You try to direct the crowd. Attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22] or @Check[intimidation|dc:22] check.

Critical Success The crowd moves at your command. You do not treat the area as difficult terrain until the start of your next turn and you can choose to have the crowd do @Damage[2d8] damage to each enemy in the area.

Success The crowd parts around you momentarily. You do not treat the area as difficult terrain until the start of your next turn.

Failure The crowd ignores you.

Critical Failure The crowd only jostles you more. On your next action or reaction until the start of your next turn, you must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:5]. On a failure, the action is disrupted.

Riot at the Prison GatesSevere 6

@UUID[Actor.6esppa0ehu2P1202]{Captain Of The Guard} @UUID[Actor.oDwRoBhAeb6u0fum]{Gate Guards (3)}

Creatures: Four guards are in the area and no other guards rush to their aid because of the mob’s presence. The guards, seeing no way out, fight until knocked unconscious or slain.

Development: The mob is thrilled by the PCs’ resistance to the guards and, as the battle concludes, begins chanting slogans, such as “Isger for Isger,” “Send the devils back to Cheliax,” and “Hellbreakers!” If the players or PCs have discussed or used any slogans among themselves, having the crowd spontaneously chant that would help convey the PCs’ growing influence and importance to the Hellbreakers League. At this point, it’s up to the PCs to decide what to do—they can abandon the mob to its own devices, try to get it to disperse for the protesters’ own safety, or recruit members for their own chapter of the Hellbreakers League as Alceo and Phoebe tasked them to do when they first arrived.

Attempting to break up the mob before it gets out of hand requires a DC 22 skill check using the basic Victory Point mechanic (GM Core 184) to measure the PCs' success. Determine how a PC wants to engage the mob and what skill makes the most sense; each PC has one chance to influence the crowd. Some likely choices include @Check[athletics|dc:22] to bodily separate people from the whole; @Check[diplomacy|dc:22] to reason with them; @Check[intimidation|dc:22] to scare them away; or @Check[society|dc:22] to explain the danger they face with the protest. If the PCs leave the mob to its own devices and flee with Siadrius, they receive 0 Victory Points.

  • 0 Victory Points: The mob continues to protest after the PCs leave until they are brutally put down by Caeto’s forces. Word of the slaughter quickly spreads, and the PCs lose 2 Uprising Points.
  • 1–2 Victory Points: The PCs persuade a few protesters to take their requested action, but can’t control most of the mob. They gain 0 Uprising Points.
  • 3–4 Victory Points: Most of the mob heeds the PCs and follows their directions, though a few protesters continue to decry Caeto’s crackdown. They gain 1 Uprising Points.
  • 5+ Victory Points: The PCs quickly persuade the protesters to do as instructed, bolstering their reputation. They gain 2 Uprising Points and increase the Hellbreakers League’s Reputation Points by 1.

Mission: Jailbreak.name: Mission: Jailbreak
Mission: Jailbreak.text:
Mission: Jailbreak

When the PCs arrive at the Gyve, they find a group of outraged citizens protesting the crackdown and preventing Siadrius's captors from bringing him into the Moil, the labor camp that surrounds the prison. The army is slow to respond as it locks down the city, giving the PCs a chance to free Siadrius without having to enter the prison itself. Read or paraphrase the following.

Towering iron gates open into a courtyard, where prisoners arrive to be led through the dark stone walls that lead into the labor camp known as the Moil. In the center of the camp, the Gyve rises above the walls. Made of black stone, the prison is a blot on the skyline, a dreadful, ominous presence among the cheerfully painted wooden homes and businesses of Elidir. Small barred windows can be seen on the second floor and in the fourth-floor tower, about 40 feet up.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.ItTionHYw9zkogLj.PlaylistSound.JYXXMoWes1iSOdnL]{Protesting Crowd}

An angry crowd spilled into the courtyard, known as Purgatory, when the outer gates were opened to allow in Siadrius's captors. The volatile crowd is currently preventing the guards from closing the outer gates or opening the interior ones. Blocked and badly outnumbered by the crowd, the guards are still trying to decide on a course of action when the PCs arrive. Siadrius is shackled hand and foot, and bound to a pole held by two guards in front of the interior gate.

Part 1: The Chains That Bind.name: Part 1: The Chains That Bind
Part 1: The Chains That Bind.text:
Part 1: The Chains That Bind

The day after the gala, the PCs hear a knock on the door of their safe house. They open it to find Quoster, who slips in followed by two human employees laden with goods. He comes bearing the grim news of the city’s lockdown along with an offer for the PCs (and any items he promised them during their first meeting), but also a request for their help.

“I know we don’t know each other well,” the halfling merchant says, “but we’ve already agreed to work together and we need to work even more closely now that the city’s locked down. I don’t want the Hellknight to find you—bad for business, bad for surviving. I can help you get out of Elidir, but it will take a little time. As a Druman, I should be able to demand that they let me leave the city, and I’ll smuggle you out with my wares.

“In the meantime, I’ll provide you a safer place to stay; if I found you here, it’s just a matter of time until Vulaunex does too. There’s also some disguises to help you move around the city safely. But I need your help; a friend of mine has been arrested. One of my rivals falsely accused him of helping the Hellbreakers—of making the deal that I actually made with you! I couldn’t warn him in time and the army is snatching up all sorts of people in a sweep. They’re bringing them all to the Gyve. He won’t survive long there, so please, I need you to go get him out before it’s too late!”

Who Are the Rookie Hellbreakers?

The number of Hellbreakers who join the PCs isn’t specified and mostly serve as background characters. You can reintroduce NPCs the PCs met in the city to fill out the ranks, including any of those they entered the city with, such as: Sarevial, the elf apprentice they met shortly after entering Elidir (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04isgericircle00]{Isgeri Circle}); Padisco, the wounded veteran (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04eventapoorde00]{Event: A Poor Death}); Ozney, if they didn’t let the authorities take her to prison (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04eventinjusti00]{Event: Injustice is Served}); and Father Kindness and the Children’s Charity (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04hhouseoffoun00]{House of Found Family}). Otton Nettlebrush, the servant from the manor (@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth.JournalEntryPage.04eventnothank00]{Event: No Thank You Bite}), definitely joins. He appears in one of the early uprisings that Jenvirick suggests, but is later captured and reveals the PCs’ locations after being tortured in the Gyve. Feel free to flesh out additional Hellbreaker recruits and give them backgrounds that emphasize the iniquity in Isger. Creating connections with NPCs during the earlier part of the chapter will increase the impact of their eventual arrest and attempts to free them.

Quoster is largely being honest with the PCs. He fears his own nascent support for the Hellbreakers League will be discovered if the PCs are captured. What he's not fully open about is that the friend is actually his secret paramour in the city, Siadrius Pott (warmhearted male halfling oddities broker 0), one of the few other people who knows about Quoster's political activities. A PC can discern that the stakes are very personal for Quoster with a @Check[perception|dc:20|traits:concentrate,secret,action:sense-motive|name:Sense Motive] check to Sense Motive.

If the PCs agree to help, Quoster’s employees unload their supplies for the PCs to use as disguises. They’re comprehensive enough that the PCs can effectively create new identities for themselves that allow them to move largely unhindered around the city. If the PCs refuse to help, Quoster tries to pressure them, using his agreement to help the Hellbreakers League. If that fails, he eventually offers gold (slowly increasing the amount until the PCs agree), but his anger over what he sees as a bribe affects his trading in the future. Reduce the Hellbreakers League’s Reputation Points by 1.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.iUdpBZrYGjaB9Zvo]{Scarves} @UUID[Actor.n8UA4TYmargiOloX]{Quoster's Gift} @UUID[Actor.9grCC1Tbq9QZPcgG]{Quoster's Extra Gift}
Each PC is given a masquerade scarf and Quoster gives the group a staff of phantasms. If the PCs immediately agree to help, Quoster is touched and also gives them a ring of fair assessment.

One Way Out.name: One Way Out
One Way Out.text:
Chapter 6: One Way Out

Subsystems

This chapter makes use of several subsystems, which are listed here for easy reference.

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06riotatthepri00]{Riot at the Prison Gates} and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionthema00]{The Manor Job} both use the Victory Point system (GM Core 184).

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missiontheta00]{The Talisman Job} uses the infiltration subsystem (GM Core 196).

@UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22206oneway.JournalEntryPage.06missionrideo00]{Ride or Die} uses the chase subsystem (GM Core 192).

Following the PCs' victory over Ezio and the transformed Hedvend VI, they're able to regroup with their fellow Hellbreakers and celebrate their successful mission in recruiting Quoster. Unfortunately, they wake the next morning to learn of disaster: Caeto Vulaunex has declared martial law and is locking down the city so he can “catch the Hellbreaker assassins and bring them to justice.” The Hellbreakers are now trapped in enemy territory and framed for murder! They must find a way to escape the city before they're hunted down. Fortunately, they've made allies in Elidir, and the combination of Hedvend's assassination and Caeto's crackdown has the city up in arms and ripe for recruiting new Hellbreakers!

This chapter lasts roughly three weeks, to the end of Abadius. There's largely little time-specific pressure on the PCs; if they fail a mission, they can generally retreat and then try again, but doing so will likely increase their Suppression Points.

Concluding the Chapter.name: Concluding the Chapter
Concluding the Chapter.text:
Concluding the Chapter

The PCs are hailed as heroes by the Hellbreakers and their army for defeating Illcayna in combat. Maire spreads tales about the party's exploits, giving them titles like “Spring's Herald” or “Wight Mother's Bane.” She takes care to leave out identifying details; the PCs can encourage or discourage her or maybe even get a say on their epithet.

With this triumph, the Hellbreakers have cemented their place not only in Isger's politics, but also the nation's history. What's not likely going to be recorded in the books is the whereabouts of the warshard Illcayna had. The Hellbreakers' leadership decides to keep it safe in their headquarters.

The Hellbreakers also decide it best to collapse Urgathoa's temple to hide the grotto's entrance from those with ill intent. The PCs have a chance to study it fully beforehand and can always access it from above with flight if necessary. There's also a bottle of shared memories among Illcayna's possessions, which hints at the last Wonder of the Seasons, the wintry Woe. The mystery of Woe is outside the scope of this adventure, however, and is best explored after the PCs have liberated Isger.

The Wight Mother of Isger.name: The Wight Mother of Isger
The Wight Mother of Isger.text:
The Wight Mother of IsgerExtreme 7

After they arrive at the grotto, the PCs have 10 minutes to prepare before Illcayna gets there. Since the sun has set, the grotto has only dim light unless artificially modified.

The Wight Mother of IsgerExtreme 7

@UUID[Actor.oAwP9eeD7Ay5LsR2]{Warshard Wights (4)} @UUID[Actor.wuN9B7DRH8Ge6vlp]{Illcayna Alonnor}

Creatures: Illcayna chides the PCs for working against their own interests as she descends from above, summoning her warshard wights to the entrance. After all, she also seeks to free Isger! Illcayna tries to diminish the PCs' accomplishments while emphasizing how she has a destiny to fulfill. Too proud to see the possibility of her destruction, she and her warshard wights fight until destroyed.

Though this is an extreme encounter (as Illcayna is still very powerful), the PCs have several ways to turn the tide in their favor. What they've learned through their research comes into play now!

Warshard Extraction: A PC who understands how to remove Illcayna's warshard using Varlario's occult magnet can perform an Interact action while adjacent to Illcayna and wielding the magnet. Illcayna must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:29] save. On a failure, the warshard is pulled forcibly from her body and into that PC's possession. Illcayna loses her ability to use the Bleeding Heart of Urgathoa as a greater symbol of conflict. She also loses her bonus to saves against holy effects and her ability to make warshard-tipped entrail melee Strikes.

Final Feast: The PCs can either disarm Illcayna of Reaper's Sigh or use the prayer they learned through research to force it to fall from her body. Once she loses Reaper's Sigh, Illcayna cannot use her Reaper's Sigh Strikes. Should the PCs retrieve the scythe and successfully hit Illcayna with it, the Strike deals an additional @Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] persistent bleed damage. Each time Illcayna takes bleed damage from this effect, each undead creature within 60 feet (even undead summoned by Illcayna) must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:27] save or spend its next turn attacking only Illcayna. Illcayna's share blessing ability doesn't trigger if she is destroyed this way. As she is once again devoured, Illcayna wordlessly cries, her tears drawn to the pool.

Treasure: The PCs receive all items under Illcayna's item entry, including Reaper's Sigh and the Bleeding Heart of Urgathoa, which reverts to a greater symbol of conflict and a blood-red lump of warshard.

Reward: The PCs gain 5 Reputation Points for defeating the Wight Mother of Isger, stopping her curse, and ending the undead scourge she brought about.

Boon of the Isgeri Spirits: @UUID[Actor.23p0Mfk4TEygziRw]{Boon (Stag)} @UUID[Actor.2UFdpl2MxbZF0WUb]{Boon (Flies)} @UUID[Actor.658d90OXZt4AYvGx]{Boon (Neither)}
The first time the PCs take a long rest after their battle with Illcayna, they collectively experience a dream. A swarm of flies washes over a frozen land like snowflakes, while a stag stands opposite on lush grounds. A voice in their heads, booming yet soothing, asks which they choose. Those who once protected these lands made their choices. What would those protecting the lands now choose?

If the PCs pick the stag and its warm spring, they wake to find clawed bracers by their side. If they pick the flies and its desolate winter, they receive a runestone with a decaying rune instead. Refusing to pick or being split in opinion results in the PCs being jolted out of the dream to find a standard-grade duskwood shield.

The Siege of Finder's Gulch.name: The Siege of Finder's Gulch
The Siege of Finder's Gulch.text:
The Siege of Finder's GulchLow 7

This event occurs on the afternoon of the 19th of Calistril. Illcayna and her army descend upon Finder's Gulch to complete her curse. Luckily, Hellbreakers scouts spot their approach, and the PCs have time to prepare against the undead.

This encounter uses the skirmish warfare rules found on pages 158–169 of Battlecry! GMs should read up on these rules before running this encounter. The objective of this encounter is to destroy Illcayna's armies. This encounter begins in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07townentryroa00]{M1}, the town outskirts, and the buildings here are intact enough to be impassable for troops. Use the Finder's Gulch map.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Macro.UEzyYCOph4ZCw9VX]{Siege of Finder's Gulch Ambience} @UUID[Macro.Uc8XUXIdYfqHzg8Q]{Cleared Finder's Gulch Ambience}

Picking Troops: For combat, each PC takes command of a 7th-level troop from the following list: @UUID[Actor.qOTNJyD9rlVJkG5q]{Bandit Gang}, @UUID[Actor.VDGdU79R7nyLxVq8]{Elite Hobgoblin Battalion}, @UUID[Actor.m7pEOMcYYm6bJo4m]{Gnome Cannon Corps}, @UUID[Actor.BnX5wZ0wTg6UKCy1]{Stumpfield War Chanter Choir}, @UUID[Actor.ShinKJoVmNiKGaCT]{Umok Beastspeaker Circle}, and a @UUID[Actor.fATMwRZquEZnPFfO]{Weak Hellknight Cavalry Brigade}. A troop is available only if the PCs have recruited them earlier in the chapter, though enough elite hobgoblin battalions arrive from Logas to give each PC a troop to command.

The Siege of Finder's GulchLow 7

@UUID[Actor.LZA7KDqz5VdgNzR2]{Skeleton Mobs (2)} @UUID[Actor.2kX2edoMvUE8Eoay]{Wight Battalions (2)}

Creatures: Illcayna has an army of undead at her command, and the PCs and their troops face off against two skeleton mobs and two wight battalions. Other groups the Hellbreakers recruited hold the rest of the undead army at bay in other parts of the town, succeeding if the PCs do well but faltering if the PCs are also being routed.

Illcayna remains out of the fray for now, believing her army to be enough to crush the living who have invaded her town. She spectates in amusement until the PCs vanquish her troops. Then, she flies in the direction of the grotto, where the PCs can confront her.

Wight Queen's Thaw: When the undead army arrives, Alceo begins the counter-ritual if the PCs successfully researched it. As the skirmish battle nears its end, Alceo completes enough of the counter-ritual to affect Illcayna as described @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07areasofresea00]{Here}. She lets out a howl of rage but doesn't approach the grotto until this fight is over.

In Case of Failure, Break Ice: Should the tide of battle turn unfavorable, Phoebe orders the PCs to retreat to area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07templeofurga00]{M9} Once the PCs make it into the temple, the Riotmongers signal to explode the rocks damming the river (above area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07towncenterun00]{M2}). This causes the dam to break and the frozen river to rapidly crack and start flowing. The sweeping current floods the town, washing away Illcayna's armies.

Reward: The PCs earn 60 XP if they rout or defeat Illcayna's troops in this skirmish encounter.

Development: Defeating Illcayna's army is only a temporary setback for her. Though she might have lost the battle, she can still win the war if she makes her way into the Grotto of the Sacrificed. The PCs should head there as soon as possible.

Areas of Research.name: Areas of Research
Areas of Research.text:
Areas of Research

The PCs can perform research checks in the following areas to learn how to stop Illcayna.

Search Finder's Gulch: The town has been Illcayna's base of operations for years, so lingering traces of her energy and other information should help the PCs uncover her weaknesses;
Maximum RP 10;
Research Checks @Check[urgathoa-lore|dc:18] to recall information about related undead creatures, @Check[occultism|dc:21|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] or @Check[religion|dc:21|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to examine sacrificial sites, @Check[diplomacy|dc:23|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] or @Check[intimidation|dc:23|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to get information from Whispering Way cultists.

Commune in the Grotto: The Grotto of the Sacrificed holds mystical and spiritual energy that could help direct the PCs' research;
Maximum RP 10;
Research Checks @Check[isger-lore|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] or @Check[society|dc:20|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to decipher the many murals; @Check[diplomacy|dc:23|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to commune with the resident spirits; @Check[occultism|dc:25|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] or @Check[religion|dc:25|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to extract meaning from visions provided by the pool of memories.

Field Research: By scouring the remains of Gillamoor or by sneaking back into Elidir to find treatises on undeath, the PCs might learn about Illcayna's methods and her grasp on existence;
Maximum RP 5;
Research Checks @Check[occultism|dc:23|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] or @Check[religion|dc:23|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to glean knowledge from any discoveries, @Check[perception|dc:25|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to find specific books or clues, @Check[stealth|dc:25|traits:concentrate,exploration,linguistic,action:Research|name:Research] to stay hidden from lingering threats.

Scene Notes Point Tracking

@UUID[Actor.JhcGypphU3lMR1sw]{Research Points Tracker}

Stopping IllcaynaResearch 7

  • Unique
  • Divine
  • Undead

Research Checks search Finder's Gulch (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07mthemysteryo00]{M}), commune in the grotto (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07nthegrottoof00]{N}), field research (outside of Finder's Gulch)

3 Research Points The PCs find an inert sample of the disease carried by all children of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}: the pallid plague. They can then concoct a temporary vaccine against it, granting them a +2 circumstance bonus to their saves against Illcayna's pallid plague.

5 Research Points The PCs learn that the illumination of Bounty's Light empowers those who stand against undead like Illcayna. PCs and allies within the bright light shed by that relic gain a +2 status bonus to all saving throws against Illcayna's spells.

10 Research Points The PCs uncover stories of how Lifebloom is enchanted to strike fear into the hearts of wights who beheld the blade. A PC who wields that relic can spend a single action to brandish it like a religious symbol. Illcayna and any wights who can see this become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} (@Check[will|dc:23] save) and can't reduce the value of their frightened condition for as long as a living creature wields Lifebloom in their line of sight. At this point, Illcayna's undead minions sense that the PCs are learning how to defeat their progenitor and move to ambush them. If the PCs are outside Finder's Gulch (or the next time they leave the town), roll on the undead encounter chart.

12 Research Points The PCs understand that Varlario's occult magnet in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07desecratedch00]{M4} might be used to extract Illcayna's warshard from her body and master its usage. How to do so and its effects are described in Warshard Extraction @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07thewightmoth00]{Here}.

15 Research Points The PCs learn the full details of the Whispering Way's counter-ritual, Wight Queen's thaw. Alceo volunteers to perform the counter-ritual when Illcayna arrives to ensure the PCs can take the fight to her. Before each of her turns in the encounter with her, Illcayna must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:10]. On a failure, she is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for that round.

20 RP The echo of Cileidia's death (as seen in the haunt in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07towncenterun00]{M2}) can be turned against Illcayna if she's damaged by Reaper's Sigh. What happens if the PCs successfully turn the weapon against her is described in Final Feast @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07thewightmoth00]{Here}. How they might disarm her of the scythe remains a challenge, especially as it's melded into her arm. Learning this information produces another echo of Cileidia's death wherever the PCs are. They encounter the haunt from area M2 again, even if it has been deactivated.

25 RP The Urgathoan temple in Finder's Gulch (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07templeofurga00]{M9}) used to be a shrine to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aLCfEgt48SRUHnMC]{Jaidi}, the Azlanti goddess known as the Blessing and Bounty and spouse of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.mm1j6UbHqFCI8fwB]{Erastil}. Urgathoa replaced her as the tribe's patron after Earthfall took place. Evoking Jaidi's name and prayer is the key to purifying Reaper's Sigh; when in Illcayna's presence, a PC can spend an action with the concentrate trait and attempt a @Check[farming-lore|dc:25], @Check[nature|dc:25], or @Check[religion|dc:25] check to implore Jaidi to reclaim the scythe. On a success, Reaper's Sigh glows, dealing @Damage[2d6[spirit]] damage with the holy trait (double on a critical success) to Illcayna, who is then disarmed of the weapon. In such an instance, she can't pick it back up again.

Reward: The PCs receive 80 XP for completing their research on the topic. Otherwise, the PCs gain 30 XP.

Winter's End.name: Winter's End
Winter's End.text:
Winter's End

While Illcayna left Finder's Gulch unguarded more out of overconfidence than strategy, it does put the Hellbreakers in an odd position. Instead of attacking Illcayna in her home, they must now keep her from reaching the Grotto of the Sacrificed to complete her ritual and enact her curse. It's more likely, therefore, that the Hellbreakers will find themselves under siege soon. Simply throwing their troops at the undead would be ineffective, but luckily, the Whispering Way has been plotting against Illcayna, seeking to weaken her through her very own curse via a counter-ritual they call Wight Queen's thaw. The PCs can learn about this counter-ritual through Varlario Demicci or her notes (area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07westtown000000]{M5}).

Once the PCs have cleared Finder's Gulch of threats, they have time to research this counter-ritual and other ways to weaken Illcayna until she returns on the 19th. Alceo suggests that they look into how to stop Illcayna if none of the PCs think to engage in this research on their own. This investigation uses the Research subsystem on page 190 of GM Core. Most of the research takes place in Finder's Gulch, but the PCs might need to venture out to other settlements to find answers. Each research check takes 4 hours, but this doesn't include any travel time to go to other places.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.kDCQGeEcnQXJYbA0]{Fortify Finder's Gulch}

Meanwhile, under the direction of the Riotmongers, any assembled Hellbreakers and their allies begin fortifying Finder's Gulch in preparation for Illcayna's return. Instead of researching, PCs can use the intervening time to perform downtime activities and continue to help settlements, recruit troops, or break the curse in Gillamoor if they haven't yet.

Pool of Memories.name: Pool of Memories
Pool of Memories.text:
N5. Pool of Memories

Were it not for its reflective surface, one might not even realize this is a pool of water. The water is surprisingly thin and does not impede movement at all.

Any PCs who drink the waters here receive a rush of ancient memories in flashes, mostly involving the past inhabitants' struggle against the four-centuries-long Taldane incursion. How this pool formed is sadly a magical art lost to time.

Each time the PCs drink, they gain the ability to understand the spirits in the grotto for 1 hour. However, they must also succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for the same duration. The DC of the save increases by 2 for each subsequent drink, and the condition also increases by 1, up to stupefied 3. Upon three failures (a critical failure counts as two), the PC is permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} as they become burdened by ancient memories. The stupefied condition can be reduced by appropriate spells, but the permanent slowed condition requires effects like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} or stronger to remove.

Mural of Winter.name: Mural of Winter
Mural of Winter.text:
N4. Mural of Winter

In a rather unusual choice, perhaps to represent themselves walking to their deaths, the artists painted the mural of winter surrounding the entrance. The border of painted frost and snow can almost be mistaken to be the real thing. Few creatures are depicted except for three humanoid figures. They huddle in a hut, making handicrafts by a hearth. One is draped in gold and silver. The other two wear clothes of many colors, and their handicrafts are just as bright.

PCs who succeed at a @Check[religion|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[society|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge recognize the figure in gold to be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.d56paSkcwvll2OhR]{Abadar} and another to be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.gxwmzxUWBOhdgFSN]{Shelyn}. If they roll at least 28, they presume by process of elimination that the other figure should be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.ZfN7jkK6boU1FuiS]{Zon-Kuthon}, though he looks nothing like the Midnight Lord. This is because the image is of the god @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.ZfN7jkK6boU1FuiS]{Zon-Kuthon} used to be, called Dou-Bral in the days before he changed.

Mural of Autumn.name: Mural of Autumn
Mural of Autumn.text:
N3. Mural of Autumn

A large wheat field serves as the mural's backdrop. Some people are harvesting, while others are hunting on horseback. There is a disconcerting aura despite the serene image, as scorpions and jackals leer at the bountiful harvest.

It's here that the PCs notice that there's a faint carving of a serpent that wraps around the entire grotto. PCs who succeed at a @Check[farming-lore|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[religion|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge recognize the favored animals of Rovagug and Lamashtu, with the serpent likely representing @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}. If they roll 28 or higher, the PCs recall that there's an ancient calendar system where a leap month would be inserted at different times of the year, and that Asmodeus might symbolize that "rogue" month. This is highly ironic as Taldor, the odd army out in the war against the wights, ended up splintered, and the province that broke the empire later dedicated itself to the Prince of Hell. It's as if the Isgeri predicted Cheliax's infernal future.

The Rightful Goddess: One of the feminine figures seated on a horse holds a black scythe (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.HofVPZ0eimPVK9jb]{Reaper's Sigh}), though the distinct lack of flies and rot suggests she is not @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}. Every time the PCs fall asleep to the effect in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07muralofsumme00]{N2}, this woman visits them in their dreams. Other than traditional Kellid attire, she wears stripes of white ash. As she approaches, the woman bleaches as she becomes a wight and her steed rots to a skeleton.

This is a spirit much like those encountered in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07muralofsprin00]{N1}, except she speaks from the perspective of those who became the wights that defended Isger. As Illcayna's direct ancestor, this spirit knows Illcayna's backstory. If questioned about Illcayna, the spirit laments that their ill choice condemned her and how their holy implement, Reaper's Sigh, was corrupted as punishment. The spirit urges the PCs to "evoke the true goddess of the harvest" to cleanse the scythe; a PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:34] check knows that the spirit is referring to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.aLCfEgt48SRUHnMC]{Jaidi}.

Mural of Summer.name: Mural of Summer
Mural of Summer.text:
N2. Mural of Summer

Though the border of this mural depicts flames, the painting is welcoming rather than intimidating. The center depicts the Kellid tribes on one side and a group of goblinoids emerging from a forest on the other. Bounty's Light sits between the two, ambiguous in which direction it's passed. A dove with a sun crown flies above the exchange, and a stag and rhinoceros flank the image as witnesses.

PCs who succeed at a @Check[religion|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[survival|dc:23|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] check to Recall Knowledge recognize the favored animals to be those of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.BNycwu3I21dTh4D9]{Sarenrae}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.mm1j6UbHqFCI8fwB]{Erastil}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.88vRw2ZVPax4hhga]{Gorum}. If a PC rolls 28 or higher, they intuit that the message is about two peoples at peace, but that the chances of war breaking out are ever present.

Midsummer Dreams: When a PC holding Bounty's Light touches the mural, everyone in the grotto must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] save against a 4th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.o4lRVTwSxnOOn5vl]{Sleep} spell. PCs who sleep for 1 minute from the spell wake as if they had taken a full long rest. Any daily preparations necessary are included in this effect. A PC who benefited from this nap must wait a week before they can benefit from it again. They can accept the sleep effect any number of times.

Mural of Spring.name: Mural of Spring
Mural of Spring.text:
N1. Mural of Spring

Flowers blooming upon branches without leaves make up the border of this mural. Members of the Twelve Tribes in varied clothing and body paint holding their sacred implements gather around a warrior who raises Lifebloom. On the trees and field flanking this image, animals rouse from sleep. A butterfly bearing the moon on its wings and a flock of whip-poor-wills stand out in particular. There are also sprays of petals that suggest wind blowing.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:23] or @Check[nature|dc:23] check recognizes the favored animals of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.JgqH3BhuEuA4Zyqs]{Desna} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma}. If their result is at least 28, they also discern that the animals and wind likely represent Gozreh.

Spring Awakening: If a PC holding Lifebloom touches the mural outside of combat, all in the grotto find themselves in a nightscape version of the grotto. Specters of the Isgeri surround them. If any PCs speak Hallit, they recognize a few words as the ghosts speak an ancient form of the language. Once they overcome the language barrier by drinking from the Pool of Memories in area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07poolofmemori00]{N5}, likely at the spirits' own urging, the PCs can communicate freely and learn about the founding of Isger from these warriors, as covered in this chapter's opening.

While these spirits don't know Illcayna's backstory, they do know she is kin. As spirits, they cannot attack her unless she attacks them first, something Illcayna knows as well. The warriors are therefore unable to help the PCs in taking down Illcayna, though they are willing to share their experiences.

The Grotto of the Sacrificed.name: The Grotto of the Sacrificed
The Grotto of the Sacrificed.text:
N. The Grotto of the Sacrificed

The walls of this 20-foot-high ellipsoid cave are fully decorated with murals whose magical pigments survived the ravages of time and weather. Despite Illcayna's influence, the plants here remain lush, though they frost over in winter. A large opening about the same size as the pool within the grotto allows the natural light in.

As perhaps one last attempt to record who they were, the last of the Twelve Tribes painted the walls to depict their culture, icons, and beliefs. There are four major murals, each dedicated to a season, and since there were three tribes per season, every season is also associated with three patron deities. This connection partially survived to modern times in the names of the months of the modern Avistani calendar.

Reward: The PCs receive 80 XP for fully exploring all areas of the grotto.

Clearing Finder's Gulch.name: Clearing Finder's Gulch
Clearing Finder's Gulch.text:
Clearing Finder's Gulch

It takes the Hellbreakers army 3 days to travel from Logas to Finders Gulch. After arriving, they camp on the outskirts, which allows the PCs to rest safely outside the town without fear of being attacked. As the army needs time to recover from their march and conduct some last-minute training, the task of clearing out the town of Finder's Gulch falls to the PCs. Once the ruins are cleared, the army moves into the town itself and Finder's Gulch effectively becomes a level 3 settlement.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Macro.Z1fYuUqosj1WeshI]{Toggle Cleared Finder's Gulch Ambience}

Treasure: The army arrives with two catapults (Guns and Gears 75), which Rhokrag eagerly gives a demonstration with. The PCs are given control of these and can put them anywhere in Finder's Gulch. Moving the siege weapons into place takes an hour each time.

Reward: If the PCs manage to clear the town of hostiles before or on the day the army arrives, they gain 50 XP and 5 Reputation Points. If they clear it after the army arrives, they only receive 30 XP and 2 Reputation Points.

Temple of Urgathoa.name: Temple of Urgathoa
Temple of Urgathoa.text:
M9. Temple of Urgathoa

This cave used to be a shrine to another goddess until Illcayna claimed it. The cultists destroyed the original reliefs and covered what remained with depictions of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}'s hedonism. The interior is draped in chains of phalanges connected with sinew, a way for Illcayna to display of the number of creatures she has recruited into her fold over the years.

Fortunately for the PCs, Illcayna is out surveying her work. She has left the temple unguarded out of arrogance, believing she and her plans are untouchable. The PCs have plenty of time to Search the location and discover the secret entrance to the tunnels that lead to the Darklands. If the PCs have Bounty's Light or Lifebloom in their possession, fluorescent stencils of hands and feet appear along the walls of the tunnels, guiding them to @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07nthegrottoof00]{The Grotto of the Sacrificed}. The journey takes only 10 minutes, though the winding path makes it feel much longer.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.dv8i9N5b7AXxf8L3]{Reveal Secret Door}

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.brbCUQ2ndeQyJYlk]{Treasury Box}
In a treasure box behind a good lock (five @Check[thievery|dc:30|traits:manipulate,skill,action:pick-a-lock|name:Pick a Lock] checks), the PCs find a potion of flying, a pallid crystal, and a discarded greater staff of healing.

Frozen River.name: Frozen River
Frozen River.text:
M8. Frozen River

This part of Finder's Gulch has been flooded since a rockslide downstream (northeast of area @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07towncenterun00]{M2}) slowed the flow of the stream. As it's currently winter, the water has frozen in slippery ice. The ice is considered difficult terrain, though a creature can attempt to move on it at full Speed. To do so, they must succeed at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:28|traits:move,skill,action:balance|name:Balance] check to maintain their balance. On failure, they fall prone.

Scene Notes SFX

@UUID[Playlist.PlNptESy0gmGTFov.PlaylistSound.AwkwXZcc2UobxgfS]{Crack}

Frozen RiverHazard 8

@UUID[Actor.sVgPKUGKXkb7TkJR]{Thin Ice}

Hazard: The river's ice is thin. If two or more PCs walk onto the ice, they hear a series of metallic cracks, indications that the ice is about to break.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.McvTNQCGYh33Ui1f]{Riverbed Bottom}
If a PC Searches the bottom of the riverbed, they find a delaying aeon stone and a greater devilwing badge that were dropped by adventurers who fell to Illcayna.

Empty Road.name: Empty Road
Empty Road.text:
M7. Empty Road Low 7

This straight path used to be the commercial heart of town, filled with businesses that were small but essential. Now, the shopfronts are devoid of goods, and the residences above them are empty.

M7. Empty RoadLow 7

@UUID[Actor.5p0bRY2CAkwUuRS0]{Skeletal Hellknight Bonesinger}

Creature: A skeletal Hellknight bonesinger patrols these streets in a mockery of Cheliax's supposed grip on the nation.

Sarcovalt Hive.name: Sarcovalt Hive
Sarcovalt Hive.text:
M6. Sarcovalt HiveModerate 7

North of the town center lie several buildings that used to be the political center of Finder's Gulch. The largest building served as an open town hall beside which the mayor lived. There are also two community gardens: one for herbs and one (surprisingly) for poisonous plants.

M6. Sarcovalt HiveModerate 7

@UUID[Actor.UeURurKrxfGOomtR]{Sarcovalt Swarm}

Creature: Where there is fervent @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} worship, there are sarcovalts. Occasionally, when Illcayna deems a person so unworthy that she wouldn't even give them the privilege of becoming undead, she summons sarcovalts to dispatch the eyesore. It's been a while since Illcayna sacrificed servants worthy or unworthy, and the hungry sarcovalt hive in the area pounces on the PCs the first chance they get.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.e9q3fDMYVhAqQ1nb]{Garden}
If the PCs Search the poisonous plant garden, they can obtain a dose of tangle root toxin and a dose of nettleweed residue.

West Town.name: West Town
West Town.text:
M5. West Town

Before Illcayna's transformation, the Ashen Church lived and operated in the west part of town. The secret basements and rooms here remained in use to create undead after the cult's annihilation. A brief exploration of the buildings reveals paperwork and correspondence left behind by Illcayna's servants, some half-finished before their authors were sacrificed to the growing curse. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[religion|dc:24], @Check[undead-lore|dc:24], or @Check[warfare-lore|dc:24] check can use the information here to research the types of troops they might face in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07thesiegeoffi00]{The Siege of Finder's Gulch}. On a critical success, they can also estimate the number of troops they'll run up against.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.ip6oQgUJ2aH5jzbl]{Buildings}
Searching through the buildings, the PCs can uncover 220 gp worth of onyx left behind from @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.c3b6LdLlQDPngNIb]{Create Undead} rituals. There's also enough information here for them to learn the ritual if they wish.

Desecrated Church.name: Desecrated Church
Desecrated Church.text:
M4. Desecrated Church Severe 7

The Urgathoans have thoroughly desecrated this former temple to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma}. All windows are broken, and the walls have been graffitied with praises to the Pallid Princess. Attempts to fully tear down the building have always failed, so the structure was eventually left alone. When the delegation from the Whispering Way requested a permanent residence, the Urgathoans arranged for them to move into this building as a stealthy insult.

The Whispering Way's assistance is naturally not altruistic, as Tar-Baphon would not mind having another Child of Urgathoa as a servant. If that servant came with a piece of territory, all the better. There's also the concern that a warshard-empowered Illcayna could become an enemy, as she would soundly reject the idea of serving anyone but @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}. The Whispering Way thus sent the dhampir witch Varlario Demicci (carefree agender dhampir witch 8) to Isger as both a goodwill ambassador and a spy. Varlario has furthered Illcayna's plans and in the process learned many of her weaknesses. The witch has even developed a spell to deprive the Wight Mother of Isger of her warshard should the need arise.

M4. Desecrated ChurchSevere 7

@UUID[Actor.hHhNGeXL0NjDoJoP]{Sarcovalt} @UUID[Actor.qmKmX6XsLTOylA1o]{Skavelings (2)} @UUID[Actor.lHLnIS4PqAL8un48]{Varlario Demicci}

Creatures: With Illcayna busy with her ritual, Varlario found time to invite a sarcovalt and two skavelings from the Whispering Way over as guests. Varlario doesn't mind the PCs overhearing their conversation, finding it amusing that anyone might consider taking Illcayna down instead of fleeing. In their opinion, the wannabe-heroes are a few months too late; if Illcayna hadn't gotten the warshard, they might have stood a chance. If they converse with Varlario, the PCs easily get the sense that the spy wouldn't mind establishing a secret alliance. While Varlario can assist the PCs in learning Illcayna's weaknesses, making a deal with the Whispering Way greatly harms the reputation of the Hellbreakers, causing the PCs to lose 5 Reputation Points.

In combat, the sarcovalt and the skavelings fight to the death, while Varlario fights until they are below 50 Hit Points. Once they hit this threshold, Varlario begs for mercy, offering anything the PCs wish in exchange for their life. If the PCs don't give up, Varlario distracts them by throwing their items at them before using their translocate spell to flee.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.cAiDvNuFkiEwhReY]{Church}
Other than loot from the enemies, the PCs can find a powerful occult magnet Varlario designed to steal Illcayna's warshard. The PCs can also learn from Varlario's notes that Illcayna's final ritual is set to take effect on the evening of the 19th of Calistril, as dusk gives way to night. To finalize the curse, Illcayna must return to a location in Finder's Gulch that Varlario hasn't been privy to. The location in question is @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07nthegrottoof00]{The Grotto of the Sacrificed}

Sacrificial Site.name: Sacrificial Site
Sacrificial Site.text:
M3. Sacrificial SiteLow 7

Worshippers of other faiths were sacrificed at this patch of scorched earth in the past. There used to be a haunt here, but with Illcayna's ritual underway, it has dissipated to allow something else to take its place.

M3. Sacrificial SiteLow 7

@UUID[Actor.xNBxWijvqTrfS9pt]{Sulfur Zombie} @UUID[Actor.ZjHssJdF1D8qZaIG]{Erinys Sister Wights (3)}

Creature: The most recent sacrifice of Illcayna's own servants created an incendiary undead known as a sulfur zombie. Illcayna considers dealing with these residues to be beneath her. She appointed three newly risen erinys sister wights to keep the fiery undead in check. Having been defeated by the PCs in the past, the undead sisters fight until destroyed. Note that the erinys sister wights only have a claw and a dart Strike instead of the usual attacks of a wight.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.hUzHeoDlHYc3CyBT]{Zombie Ashes}
The sulfur zombie crumbles to dust once defeated. Its ashes can be collected into a dose of dust of corpse animation.

Town Center.name: Town Center
Town Center.text:
M2. Town CenterModerate 7

After her original transformation into a Child of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}, Illcayna took control of the undead that killed her and had them track down their makers. She made sure to capture the head priestess of the Ashen Church, Cileidia Iomandi. Illcayna always thought Cileidia was unworthy to serve Urgathoa, as the old Ustalav woman was more focused on planning how to attack her homeland than enacting the Pallid Princess's will. Much like how she fed herself to the undead, Illcayna cut Cileidia and let the wights devour the priestess. While it was technically a proper final sacrifice in honor of a servant of Urgathoa who completed their task, Illcayna was personally glad to rid the cult of what she considered to be an embarrassment of a worshipper.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.QRUqjL9X4BCXOzDC]{Cannibalization of the Priestess}

M2. Town CenterModerate 7

@UUID[Actor.LzADvDePFF4XOMml]{Cannibalization of the Priestess}

Haunt: The echoes of Cileidia's gruesome end manifested as a haunt in the years after her death. The cultists serving Illcayna tolerated it, especially since she was fond of rewatching Cileidia's demise. Since the curse ritual began, however, echoes of Illcayna's own death have resurfaced as well. The similarities between the two priestesses' deaths caused the two spiritual echoes to resonate until they merged.

When the haunt is active, creatures trained in Perception and not caught by the haunt notice a feminine figure flickering in the center of the haunt, which throngs of undead descend upon and devour. The visage of the figure changes rapidly, alternating between images of two different priestesses. The young priestess cries tears of joy as she holds out her arms to accept her fate, while the elderly priestess cries out in pain and panic, her arms bound to pillars with ropes. Both appear to be bleeding from long cuts made to the body.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.IaTuhpju7Ob3QBc2]{Red Cloth}
The first time the PCs disable the haunt, it disappears with a scream and leaves behind a tattered red cloth that acts like a blade thousand-pains fulu.

Town Entry Road.name: Town Entry Road
Town Entry Road.text:
M1. Town Entry RoadTrivial 7

The abandoned farms that flank the path into town used to house an acolyte and a necromancer who served as lookouts. Both have been sacrificed to the curse unwillingly.

M1. Town Entry RoadTrivial 7

@UUID[Actor.lWeJ29q2g2PikrvW]{Redcaps (2)}

Creatures: As she still needed someone to keep watch, Illcayna infected the redcaps on the outskirts of town with a fungal affliction known as the red drip. She held the disease in remission and threatened to withdraw her protection should the fey refuse to serve her. The redcaps grudgingly accepted, as they preferred to continue their murderous ways here instead of back in the First World.

While the redcaps are more than happy to make the PCs their latest victims, any offer to cure the visibly infected fey makes them hesitate. If the PCs successfully cure the redcaps, they decide to look away for a few minutes and let the PCs pass. They warn that if the PCs return this way, though, they'll view it as a sign that the PCs wish to be murdered and will fight to the death.

The Mystery of Finder's Gulch.name: The Mystery of Finder's Gulch
The Mystery of Finder's Gulch.text:
M. The Mystery of Finder's Gulch

Map Usage

The scale of the Finder's Gulch's town map makes it more suitable for the skirmish encounter below than for individual encounters. GMs should use appropriate settlement Flip-Mats or maps of their choosing to better represent the area the PCs are in. Some particularly useful maps are noted below.

  • Pathfinder Flip-Mat Classics: City Streets
  • Pathfinder Flip-Mat: Ghost Towns
  • Pathfinder Flip-Tiles: Urban Slums Expansion
  • Pathfinder Flip-Tiles: Urban Starter Set
  • Pathfinder Map Pack: Urban Sites

The town of Finder's Gulch suffered a fate similar to Gillamoor's over a century ago, though rather than a curse, it was Illcayna herself who brought ruination. She didn't discover the significance of her lair until she explored the twisting tunnels beyond the cave of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}'s temple. Though most led to the Darklands, there was one that led upward, ending at a grotto that featured a pool clearer than crystal. While observing the ancient murals on the walls and drinking from its waters, Illcayna learned this chamber was the site where her ancestors first accepted Urgathoa's grace.

It was also here that the last warband of the Twelve Tribes of the Seasons gathered before they took up arms against their undead brethren and became the Isgeri. The truth was in the settlement's name all along: this valley was the place where Isger was founded, spiritually and philosophically, in both undeath and death. Most would have been humbled by such revelations, but when Illcayna gained this knowledge, it only solidified her belief that she was the chosen ruler of Isger.

Scouting Finder's Gulch: Illcayna's name is whispered as an urban legend; learning that she's the mastermind behind the current undead horde shocks the Hellbreakers' recruits. Many begin to despair, as they were expecting to fight cultists or destroy a cursed item, not take up arms against a being of legend and nightmares. As the Riotmongers do all they can to repair the nascent army's morale, they ask the PCs to scout out Finder's Gulch and prove that Illcayna's forces are not invincible.

After she obtained a warshard, Illcayna believed she'd become untouchable and decided that her strongest servants would be of more use fueling the undead reservoir needed for her nationwide curse than they would protecting her. Some of these servants readily give their existence, while others futilely attempt to resist her. Finder's Gulch is therefore low in security for the first time in decades—an opportunity the PCs must seize.

The Cursed Grave.name: The Cursed Grave
The Cursed Grave.text:
L3. The Cursed GraveModerate 7

Safe Havens

The PCs only have Saringallow to return to when they start this chapter, since both Elidir and Logas are under martial law or overrun by undead, respectively. With the success of the Chitterwood Offensive, Logas becomes available as a place where the PCs can recuperate from the 7th of Calistril onward. The city is considered a level 8 settlement. Logas also provides two @UUID[Actor.CtBBPQ2rGt8ufHEn]{Hobgoblin Battalions} to the PCs' forces.

The merchant Illcayna cursed was an aiuvarin man from rural Druma named Dottol Harpier. Though his future with the caravan looked bright, Dottol's life was cut short when he caught dysentery and died. Without a will to execute and not wanting to transport a possibly infectious body back to Druma, the caravan opted to bury him in a respectable grave in Gillamoor, unknowingly dooming the town.

Gillamoor's graveyard is up on a 10-foot-high hill, surrounded by a brick-and-iron fence that's 5 feet tall. All of the graves look like they've been dug up and desecrated. Dottol's grave has been dug up as well, but his gravestone is still intact. Other than his name, the gravestone notes the year of his death (4702 ar) and a single sentence that reads, “Forever in the memory of the 27th contingent of the Mercenary League.”

The PCs can deduce Dottol's ancestry and cause of death with a successful @Check[medicine|dc:28] check. If they succeed at a @Check[religion|dc:23] or @Check[occultism|dc:23] check, they also learn that his bones are saturated with void energy that's bleeding into the surrounding soil. If the PCs surpass this check by 5, they notice that there's an even deeper well of undeath feeding and amplifying the curse on the body. In fact, an entire ocean's worth of void energy rumbles beneath Isger, which can only be observed here because the body is tapping into it.

Lifting the Curse: If Brakknap isn't with the party, the PCs can break the curse with rituals such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Dbd5W6G8U2vzWolN]{Consecrate} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.xKHq2Eisapixvj6q]{Divine Keystone} of 4th rank or higher. Other than the cost of time, the PCs might need to head to Logas or Saringallow to obtain ingredients if they don't have any on hand.

If Brakknap is with the party, however, he reveals he knows of a faster method to break the curse that is made possible with the help of his ancestors.
