Some goblins request that the PCs establish a formal holiday to celebrate the alliance of goblinoids and humanoids in Isger, as goblins did much to fight against both Cheliax's forces and the undead invasion. The passing of Bounty's Light between the two groups could be reestablished as a tradition, or a new way to highlight peace might be implemented. Here are some suggestions.

  • A festival (the goblins suggest a pickle festival)
  • Replanting trees in the Chitterwood
  • A day of reconciliation
  • Educational reforms

All in all, peace is still a work in progress for Isger as it recovers from the undead scourge and the aftereffects of Cheliax's neglectful rule.

Hellish Remnants.name: Hellish Remnants
Hellish Remnants.text:
Hellish Remnants

Though Cheliax is formally detached from Isger, its hellish claws dug deep into the very bones of the nation's structure and society, and its influence remains strong. Most notably, the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys has an impeccable reputation and holds substantial social power. Even if Isger is free, these nuns have a mission: to spread the faith of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} and care for orphans in need of their deity's strict and vengeful guidance. In fact, there are plenty of new orphans for them to care for in the aftermath of the undead uprising that Caeto neglected to address.

PCs may wish to oust the Sisterhood from Isger, along with all traces of Asmodeus, or they might partner with them. Sister Marcella (pious human monk 6) comes forward as the Sisterhood's representative and beseeches the PCs to allow the Sisterhood to continue their charitable work, swearing the Sisters' allegiance is to Asmodeus and not to Cheliax. She is willing to sign a (non-magical) contract to formalize the agreement and concedes to most stipulations unless they directly interfere with her faith's practices. In return for the Sisterhood's continued existence, she offers a prize: the location of a small warshard at a nunnery in the Aspodell Mountains, where the stone's presence has mutated a herd of stony goats in the Sisters' care into living dawnsilver.

Should the PCs prefer to oust the Sisters, most go without protest except for Sister Kavinna (fanatical female human nun 10), who rallies pious Asmodeans against the new governors of Isger and demands that Asmodeus be formally named the patron deity of Isger. If her demands aren't met, she begins kidnapping children to indoctrinate them to the ways of Asmodeus, determined to fulfill her duties to her deity no matter the cost.

Fractured Army.name: Fractured Army
Fractured Army.text:
Fractured Army

Not all are eager to accept Isger's new direction. Its official military splinters into several factions, with only one electing to accept Isger's new leadership. Commander Nil Harovin (militaristic male human soldier 12) leads one such faction, the Blazing Sword, striking at Elidir before the Hellbreakers can cement their position there. Nil believes that the Hellbreakers are too soft to properly lead the country and determines that military governance is the only appropriate answer. He is backed by the noble Vittoria Legoto (churlish female human aristocrat 10), who hopes to become Isger's new governor. Vittoria's funding and social status keeps Elidiran socialites in check as the Blazing Sword attempts to take hold of the capital and declare itself the new leaders of Isger.

Other factions become bands of roving bandits, preying on the chaos of change, while others yet turn to vigilantism, untrusting of the new order. Captain Carista Frey (charismatic female human soldier 9) leads the largest vigilante group, the True Army, and refuses to join any forces led by revolutionaries.

The Iron Queen.name: The Iron Queen
The Iron Queen.text:
The Iron Queen

Lady Kaltessa Iyis has made Isger her domain for centuries, biding her time to perfect her plans. She isn't pleased to learn the nation has been taken by a group of rebellious upstarts. While she doesn't directly intervene, she sets her agents to work on unraveling the authority of the Hellbreakers League, forcing them into a position that better serves Mammon's desires.

The first of these agents is Niceforo Zikka (stern male human champion of Mammon 12), a financier who petitions for a seat in government as the treasurer. Niceforo is upfront about his intentions to see Isger profit off its new independence and won't take no for an answer, swaying citizens to support him lest Isger fall into financial disaster after detaching from Cheliax. His true motive is to disseminate coins from Erebus throughout Isger's population via the bank, organically spreading his master's influence throughout the region through trade and market.

Petricca Segracci (ostentatious female nephilim crime boss 10) is another lackey of Kaltessa's, paid to attack shipments and starve the nation of incoming resources to keep the Hellbreakers busy while the priestess sets up her plans. Kaltessa also has connections to the Druman merchant Silgrey Dawnsleeve (ambitious female dwarf capitalist 9), who owns swaths of Isgeri land and plans to own more on behalf of the Prophecies of Kalistrade. Silgrey works with Petricca to lower the costs of settlements so she can easily purchase land while promising a portion to Kaltessa.

Seeking Woe.name: Seeking Woe
Seeking Woe.text:
Seeking Woe

When Illcayna is defeated, the PCs find a potion of shared memories in her possession. Drinking the potion reveals a memory of Illcayna finding a magically hidden message in the mural of winter in the Grotto of the Sacrificed, leading to a vision of the fourth Wonder of the Seasons, Woe.

The vision details an icy figure in the mountains wearing a mantle of snowflakes. The PCs can seek Woe in the Menador Mountains, where it's currently in the possession of a powerful winter hag named Zamoranna (artistic female hag 10). Zamoranna desires to preserve the beauty of the world and ignore the ugliness of humanoid societies. Believing people are most beautiful when they're happy, she visits villages and takes in travelers, lavishing them with gifts and working to help people gain their heart's desires only to freeze them into solid ice sculptures at the height of their happiness. Her icy mountain lair is filled with dozens of such frozen art pieces.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.rikanygoG7zWhb59]{Woe}Item 10

  • Unique
  • Magical
  • Relic
  • Water

Repairing the Capital.name: Repairing the Capital
Repairing the Capital.text:
Repairing the Capital

Elidir suffered great damage from the PCs' escape and is still in the hands of Hellknights. The Hellbreakers League must negotiate a surrender from maralictor Lucia Devona (serious female human Hellknight 10), whom Caeto left in charge in his absence. Even if Caeto survived and surrendered, Lucia refuses to give in and must be persuaded via a thorough legal battle or trial by combat. Killing Lucia is an option, but this foments deep fear and resentment among the pro-Cheliax elites and makes them more likely to stage their own eventual rebellion.

Even without Cheliax's direct intervention, there are plenty of loyal Chelaxians determined to bring down the Hellbreakers League and restore fiendish order so they can continue to benefit off a government that cares more about appeasing its patrons than helping its people. Cygnetus Frawn (flamboyant nonbinary human dandy 9) prances about the city bemoaning its fall from glory, lamenting the lack of riches Elidir once had and besmirching the name of the Hellbreakers as much as they can. Nerina Halfsong (spoiled female dromaar socialite 10) demands reparations for all the destruction the Hellbreakers wrought on the city, starting with throwing her a birthday ball since hers was canceled thanks to Hellbreaker-inspired riots. Priest Vindictus Ricci (fanatical male human priest 8) protests daily outside the cathedral of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}, crying out that the Hellbreakers have sinned against their patron deity and will bring destruction to Isger. These elites, while petty and frivolous, hold most of Elidir's (and therefore the nation's) wealth and have substantial influence over the direction of the city.

Hell's Destiny.name: Hell's Destiny
Hell's Destiny.text:
Hell's Destiny

While Isger still has plenty of adventure left, PCs who wish to continue the fight against Cheliax can transition into the next Adventure Path, Hell's Destiny. In this campaign, the PCs join various factions such as Andoran and Ravounel to directly confront Cheliax and mount an attack against its hellish forces as their enemy prepares their most diabolical plan yet.

Further Adventures.name: Further Adventures
Further Adventures.text:
Further Adventures

The following scenarios are potential storylines contingent upon the PCs successfully completing the objectives of the adventure.

The Knight Steward.name: The Knight Steward
The Knight Steward.text:
The Knight Steward

In the event that the PCs fail to defeat Caeto in Saringallow, he quickly amasses the forces and authority to crush the Hellbreakers League leadership in one swift blow. Saringallow is swept up in a wave of brutal interrogations, weeding out anyone with even the slightest sympathy for rebels. The most prominent leaders are transported back to Elidir, where a public execution is held for each individual rebel leader every week so as to draw out anyone foolish and loyal enough to attempt a rescue. The Riotmongers are saved for last and executed together in a small show of kindness from Caeto.

Ardano Grizzi III (exacting male human governor 12) is chosen as the new steward of Isger. Unlike Hedvend, Ardano is ruthlessly efficient and has little love for finery or the spoiled elites. He quickly purges the government of anyone he deems too soft and promotes officials of his own choice such as Reverine Hallowell (cunning female human politician 9) and Justiro Adama (precise male gnome machinist 10). His rule is severe to make up for the recent chaos and even the elites of Elidir find themselves stifled under his iron hand.

The Hellbreakers are broken, but their story doesn't end. The numerous allies they made and the people they helped remember who it was that truly cared for and defended Isger in its time of need. The image of a rose growing through Abrogail Thrune's broken crown becomes a widespread symbol of resistance, along with an anti-Caeto version popular in the countryside that depicts his cracked face with thorny roses bursting through it. In this bleak present, hope is still alive, as are the PCs, and it will persevere as they continue to fight oppression.

Reign of the Wight Mother.name: Reign of the Wight Mother
Reign of the Wight Mother.text:
Reign of the Wight Mother

Should Illcayna succeed in her ritual, she becomes the mortal herald of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} and restores the might of the warshard embedded in her chest. This turns her into a powerful mythic being who quickly takes over Isger as she weaves a curse of undeath into the very bones of the nation, transforming it into a tribute state for Urgathoa. The goblins of the Chitterwood burrow deep underground, while those above ground are forced to flee or perish as fodder for Illcayna's endless army of wights. Isger is at last free from Cheliax's devilish grasp only to find itself bound by a different type of tyrant.

Ironically, Illcayna's greatest enemy might be another terrible force of undeath: the Whispering Tyrant, Tar-Baphon. Tar-Baphon is displeased to find a rival for world domination, especially since they use similar methods of manipulating undeath, and plots to raise Whispering Way supporters against Illcayna. He also sends spies and infiltrators into the camps of his own enemies to manipulate them into taking down the Wight Mother for him, hoping his foes will weaken each other enough to allow him to destroy them all in one fell swoop.

Kinza (passionate female human cleric 6), a descendant of the original Isgeri tribes, suggests seeking warshards to aid in striking down Illcayna. The Hellbreakers League knows the approximate location of one: the very warshard they gave the Eagle Knights in exchange for their alliance, which went missing along with its carriers in the town of Falcon's Hollow in Darkmoon Vale.

An unexpected ally is Caeto Vulaunex himself. Horrified and chastened by the chaos unleashed by his refusal to prioritize the people over his ambitions, he dedicates himself to Illcayna's defeat in repentance. The Hellknight has little support from Cheliax, which is cutting its losses to focus on other parts of the growing war, but he's stalwart in his devotion to seeing Illcayna's downfall and more open to compromise than previously. Caeto is able to utilize his Chelaxian connections to learn of other warshards rumored to lie in the Iron Rose palace in the Menador Mountains and one embedded in a mysterious aquatic creature in the Conerica River.

Campaign Consequences.name: Campaign Consequences
Campaign Consequences.text:
Campaign Consequences

The following scenarios happen if the PCs fail to defeat certain enemies or achieve their objectives.

Continuing the Campaign.name: Continuing the Campaign
Continuing the Campaign.text:
Continuing the Campaign

The PCs should be level 10 at the end of the Hellbreakers Adventure Path, having faced the many political and supernatural crises of Isger. The players are primed to continue their PCs' adventures in the next Adventure Path, Hell's Destiny, but there's plenty to be done if the players wish to continue in Isger.

Notable Locations.name: Notable Locations
Notable Locations.text:
Notable Locations

With small villages and farmsteads dotting the landscape, Isger is full of locations to visit or explore. Below are a few of the country's most interesting or important locations.

Breachill: This small town is relatively young compared to other Isgeri settlements. Situated in the shadow of the Five Kings Mountains, its origins are similarly shrouded in mystery, as the first people found there in 4520 ar were 50 humans with no memory of who they were or how they got there. A passing wizard named Lamond Breachton discovered this outpost and helped its lost inhabitants build up their camp into a full-fledged town. Though he couldn't uncover their past, the grateful villagers named the town after him. As Breachill's population grew over the years, Lamond Breachton remained to guide them in a paternal fashion until he one day disappeared. The townsfolk erected a statue in his honor and continued his legacy of benevolence. Breachill's peaceful populace attracted the attention of the newly formed Hellknight Order of the Nail, who built their citadel 10 miles northeast of the town in 4638. Though they were lured to Korvosa by Queen Domina only 44 years later, the citadel still stands.

In recent months, rumors spread that Breachill was harboring members of the Hellbreakers League, and Hellknights from the Order of the Rack quickly occupied the town. These Hellknights established strict curfews and other laws, much to the dismay of the Breachill town council. Councilor Greta Gardania (passionate female human councilor 1) in particular was incensed by this overreach from Cheliax and sent secret missives to all neighboring countries, asking for help. Eventually Andoran responded, sending retired Eagle Knight general Reginald Cormoth to effect a diplomatic solution. The Hellknights executed him for meddling in their affairs, setting off a chain of events that culminated in the bloody Battle of Hellknight Hill in the fields between Breachill and Citadel Altaerein. Andoran's forces won the day, and now Breachill must deal with the aftermath of the fight.

Chitterwood: This old-growth forest is home to many tribes of goblins, though markedly fewer since the end of the Goblinblood Wars. Far more dangerous creatures lurk among the trees. Detailed information about the Chitterwood can be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22212chitte]{Article}.

Citadel Altaerein: Only a short distance from Breachill, this Hellknight citadel was built as the base of operations for the Order of the Nail before they moved to Korvosa in 4682. The building housed fewer than three dozen Hellknights for the following decades until it was completely abandoned in 4711. Goblins moved into the lower and basement levels of the citadel in 4717, but they were targeted by a cult of Norgorber who was defeated by a group of heroes only two years later. After defeating a manifestation of Dahak, the heroes gifted the citadel to the town of Breachill. However, the Godsrain brought more strife to the area, and when Hellknights from the Order of the Rack marched into Breachill, they also occupied Citadel Altaerein. Recently, a major battle between those Hellknights and Andoran's Eagle Knights occurred in the surrounding area, part of which included a siege of the citadel. Once again, ownership of the fortress changed hands after the Hellknights were routed in the Battle of Hellknight Hill, and its future providence is now uncertain.

Citadel Dinyar: Located among the peaks of the Aspodell Mountains, this sturdy fortress serves as the headquarters for the Hellknight Order of the Godclaw. After the recent change in the deities promoted by this religious order and the looming threat of war between Cheliax and Andoran, many Hellknights at Citadel Dinyar have begun venturing forth into the countryside with more regularity. Rather than demand obedience like so many other Hellknight orders, those who worship the pantheon known as the Talons of the Godclaw have been focused more on educating the common folk on the everyday benefits of an ordered and disciplined life. Friction with the more traditional Hellknights of the Godclaw has forced many of these worshippers to return to the citadel to ensure newly enlisted armigers aren't overly influenced against their newer philosophy.

Dustpawn: The citizens of this once prosperous iron mining town near the Drumish border built a thriving industry around the town's many goats after the mines were exhausted. Merchants from all over Isger, Druma, and Andoran regularly visit to purchase the town's goat milk, butter, cheese, meat, and hides. This constant trade traffic also makes the caravans traveling the roads into and out of Dustpawn prime targets for bandits, many of whom make their hideouts in the former mining tunnels. Recently, Elladas Demos, a smuggler who extorted money from the Dustpawn government to keep bandit attacks to a minimum, was found decapitated in the town square. Some say she was targeted by House Thrune after spreading conspiracy theories about Abrogail II's lineage. Others believe she faked her death to live a life of luxury in Druma after hoarding several years' worth of monetary gains. Since her death, though, merchants have become wary of making the journey to Dustpawn for fear of the bandits. The town's current mayor, Ruprecht Haesmith (anxious male human politician 1), has repeatedly sent requests for aid from Elidir to no avail.

Elidir: Situated at the junction where the Summerun River merges with the North Conerica River, Isger's capital is a hub of trade from Molthune, Druma, and even from the more distant Cheliax. The city escaped much of the damage caused by the Goblinblood Wars, being over 100 miles away from the Chitterwood. This remoteness allowed the Isgeri government to continue to function normally during the conflict, but many soldiers and villagers now feel this safety was undeserved, especially since the officials and generals in Elidir couldn't put an end to the war without help from neighboring nations. Some even accuse the government of dragging its feet in stopping the goblinoids or somehow profiting off the misery of the nation's common folk. As such, the average Isgeri farmer tends to sneer when talking about Elidir, believing its residents to be no better than fools. Somewhat ironically, the Chelaxian government has similar views of Hedvend VI, Isger's current steward. Though he's served Cheliax faithfully for decades, many Chelaxian nobles believe the country should be in more capable hands. Rumors of his replacement have been swirling around Elidir for over five years, but for whatever reason, Cheliax has yet to send the order. Hedvend is painfully aware of this looming threat, and his closest allies have been encouraging him to act with more boldness, especially in light of the recent defeat of the Hellknights at Citadel Altaerein. More about Elidir can be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22213elidir]{Article}.

Fernsby: A small farming village north of the Chitterwood, Fernsby has a slightly strained relationship with the nearby artist colony of Stumpfield. More information can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02efernsby000000]{Here}.

Finder's Gulch: @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} is the undisputed master of this haunted place. Once a simple and remote quarry town, Finder's Gulch was overrun by malicious undead several decades ago. Illcayna, priestess of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}, followed the horde of wights to establish a base of operations from which she has continually raided other Isgeri villages, Cheliax, and Molthune, all to grow the ranks of her undead armies. Over time, Illcayna wishes to turn Isger's entire populace to the worship of her god, though this goal will likely need to be achieved by force. More about Finder's Gulch and Illcayna Alonnor can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22207wightq.JournalEntryPage.07mthemysteryo00]{Here} and @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Here}, respectively.

Gillamoor: Located at the edge of the Chitterwood, Gillamoor survived both attacks from goblins and several fires that claimed much of the nearby forest, only to fall to a curse of undeath. As part of her campaign to infest all of Isger with undead, Illcayna Alonnor chose Gillamoor because of its tragic history and, consequently, its rather large graveyard. Hoping the town would soon be overrun with undead, she laid a curse on the settlement, making it so that anyone who perished within Gillamoor would quickly rise as a brain-eating zombie. To light the fuse of this mystical bomb, Illcayna then used her necromantic powers to raise a few zombies from the Gillamoor cemetery in the dead of night. The first death occurred hours later, and though the original zombies were destroyed, the chain reaction had already begun. Within weeks, the entire population of Gillamoor had perished or fled. The Isgeri military quarantined the area, believing the tragedy to have been caused by plague, but they soon abandoned their post when no plague could be detected.

Good Home: This small town was abandoned during the Goblinblood Wars and taken over by Mama Grimclaw, who renamed it Good Home. She raises her numerous kidnapped children here, shielding the town with magic so no one will notice it. The town is in working condition, with the kidnapped children learning to be self-sufficient so that they never have to leave. Travelers who wander too close are sometimes murdered so Mama Grimclaw can gift her children with their possessions.

Haugin's Ear: The inhabitants of this quiet fishing village trade their daily catches, as well as cured fish, with passing vessels on the River Keld—mostly Chelaxian military and trade ships—and to miners panning for gold in the Aspodell foothills. A few families also make a living selling tamed firefoot fennecs, which are regarded as symbols of good luck by many in the region. Haugin's Ear is named after an unusual 30-foot-tall outcropping of rock along the riverbank near its docks that resembles the half-buried head and ear of a giant lying on his side. Legends claim this stony protrusion is part of the petrified remains of Haugin, a flesh-eating giant who ran afoul of a Taldan wizard centuries ago. Occasionally, treasure hunters from outside Isger venture to the area in search of shattered pieces of Haugin, which are rumored to hold great power. In years past, many believed the stone head was somehow luring children inside, but in truth, these missing children were devoured by a sweet hag named Marjulla, who was recently discovered and slain by one of the visiting treasure hunters. With her dying words, Marjulla warned of retribution from her two sisters.

Iron Rose: With its elaborate stone arches, this palace flaunts its Chelaxian influence for all who dare to approach. Centuries ago, Lady Kaltessa Iyis staked her claim on a lush valley near the border of Druma and conscripted dozens of devils to build the impressive edifice she calls home. The opulent fortress is rumored to be filled with enough gold to buy entire nations, though no one has ever had the privilege to step inside and find out.

Merrywim: This small riverside town was mainly known for its shell jewelry; beyond that, its people eked out a quiet living in the countryside. That all changed after the Godsrain. Now, the people of Merrywim have become rambunctious, throwing enormous parties nightly and often drinking until sundown. The realization that even a god can fall terrified the town's inhabitants so much that they've become hedonistic nihilists, intent on enjoying their lives as much as they possibly can. However, of late the partying has had to stop because of a mysterious creature that's been spotted in the Conerica River, something massive enough to be a threat to those who live ashore. A few brave fishers banded together to capture the beast but returned with only broken nets and lines. It seems that professional adventurers might be the solution for this issue, which the town is eager to address so that they can return to their frantic revelry.

Logas: Once the capital of Isger, the scars of the Goblinblood Wars, both physical and mental, can still be found in this riverside city's architecture and citizens. Logas was continually under siege during the conflict, leading to a lasting distrust of goblinoids. The city's current mayor, Valenia Remingward (progressive female human politician 2), fought in the war but ceased the practice of regularly firing trebuchets into the nearby Chitterwood and dismantled the display of goblin skulls along the city walls immediately after her appointment in 4723. These mandates caused some consternation among the city's nobles, who claimed that Mayor Remingward's policies would be seen as a sign of weakness by the goblin tribes and ignite a second round of hostilities. Most of their complaints have been silenced in the wake of recent events as Hellknights amass within the city, either fleeing from their defeat at the Battle of Hellknight Hill or arriving from across the Chelaxian border as reinforcements. Tensions run high in Logas, though the majority of its citizens support Chelaxian rule over Isger.

Saringallow: Centuries ago, this city began as a small garden estate named Sarini's Hollow, founded by House Sarini of Cheliax, a minor noble house. Over time, it slowly grew into a village with its own farms, shops, and trade via the nearby river. Though it seemed idyllic from the outside, it harbored a sinister secret. The nobles of House Sarini dabbled in diabolism long before House Thrune rose to power, and their hideous rituals resulted in the deaths of several of the village's young people. The citizens rebelled and hung every member of House Sarini they could find. The town was then nicknamed Sarini Gallows, which over time evolved into the city's current name. The Sarini estate still stands as a grim warning to other Chelaxian nobles who might think to take advantage of the populace, and they ensure that noble outsiders don't feel welcome, especially if their last name is Sarini. The city's history is likely the reason that Hellbreakers League activity is most prevalent there, leading many to believe that Saringallow is the rebellious organization's headquarters. More about Saringallow can be found in the @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22215saring]{Article}.

Stumpfield: Founded by goblin and human artists, Stumpfield is a haven for creators of all stripes. It relies on trading with nearby Fernsby for much of its practical goods. More information can be found on @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02stumpfield0000]{Here}.

Swiftrun: This small village is most known for its priests of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.mm1j6UbHqFCI8fwB]{Erastil} who teach how to homestead and defend one's community. The community is nearly all Erastilian, with an emphasis on helping one another. Rather than individual gardening, the village has an enormous community garden that everyone takes turns caring for. Everything is shared in the village, from tools to carts, and hospitality is seen as the greatest virtue.

Twin Horns: This nunnery of the Sisters of the Golden Erinys lies in the Aspodell Mountains, quietly serving as a place for aspiring young women to train as sisters. The convent is small and its training rigorous, the nuns practicing both religious duties and martial arts from dawn to dusk. Many of the girls raised in the sisters' orphanages end up traveling here to become nuns. Recently, the nunnery discovered a piece of a warshard that affected their livestock, turning their goats into dawnsilver.

Umok: This centuries-old gnome village has outlawed fire within 500 yards of its buildings due to past run-ins with fire-loving goblins from the Chitterwood. The residents now use alchemy and magic for heat and light. More information about Umok can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02umok0000000000]{Here}.

Vordia: After the Goblinblood Wars, the Sisters of the Golden Erinys and, by extension, the Church of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} worked hard to rebuild Vordia and take care of its citizens. As such, its citizens are generally grateful and loyal to Cheliax. Vordia is the proud location of one of the first orphanages built by the sisters after the wars. More information can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02vordia00000000]{Here}.

Wolfpoint: A reserve garrison for the Isgeri army, Wolfpoint has been left empty since the Battle of Hellknight Hill, its soldiers called to active duty in other parts of the country. As a result, the local river bandits have grown bolder and often use Wolfpoint as a meeting place. More information about Wolfpoint can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02wolfpoint00000]{Here}.

Notable Figures.name: Notable Figures
Notable Figures.text:
Notable Figures

Alceo Demetrias (wise male aiuvarin human cleric of Milani 7) and Phoebe Demetrias (righteous female human commander 7) are the rebellious leaders of the Hellbreakers League, an organization formed to free Isger. More about them can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole04]{Here}.

Brakknap (haunted male goblin oracle 4) is a goblin elder working toward restoring humanoid and goblinoid relations. More information about Brakknap can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole00]{Here}.

The Isgeri Army is led by General Harwin Balefellow (principled male soldier 10), a stern man caught between his morals and his duty. Harwin is frustrated by the state of Isger but follows orders to a fault, secretly hoping for change yet unwilling to be the one to bring it about.

Hedvend VI has ruled Isger for decades, and his legacy won't be a proud one. The ramifications of his decision to ignore the plight of the countryside during the Goblinblood Wars still echo throughout Isger to this day in the form of permanently wounded veterans, innumerable orphans, and towns completely wiped from the map. It's well known that Hedvend cares only about pleasing Cheliax and is happy to let the rest of the nation fester so long as the elites are satisfied with their spoils.

The powerful daughter of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa}, Illcayna Alonnor, has been working her machinations in the countryside for decades, infesting the land with undead. Her plans have largely run unhindered, thanks to the government's lack of interest in the rural areas. More information about Illcayna can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Here}.

Lady Kaltessa Iyis (mysterious female human priestess of Mammon 20) is a seemingly immortal priestess of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.sNjPI1iaS8Z43YJf]{Mammon} who has lived in the Menador Mountains for an uncounted period of time. Surrounded by devilish servants, she watches over the nation from her fortress while she plots on behalf of her master. These devils and her unnaturally long life are the result of an infernal pact with the archdevil Mammon as part of Kaltessa's designs on ruling Isger, and perhaps one day, Cheliax as well. Her devotion to Mammon instead of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} makes her somewhat of a rogue element within the borders of Cheliax, so she plots and schemes from hundreds of miles away. With her acquisition of a warshard after the Godsrain and rising tensions between Cheliax and Andoran, Lady Iyis the Widow Queen is poised to make her move any day now.

For decades while the countryside was riddled with strife, Mama Grimclaw (devious female iron hag 9) had easy pickings among the numerous children left orphaned by the Goblinblood Wars. She keeps her victims hidden in a small town shielded from scrying magic. Illusions surround the town, ensuring that travelers pass by without a thought. In recent years, improvements in village sheriffs and security have made it more challenging for the hag to find victims, but Mama Grimclaw simply orders her current children to cause distractions so she can snatch up their newest sibling. Villages are coming to be aware of her brand of terror and warn their children to be good or the nightmare witch will get them—though Mama Grimclaw cares not for how good a child is, only that they're easy to kidnap. Now, with the chaos of potential war sowing discord and fear throughout the nation, Mama Grimclaw has found plenty of new opportunities to prey on the vulnerable.

The most influential member among the Sisters of the Golden Erinys is Sister Marcella (pious human monk 6), an unassuming elderly woman who's served the church of Asmodeus since she was a child. As the grand overseer of the sisterhood's charities, she has great influence over the countryside thanks to the sisters' stellar reputation. Marcella loves children and can often be found reading infernal passages from religious tomes to children too young to understand what they mean.

Varskand Gilwrad (vengeful male human bigot 8)is a veteran of the Goblinblood Wars and one of the founders of the notorious Isgeri Slayers. He lost his home and his left eye to hobgoblin raiders and has never forgiven goblinkind for its sins against him. Varskand sees himself and his gang as crusaders, doing the work no one else will by taking up the sword to enact justice that the government has failed to serve. He works hard to pass off the Isgeri Slayers as a legitimate organization of mercenaries and adventurers rather than what they truly are: angry bigots.

Culture and Society.name: Culture and Society
Culture and Society.text:
Culture and Society

Isger is a land full of contradictions. The ultrarich dwell in the capital city, where they live lavishly at the height of excess. More about Elidiran culture can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22213elidir.JournalEntryPage.13cultureandso00]{Here}. Most of those who dwell outside the capital are humble, rustic people still struggling to recover from the Goblinblood Wars and deal with the consequences of that terrible conflict.

Those in small cities and large towns like Saringallow can afford some luxuries thanks to traveling merchants. Those in the countryside have no such luck and have become stubborn and resilient to survive. As those who have survived war and vowed to never face such loss again, these rural areas have fostered a strong sense of community. Neighbors tend to lend a hand without being asked and without expecting thanks, simply doing what needs to be done.

Spices are expensive for the countryside, making for bland meals. The typical Isgeri (outside Elidir) prefers an unsalted meal and will wrinkle their nose at heavily spiced cuisine. Porridges, roast chicken, and salads are common.

Fashion is usually the last thing on the mind of an Isgeri farmer, yet it's still an important function of life. Hats are vital to keep the sun and wind from one's eyes, and scarves protect from dust and cold. Those who are more fashion-forward dye their hats bright colors and decorate them with twigs and flowers, while knitters take pride in their families' elaborate scarves. Symbols are often subtly woven into clothing, such as certain flowers for good luck or skulls to indicate hard times. Coloring one's nails with a local flower's dye has become popular, though such lacquers must be tough to withstand a full day's labor.

Loyalty to Cheliax is mixed. Some fear and hate the patron nation, seeing it as the source of most of their troubles. Others can't deny the good Cheliax did in the aftermath of the Goblinblood Wars and view the Church of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus} positively, seeing both them and Cheliax as benevolent benefactors. Many young women were raised and indoctrinated by the Sisters of the Golden Erinys, who have a strong presence in the countryside. While some see such “charity” as a scam, no one can deny that Cheliax did help those in need.

Religion.name: Religion
Religion.text:
Religion

As a vassal of Cheliax, Isger's patron deity is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}, but other deities are quietly worshipped as well. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.d56paSkcwvll2OhR]{Abadar} has the second greatest following, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.fTJLgTfEMZreJ19r]{Milani} has grown popular with rebels and freedom fighters who chafe against Cheliax's boot. @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22214plotso.JournalEntryPage.14plotsofthepa00]{Urgathoa} has a small but strong presence thanks to her servant @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22216advent.JournalEntryPage.16campaignrole03]{Illcayna Alonnor} (malevolent female daughter of Urgathoa 9) making a stronghold for undead forces in the countryside. Her servants work in the shadows of the nation to bring about her nefarious plans.

Asmodeus is popularly worshipped by those loyal to Cheliax, but otherwise, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.mm1j6UbHqFCI8fwB]{Erastil} is popular among the Isgeri countryside. His edicts of taking care of community resonate with those who lost so much and wish to rebuild. Many towns have shrines to Erastil, though they always have a larger one for Asmodeus just in case the authorities ever come around.

In the capital, an old temple of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.jL1qiVOZBKXETtVD]{Nocticula} has become a focal point in the great clash between Nocticula's old followers from her incarnation as a demon and her newer converts who revere her current incarnation as the Redeemer Queen.

Government.name: Government
Government.text:
Government

Isger is ruled by a steward appointed by Cheliax who oversees the nation and its trade. However, the elites of Isger are often preoccupied with the trade along the Conerica River and neglect any settlements outside the capital. Therefore, most towns and villages are self-governed with little interference from the wider government. Sheriffs, mayors, and guards take up civic duties for those forgotten by their own rulers.

At a Glance.name: At a Glance
At a Glance.text:
At a Glance

Isger is a temperate country bounded by the River Keld and the Aspodell Mountains to the south, the Menador Mountains to the north, and the Five Kings Mountains to the east. It shares borders with Cheliax, Andoran, Druma, and Molthune, though the most direct routes to Molthune must pass through the northern mountains. Its geography is mostly plains and hills, with the Chitterwood being the nation's largest forest. The Conerica River, a major corridor of trade, runs through the center of Isger and forms a major part of its western border. The Conerica is fed by the North Conerica River, which joins with the Summerun River at the capital of Elidir.

Isger is a vassal state of Cheliax and must abide by its laws and decrees. Hedvend VI (sniveling male human aristocrat 9) is the latest in a long line of stewards appointed by the Chelaxian government to oversee Isger. The nation is required by Cheliax to maintain a standing army to protect the important routes but receives little money, material support, or training from Cheliax to do so. The Isgeri army consists of volunteer recruits and watches over travel on the Conerica River as well as the borders of Druma and Andoran. Since the Battle of Hellknight Hill, most soldiers have been pulled back to protect Elidir.

Most of the people of Isger are human, the majority being either of Taldan or Kellid descent. The next biggest bloc of population are goblins, with most of them residing in the Chitterwood. Surprisingly, gnomes are plentiful in Isger, thanks in part to the gnome settlement of Umok. Other ancestries and ethnicities are present throughout the nation, concentrated mostly in the riverside cities.

History.name: History
History.text:
History

Isger Facts

  • Capital: Elidir (11,900)
  • Founding Date: 2133 ar
  • Ruler: Hedvend VI, Steward of Isger
  • Main Peoples: Gnome, Goblin, Human (Taldan)
  • Languages: Common, Diabolic, Gnomish, Goblin
  • Religions: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.QRkcFciCOmFoxF1B]{Asmodeus}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.mm1j6UbHqFCI8fwB]{Erastil}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.fTJLgTfEMZreJ19r]{Milani}
  • Resources: Livestock/hides, lumber, textiles

Like many areas of Avistan, the land that would become Isger was occupied by Kellid tribes for thousands of years. These hardy people roamed the plains, hunted in the hills, and fished in the rivers as a way of life. There were 11 tribes in all, collectively known as the Isgeri, who lived off the land between the Menador Mountains and the Five Kings Mountains. When these tribes met regularly with one another to trade and intermingle, they did so at the confluence of rivers close to where the city of Elidir would be built. When conflicts between the tribes couldn't be settled at this moot, they would occasionally result in battles, though one tribe never fully conquered another.

This all ended in 2133 ar when Taldor's Seventh Army of Exploration marched into the region and claimed it as their own. The Isgeri fought back, but their tenacity was no match for the sheer size of Taldor's army. The land was conquered and its people subjugated, though the newfound country was named Isger in their honor—no consolation to the Kellids killed in battle. Taldor ruled over Isger for almost 2,000 years until Cheliax won its own independence in the Even-Tongued Conquest of 4081. Shortly after, Cheliax acquired Isger by force as the first vassal state of a burgeoning empire.

Isger experienced relative peace for the next few centuries, but the Chelaxians eventually got greedy and encroached upon the Chitterwood in an attempt to take it for themselves. What initially began as self-defense soon grew into all-out war as bloodthirsty hobgoblin warlords, who only needed an excuse for conflict, used the goblin tribes of the Chitterwood to form a massive army. Fed up with their mistreatment at the hands of humans, many of these goblinoids were happy to enlist, but an equal number were conscripted by force.

The Goblinblood Wars began in 4697 and lasted for four years. The deaths of thousands of Isgeri citizens were accompanied by untold property damage as the goblin hordes moved north across the Conerica River and toward the foothills of the Five Kings Mountains. Only an unlikely alliance between Cheliax's Hellknights, Druma's Mercenary League, and Andoran's Eagle Knights halted the offensive. These groups set the edges of the Chitterwood aflame, and though the forest wasn't completely burned down, its size was greatly reduced. Since that time, many goblins have reemerged from the caves they hid within to reclaim their forest.

In the aftermath of the war, the Church of Asmodeus, with the support of House Thrune—the current rulers of Cheliax—enacted programs to help those affected by the fighting. These acts weren't of pure charity; the wounded were cared for by Asmodean priests in exchange for future favors. Orphaned children were placed in newly built orphanages run by a group called the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys that has spent the last two decades indoctrinating those children into their faith. Many Isgeri citizens felt grateful for this support and became more loyal to Cheliax while their prejudice against goblinoids waned and waxed.

The Godsrain ignited a spark of revolution in the hearts of some of Isger's citizenry. They saw how even the mightiest of gods could be laid low and began to wonder if it was possible to throw off Cheliax's yoke. A group called the Hellbreakers League became the forefront of this dissidence, having discovered a warshard—a piece of the dead god @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.88vRw2ZVPax4hhga]{Gorum}—and used it as a rallying symbol. This displeased Her Infernal Majestrix Abrogail Thrune II of Cheliax, who's been seeking these implements of power for her own. She recently sent a contingent of Hellknights of the Order of the Rack to root out the Hellbreakers League in the city of Breachill. After weeks of occupation, the Andoren government sent retired Eagle Knight Reginald Cormoth to intervene on behalf of Breachill's council. He was publicly executed by the Hellknights, who claimed without evidence that he was an enemy spy. It eventually led to a massive clash in the fields near Citadel Altaerein that has come to be known as the Battle of Hellknight Hell. Some say it's the first salvo of an all-out war between Cheliax and Andoran.

Isger.name: Isger
Isger.text:
Isger

Known throughout the Inner Sea Region as a vassal state under the thumb of Cheliax, Isger is poised on the brink of a major milestone. With recent events, the nation could either gain its full independence or have its spirit thoroughly crushed by those who claim to be its betters. After centuries of being controlled by one nation or another, many of the Isgeri people are just one small push away from rising up en masse against House Thrune. But such an event wouldn't be without bloodshed, and Isger is still healing from its recent internal conflict with the goblinoid residents of the Chitterwood. Another war could leave Isger a broken husk, ripe pickings for yet another nation to consume.

Sunless Tunnels.name: Sunless Tunnels
Sunless Tunnels.text:
Sunless Tunnels

The Sunless Tunnels are where the Hookback goblins live in the southern Chitterwood, deep below the surface. These caves are uniquely rife with ores the goblins use to create their iconic piercings, smelting them with specialized techniques. Despite their limited use of fire, the Hookback goblins have mastered its use, and their tunnels are filled with valuable chunks of metal that would make Elidir's wealthiest nobles swoon.

Something else lives deep in the tunnels, where no Hookback goblin dares tread. It's unknown what beast breathes so heavily in the dark, but all Hookback goblins know not to brave the specific tunnels it can be heard in.

Stagfall Caves.name: Stagfall Caves
Stagfall Caves.text:
Stagfall Caves

This set of caves has existed since ancient days, serving as a home and shelter to many creatures. Deep within the caverns is a nexus of primal power, which has lain dormant for centuries until the events of this campaign. More about the Stagfall Caves can be found @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils.JournalEntryPage.03gstagfallcav00]{Here}.

Shrieking Caverns.name: Shrieking Caverns
Shrieking Caverns.text:
Shrieking Caverns

The People of the Swarm reside in the Shrieking Caverns, named for the cry of the thousands of bats swarming in the caves. These caves are filled with threats like cave bears but also nourishment, such as fish and lichen, thanks to an underground river.

High ceilings and low pits establish a dangerous environment in the caverns, yet it's also filled with nooks and crannies that make for the perfect resting spots for goblins. The humidity in the caverns makes lighting fires difficult at times, so goblins sometimes rely on glowing worms and fungi for a source of light.

Goldenmouth.name: Goldenmouth
Goldenmouth.text:
Goldenmouth

Goldenmouth is the rumored hoard of the dragon Jurinex, said to be lost deep in the Chitterwood when humans burned down the landmarks that marked its location. Many still delve into the Chitterwood in attempts to find this lost treasure, braving the dangers of the woods in hopes of securing a valuable prize. The hoard is said to be a century's worth of accumulated gold and treasures, along with powerful artifacts that can grant wishes and immortality.

Frog Bog.name: Frog Bog
Frog Bog.text:
Frog Bog

Frog Bog is the colloquial name for the swampy eastern Chitterwood, where the Mudrub goblins make their home. It's a consistently soggy environment in the warm months, drying out in the winter. Frog Bog is most known for its large population of frogs as well as housing the frog-like Mudrub goblins.

Each year, the frogs get larger and larger, a sign that the Chitterwood is healing. Rumors have it that an enormous frog the size of a cart lives deep within the dirt, and many a Mudrub goblin has attempted to find it to lay claim to a most glorious and filling meal.

Burnt Ends.name: Burnt Ends
Burnt Ends.text:
Burnt Ends

The Burnt Ends is what the goblins call the edges of the Chitterwood where the Bulbhead goblins make their homes. The trees are much younger here, renewing after the effects of the war, and there's less cover than most goblins would like. Nevertheless, the Bulbhead goblins call it home and have made a good living farming in the once-charred soil, planting their iconic gourds and various vegetables to trade.

The Big Fire.name: The Big Fire
The Big Fire.text:
The Big Fire

This large bonfire deep in the woods is said to burn eternally, fed and cared for by the Cinder Seekers. The Cinder Seekers view the Big Fire as near-sacred, lighting their torches from it in hopes of an extra powerful flame. Yet in truth, it's an ordinary fire that simply hasn't gone out thanks to the diligence of its keepers, who insist it's special in every way and feed it only the best of kindling (including, occasionally, an unfortunate Isgeri Slayer). The Big Fire is protected from rain by a canvas tied to the tree branches above it, which makes its smoke billow out low to the ground, causing coughing fits whenever anyone approaches.

Barking Caverns.name: Barking Caverns
Barking Caverns.text:
Barking Caverns

The Spine Threshers live in the Barking Caverns, named for the barks of their mounts. This cave system is one of the most expansive in the Chitterwood, with wide caves that create plenty of room to run and train their mounts. The smaller tunnels are used for racing and practice, for squeezing through narrow passageways can prove one's worth as a rider.

Locations.name: Locations
Locations.text:
Locations

The Chitterwood houses several unique environments. Though much was destroyed, some survived the fires of the Goblinblood Wars, while others came to be afterward.

Monsters.name: Monsters
Monsters.text:
Monsters

While goblinoids are the most well-known of the Chitterwood's residents, other creatures also lurk in the decrepit woods. Ghosts and haunts are quite common, for much blood was shed during the war, as are polluted fey spirits twisted by the burning of the woods and the blood soaked into the ground. The most infamous of these haunts is the rumored goblinblood beast, a creature said to be made up purely of the blood shed during the war, that longs for violence and battle. It's said to cause visions of war and fire in its victims, who believe they're burning in the razing of the Chitterwood.

Dragons are also said to reside in the woods, though few have been seen since the Goblinblood Wars. Rumor has it a forest dragon is attempting to lay claim to a large section of the Chitterwood and battling goblins to do so. There's also said to be an ancient beast of living shadow haunting the Chitterwood, though no one living has been able to confirm its existence.

Non-goblinoids.name: Non-goblinoids
Non-goblinoids.text:
Non-goblinoids

Most humans and others who aren't of goblinoid ancestry choose not to live in the Chitterwood—which is precisely why some do decide to reside here. Whether they make their living by preying upon caravans along the Chitterwood's trade route or simply need a place to lie low for a while, non-goblinoid residents appreciate the seclusion offered by these woods.

The town of Stumpfield is the most well-known of any humanoid settlements near the woods, along with its neighbor Fernsby. Stumpfield is unique for its large mix of both goblinoid and non-goblinoid residents. More information on Stumpfield is @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe.JournalEntryPage.02stumpfield0000]{Here}.

Hobgoblins.name: Hobgoblins
Hobgoblins.text:
Hobgoblins

With the establishment of Oprak in 4717 ar, hobgoblins now have a nation to call home. Though seemingly small in size, Oprak is rich in resources both natural and wondrous and is thriving under General Azaersi's leadership. The few hobgoblins who continue to live in Isger do so in the caverns of the Chitterwood, patiently biding their time until circumstances are right for them to make their presence known. Local goblin tribes rarely cooperate willingly with hobgoblins anymore; some, however, remain in thrall to these powerful hobgoblins.

True Hoard.name: True Hoard
True Hoard.text:
True Hoard

Those encountering the True Hoard goblin tribe for the first time typically underestimate these goblins' talents and capabilities. Unlike the Spine Threshers, True Hoard goblins don't make fighting their priority, preferring to scavenge, steal, or create. They're gatherers more than hunters, though they can and do hunt quite well when the need arises; when it comes to fashioning snares, nets, or clever traps, few are as talented as the goblins of the True Hoard. During the Goblinblood Wars, the tribe very nearly lost their knowledge of such things since most of their skilled trap makers and hunters were conscripted by hobgoblins and subsequently perished in battle. What the survivors did know, they passed on to their children, and everything else the tribe rediscovered along the way through trial and error.

Endlessly curious and innovative, True Hoard goblins make the most of everything they have. It's a trait that's served them well in the caverns; knowing how to make something out of junk and something tasty (or at least edible) out of scraps and detritus means the difference between life and death. True Hoard goblins rarely throw anything away, even items that seem totally useless to everyone else. Maybe not today, and maybe not tomorrow, but someday—they're sure of it!—whatever it is will be just the thing they need. And of course, if it's shiny or pretty, it doesn't need a purpose. It's a treasure!

This belief actually puts them in an odd relationship with a particular species of rat living in the caverns: the bushy-tailed woodrat. Most folks in Isger who have encountered woodrats call them pack rats; the True Hoard calls them gully-rakers. Like the True Hoard tribe, woodrats love shiny things and spend a great deal of their time and energy collecting treasures and stashing them in their nests. Some treasures are edible, but most aren't—they're just pretty or interesting in some way. Woodrats will even drop what they're carrying if they come across something they find more interesting.

When it rains in the Chitterwood, floodwaters rush into the caverns, bringing all manner of debris, muck, and sometimes delightful surprises; True Hoard goblins and woodrats frequently clash over who gets to claim which items. Despite their irritation, the True Hoard has a degree of respect for woodrats and even finds them useful (and occasionally tasty). Finding a woodrat's nest sometimes yields amazing finds, provided the items haven't been “claimed” yet; woodrats urinate on their stash, and eventually everything gets stuck in place so firmly that nothing can be removed. Figuring out what to do with woodrat urine–soaked items actually led some members to make fascinating discoveries. As they eventually realized, there are lots of useful components in woodrat waste!

After six generations of exploration, discovery, and experimentation, the tribe is better equipped than ever for a fight should one come their way. Today, if you meet a goblin alchemist or inventor in Isger, there's a good chance they're from the True Hoard tribe. Their formulas aren't recorded in words, so anyone attempting to understand a goblin alchemist's notes will have a hard time of it, and the True Hoard prefers it that way.

Spine Threshers.name: Spine Threshers
Spine Threshers.text:
Spine Threshers

Of all the goblin tribes in the Chitterwood, the Spine Threshers might be the one best known for skill in combat. Whereas the People of the Swarm prefer to attack on foot, the Spine Threshers rely heavily on mounted combat, excelling in the art as an act of devotion to their favored creator god, Zarongel. During the Goblinblood Wars, hobgoblin commanders used members of this tribe to carry out particularly vicious attacks, caring little about whether they or their mounts—typically goblin dogs or wolves—survived for long. By the end of the wars, there were precious few Spine Thresher warriors alive. Those who made it to safety were determined that their knowledge wouldn't be lost.

When they first arrived in the caverns, the Spine Thresher tribe had little apart from some of their mounts, which were simply too important to leave behind; the tribe's physical survival, and the survival of their culture, depended upon these creatures. The Spine Threshers trace their founding to a warrior whose mount was a gift from Zarongel himself, a reward for her great skill and devotion. Regrowing the tribe meant increasing not only the goblin population, but that of their animals as well. Today, the Spine Threshers claim one of the larger territories in the caverns. A sizable portion of their area is dedicated to the care and training of their mounts and the warriors who ride them. A favorite pastime involves mounted Spine Threshers racing through an extensive, often cramped, network of naturally formed tunnels. It's an exhilarating and dangerous game that serves as an important proving ground for young warriors.

The Spine Threshers are also particularly fond of dares. If there's a goblin sneaking topside to do something foolhardy (or brave, as they see it), it's frequently someone from this tribe. Hunting is fun, but it isn't enough; young warriors who grew up hearing songs about the before times are eager to have a chance to fight and make names for themselves like the heroes of past generations did. Games and dares help channel some of their growing restlessness and keep their skills honed.

Unsurprisingly, members of this tribe make effective fighters and rangers, but some serve their people in other ways. Those who feel an especially strong connection to fire might become a pyrokineticist; despite goblins' usual misgivings about magic, those who command fire are thought to be favored by Zarongel. Given the tribe's deep understanding of animals and their zeal for hunting, some members of the tribe become effective rangers. In stark contrast to the People of the Swarm, the Spine Threshers regard cave bears with awe, considering them role models in combat, but wisely never attempt to train them as either companions or mounts. Whatever role they occupy in the tribe, Spine Threshers goblins, like cave bears, tend to be aggressively territorial and rarely end a fight until they know their foe is dead.

People of the Swarm.name: People of the Swarm
People of the Swarm.text:
People of the Swarm

Goblins sneak and goblins spring

Goblins swarm and goblins sting

Trap the hob and slice their gut

Goblins here to blow them up!

Break the chains and beat the drum

Burn their bread and steal the rum,

All the blood we goblins shed

Now goblins rise and they be dead!

—People of the Swarm anti-hobgoblin song of resistance

One of the largest and most prominent of Isger's goblin tribes, the People of the Swarm have long been famous—or infamous, depending on one's perspective—for the tactics they employ when on the offensive. Though goblins aren't generally known for their ability or willingness to effectively organize, it's a hallmark of the People of the Swarm tribe. Early on in their history, they realized that working as a group meant that more of them were likely to survive a fight and come away with whatever treasures they were seeking. Where a single goblin might be unable to take down a target, a group of goblins can. Swarm goblins work together in battle to distract and overwhelm their target as they “sting” with arrows, daggers, and dogslicers. Members of this tribe tend to make successful rogues, even if subtlety is sometimes a challenge.

Still, there are limits to the tribe's favored approach—a fact they learned the hard way when some particularly hungry Swarm goblins tried to turn a grizzly bear into a meal for the tribe. Lest this lesson be forgotten, the People of the Swarm have nearly 200 songs describing in gory detail the horror of bear attacks. Their repertoire of bear songs grew when they fled to the Caverns of Chitterwood and discovered the cave bears living there.

If there's one thing that goblins are known for (other than how much they love fire), it's their ability to adapt. The first Swarm goblins to take refuge in the caverns had little interest in fighting; they were scared and traumatized, and most, if not all, of their warriors were dead. They wandered the caves, looking for one they might call home, and eventually stumbled across a massive colony of bats. Disturbing thousands of bats results in more noise and chaos than most folks can handle, but to the People of the Swarm, it was a sign they'd found their spot. In this safe place, the tribe began to heal and regrow their numbers. The elders sang about the wars, their old lives, and the mighty heroes lost, and as the tribe sang, they strengthened. Now they sing songs not only about bear attacks and legendary deeds, but also resilience. One day, goblins will be many again, and hobgoblins few. There's power in the swarm.

To this tribe, bats are kindred spirits; they only sleep where it's safe to do so, they forage at night, and they almost always leave their caves as a group. While goblins can't hang upside down from the cave ceiling, the Swarm did learn the importance of not sleeping on the ground—better, instead, to be as high as possible, away from floodwaters and out of the easy reach of cave bears. Adult members of the tribe seek out goblin-sized nooks and crannies to sleep in, atop simple bedding made from animal hides or plants gathered during nighttime excursions above. Children are kept in enclosures nestled into nooks of their own near the adults.

Swarm goblins are also expert rock climbers, learning to climb as soon as they can walk. They've adapted the traditional swarming techniques to make greater use of height and even sound. Taking inspiration from bats, the tribe learned how to navigate the caves by paying attention to what they heard. Darkvision only works so far, after all, and fire doesn't always stay lit in the dampness of the caves. Swarm goblins have developed a way to communicate with each other in a series of clicks, chirps, and other sounds that make up a language only they understand.

Mudrub.name: Mudrub
Mudrub.text:
Mudrub

The small Mudrub tribe is rarely seen without a thick layer of muck and mud across their bodies, covering up the burn scars that mark them as Mudrub. They were once branded with words and took to fire to remove the evil of literacy from their bodies, turning it into tradition to burn artful patterns into their members—though it's rare for strangers to see said patterns, as a Mudrub goblin is sure to be covered in filth. It's a great sign of intimacy and respect for a Mudrub goblin to remove the muck on their skin and reveal their burns to someone.

Being a small tribe, Mudrub goblins prefer hiding to fighting, using their superior stealth skills to slink into the muddy banks and lie still until danger has passed. The thick coating of muck hides their scent, and they have no issue with waiting for hours in a comfortable spot. Few Mudrub goblins adventure outside of their home domain, uncomfortable anywhere their muddy second skin can't conceal them.

The tribe lives in tall mud huts structured to last through flooding season, with paths of rocks that can be used as stepping stones when the waters rise. Though they take precautions to keep themselves out of dangerously high waters, Mudrub goblins are expert swimmers. They're often compared to frogs as they sweep through brush and muck, darting around their swampy environment with ease. This comparison has led to them calling their children tadpoles, with coming of age jokingly described as “becoming a frog.” They use bird calls to communicate from afar and stay hidden, content to observe rather than interact with strangers.

Living in the flooded eastern Chitterwood, the Mudrub goblin diet relies on frogs. They camouflage in the mud and detritus to sneak up on and then snatch their unsuspecting prey with their bare hands. They enjoy their meals both raw and cooked, and they also catch snakes and birds as part of their diet. Pickled frog legs are a popular snack as are fried snake heads.

Hookback.name: Hookback
Hookback.text:
Hookback

The deep caverns beneath the Chitterwood are home to the Hookback tribe, where goblins distinguish themselves with unique piercings. The Hookback goblins have learned to see even in the darkest cave and listen for the smallest footsteps, aiding them in the endless shadows of the underground. Because of this, most Hookback goblins are reluctant to breach the surface with its painfully bright light, preferring to dwell in the shadows.

The Hookback tribe's most meaningful practice stems from a tragic history of torment and pain. Survivors of grievous torture during the Goblinblood Wars were ashamed of their piercings, signs of weakness that they were, until a brave young goblin declared that they wished to be pierced as well to honor the pain of their people. With that, a tradition was born, and now all Hookback goblins take the piercings when they come of age.

Having lived in the deep caverns of the Chitterwood for several generations, Hookback goblins are expert foragers, scouring the dark for what little nutrition there is to find. They farm mushrooms and lichen as well as fish and newts.

The tribe sees creatures of the dark as their brethren and fears the light, making them the unusual goblin tribe that isn't pyromaniacal. Fire is reserved for the creation of piercings and for special ceremonies, where the tribe gathers for a coming of age or to tell stories of the past; it's feared and revered, the greatest light of all, and the one that destroyed their original homes in the Chitterwood. For the Hookback goblins, darkness is preferred to a light that burns.

Cinder Seekers.name: Cinder Seekers
Cinder Seekers.text:
Cinder Seekers

The Cinder Seekers are a group of goblins determined to remember history and learn from its mistakes. This movement is small but fervent, spreading among the older generations of goblins. They constantly recall the atrocities of the Goblinblood Wars and the cruelty from hobgoblins against their people, and they've vowed to ensure such oppression never happens again.

History is preserved in powerful dirges about the wickedness of hobgoblins and the plight of goblins, though some would argue that these songs are highly biased and even bigoted. Hobgoblins are depicted as monstrous oppressors and all goblins as innocent victims, ignoring the fact that some goblin tribes were quite willing to join in the war against their humanoid neighbors. Many Cinder Seekers tend to look at all hobgoblins with suspicion and paranoia, sure that they have an agenda. The most zealous Cinder Seekers attack hobgoblins indiscriminately, while those wiser will take the time to discern one's intentions.

The Cinder Seekers believe that the purifying force of fire will burn away both their enemies and the will to harm them, making their pyromania almost fanatical. The Cinder Seekers persist in hunting down any who might try and repeat history and burn them with fire to ensure the past stays in the past. If peace comes to the Chitterwood, it'll likely be in spite of the Cinder Seekers rather than because of them.

Bulbhead.name: Bulbhead
Bulbhead.text:
Bulbhead

Bulbhead goblins are distinguished by their iconic gourd helmets, a cultural fashion statement that ties back to the Goblinblood Wars. While the helmets were once used as tools of torment against these goblins, they now wear them with pride, having overcome the humiliation and pain their hobgoblin leaders inflicted upon them. Even babies wear tiny gourds, which are said to help shape their heads to be nice and round. This penchant for gourds also makes these goblins famous for pumpkin recipes such as mashed gourd and rat stew and caramelized pumpkin squares.

The Bulbhead goblins are loosely nomadic, living in tents as they move about the border of the woods. These tents are covered in leaves and sticks to blend in with the brush, granting the goblins both shelter and camouflage. While they might settle in one spot for a week or so, they never stay too long to avoid enemies pinning down their locations. The Bulbhead goblins always make sure to mark the best spots with patches of gourds so they can return at harvest.

Life on the edges of the Chitterwood has the Bulbhead goblins interacting with non-goblinoids more than any other goblin tribe. While the early days postwar had high tensions between goblins and humanoids, the Bulbheads have learned that humanoids can be either friend or foe and adapted accordingly. Bulbhead goblins are now known for setting up small pop-up stalls to trade goods from within the Chitterwood with merchants and abandoning said stalls the moment they sense danger. They're some of the most social goblins around, easily haggling with traders and happily selling flora and fauna from deeper within the woods.

These interactions with non-goblinoids have also pitted the Bulbheads against the Isgeri Slayers, a bigoted anti-goblin organization. The Bulbheads loathe the Slayers and take every opportunity they can to humiliate them, raiding their camps and leaving gourds as taunts so the Slayers know exactly who sabotaged them. They'll even set tents aflame with Slayers sleeping inside without remorse, declaring that war is war and so is this!

Bulbhead goblins make fierce enemies and even fiercer friends, happy to share their bounty with any who come to them with open arms. They don't trend toward adventuring, but the occasional Bulbhead has gone off to become a daring fighter and returned with even better helms than gourds.

Chitterwood Goblins.name: Chitterwood Goblins
Chitterwood Goblins.text:
Chitterwood Goblins

Six generations have passed for goblinoids since the end of the Goblinblood Wars. During that time, many, if not most, goblins in Isger have called the caverns of Chitterwood home. While tribes like the People of the Swarm, Spine Threshers, and True Hoard are well known, hundreds of goblinoid cultures live in or beneath the Chitterwood, only a few of which are presented here. 

Some traits common across goblin society—fear of dogs and horses, love of song and fire, and wariness of the written word—endure among the goblins of the Chitterwood despite their horrific losses and subsequent displacement. Significant differences exist, however; in the war's aftermath, distinctions between cultural groups deepened as each dealt with the experience in their own way. The People of the Swarm tribe, for example, sings inspiring fight songs about taking revenge on their former hobgoblin commanders, while the Spine Threshers tribe excels in combat. The Hookback tribe, which now resides in the caves of the southern Chitterwood, takes its name from the particularly vicious torture it endured during the war. Surviving Hookback goblins inflicted their children with the same permanent, bone-deep piercings that had been forced upon them, transforming their pain into a symbol of survival and rite of passage into adulthood.

Before the Goblinblood Wars, goblins of the Chitterwood, like many forest goblins, tended to be fairly reclusive. This inclination doesn't mean they weren't dangerous when they wanted to be, however. Contact with non-goblinoids was generally limited, with the notable exception of scavenging and stealing from unwary travelers who passed through their territory. Goblin ambushes, when they did happen, could be as fierce as they were chaotic—a fact that hobgoblin commanders exploited for their own ends. The terror of the war reinforced the Chitterwood goblins' desire to keep to themselves as much as possible. With virtually all of their warriors dead, those goblins who survived the war were left largely defenseless. Today, goblins typically venture aboveground only when necessary and preferably under cover of night, lest they be discovered by someone bigger and more dangerous.

Some smaller tribes chose not to flee to the caverns at all, for different reasons and with mixed results. The area along the burned edges of the Chitterwood is home to the Bulbhead tribe, whose name comes from their distinctive practice of wearing masks made from gourds. During the war, sadistic hobgoblins commanders forced their goblin troops to wear gourds filled with wasps or spiders; goblins reclaimed their power by wearing masks on their own and robbing the hobgoblins of their fun. The crude masks are of dubious help in battle, but Bulbhead warriors make formidable foes nonetheless.

The Cinder Seekers are not actually a tribe at all, but rather an activist movement. Members travel throughout the Chitterwood on a mission to ensure that goblins never serve hobgoblins again. With arson as their weapon of choice, they take fiery vengeance against hobgoblins and their goblin collaborators.

Floods are common along the eastern edge of the Chitterwood, yet this area is where the tiny Mudrub tribe claims territory. As their name suggests, these goblins prefer to coat themselves in a thick layer of swamp muck and abhor any attempt to wash it off. During the war, hobgoblins punished Mudrub goblins by branding them with words. Survivors, ashamed and desperate to remove them, turned to burning and scarring themselves where they'd been branded, and eventually they began marking their children in a new tradition. Rejecting the written word, Mudrub goblins burn and scar their children with random patterns or images.

In some cases, the decision to not take refuge in the caverns has paid off. The Crookedtoes tribe became travelers and adventurers, journeying as far as Absalom and becoming valued allies to the Knights of Lastwall. The Dragondweller tribe has likewise provided aid to various human nations, earning the respect and protection of their allies.

Inhabitants.name: Inhabitants
Inhabitants.text:
Inhabitants

Aboveground and below, the Chitterwood's population is higher than many realize. While goblins represent the largest percentage of residents, one can also find a small number of hobgoblins and even non-goblinoids here.

The Caverns of the Chitterwood.name: The Caverns of the Chitterwood
The Caverns of the Chitterwood.text:
The Caverns of the Chitterwood

The Goblinblood Wars claimed a staggering number of lives on all sides, but for the goblin tribes, subjugated by hobgoblin commanders and hunted by the genocidal Isgeri Slayers, the conflict brought almost total annihilation. With most of the Chitterwood a smoldering ruin, there remained only one place for the surviving goblins to flee: underground.

Deep beneath the remains of the Chitterwood lies a vast network of caverns and warrens—an ideal, if less than pleasant, place for a devastated people to hide, regroup, and rebuild. Much to the tribes' annoyance, however, the caverns were already home to a number of creatures who weren't exactly keen to share their space. The bats and rats at least proved tolerably tasty, but the cave bears were another story altogether; the People of the Swarm tribe, which already had over 190 songs graphically describing the danger of bear attacks, soon added new songs specifically warning about cave bears.

Surviving the caverns of Chitterwood for an extended period is difficult for several reasons outside of ursine encounters. The only light to be found is near the cave entrances, humidity is high, and food is limited. Fortunately for goblins, their darkvision, resourcefulness, and ability to digest pretty much anything organic means they're better suited for living in caves than most other Golarion residents. Goblins prefer meat when they can get it—rats make a good stew, and bats pickle well—but most of their diet in the caverns consists of fungi and insects, with frogs and fish occasionally rounding out the menu.

Every once in a while, sometimes out of boredom and sometimes on a dare, a cavern-dwelling goblin risks a trip to the world above in search of tastier eats or shiny new treasures. This is generally frowned upon by the eldest tribe members, whose parents and grandparents were survivors of the war; visibly scarred and deeply afraid, that first generation passed their understandable fear on to their children. Younger goblins who have never known life outside the caverns are more willing to explore the world above, even when not patrolling or hunting. Some particularly wise goblin leaders have begun the delicate process of reestablishing diplomatic relations with non-goblins to better deal with the increasing threat of undead roaming the countryside.

Welcome to the Chitterwood.name: Welcome to the Chitterwood
Welcome to the Chitterwood.text:
Welcome to the Chitterwood

Isger is a land of many scars, both literal and metaphorical, and no place better illustrates this quality than the once-dense hardwood forest known as the Chitterwood. Located in southern Isger near the Conerica River, the Aspodell Mountains, and the city of Logas, the Chitterwood has long been home to hundreds of goblinoid tribes. It's also home to a trade route favored by smugglers. Travel through these woods has always been a risky affair due to the threat of bandits, but desperate and unsavory travelers are willing to traverse the Chitterwood to stay off Isger's main roads.
